The blocker (per D77) was that this port modelled a field as just a name string on `LdsFlda`/`LdFlda`, with no token or attributes, so the C# `cacheField.IsCompilerGeneratedOrIsInCompilerGeneratedClass()` check (the gate that recognises a compiler-synthesized cache field -- a `<PrivateImplementationDetails>` static or a display-class field) could not be faithful. Three pieces landed: (1) `LdFlda` and `LdsFlda` (MemoryInstructions.hpp) gained an `IsCompilerGeneratedField` bool and a `FieldToken` (the raw metadata token, table 0x04 FieldDef or 0x0A field MemberRef, the reader resolved the name from), both default false/0. (2) The IL reader (ILReader.cpp) populates both for every field access (ldfld/ldflda/stfld/ldsfld/ldsflda/stsfld) from the token it already reads, via a new `MetadataFile::IsFieldCompilerGeneratedOrInCompilerGeneratedClass(fieldToken)` (the resolution is once per field-access site at read time; this port's transforms have no MetadataFile handle, so the check is pre-resolved and stored on the node, matching the field-name / Call::DeclaringType precedent). (3) `MetadataFile::IsFieldCompilerGeneratedOrInCompilerGeneratedClass` mirrors the C# `NRExtensions.IsCompilerGeneratedOrIsInCompilerGeneratedClass`: the field's own `[CompilerGenerated]` (System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CompilerGeneratedAttribute) custom attribute, or (recursively up the nesting chain) its declaring type's. For a FieldDef (0x04): check the field's CustomAttribute range, then walk `f.Parent()` (the declaring TypeDef) up via `TypeDef::EnclosingType()` (winmd's NestedClass table lookup), checking each type's CustomAttribute range (a 64-level depth guard stops a malformed cyclic NestedClass chain). For a field MemberRef (0x0A): only an in-module TypeDef parent is checked (a cross-assembly TypeRef needs the full type system, matching the C# which needs it too); TypeRef/TypeSpec parents return false. The attribute match is a file-local `RangeHasCompilerGenerated` template helper that iterates the winmd `CustomAttribute` equal_range pair (the row type IS the iterator -- row_base is a random-access iterator -- so the pair is std::pair<Row,Row>, not std::pair<iterator,iterator>) and compares `TypeNamespaceAndName()` to "System.Runtime.CompilerServices"/"CompilerGeneratedAttribute" (the try/catch mirrors the existing GetCustomAttributes `collect` lambda, since `TypeNamespaceAndName()` throws for an unexpected MemberRefParent). The `ArrayInitializers` setting (default true, matching DecompilerSettings) is added to ILTransformSettings; it gates `CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization` (the next in-order transform). This is a tested-but-not-yet-wired foundation (no pipeline transform consults the flag yet, so `--csharp` output is unchanged), mirroring the D63/D66/D68/D70/D74/D76 foundations. 6 new gtest cases (NodeCarriesFlagAndToken; ArrayInitializersSettingDefault; InvalidTokenIsGraceful; NonCompilerGeneratedField on System.String's first field; MscorlibHasCompilerGeneratedFields scanning every TypeDef's fields via the helper and asserting the corpus carries CG fields -- the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib has cached-delegate / display-class CG fields; ReaderPopulatesFlag decoding 8000 methods, finding LdsFlda/LdFlda, and cross-checking each node's `IsCompilerGeneratedField == file.IsFieldCompilerGeneratedOrInCompilerGeneratedClass(FieldToken)` plus the invariant holds). 379/379 gtest cases pass (6 new; was 373). The CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- the per-field-access helper call adds negligible cost). The transform itself stays the next concrete target: `CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization` (the next in-order transform after CachedDelegateInitialization) now has its IField dependency met; the remaining work is the block-model adaptation (the C# reads the cache `if (V == null) { body }` with the body nested as a Block in the if's TrueInst, but this port's if-as-final model leaves the body as a separate container block reachable by the if's Branch TrueInst, and ConditionDetection's TryInlineIfFallThrough inlines the single-pred fall-through into the if's FALSE arm, so the body ends up as the if's FalseInst Block, not the TrueInst -- the adaptation must match this port's inverted shape, which has no real corpus occurrence to probe since ReadOnlySpan is not in the .NET Framework 4 mscorlib, so a hand-built probe through the pre-pipeline is needed, the D73/D75 precedent), and the six field-cached delegate shapes (now unblocked on the IField side) still need the same block-model adaptation plus the per-variable store-list tree walk and a corpus probe of the real field-cached if/Block shape. |
| D79 | CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization (Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/Transforms/CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization.cs (the next in-order transform after CachedDelegateInitialization, the D78 IField foundation having unblocked it). It collapses the compiler-synthesized lazy cache Roslyn emits for a ReadOnlySpan<T> created from an array literal on target frameworks without RuntimeHelpers.CreateSpan (e.g. .NET Framework or netstandard2.0 + System.Memory) -- `stloc V(ldobj T[](ldsflda <PrivateImplementationDetails>.cache)); if (comp(ldloc V == ldnull)) { stloc V(arrayInitializer); stobj T[](ldsflda cache, ldloc V) }; <single usage of V>` -- into the unconditional init `stloc V(arrayInitializer); <usage>`, so a later array-initializer transform recovers the array literal and the reference to the escaped <PrivateImplementationDetails> cache field (whose name is not expressible in C# and is never declared, so the un-transformed output does not recompile -- CS0400) disappears. It mirrors CachedDelegateInitialization and runs right after it (the GetILTransforms() BlockILTransform post-order position). Adapted to this port's if-as-final block model: the C# carries the if as a non-terminal at block.Instructions[i] with the cache-load store at [i-1] and the body as a Block in the if's TrueInst; this port makes the IfInstruction the block's FinalInstruction, so the cache-load store is the block's last non-terminal instruction (Instructions.back()) and the if is the final. KEY FINDING (correcting D78's prediction): a hand-built probe through the pre-pipeline (CFS + LoopDetection + ConditionDetection) confirmed this port's post-ConditionDetection shape IS the C# shape, NOT the inverted shape D78 feared. The reader emits `if (comp(V != null)) br usage` for `brtrue usage` (skip the body when the cache is populated -- the cache-hit fast path), with the body as the separate fall-through block; ConditionDetection's TryInlineIfFallThrough inlines that body block (single predecessor) into the if's FalseInst, then TryInvertIfExit (the usage block is the next block after the inlined body is removed) inverts -- negating the condition to `comp(V == null)` (Equality) and moving the body into the TrueInst as a Block (FalseInst null, fall-through to the usage) -- exactly the C# shape. The one port-specific difference: the body Block carries a trailing Branch to the usage block (the reader makes fall-through explicit), which the C# body does not; the fold preserves that trailing control flow as the host block's new final, dropping the goto when the body falls through to the next block (the common cache-pattern case, verified by the probe) so no spurious `goto IL_XXXX` survives (matching the C#, which just removes the if), and otherwise keeping the body's exit so the control flow is preserved. A body with no trailing control flow (the C# shape) just drops the if. The cache-field gate uses the D78 `LdsFlda::IsCompilerGeneratedField` flag the IL reader pre-resolves from the field token's [CompilerGenerated] custom attribute (or its declaring type's); two LdsFlda nodes are the same cache field by FieldToken (the reader populates it) or, failing that, FieldName. The transform is an IILTransform iterating every container's blocks (mirroring CachedDelegateInitialization, not the C# IBlockTransform), gated on the ArrayInitializers setting (default true, from D78). The fold nulls the block's final (destroying the if and the body Block, an if-arm that holds no nested BlockContainer), so no container is destroyed and a single gathered container list stays valid (the CachedDelegateInitialization structure, not the UsingTransform re-gather pattern); ComputeVariableUsage + RecomputeIncomingEdgeCounts run before and after so the StoreCount==2/LoadCount==3/AddressCount==0 guards and the post-fold counts are fresh. ReadOnlySpan<T> is absent from the .NET Framework 4 mscorlib corpus, so this fires 0 times on it (it fires on Roslyn-compiled / modern .NET with System.Memory); ported for faithfulness -- the hand-built tests verify the rewrite (the positive test builds the post-reader shape and runs the full pre-pipeline through ConditionDetection so the transform is exercised on the real post-ConditionDetection shape) and the 8000-method sweep verifies the ILAst invariant holds (not a fold count), matching the DetectCatchWhenConditionBlocks / LdLocaDupInitObj / SwitchOnNullable precedent. Wired into the CLI pipeline after CachedDelegateInitialization and before AssignVariableNames (the GetILTransforms() position); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression). 10 new gtest cases (FoldsCacheToInitializer; RejectsNonCompilerGeneratedCacheField; RejectsExtraStore; RejectsExtraLoad; RejectsElseArm; RejectsInequalityCondition -- a direct construction of the C# shape with Inequality to test the Equality guard in isolation, since the real pipeline always inverts to Equality; RejectsInitStoreDifferentVariable; RejectsWritebackToDifferentField; ArrayInitializersOffIsNoOp; MscorlibSweepPreservesInvariant). 389/389 gtest cases pass (10 new; was 379). |
| D80 | StatementTransform orchestration + ILInlining per-statement (Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/Transforms/StatementTransform.cs (the next in-order block after CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization, the final member of the GetILTransforms() BlockILTransform post-order set). The C# StatementTransform is an IBlockTransform that runs a list of IStatementTransform children interleaved per-statement with rerun mechanics: it walks the block's instructions last-to-first, and at each position runs every child; a child may call RequestRerun(pos) to jump the driver back to pos and re-run all children (the C# driver asserts rerunPosition >= the current pos, so the jump is forward to an already-processed statement), or RequestRerun() to re-run at the current position -- the interleaving lets a transform that opens up a new inlining opportunity (e.g. TransformAssignment) trigger the ILInlining child to fold it without a separate full-block pass. This port models the BlockILTransform post-order transforms as IILTransform (whole-function, iterating blocks internally), so StatementTransform is an IILTransform that walks every Block and runs the per-statement driver on each. Three pieces landed: (1) the IStatementTransform interface (Run(Block&, pos, StatementTransformContext&)), the StatementTransformContext (wraps the underlying ILTransformContext + the current Block + the rerunPosition/rerunCurrentPosition state + RequestRerun/RequestRerunCurrentPosition), and the StatementTransform IILTransform driver (RunBlock walks pos from Instructions.size()-1 down to 0, running each child and handling the rerun-current/rerun-position jumps); (2) ILInlining now also implements IStatementTransform (a per-statement Run overload that loops InlineOneIfPossible at the given position until no change, mirroring the C# ILInlining.Run(Block, pos, ctx)); (3) the CLI wires StatementTransform{ILInlining} after CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization and before AssignVariableNames. Adapted to the port's if-as-final block model: the final lives separately (FinalInstruction, not in Instructions), so the per-statement positions range over the non-terminal Instructions only (the C# ranges over Instructions including the final, but the final is never a StLoc, so the C#'s first iteration at the final is a no-op -- starting at the last non-terminal is equivalent); the per-statement ILInlining's while (InlineOneIfPossible(block, pos)) loop re-checks pos < size after a removal shrank the block (the C# avoids this because the final lives in Instructions, so the last non-terminal is at Count-2 and the shifted-in instruction stays in range -- a bounds guard is essential in this port and was added to InlineOneIfPossible). The driver runs on every block (including if-final blocks): the if-as-final model makes the if the block's FinalInstruction, so a stloc at the last non-terminal position inlines into the if's condition (the "next" for the last non-terminal is the final), matching the C# where the stloc before the if non-terminal inlines into the if. The remaining 15 per-statement children (ExpressionTransforms, DynamicIsEventAssignmentTransform, TransformAssignment, NullCoalescingTransform, NullableLiftingStatementTransform, NullPropagationStatementTransform, TransformArrayInitializers, TransformCollectionAndObjectInitializers, TransformExpressionTrees, IndexRangeTransform, DeconstructionTransform, NamedArgumentTransform, RemoveUnconstrainedGenericReferenceTypeCheck, UserDefinedLogicTransform, InterpolatedStringTransform) and the ILInlining AllowInliningOfLdloca option (the ldloca-into-addressof path the C# second pass enables, which needs an AddressOf node + IsGeneratedTemporaryForAddressOf + ClassifyExpression + the value-type/readonly/in-parameter copy semantics) are deferred to later iterations. The ILInlining IILTransform whole-function pass (the early inlining, D40) is unchanged; the per-statement Run is the C# pipeline's SECOND inlining pass, which folds the single-use variables the intervening transforms (ConditionDetection / Lock / Using / CachedDelegate / CachedReadOnlySpan) created. Wired into the CLI pipeline after CachedReadOnlySpanInitialization and before AssignVariableNames (the GetILTransforms() position); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 517 lock / 313 using statements unchanged; the second inlining pass is a safe fold across the corpus). 6 new gtest cases (OrchestrationRunsChildrenLastToFirst; OrchestrationRequestRerunCurrentPosition; OrchestrationRequestRerunPosition -- the three orchestration tests use a mock IStatementTransform to pin the rerun mechanics without a real transform; PerStatementInliningFoldsSingleUseLocal; PerStatementInliningFoldsIntoIfFinalCondition -- pins the if-as-final block-model shape where the stloc before the if-final inlines into the if's condition; MscorlibSweepPreservesInvariant running the full pre-pipeline through StatementTransform{ILInlining} over 8000 methods). 395/395 gtest cases pass (6 new; was 389). |
| D81 | ExpressionTransforms (VisitComp subset, Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports the self-contained VisitComp subset of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/Transforms/ExpressionTransforms.cs (the second per-statement child of the GetILTransforms() StatementTransform, after ILInlining -- the next in-order target after the D80 orchestration). The C# ExpressionTransforms is an ILVisitor IStatementTransform folding simple expression patterns; this iteration ports the three highest-value, self-contained VisitComp rewrites: (1) `logic.not(comp op) -> comp(op.Negate)` (push negation into the comparison -- `!(a == b)` -> `a != b`), where `logic.not` is this port's `comp(Equality, X, ldc.i4 0)` shape (the reader's brfalse, D55/D64/D68); the C# MatchLogicNot is `Kind == Equality && LiftingKind.None && Right.MatchLdcI4(0)` (the port drops LiftingKind -- no nullable-lifting model); if X is a Comp the negation is pushed (the float guard `!comp.InputType.IsFloatType()` is approximated by checking the inner comp's operands' StackType for F4/F8, since the port's Comp carries no InputType; an equality/inequality is always pushed, the `|| IsEqualityOrInequality`), else the logic.not is kept and X's subtree is visited; (2) `comp(x != 0) -> x` when the comp is in a condition slot (an if condition, or nested in an if's true/false arm, or as one side of a comp whose other side is ldc.i4 0) or its left is itself a comp (`comp(comp(...) != 0)` -> `comp(...)`) -- a port of IfInstruction.IsInConditionSlot via Parent + ChildIndex (Condition=0, TrueInst=1, FalseInst=2; the NullCoalescingInstruction.FallbackInstSlot case is dropped, no NullCoalescing node); (3) `comp.unsigned(left > 0) -> comp(left != 0)` and `comp.unsigned(left <= 0) -> comp(left == 0)` (an unsigned compare against 0 is a (non-)zero test), with the C# `UnwrapConv(SignExtend/ZeroExtend)` of the right operand approximated by `IsLdcI4ZeroMaybeConv` (a bare `ldc.i4 0` or a Conv wrapping it -- the port's Conv carries no Kind, so UnwrapConv-by-Kind cannot be faithful; the rare non-sign/zero-extend conv around 0 does not arise from the reader's comparisons). The transform is a recursive Visit dispatching on OpCode (the C# ILVisitor's AcceptVisitor / Default): non-Comp nodes recurse into their children; VisitComp runs the head rewrites (logic.not, comp(!=0)) before recursing into the operands, then the tail rewrite (unsigned normalization) after, re-visiting the node on a rewrite (matching the C# `VisitComp(inst); return;`). KEY block-model work: the C# carries the if as a non-terminal at Instructions[Count-2] so the per-statement driver visits it and recurses into its condition; this port makes the if the FinalInstruction (not in Instructions), so (a) ExpressionTransforms::Run visits the if-final's Condition at `pos == Instructions.size()-1` (the port's equivalent of the C# visiting the if at Count-2) so the `if (comp(x != 0))` -> `if (x)` rewrite fires on if-final blocks with non-terminal statements, and (b) the StatementTransform driver gained a block-model compensation: a block whose ONLY instruction is the if-final (no non-terminal Instructions, `pos` starts at -1 so the per-statement loop never enters) is visited by running each child once with the sentinel `pos = -1`; children that only handle non-terminal positions (ILInlining, which guards `pos >= 0 && pos < size`) no-op, and ExpressionTransforms visits the if-final's Condition at `pos == size-1` (which is `-1 == -1` for the size==0 case). This is essential: if-final-only blocks (every `if (cond) { ... } else { ... }` with no preceding statements) are the COMMON case after ConditionDetection, so without the compensation the comp(!=0)->x / logic.not rewrites would almost never fire on the corpus -- the CLI output now shows `if (array.Length)` (from `comp(ldlen != 0)` -> `ldlen` in a condition slot) and `if (!value)` (the kept logic.not of a bool param). Deferred vs the C#: the NullableLiftingTransform call (needs the full nullable-lift transform), FixComparisonKindLdNull (already in the standalone EarlyExpressionTransforms, D61), the ldlen / conv o->i null-comparison special cases (need Conv Kind), and every other visit method (VisitConv / VisitBox / VisitLdElema / VisitNewArr / VisitCall / VisitNewObj / VisitLdObj / VisitLdObjIfRef / VisitStObj / VisitStLoc / VisitIfInstruction [HandleConditionalOperator, logic.and/or canonicalization, NullableLifting, UserDefinedLogic, match(x)?true:false] / HandleSwitchExpression [needs SwitchExpressions setting + SwitchInstruction guards] / VisitDynamic* / VisitBinaryNumericInstruction [shift-size] / VisitTryCatchHandler) -- each needs further infrastructure (AddressOf, LdcDecimal, dynamic nodes, the resolver, MatchLogicAnd/Or, IndexRangeTransform, TransformAssignment, ...) and is a later iteration; the logic.and/logic.or negation push in VisitLogicNot is deferred (needs MatchLogicAnd/Or on IfInstruction true/false-arm patterns plus new Comp/If construction). This is faithful to the C# (its IsPatternMatch also treats a Comp-with-constant-right as a constant pattern), so the fold is correct, not a mis-fire. NOTE: the CLI `--csharp` line count is non-deterministic across runs (~+/-140 lines for the SAME binary, a pre-existing pipeline issue from unordered-container iteration order, unrelated to this change), so the line-count is not a reliable regression signal; the 415/415 gtest suite (including the deterministic 8000-method mscorlib sweep asserting the ILAst invariant holds and the ternary-fold count is monotone non-decreasing) is the correctness gate. 5 new gtest cases (MatchTrueFalseFoldsToMatchInValuePosition -- the if as a sub-expression value `stloc V(if (match) 1 else 0)` folds to `stloc V(match)` via in-place ReplaceWith; MatchTrueFalseFoldsToMatchAsBlockFinal -- the if as a block FinalInstruction folds to a non-terminal match + a Branch-to-next-block final; MatchTrueFalseRejectsNonPatternCondition -- a bare ldloc condition does not fold; MatchTrueFalseRejectsNonOneTrueArm; MatchTrueFalseRejectsNonZeroFalseArm). 415/415 gtest cases pass (5 new; was 410). |
| D84 | ExpressionTransforms (VisitBox subset) + shared IsReferenceType helper (Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports the `VisitBox` subset of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/Transforms/ExpressionTransforms.cs (extending the D81/D82/D83 ExpressionTransforms subset of the second per-statement child of the GetILTransforms() StatementTransform) and promotes the previously file-local `IsReferenceType` query to a shared, faithful header. The rewrite is `box ref-type(arg) => arg`: for a reference type, `box` is a no-op (the value is already on the heap), so the C# checks `inst.Type.IsReferenceType == true && inst.Argument.ResultType == inst.ResultType` and replaces the box with its argument. The `ResultType` guard (the argument is stack-type O, the box is O) is the real protection against a value-type mis-fire: a value type's argument is I4/I8/F4/.. (never O), so even a non-known TypeRef whose `Kind` defaulted to `Class` (this port's plain `MakeTypeRef` leaves an unresolved type as Class) does not fold when the argument is not object-typed. `IsReferenceType` returns `nullopt` for the uncertain kinds (TypeParameter/ByRef/Pointer/Unknown/None/Other/UnboundTypeArgument/ArgList/Tuple/Intersection/ModOpt/ModReq), so a `box T(arg)` over a generic T does not fold (the C# folds it only when T has a `class` constraint this minimal type system does not track) -- conservative, matching the C# `IsReferenceType == true` requirement. The fold is `TakeChild(0)` (detach the argument) then `ReplaceWith(arg)` (the C# `inst.ReplaceWith(arg)`); the argument is visited first (the C# `inst.Argument.AcceptVisitor(this)`) so the Comp/StLoc rewrites cascade into the boxed expression before the box is considered for removal. Foundation piece: a new header `Decompiler/TypeSystem/TypeUtils.hpp` declares `std::optional<bool> IsReferenceType(const IType*)` faithful to the C# `bool? IType.IsReferenceType` (true for Class/Interface/Delegate/Array/Dynamic/Null; false for Struct/Enum/Void/NInt/NUInt/FunctionPointer; nullopt otherwise -- a null ITypePtr is nullopt; ParameterizedType/ModifiedType/Tuple defer to their underlying Kind() which this port's Kind() overrides already fold in). This dedups the previously file-local `IsReferenceType` in PatternMatchingTransform.cpp (which had minor faithfulness bugs: Dynamic/Null mapped to nullopt instead of true, NInt/NUInt mapped to true instead of false) to the shared faithful one, and supersedes the inline `IsRef(TypeKind)` bool checks in EarlyExpressionTransforms / LdLocaDupInitObjTransform (left as-is -- different signature/purpose). The PatternMatchingTransform dedup is behavior-preserving on the common kinds (Class/Interface/Delegate/Array -> true, Struct/Enum/Void -> false, TypeParameter/ByRef/Pointer/Unknown -> nullopt) and more faithful on the edge kinds (Dynamic/Null -> true, NInt/NUInt -> false) that never arise as an isinst target, verified by the unchanged PatternMatchingTransform sweep. KEY FINDING: the VisitBox fold DOES fire on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus (not 0, unlike several earlier transforms) -- the sweep counted 42 firings across 8000 methods; the C# compiler/codegen does emit `box <ref-type>(arg)` (redundant boxes the JIT would elide) at that rate, so this is a real-corpus ILAst-cleaning transform, not a faithfulness-only one. The ILAstToCSharp seed already renders `box(arg)` as just `arg` for ALL boxes ("boxing is implicit in C#"), so the CLI `--csharp` output is unchanged (the seed drops the box at render time regardless); the value is ILAst-level cleanliness for the future real back end (the Phase 5 seed is a placeholder) and the 42 redundant boxes are removed from the ILAst. Deferred vs the C#: VisitConv (the next visit method in file order -- its first rewrite `conv.i4(ldlen) => ldlen.i4` is blocked by this port's LdLen model divergence: the C# LdLen returns native int `I` and the conv converts it, but this port's LdLen already returns `I4`, so the conv is a no-op I4->I4 and `conv.i8(ldlen)` cannot be faithfully rewritten since the port's LdLen cannot produce `I8`; the second `conv.rN(conv.r.un(...))` rewrite needs `Conv::Kind` (ConversionKind.IntToFloat) which the port's Conv does not carry), VisitLdElema/VisitNewArr's `CleanUpArrayIndices` (needs `Conv::Kind` -- Truncate/ZeroExtend/SignExtend -- the same recurring blocker), and the other visit methods (see D81/D82/D83). Wired into the CLI pipeline as the second child of StatementTransform (unchanged -- the same ExpressionTransforms IStatementTransform now also dispatches `OpCode::Box`); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression). 5 new gtest cases (VisitBoxDropsBoxOfReferenceType -- `box string(ldloc s)` folds to `ldloc s`; VisitBoxKeepsBoxOfValueType -- `box int(ldloc i)` stays, the I4 argument does not match the O box result; VisitBoxKeepsBoxOfTypeParameter -- `box T(ldloc t)` stays, IsReferenceType is nullopt; VisitBoxKeepsBoxWithNullType -- a null type does not dereference; VisitBoxDropsBoxOfObjectReferenceType -- `box object(ldloc o)` folds to `ldloc o`; plus the updated MscorlibSweepPreservesInvariant asserting the Box count is monotone non-increasing across the corpus and printing the fold count). 420/420 gtest cases pass (5 new; was 415). |
| D85 | Conv ConversionKind model + ExpressionTransforms (VisitLdElema/VisitNewArr CleanUpArrayIndices) (Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports the faithful `ConversionKind` model for the Conv node (the recurring blocker D84 identified for the next several ExpressionTransforms visit methods) and the `VisitLdElema`/`VisitNewArr` `CleanUpArrayIndices` rewrite that consumes it. The C# Conv carries `Kind` (ConversionKind), `InputType` (StackType), `InputSign` (Sign), `TargetType` (PrimitiveType), `CheckForOverflow`, `IsLifted`; the Kind is derived via `GetConversionKind(targetType, inputType, inputSign)` (Ecma-335 Table 8). This port previously stored only the target `StackType` + a `CheckForOverflow` bool on Conv, collapsing the signed/unsigned sizes (I4 covered both I4 and U4, I8 both I8/U8, I both I/U) so the sign- vs zero-extension distinction CleanUpArrayIndices needs (conv.i vs conv.u) was unrepresentable. Foundation: three new headers -- `Decompiler/TypeSystem/Sign.hpp` (the `Sign` enum None/Signed/Unsigned, mirroring TypeUtils.cs), `Decompiler/IL/PrimitiveType.hpp` (the `PrimitiveType` enum None/I1/I2/I4/I8/R4/R8/U1/U2/U4/U8/I/U/Ref/R/Unknown plus `GetStackType`/`IsIntegerType`/`IsFloatType` helpers faithful to ILTypeExtensions), and `Decompiler/IL/ConversionKind.hpp` (the `ConversionKind` enum Invalid/Nop/IntToFloat/FloatToInt/FloatPrecisionChange/SignExtend/ZeroExtend/Truncate/StopGCTracking/StartGCTracking/ObjectInterior plus a faithful `GetConversionKind(PrimitiveType, StackType, Sign)` porting Conv.cs's Ecma-335 Table 8 verbatim, including the I8/U8 and I/U signedness-decides-when-inputSign-is-None branch and the input-sign-decides branch when overflow-checking). The Conv node (`Decompiler/IL/Instructions/Conv.hpp`) is rewritten to store `Kind`/`InputType`/`InputSign`/`TargetType`/`CheckForOverflow`; the constructor mirrors the C# Conv constructor's `needsSign = checkForOverflow || (!IsFloatType(InputType) && IsFloatType(targetType))` rule (InputSign is the passed sign when needsSign, else None) and derives Kind via GetConversionKind; ResultType is `GetStackType(TargetType)`; DirectFlags adds MayThrow when CheckForOverflow; the dump renders the target/sign/Kind annotation (sign/zero-extend) faithful to the C# WriteToCore. The IL reader is restructured: the generic `IL_CONV(opc, target)`/`IL_CONVOVF(opc, target)` macros (which emitted `Conv(v, StackType::target, ...)`) are replaced by per-sign macros `IL_CONV` (Sign::None), `IL_CONV_S` (Sign::Signed -- conv.r4/r8), `IL_CONV_U` (Sign::Unsigned -- conv.r.un), `IL_CONVOVF` (Sign::Signed), `IL_CONVOVFU` (Sign::Unsigned -- the _un overflow variants), each passing the opcode's `PrimitiveType` (I1/I2/I4/U1/U2/U4/I8/U8/I/U/R4/R8/R) -- faithfully mirroring the C# ILReader's per-opcode `(Pop(), PrimitiveType.X, checkForOverflow, sign)` emission. The two existing Conv constructor call sites outside the reader are updated: SwitchDetection.cpp's switch-value conv to I8 (`Conv(switchValue, PrimitiveType::I8, false, Sign::None)`, the Kind is SignExtend/Nop/Truncate depending on the switch value's StackType -- harmless, the switch value is already I4/I8) and the ILAstToCSharp seed/test conv-over-ldlen (`Conv(ldlen, PrimitiveType::I4, false, Sign::None)`, a Nop). The seed's Conv rendering (`ILAstToCSharp.cpp`) is updated to consult `conv.ResultType()` (was the removed `TargetStackType` field) for both the ldlen-implicit special case and the cast-name lookup. Consumer: `CleanUpArrayIndices` (ported into ExpressionTransforms as `VisitLdElema`/`VisitNewArr` -- the C# VisitLdElema additionally calls `IndexRangeTransform.HandleLdElema`, deferred; the CleanUpArrayIndices part is self-contained). It drops a `conv.i` (or `conv.ovf.i`) widening of an array index -- a Conv whose ResultType is I (native int) and whose Kind is SignExtend, ZeroExtend, or a checked Truncate (Kind == Truncate && CheckForOverflow) -- replacing the conv with its argument (the index is implicitly native-int in C#). An unchecked Truncate (conv.i from I8, no overflow check) is a real truncation and is kept; a Nop conv (conv.i4, ResultType I4) is excluded by the `ResultType == I` guard. The replacement is `conv->TakeChild(0)` (detach the argument) then `index->ReplaceWith(arg)` (the C# `index.ReplaceWith(conv.Argument)` -- ReplaceWith destroys the conv and reparents the argument into the LdElema/NewArr Indices slot, mirroring the VisitBox pattern). The Visit dispatch gains `OpCode::LdElema`/`OpCode::NewArr` cases routing to VisitLdElema/VisitNewArr (which visit the children first, mirroring the C# `base.VisitLdElema`/`base.VisitNewArr`, then CleanUpArrayIndices). The D81 `IsLdcI4ZeroMaybeConv` approximation (which accepted ANY conv around ldc.i4 0 because the Conv carried no Kind) is retired in favor of a faithful `UnwrapConv` free function (a non-owning port of `ILInstruction.UnwrapConv(kind)`): `UnwrapConv(UnwrapConv(inst, SignExtend), ZeroExtend)` peels sign/zero-extending convs around the 0 before the ldc.i4 0 test -- the real array-length-comparison pattern (`comp.unsigned(ldlen > conv.i(ldc.i4 0))` -> the conv.i SignExtend unwraps to ldc.i4 0), and a Nop conv.i4 around 0 no longer mis-folds. KEY FINDING: the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus emits `conv.i` before ldelema only rarely -- the 8000-method sweep counted 1 array-index-conv drop (the legacy csc mostly emits ldelema with bare I4 indices); CleanUpArrayIndices is a real-corpus ILAst-cleaning transform that fires on Roslyn-compiled / 64-bit-indexed code more than on this corpus, but it does fire (1 drop), so it is not faithfulness-only. The Conv Kind model is exercised on the corpus via the existing ILReader tests (every conv.* opcode the reader emits now carries the faithful Kind). The conv.ovf.u from I4 with a Signed input sign-EXTENDS (not zero-extends) -- the C# GetConversionKind for the I/U target decides SignExtend vs ZeroExtend by the INPUT sign when overflow-checking, not the target -- a faithful-but-surprising behavior the Conv_Test pins. Deferred vs the C#: VisitConv (the next visit method in file order -- its `conv.i4(ldlen) => ldlen.i4` rewrite is still blocked by the LdLen model divergence: this port's LdLen already returns I4 so conv.i4(ldlen) is a no-op I4->I4 -- droppable for the I4 case but conv.i8(ldlen) cannot be faithfully rewritten since LdLen cannot produce I8; its `conv.rN(conv.r.un(...))` rewrite is now UNBLOCKED by the Conv Kind model but is a separate iteration), the remaining visit methods (VisitCall/VisitNewObj/VisitLdObj/VisitLdObjIfRef/VisitStObj/VisitStLoc -- HandleCompoundAssign needs TransformAssignment; VisitIfInstruction's NullableLifting/UserDefinedLogic/TransformDynamicAddAssignOrRemoveAssign; HandleSwitchExpression; VisitDynamic*; VisitBinaryNumericInstruction; VisitTryCatchHandler), and the remaining StatementTransform per-statement children -- each needs further infrastructure. Wired into the CLI pipeline as the second child of StatementTransform (unchanged -- the same ExpressionTransforms IStatementTransform now also dispatches LdElema/NewArr); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, 451941 lines). 24 new gtest cases (18 in a new `tests/Decompiler/IL/Instructions/Conv_Test.cpp` covering the PrimitiveType/StackType helpers, the per-opcode Kind computation -- conv.i/conv.u/conv.ovf.i/conv.ovf.u/conv.ovf.i_un from I4, conv.i from I8/native, conv.i4/i1/i8/u8, conv.r4/r8/r.un, conv.r4 from F8/F4, the CheckForOverflow MayThrow flag, and UnwrapConv; plus 6 CleanUpArrayIndices cases -- DropsConvIFromLdElema, DropsConvUFromNewArr, DropsConvOvfIFromLdElema, KeepsConvIFromI8, KeepsConvI4, LeavesBareIndex -- and the updated MscorlibSweepPreservesInvariant asserting the array-index-conv count is monotone non-increasing). 444/444 gtest cases pass (24 new; was 420). |

| D87 | ExpressionTransforms (VisitBinaryNumericInstruction shift-size subset) (Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports the `VisitBinaryNumericInstruction` shift-size subset of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/Transforms/ExpressionTransforms.cs (extending the D81-D86 ExpressionTransforms subset of the second per-statement child of the GetILTransforms() StatementTransform). The C# VisitBinaryNumericInstruction has two cases: (1) the ShiftLeft/ShiftRight case -- `a << (b & 31) => a << b` / `a >> (b & 63) => a >> b` -- a shift's right operand masked with the bit-width minus one is redundant in C# (the shift already masks the count), so the `& mask` is dropped (the BitAnd's Left becomes the shift's new Right); the mask must be the expected width for the shift's result type (`MatchExpectedShiftSize`: ldc.i4 31 for I4, ldc.i4 63 for I8, or the native-int `sizeof(IntPtr) * 8 - 1` for I). This case is ported here. (2) the BitAnd case -- `bitAnd(bool, bool)` when both operands InferType to Boolean runs NullableLiftingTransform (e.g. `(a.GetValueOrDefault() == b.GetValueOrDefault()) & (a.HasValue & b.HasValue)`) -- is deferred (needs the full NullableLiftingTransform + InferType, neither of which this minimal type system carries). The `MatchExpectedShiftSize` helper covers I4 (ldc.i4 31) and I8 (ldc.i4 63); the native-int (I) case -- `sizeof(IntPtr) * 8 - 1` -- is deferred (the port's SizeOf is a minimal SimpleInstruction carrying only a name string, no IType, so the C# `size.MatchSizeOf(out var sizeofType) && sizeofType.GetStackType() == StackType.I` check cannot be faithful; it returns false so the native-int mask is left in place). The children are visited first (the C# `base.VisitBinaryNumericInstruction`) so the Comp/StLoc/Box/Conv rewrites cascade into the operands before the shift-size mask is considered; the C# does not `RequestRerun` here, so the port does not re-visit the replacement. The `OpCode::BinaryNumericInstruction` case is wired into the recursive `Visit` dispatch (after `NewArr`, before the Default). The existing `IsLdcI4(inst, value)` file-local helper (the non-owning ldc.i4 value test) is reused for the 31/63 mask checks. The existing tests sidestep this by separating the declaration from the preceding ASSERT with an intervening `EXPECT_EQ` (no goto) or by declaring the variable before the ASSERT; the new `BitAndStaysForDeferredNullableLift` test follows the latter (declares `bni` right after `st`, before any ASSERT). | D99 | BitSet util (foundation for the next in-order NullableLifting DoLift/DoLiftBinary relevance analysis and the deferred DefiniteAssignment/Dominance/ReachingDefinitions, Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports `BitSet` (`cpp/Decompiler/Util/BitSet.hpp`, header-only in `namespace ILSpy::Decompiler::Util`, faithful to `ICSharpCode.Decompiler/Util/BitSet.cs`) as a tested-but-not-yet-wired foundation, ahead of the next in-order NullableLifting piece (the `MatchCompOrDecimal`/`LiftCSharp*` comparison-lift path, the first deferred item in D98's list), following the D63 LongSet / D66 LoopContext / D68 NullableLifting helpers / D70 MatchInstruction / D74 UsingInstruction / D88 NullCoalescingInstruction / D91 Comp-lifting-model / D93 ILVariable helpers / D95 ThreeValuedBool / D98 Conv IsLifted precedent (port the self-contained util/node the next in-order transform needs ahead of the transform, so the transform port is a separate lower-risk iteration). `BitSet` is the relevance-analysis data structure `DoLift`/`DoLiftBinary` return: a `BitSet(nullableVars.Count)` whose bit i is set iff nullable var i was "relevant" to the lifted expression, and the `bits.All(0, nullableVars.Count)` gate is the "every nullable var contributed to the result" check that decides whether a lifted expression is allowed. The full faithful API is ported: a capacity constructor rounding up to whole 64-bit words (`max(1, ceil(capacity/64))` words, matching the C# `new ulong[Math.Max(1, WordIndex(capacity + 63))]` -- a 0-or-negative capacity yields a single all-clear word), the `operator[]` getter, `Any()`, `All(start, end)` (the relevance gate; true for the empty/vacuous range, matching the C# `if (startIndex >= endIndex) return true`), the set-relation predicates `SetEquals`/`IsSubsetOf`/`IsSupersetOf`/`IsProperSubsetOf`/`IsProperSupersetOf`/`Overlaps`, the mutators `UnionWith`/`IntersectWith`/`Set(i)`/`Set(start,end)`/`Clear(i)`/`Clear(start,end)`/`ClearAll`, `NextSetBit(start,end)`/`SetBits(start,end)` (the C# enumerable returned as a `std::vector<int>` -- the C++-idiomatic eager form the consumers iterate), `ReplaceWith`/`Clone`/`Capacity`/`ToString`. KEY C#-vs-C++ divergence handled: C# `ulong` shift counts are masked to 6 bits by the runtime, so `1UL << index` and `Mask << index` are well-defined for any index; in C++ a shift of >= 64 bits is undefined behaviour, so every shift is masked to the low 6 bits explicitly (`(index & 63)` / `(startIndex & kMask63)`). The C# `Mask >> -endIndex` end mask is replicated as `Mask >> ((64 - (endIndex & 63)) & 63)`, which reproduces the C# 6-bit masking (when `endIndex` is a multiple of 64 the shift collapses to 0 and the whole word is selected -- verified by the AllAtWordAlignedEnd test). `NextSetBit` uses a portable `TrailingZeroCount64(uint64_t)` helper (`_BitScanForward64` on MSVC, `__builtin_ctzll` on GCC/Clang; returns 64 for 0, faithful to the vendored `BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(ulong)`) since `std::countr_zero` is C++20 and the project is C++17. The set-relation/mutation methods are defensive about mismatched capacities (a private `WordAt(i)` returns 0 for an out-of-range word) so they are safe and behaviour-preserving for the equal-capacity case the callers use, where the C# Debug.Asserts equal word counts. The `BitSet` is NOT wired into any pipeline transform yet (it is a foundation), so the CLI `--csharp` output is unchanged; it is exercised by the unit tests (no mscorlib sweep is needed -- it is a pure data structure with no ILAst/decoder dependency). 32 new gtest cases in `cpp/tests/Util/BitSet_Test.cpp` (CapacityRoundsUpToWholeWord; DefaultConstructorIsOneAllClearWord; SetAndReadBitsWithinFirstWord; SetAndReadBitsAcrossWordBoundary; ClearAll; SetRangeWithinOneWord; SetRangeAcrossWordBoundary; SetRangeWholeWords; SetEmptyRangeIsNoOp; ClearRangeWithinOneWord; ClearRangeAcrossWordBoundary; AnyIsFalseForEmptyAndTrueAfterSet; AllSingleWordRange; AllEmptyRangeIsVacuouslyTrue; AllAcrossWordBoundary; AllAtWordAlignedEnd; SetEqualsSubsetSuperset; SetRelationsAcrossWordBoundary; Overlaps; UnionWith; IntersectWith; NextSetBitSingleWord; NextSetBitAcrossWordBoundary; NextSetBitEmptyRange; SetBitsEnumeratesAscending; ReplaceWith; CloneIsIndependent; ToString; plus the four RelevanceGate tests -- RelevanceGateAllIsTrueWhenEveryVarRelevant, RelevanceGateAllIsFalseWhenAnyVarIrrelevant, RelevanceGateSingleVar, RelevanceGateFoundIndicesAny -- pinning the exact `DoLift`/`DoLiftBinary` `bits.All(0, nullableVars.Count)` and `foundIndices.Any()` contract). The test is wired into the ilspy_tests CMake build (`cpp/tests/CMakeLists.txt`); `BitSet.hpp` is header-only so no ilspy CMake source change is needed (matching the LongSet/Interval header-only precedent). 592/592 gtest cases pass (32 new; was 560); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 451769 lines, within the D30 non-determinism range). The next in-order target the foundation unblocks is the `MatchCompOrDecimal`/`LiftCSharp*` comparison-lift path of `NullableLiftingTransform.Run(IfInstruction)`'s `Lift` (the C# section after the D97/D98 LiftNormal pieces): the Comp-branch subset (the Decimal branch and the user-defined-operator paths need `Call.Method.IsOperator` + `IMethod` parameters + `CSharpOperators.LiftUserDefinedOperator`, deferred to Phase 5+), which needs `DoLift`/`DoLiftBinary` (now unblocked by BitSet) + the `CompOrDecimal` struct's `MakeLifted` Comp branch (building a C#-lifted Comp, the D91 model) + `LiftCSharpEqualityComparison`/`LiftCSharpComparison` + the `nullableVars` per-transform list (the C# field populated by `AnalyzeCondition` and the equality-comparison paths). |

Added a new `NullPropagationStatementTransform` class (IStatementTransform, in NullPropagationTransform.{hpp,cpp}) mirroring the C# `NullPropagationStatementTransform` (an IStatementTransform child of StatementTransform that calls `NullPropagationTransform.RunStatements`). The C# `RunStatements(block, pos)` checks `block.Instructions[pos] is IfInstruction` -- the if is a NON-TERMINAL in the C# block model. This port's if-as-final block model makes the if the block's FinalInstruction, so the per-statement driver visits it at the last non-terminal position (pos == size-1, matching how ExpressionTransforms visits the if-final) or for an if-final-only block (pos == -1 == size-1). The `Run` method bails at any other position so the fold fires once. The void-call `?.` pattern: the if is the block's FinalInstruction with FalseInst == nullptr (no else, the C# `ifInst.FalseInst.MatchNop()`), the condition is `comp(ldloc v != null)` (Inequality only, the C# `comp.Kind == ComparisonKind.Inequality`) for ReferenceType or `call get_HasValue(ldloca/ldloc v)` for NullableByValue/NullableByReference, and the TrueInst is a Block with exactly one instruction (the void call, the C# `body.Instructions.Count == 1`). `TryNullPropForVoidCall` (a new file-local function in NullPropagationTransform.cpp): strips a NullableRewrap wrapper from the body instruction (the C# `bodyInst.MatchNullableRewrap(out arg); bodyInst = arg`), calls `IsValidAccessChain` (the D104 helper, shared for all three modes via the dispatching `IsValidEndOfChain`), calls `IntroduceUnwrap` (wraps the receiver load at the end of the access chain in a NullableUnwrap -- the D104 ReferenceType / D106 NullableByValue/Reference construction), detaches the bodyInst from its parent, builds a `NullableRewrap(bodyInst)` (Void ResultType for a void call -- the `?.` statement form), and applies the block-model adaptation: the void NullableRewrap becomes a non-terminal statement (block->Add) and a Branch to the next block (NextBlockInContainer) replaces the if-final (block->SetFinal), destroying the if and the now-empty body Block (the same adaptation NullCoalescingTransform / ReplaceIfWithLiftedValue use). KEY ownership fix: when the NullableRewrap is stripped, `bodyInst` points to the inner instruction (the Call) inside the NullableRewrap (body->Instructions[0]->Argument), NOT to body->Instructions[0] (the NullableRewrap itself). Detaching via `DetachFromParent(bodyInst)` (bodyInst->Parent->TakeChild(bodyInst->ChildIndex)) correctly detaches the inner Call from the NullableRewrap, leaving the NullableRewrap with a null Argument (destroyed harmlessly when the if-final is replaced). A naive `body->TakeChild(0)` would detach the NullableRewrap (not the Call), producing a double `NullableRewrap(NullableRewrap(Call(...)))` -- a bug caught by the `RunStatementsUnwrapsNullableRewrapFromBody` test. The fall-through target (NextBlockInContainer) is resolved BEFORE the bodyInst is detached (the precondition-before-mutation discipline: a detached bodyInst with no next block would leave the tree in a corrupt state). Wired as the 4th child of StatementTransform in the CLI pipeline (after ILInlining, ExpressionTransforms, NullCoalescingTransform -- the C# GetILTransforms() order, skipping the deferred DynamicIsEventAssignmentTransform / TransformAssignment / NullableLiftingStatementTransform). The value-position `Run` entry (D104/D105/D106, wired into ExpressionTransforms.LiftNullableCore) does NOT conflict with the void-call `RunStatements`: the value-position `Run` requires the if's arms to be values (not a Block TrueInst + null FalseInst), and `TryNullPropagation` returns nullptr when nullInst is nullptr (the void-call has no false arm) or when nonNullInst is a Block (IsValidAccessChain rejects a Block as not a valid access chain start). So ExpressionTransforms' VisitIfInstruction visits the if-final first but does not fire for the void-call shape; the NullPropagationStatementTransform then fires. KEY FINDING: the void-call `?.` is a Roslyn-era (C# 6.0) codegen pattern that fires 0 times on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus (the legacy csc does not emit the `?.` operator; it fires on Roslyn-compiled / modern .NET), matching the D59 DetectCatchWhenConditionBlocks / D60 LdLocaDupInitObj / D69 SwitchOnNullable / D90 NullCoalescingTransform / D104/D105/D106 `?.` precedent -- the hand-built tests verify the rewrite (the ReferenceType void-call fold, the NullableByValue void-call fold, the NullableByReference void-call fold with refInput=true, the NullableRewrap-strip fold, and 5 negatives: else arm, multi-instruction Block, non-Block TrueInst, Equality condition, non-access-chain body) and the mscorlib sweep (updated to include the NullPropagationStatementTransform in the StatementTransform pipeline) verifies the ILAst invariant holds across the corpus (not a fold count). The CLI `--csharp` output is unchanged (451838 lines, 517 lock, 313 using, 0 ?? -- within the D30 non-determinism range; the seed renders a void NullableRewrap as its argument, but the current pipeline never constructs one on this corpus). Deferred vs the C#: the UnconstrainedType mode (RunStatements only), the `TransformNullPropagationOnUnconstrainedGenericExpression` pattern (a 5-instruction block sequence -- `stloc target(targetInst); stloc defaultTemporary(default); if (logic.not(comp.o(box(ldloc default) != ldnull))) Block { ... }; stloc result(leave(constrained call)); br endBlock` -- needs the if-as-final block-model adaptation for the multi-instruction shape + a corpus probe, the D73/D75 precedent), the `NullCoalescing` output case (needs InferType + NullableType.IsNonNullableValueType + IsByRefLike), the AddressOf/LdObjIfRef/Dynamic* access-chain cases, and the Call IsStatic/IsExtensionMethod/IsAccessor/IsGetter/ConstrainedTo checks (need Call method metadata) are the subsequent in-order targets. 9 new gtest cases (RunStatementsFoldsReferenceTypeVoidCall; RunStatementsFoldsNullableByValueVoidCall; RunStatementsFoldsNullableByReferenceVoidCall; RunStatementsRejectsElseArm; RunStatementsRejectsMultiInstructionBlock; RunStatementsRejectsNonBlockTrueInst; RunStatementsRejectsEqualityCondition; RunStatementsRejectsNonAccessChainBody; RunStatementsUnwrapsNullableRewrapFromBody). 673/673 gtest cases pass (9 new; was 664); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression). |
| D108 | Call::IsOperator flag + MatchCompOrDecimal Decimal branch (the next in-order NullableLifting piece, Phase 4) | port | Ports the `Call::IsOperator` flag (a new bool on Call, set by the IL reader from the resolved method name) and the Decimal/Call branch of `NullableLiftingTransform::MatchCompOrDecimal` -- the piece the D91 MatchCompOrDecimal foundation explicitly deferred ("the Decimal branch needs Call.Method.IsOperator"). The C# `IMethod.IsOperator` is a SymbolKind derived from the MethodDef's SpecialName/RTSpecialName flag + the `op_` name prefix recognised by `OperatorDeclaration.GetOperatorType`; this port approximates it by the method name alone: a Call is an operator when the short name (the substring after '::') is one of the recognised `op_*` names (op_Equality, op_Addition, op_Implicit, op_CheckedAddition, op_UnsignedRightShift, ... -- the full OperatorDeclaration.GetOperatorType table). A new `IsOperatorName` helper + `ShortMethodName` helper in the IL reader's anonymous namespace set `call->IsOperator` for every call/callvirt/newobj from the resolved MethodName. The C# additionally requires the MethodDef's SpecialName flag; reading it for in-module MethodDefs (the MethodDef Flags column) and resolving it for cross-assembly MemberRefs/MethodSpecs would need the full type system for no practical gain on C#-compiled corpora (every C#-compiled operator overload carries SpecialName, so the name is the real signal) -- the name-only approximation is faithful for C#-compiled code. The MatchCompOrDecimal Decimal branch: a Call with `IsOperator`, exactly 2 arguments (the C# `call.Arguments.Count == 2`), a short name that is one of the 6 comparison operators (op_Equality/op_Inequality/op_LessThan/op_LessThanOrEqual/op_GreaterThan/op_GreaterThanOrEqual -- the C# switch), and a declaring type that is `KnownTypeCode::Decimal` (the C# final gate `call.Method.DeclaringType.IsKnownType(KnownTypeCode.Decimal)`, checked via the D93 `IsKnownType` helper). It reports `Kind` from the name switch, `Left`/`Right` = the call's two arguments, and `IsLifted = false` (the C# `!call.IsLifted`; this port's Call has no IsLifted field, but the C# `Call.IsLifted` is for lifted user-defined operators produced by CSharpOperators.LiftUserDefinedOperator, which this port does not produce, so every Call is non-lifted -- faithful). A non-Decimal operator (e.g. a user op_Equality on another type) passes IsOperator + the name switch but FAILS the Decimal-declaring-type check, so MatchCompOrDecimal returns false for it -- the branch is narrow (Decimal comparison operators only). Decimal has no IL Comp instruction, so a Decimal comparison (`a == b` for Decimal) lowers to an `op_Equality` call; the MatchCompOrDecimal Decimal branch recognises these. The Decimal lift (LiftCSharpUserEqualityComparison / LiftCSharpUserComparison, which build a lifted user-defined operator via CSharpOperators.LiftUserDefinedOperator) is deferred -- needs the Phase 5 C# resolver (CSharpOperators + IMethod ReturnType/Parameters + NullableType.IsNonNullableValueType); the recognition here is the foundation those consumers will consult. KEY safety analysis: adding the Decimal branch is safe for the existing wired LiftCSharp* paths. A Decimal Call CompOrDecimal flows into `RunIfNullableLift`'s equality branch (when falseInst is ldc.i4 0/1) -> `LiftCSharpEqualityComparison`, which checks `hasValueTest->Op == Comp` (the trueInst); if the trueInst is a Comp, DoLift on the Call's non-nullable arguments bails -> null; the fall-back `MatchHasValueCall(hasValueTest, v)` -> `LiftCSharpComparison`, whose `!comp.IsLifted` branch runs DoLiftBinary on the Call's arguments (bail -> null). `CompOrDecimal::MakeLifted` returns null for a Call (the `Instruction->Op == OpCode::Comp` check fails). So no fold fires for a Decimal Call CompOrDecimal -- the recognition is a no-op until the resolver-backed lift lands (behavior-preserving: a Decimal Call condition with falseInst == ldc.i4 0/1 now exits the equality branch early via `return nullptr` instead of falling through to the bool? folds, but the bool? folds would not match a Call condition anyway). KEY FINDING: the recognition IS exercised on the real .NET Framework 4 mscorlib corpus -- System.Decimal defines the 6 comparison operators (op_Equality/op_Inequality/op_LessThan/op_LessThanOrEqual/op_GreaterThan/op_GreaterThanOrEqual) as in-module MethodDefs, so the reader marks them `IsOperator` and `MatchCompOrDecimal` recognises them (the MscorlibOperatorAndDecimalSweep asserts `operatorCalls > 0` and `decimalCompMatches > 0`); the fold is deferred (resolver), so the CLI `--csharp` output is unchanged (no lifted Decimal comparisons appear). This is a tested-but-not-yet-wired foundation matching the D63 LongSet / D66 LoopContext / D68 NullableLifting helpers / D70 MatchInstruction / D74 UsingInstruction / D76 MatchDelegateConstruction + Call::IsNewObj / D88 NullCoalescingInstruction / D91 Comp-lifting-model / D95 ThreeValuedBool / D98 MatchGetValueOrDefault-v / D103 NullableRewrap/Unwrap precedent: the recognition lands ahead of the resolver-backed lift, so the lift port is a separate lower-risk iteration once the resolver is in place. The existing `MatchCompOrDecimalRejectsCall` test (which built a Decimal op_Equality Call without IsOperator) was renamed `MatchCompOrDecimalRejectsCallWithoutIsOperator` (it now tests the IsOperator gate, not the deferral). 7 new gtest cases (MatchCompOrDecimalOnDecimalEqualityCall; MatchCompOrDecimalOnDecimalLessThanCall; MatchCompOrDecimalRejectsNonDecimalOperator; MatchCompOrDecimalRejectsNonComparisonOperator; MatchCompOrDecimalRejectsCallWithWrongArgCount; MscorlibOperatorAndDecimalSweep; plus the renamed MatchCompOrDecimalRejectsCallWithoutIsOperator). 679/679 gtest cases pass (6 new + 1 renamed; was 673); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 451792 lines, 517 lock / 313 using, within the D30 non-determinism range). Deferred vs the C#: the Decimal lift (LiftCSharpUserEqualityComparison / LiftCSharpUserComparison, need CSharpOperators.LiftUserDefinedOperator + the C# resolver), the IsGenericNewPattern fold (needs `c.Method.TypeArguments.Count` -- the MethodSpec instantiation count, a Call metadata addition + `MatchDefaultValue` + `TypeKind.TypeParameter` + IType equality), the NullCoalescing output case (needs InferType + NullableType.IsNonNullableValueType + IsByRefLike), the UnconstrainedType mode + TransformNullPropagationOnUnconstrainedGenericExpression (a 5-instruction block sequence, needs a corpus probe), the AddressOf/LdObjIfRef/Dynamic* access-chain cases, and the Call IsStatic/IsExtensionMethod/IsAccessor/IsGetter/ConstrainedTo checks are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D109 | ResolveTokenToString MethodSpec unwrap + Call::TypeArgumentsCount + IsGenericNewPattern fold (the next in-order NullableLifting piece, Phase 4) | port | Ports the three pieces the D108 deferred list grouped as the IsGenericNewPattern fold ("needs `c.Method.TypeArguments.Count` -- the MethodSpec instantiation count, a Call metadata addition + `MatchDefaultValue` + `TypeKind.TypeParameter` + IType equality"): (1) `MetadataFile::ResolveTokenToString` now unwraps a MethodSpec token (table 0x2B) to its underlying MethodDefOrRef (column 0, the same MethodDefOrRef coded-index unwrap `GetMethodSignature` / `ResolveMethodDeclaringType` already use) and resolves THAT name, so a generic-instantiation call renders its resolved method name (`System.Array.IndexOf(...)`, `System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.SizeOf(...)`) instead of the raw hex token -- a general improvement to the `--csharp` output (before this, every generic call rendered as `0x2B000007(...)`). (2) `Call::TypeArgumentsCount` (a new int field, default 0) populated by the IL reader from a new `MetadataFile::GetMethodSpecTypeArgumentCount(token)`, which reads the MethodSpec row's Instantiation blob (column 1) and decodes the ECMA-335 II.23.2.15 MethodSpecSig (a 0x0A GENERICINST marker, then a compressed generic-argument count, then that many Type blobs) via a new `DecodeMethodSpecTypeArgCount` helper in SignatureDecoder (it validates the count by skipping each Type blob; a non-0x0A marker or a malformed blob returns -1 -> 0). (3) `NullableLiftingTransform::MatchDefaultValue` (the general ILInstruction.MatchDefaultValue extension -- a DefaultValue reports its Type; the general form of the D93 MatchNull which narrows to Nullable<T>) and `NullableLiftingTransform::IsGenericNewPattern` (the `(default(T) == null) ? Activator.CreateInstance<T>() : default(T)` => `Activator.CreateInstance<T>()` fold): the false arm is `default(T)`, the true arm is a Call to `System.Activator::CreateInstance` with `TypeArgumentsCount == 1`, the Type's Kind is `TypeParameter`, the comp's left is another `default(T)` of the SAME type (`IType::Equals`), and the comp's right is ldnull. Wired into `ExpressionTransforms.RunIfNullableLift`'s MatchCompOrDecimal equality branch (after the `IsLdcI4(eqFalseInst, 0/1)` LiftCSharpEqualityComparison checks, matching the C# `else if (!comp.IsLifted && IsGenericNewPattern) return trueInst`): the C# `return trueInst` returns the Activator call; this port detaches it from the if (it is the if's TrueInst arm) via `DetachFromParent` and returns it, so `RunIfNullableLift`'s `ReplaceIfWithLiftedValue` applies the block-model adaptation (a Call is a value, so a clean ReplaceWith for a sub-expression value-if; the pattern's arms are values -- a Call + a DefaultValue -- so the if-as-final after ConditionDetection with Branch arms never matches, and the block-final path does not arise). The equality swap (the C# `Swap(ref trueInst, ref falseInst)` for Inequality) is local to the equality branch, so the port uses `eqTrueInst`/`eqFalseInst` (the swapped views); for Equality (no swap) these are the original arms (Activator / default) and the pattern matches; for Inequality (swap) `eqFalseInst` is the Activator (not a default), so the pattern's `MatchDefaultValue(falseInst)` rejects it -- faithful, the pattern only fires for Equality. KEY FINDING (MethodSpec blob format, settled empirically): the MethodSpecSig format is `0x0A <GenArgCount: compressed> <Type0>...` (the 0x0A is the GENERICINST marker for a method spec, distinct from the type-encoding 0x15 GENERICINST). A corpus probe (the new `MscorlibMethodSpecTypeArgumentsSweep` test) confirmed this on the real .NET Framework 4 mscorlib: scanning 8000 methods found 345 generic-instantiation calls, ALL with resolved method names (EXPECT_EQ(genericCalls, resolvedGenericNames)), zero raw-hex `0x2B` fallbacks (EXPECT_EQ(rawHexCalls, 0)), and a max type-arg count of 8; the first sample was `System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal::SizeOf` with count 1 (`Marshal.SizeOf<T>()`). If the format had been wrong, `genericCalls` would be 0 (the parser returns 0 for every non-0x0A blob). The IsGenericNewPattern is a Roslyn-era codegen pattern (the `new T()` constraint check `default(T) == null` + `Activator.CreateInstance<T>()`) that fires 0 times on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus (ported for faithfulness, matching the D59/D60/D69/D90/D92/D94/D96/D97/D98/D100/D101/D104/D105/D106/D107 precedent); the hand-built tests verify the fold + 4 negatives (non-type-parameter default, mismatched default types, non-Activator name, non-generic Activator) and the corpus sweep verifies the foundation. 5 new gtest cases (MscorlibMethodSpecTypeArgumentsSweep; RunIfNullableLiftFoldsIsGenericNewPattern; RunIfNullableLiftIsGenericNewPatternRejectsNonTypeParameter; RunIfNullableLiftIsGenericNewPatternRejectsMismatchedDefaults; RunIfNullableLiftIsGenericNewPatternRejectsNonActivatorAndNonGeneric). 684/684 gtest cases pass (5 new; was 679); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression) and the `--csharp` output now renders generic method calls with their resolved names (e.g. `System.Array.IndexOf(...)`, `Marshal.SizeOf(...)`) instead of raw `0x2B...` tokens -- a visible improvement. Deferred vs the C#: the Decimal lift (LiftCSharpUserEqualityComparison / LiftCSharpUserComparison, need CSharpOperators.LiftUserDefinedOperator + the C# resolver), the NullCoalescing output case (needs InferType + NullableType.IsNonNullableValueType + IsByRefLike), the UnconstrainedType mode + TransformNullPropagationOnUnconstrainedGenericExpression (a 5-instruction block sequence, needs a corpus probe), the AddressOf/LdObjIfRef/Dynamic* access-chain cases, and the Call IsStatic/IsExtensionMethod/IsAccessor/IsGetter/ConstrainedTo checks are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D110 | ExpressionTransforms VisitTryCatchHandler (TransformCatchVariable / TransformCatchWhen, Phase 4 next-in-order) | port | Ports the `VisitTryCatchHandler` subset of `ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/Transforms/ExpressionTransforms.cs` -- the catch-variable copy inlining that the D81 deferral list explicitly named ("VisitTryCatchHandler visit methods") and that is now the most self-contained remaining ExpressionTransforms visit method (the rest -- VisitCall/VisitNewObj/VisitLdObj/VisitStObj/VisitStLoc HandleCompoundAssign, HandleSwitchExpression, VisitDynamic* -- need TransformAssignment / Span / dynamic nodes / the resolver, all deferred; the NullableLifting/NullPropagation pieces the D92-D109 iterations ported are wired into VisitComp/VisitIfInstruction/VisitCall/VisitBinaryNumericInstruction and are now largely blocked by the Phase 5 resolver). The C# `TransformCatchVariable` inlines the catch-variable copy csc emits at the start of every catch block: the runtime pushes the caught exception into the `E_<offset>` exception stack slot (the handler's `Variable`, an `ExceptionStackSlot`), and csc copies it into a local `V_0` (`stloc V_0(ldloc E)`); the body uses `V_0`. The transform promotes `V_0` to the handler's catch variable (`Kind=ExceptionLocal`, name/type/generated-name copied from the E slot) and drops the copy stloc, giving `catch V_0 : T { <body using V_0> }`. KEY enabling finding (no UsesInitialValue model needed): the C# guard `!handler.Variable.IsSingleDefinition || handler.Variable.LoadCount != 1` on the E slot requires the slot to have `StoreCount == 1` (the caught exception is its initial value, modelled via `UsesInitialValue`). This port's `ComputeVariableUsage` ALREADY counts the `TryCatchHandler` itself as a store for its `Variable` (the caught exception -- `case OpCode::TryCatchHandler: ++h->Variable->StoreCount`), so an E slot loaded once by the copy stloc is `IsSingleDefinition` with `LoadCount == 1` NATURALLY, with no `UsesInitialValue` field or DefiniteAssignment analysis (the D62-deferred `ResetUsesInitialValueFlag` dataflow) required -- the transform fires on the existing variable-usage model. (After the promotion, the new catch variable `V_0` -- now `ExceptionLocal` -- is likewise `IsSingleDefinition` after a recompute, since the `TryCatchHandler` counts as its store, faithfully matching the C# catch-variable `StoreCount == 1`.) The per-variable `LoadInstructions`/`StoreInstructions`/`AddressInstructions` lists the C# `allUses` check consults are replaced by a tree walk (`CollectCatchVariableUses` over the whole function body, gathered by walking the `Parent` chain to the `ILFunction` root -- `FunctionOf`, since the IStatementTransform `Run` has no function handle, unlike PatternMatchingTransform's whole-function `Run`); each use of the promoted local must be a descendant of the handler (`IsDescendantOf`, the UsingTransform/PatternMatchingTransform precedent). The `UnboxAny` unwrap for a type-parameter catch (`stloc V_0(unbox.any T(ldloc E))` -> the slot load unwrapped when `unboxAny.Type.Equals(handler.Variable.Type)`) is ported with a null guard -- this port's `handler.Variable.Type` stays null until catch-type resolution lands, so the type-parameter catch case bails (deferred with the catch-type resolution slice); the common case (a concrete catch type, no unbox.any) fires. `TransformCatchWhen` additionally inlines a single-Leave catch-when filter condition: the C# `entryPoint.Instructions.Count == 1 && [0].MatchLeave` becomes this port's `entryPoint->Instructions.empty() && FinalInstruction is a Leave with a Value` (the filter entry's leave is this port's `FinalInstruction`, not a non-terminal as in the C# block model -- the same divergence the D59/D73/D75 iterations documented); the filter `BlockContainer` is replaced by the leave's `Value` (detached via `TakeChild` before the old filter is destroyed, then re-parented to the handler). The "remove inlined UnboxAny" branch (when the copy was already inlined and the E slot's single load sits inside an `UnboxAny` -- `handler.Variable.LoadInstructions.Single().Parent is UnboxAny`) is deferred (needs catch-type resolution + per-variable load lists). `ILVariable` gained a `HasGeneratedName` bool (default false), set `true` for the `ExceptionStackSlot` at IL-reader creation (faithful to the C# ILReader's exception-slot name) and copied to the promoted local -- the port's `AssignVariableNames` does not consult it yet, so it is faithful-but-currently-cosmetic. Wired into `ExpressionTransforms::Visit`'s `OpCode::TryCatchHandler` dispatch (the recursive `Visit` reaches it by descending into a `TryInstruction` -- the `BlockBuilder` places the `TryInstruction` as a non-terminal in a wrapper block, so the per-statement driver visits it and recurses into the handlers); the C# order (visit the Filter + Body children first, then `TransformCatchWhen` on a single-block filter container, then `TransformCatchVariable` on the catch body) is preserved. KEY FINDING (real-corpus, unlike many recent faithfulness-only transforms): the fold fires on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus -- 28 promotions across 8000 methods (the sweep's `CountExceptionLocalHandlers` is monotone non-decreasing and `EXPECT_GT(totalCatchVarPromotions, 0)`); the rest of the ~692 catches are either single-use copies the per-statement `ILInlining` (the first StatementTransform child) already inlined (leaving the catch using the E slot directly -- already the desired form, no promotion needed), or have escaped uses / unused variables / non-Local copy targets. The CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 451978 lines, within the D30 non-determinism range); the promotion is internal (the promoted local inherits the E slot's `E_<offset>` name, so the `--csharp` catch output shows `catch (System.Exception E_33)` in both the promoted and the inlined cases -- the value is ILAst-level cleanliness for the future real back end, like the D84 VisitBox fold). 9 new gtest cases (TransformCatchVariablePromotesCopyLocalToCatchVariable; TransformCatchVariableRejectsNonLocalCopyTarget; TransformCatchVariableRejectsNonLdLocSlotValue; TransformCatchVariableRejectsEscapedUse; TransformCatchVariableRejectsMultiLoadSlot; TransformCatchVariableUnwrapsUnboxAnyForTypeParameterCatch; TransformCatchVariableRejectsMismatchedUnboxAnyType; TransformCatchVariableRejectsNonStLocFirstInstruction; TransformCatchWhenInlinesSingleLeaveFilter). 693/693 gtest cases pass (9 new; was 684); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression). Deferred vs the C#: the "remove inlined UnboxAny" branch (needs catch-type resolution + per-variable load lists), the type-parameter catch unwrap (needs catch-type resolution), and the rest of `ExpressionTransforms` (VisitCall/VisitNewObj/VisitLdObj/VisitStObj/VisitStLoc HandleCompoundAssign, HandleSwitchExpression, VisitDynamic*, the VisitConv `conv.i4(ldlen)` first rewrite -- still blocked by the LdLen model divergence) are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D111 | NullCoalescingTransform throw-expression (reference-types `a ?? throw ...` arm, the next in-order NullCoalescingTransform piece, Phase 4) | port | Ports the reference-types throw-expression case of `NullCoalescingTransform.TransformRefTypes` (the C# 7.0 `a ?? throw ...` form) -- the next self-contained piece of the NullCoalescingTransform after the D90 reference-types simple/temp folds, unblocked now that the Throw node carries a mutable resultType. The C# `TransformRefTypes` has three true-arm shapes: (1) `stloc s(fallback)` (the simple fold, D90); (2) the 2-instruction temp Block `{ stloc temp(fallback); stloc s(ldloc temp) }` (the temp fold, D90); (3) `context.Settings.ThrowExpressions && trueInst is Throw throwInst` -> `stloc s(if.notnull(valueInst, throw(...)))` (the throw-expression fold, this iteration). The C# mutates `throwInst.resultType = StackType.O` so the `NullCoalescingInstruction`'s `ResultType` (the FallbackInst's, the Throw) matches the reference-type value (O); this port's Throw node previously had a fixed `ResultType() = StackType::Void` override, so a new mutable `StackType resultType = StackType::Void` field (faithful to the C# `internal StackType resultType = StackType.Void` in TryInstruction.cs) was added and the `ResultType()` override now returns it -- a no-op for every ordinary `throw ...;` statement (the field defaults Void) and only the throw-expression fold sets it to O. The fold detaches the Throw's argument via `TakeChild(0)` before the if is destroyed (no GC; a raw pointer would dangle), builds a fresh `Throw` carrying the argument with `resultType = O` as the `NullCoalescingInstruction(Ref)`'s FallbackInst, and replaces the if-final with a `Branch` to the next block (the same block-model adaptation the D90 simple/temp folds use -- the if is the block's `FinalInstruction` in this port's block model, not a non-terminal at `Instructions[pos+1]` as in the C#; `BlockUnwrap` peels a single-instruction expression Block wrapping the Throw so both the bare-Throw and the Block-wrapped-Throw true arms fire). The `ThrowExpressions` setting (DecompilerSettings.ThrowExpressions, a C# 7.0 setting, default true -- false only for the C# 6 / .NET Framework 1.x compatibility profile) gates the fold; added to `ILTransformSettings`. KEY FINDING: the `a ?? throw ...` throw-expression is a Roslyn-era (C# 7.0) codegen pattern that fires 0 times on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus (the legacy csc emits `if (s == null) throw ...` as a statement, not the `??`-with-throw lowering; the reference-type `??` itself fires 0 on the corpus per D90), so the fold is faithfulness-only on this corpus -- matching the D90 NullCoalescingTransform / D59 DetectCatchWhenConditionBlocks / D60 LdLocaDupInitObj / D69 SwitchOnNullable precedent: the hand-built tests verify the rewrite (the bare-Throw fold, the Block-wrapped-Throw fold, the ThrowExpressions-off no-op, the non-Throw-true-arm reject) and the mscorlib sweep verifies the ILAst invariant holds across the corpus (not a fold count). The CLI `--csharp` output is unchanged (the throw-expression fold fires 0 times on the corpus; the seed renders a `NullCoalescingInstruction` whose FallbackInst is a Throw as `(value ?? throw ...)` -- the seed's Throw case is a statement form, so the expression-position rendering is a placeholder the future real back end will replace, but the current pipeline never constructs one on this corpus). The compiler hoists the null-guard `if (comp(ldloc param == ldnull)) throw(...)` in front of the chained `: base(...)`/`: this(...)` call when an argument is `arg ?? throw ...` and `arg` is evaluated more than once. The C# fold replaces the guard with `stloc temp(if.notnull(ldloc param, throw(...)))`, redirects the parameter's first following use (inside the chained call's arguments) to `temp`, and calls `InlineOneIfPossible` to move the coalescing into the call argument. KEY BLOCK-MODEL DIVERGENCE (confirmed by a pre-pipeline probe, the D73/D75/D79/D113 precedent): the C# reads the guard `if (comp(ldloc param == ldnull)) throw` as a NON-TERMINAL at `block.Instructions[pos]` with the use (the call) as a sibling at pos+1. This port's ConditionDetection INVERTS the early-exit pattern: the reader emits `if (comp(eq, ldloc param, ldnull)) br THROW` (brfalse) with fall-through to the call block; `TryInlineIfFallThrough` inlines the call block into the if's FalseInst, then `TryInvertIfExit` negates the condition (`comp(eq, ..)` -> `comp(ne, ..)` Inequality) and moves the call Block into the TrueInst (FalseInst = null, fall-through to THROW). So the post-ConditionDetection shape this transform sees is: the guard block has no non-terminal Instructions, the `FinalInstruction` is `if (comp(ne, ldloc param, ldnull)) { Block { call(..., ldloc param, ...); leave } }` (FalseInst null), and the throw is in the fall-through block (the next block's `FinalInstruction` is a `Throw`). The condition is INEQUALITY (the inverted form), the use (the call) is INSIDE the if's TrueInst Block (not a sibling), and the throw is in the fall-through block (not the if's true arm). The fold: matches the condition as `comp(Equality/Inequality, ldloc param, ldnull)` where param is a `Parameter` (the inverted Inequality form is what arises; the non-inverted Equality form is accepted for robustness but does not fire after ConditionDetection); the if has no else (FalseInst == null); only the Inequality form proceeds (the use is inside the TrueInst Block, the throw is in the fall-through); the TrueInst is a Block; `IsInConstructorInitializer(function, guard)` is true (the guard ends before the chained call starts); the throw is in the next block's `FinalInstruction`. The fold detaches the `ldloc param` from the condition `Comp`, moves the throw out of the throw block (replacing it with a `Leave` placeholder -- a dead but valid block, per the D58 don't-delete-unreachable-blocks convention), builds a fresh `Throw` carrying the argument with `resultType = O` (the throw-expression form), and builds `NullCoalescingInstruction(Ref, ldloc param, throw)`. `FindLoadInNext(TrueInst Block, paramVar, nc)` finds the first `ldloc param` inside the call (recursing into the Block's children, past the `ldloc this` first argument via `MayReorder`); the load must be an `LdLoc` (not `LdLoca`, the C# `result.LoadInst is not LdLoc` gate). On Found, the fold allocates a temp via `function->RegisterVariable(StackSlot, param.Type)`, redirects the first use (`firstUse->Variable = temp`), builds `stloc temp(nc)` with the guard's ILRange, adds it as the first non-terminal, then INLINES the TrueInst Block back into the host block (detach the Block via `TakeChild(1)`, move its Instructions after the stloc, `SetFinal` the Block's `FinalInstruction` -- the leave replaces the if-final, destroying the if with its redundant condition). `ComputeVariableUsage(*function)` is called before `InlineOneIfPossible` so the fresh temp's counts are fresh (StoreCount=1, LoadCount=1); without this, `InlineOneIfPossible`'s dead-store path would fire (stale LoadCount==0) and replace the stloc with the nc as a standalone instruction, leaving the call's `ldloc temp` dangling -- the C# avoids this via incremental variable-usage tracking (`AddStoreInstruction` / the load's `Variable` reassignment), which this port's `ComputeVariableUsage` tree walk is the equivalent of. `InlineOneIfPossible` then inlines the stloc into the call (replacing `ldloc temp` with the nc, removing the stloc), giving `call Base..ctor(..., if.notnull(ldloc param, throw), ...)`. On failure (FindLoadInNext not Found, or the load is an LdLoca), the fold restores the `ldloc param` into the condition and the throw in the throw block (replacing the Leave placeholder) -- the precondition-before-mutation discipline (no GC; the detached children are moved back). Wired into `NullCoalescingTransform::Run` after `TransformRefTypes` and before `TransformThrowExpressionValueTypes` (the C# order).
