A non-Block parent (the if's `Parent` is not a Block, e.g. the if is another if's TrueInst), a non-Block `FalseInst` (e.g. a bare Leave, or null -- no else), or a Block A not found in its container are defensive no-ops (the C# casts both `Parent` and `FalseInst` to Block). KEY BLOCK-MODEL ADAPTATION (the recurring D73/D75 divergence, the crux D159's deferral flagged -- the C# single-block `[ifInst, exit]` split into Block A [if-final] + Block B [exit-final]): the C# operates on a single block where the if is a non-terminal and the exit is a sibling (case a) or the fall-through `nextInstruction` (case b). This port splits that into Block A (the if is the FinalInstruction) + Block B (the exit is the FinalInstruction, the fall-through from Block A); the C# case a (the exit is a sibling in the block) does NOT arise (the if is Block A's final, so nothing follows it in Block A -- the exit is always in Block B). The C# steps map as: (step 3) `EnsureEndPointUnreachable(block, exitInst)` -- a no-op in this port; the C# appends `exitInst` to the block when it falls through to `nextInstruction` (case b) so the block ends in the exit and InvertIf's `GetExit(block)` finds it, but this port's Block A always falls through to Block B (which holds the exit) and InvertIf reads the exit from Block B (not the block's last instruction), so there is nothing to append. (step 4) `EnsureEndPointUnreachable(ifInst.TrueInst, block.Instructions.Last())` -- ensure the then exits via the keyword `exitInst` (the C# case-b net result, since the C# step 3 appended the keyword clone; this port's step 3 is a no-op, so the equivalent is to use `exitInst` directly). (step 5) `ConditionDetection::InvertIf` -- reads Block B's FinalInstruction (the exit) into the if's TrueInst and moves the old then into Block B. (step 6) `if (!ifInst.TrueInst.Match(exitInst)) ReplaceWith` -- ensure the if's TrueInst is the keyword; InvertIf made it Block B's original FinalInstruction (the exit), which may be a leave-from-try (not the keyword `exitInst` the caller found by walking out of the try), so it is replaced with the keyword clone. The fold bails (returns false, no mutation) if: the if has an else (the else-if-tree case, deferred), the then is shallow (`maxDepth < 2`), Block B is missing or has falseCode (the no-else case requires the exit directly after the if), Block B is not single-predecessor (InvertIf's requirement -- the C# has the falseCode in the same block, single-pred by construction), or the then cannot be made to exit (an if-as-final Block or a bare non-exit -- InvertIf would bail, leaving the fold incomplete; a new `ThenCanBeMadeToExit` file-local helper checks this without mutating, so the fold is atomic -- it bails before any mutation if any precondition fails). The bail distribution (for the ~114 candidates with a duplicable exit): `bailMaxDepth=109` (a shallow then -- the ImproveILOrdering-inverted early-returns `if (!cond) return; rest...` have a shallow then = the return), `deepCandidates=4` (passed maxDepth >= 2 + Block B exists/empty/single-pred), of which `fired=1` and 3 bailed on `ThenCanBeMadeToExit` (the then is an if-as-final Block or a bare non-exit); the remaining ~2673 candidates lack a duplicable next-block exit (`CanDuplicateExit` false -- the next block is regular code, a Branch, or a non-keyword Leave). So the fold fires once (a real, safe fire), not faithfulness-only like D146/D154, but far rarer than the wired ImproveILOrdering fold (1355 fires). Step 4 (`EnsureEndPointUnreachable`) is effectively a no-op on the firing candidates: the no-else case's then must EXIT (a Leave/Throw final) for the fold to fire, because if the then falls through, its fall-through target is Block B (the exit), making Block B multi-pred and the fold bail on the single-pred check -- so the then always exits in the firing case and step 4 is a no-op (a documented consequence of the InvertIf single-pred adaptation [D151]; the C# fires on a falling-through then because InvertIf has no single-pred check there -- a faithfulness gap that does not arise on this corpus since the firing thens all exit). 7 new gtest cases (`ReduceNestingNoElseFoldsDeeplyNestedThen` [the fire case: a deep then (depth 2, two nested ifs) that exits, Block B = the return; the if is inverted, its TrueInst becomes the return, the deep then moves into Block B], `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsOnShallowThen` [maxDepth < 2], `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsOnElse` [the else-if-tree case, deferred], `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsWhenNoBlockB` [no Block B], `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsWhenBlockBHasFalseCode` [Block B has falseCode], `ReduceNestingNoElseReplacesLeaveFromTryWithKeyword` [Block B's exit is a leave-from-try inside a try-finally; step 6 replaces the if's TrueInst with the keyword return after the try-finally], `MscorlibReduceNestingNoElseSweep` [the corpus sweep + invariant sweep, with bail-reason diagnostics counting bailMaxDepth/bailNoBlockB/bailFalseCode/bailMultiPred/deepCandidates]). 1156/1156 gtest cases pass (7 new; was 1149); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 517 `lock` / 314 `using` / 79 `??` / 421412 lines, the deterministic counts match the D159 baseline exactly; the fold is not wired so the output is byte-identical to D159 modulo the D30 run-to-run non-determinism). | D161 | ReduceNestingTransform.ReduceNesting (else-if-tree case) exposed as a public static (completing the wired fold's core, tested-but-not-yet-wired, Phase 4 next-in-order after D160) | port | Ports the else-if-tree case of `ReduceNestingTransform.ReduceNesting` -- the C# `private bool ReduceNesting(Block block, IfInstruction ifInst, ILInstruction exitInst)` else branch (the no-else case landed at D160; this iteration completes the function by handling the `if (cond) { then } else { ... } exit;` and the `if (c1) { t1 } else if (c2) { t2 } else { elseBlock } exit;` shapes). It reduces the nesting by duplicating the keyword `exit` into each then block and moving the else content out so the (exiting) thens stay nested but the else content (the bulk) flattens to the fall-through after the if chain: `if (c1) { t1; exit; } if (c2) { t2; exit; } elseBlock...; exit;`. `exitInst` is the keyword exit (return/break/continue) the caller found via `CanDuplicateExit` (the C# `Visit` passes `keywordExit`). Ported as a tested-but-not-yet-wired foundation following the D146/D149/D150/D151/D153/D155/D157/D158/D159/D160 precedent (the fold lands ahead of the wired Visit walk that consumes it, so the wiring is a separate iteration); no pipeline transform consults it yet (Run does not call it -- only ImproveILOrdering + EliminateRedundantTryFinally are wired). The C# logic: the no-else case (D160) handles `ifInst.FalseInst.MatchNop()`; otherwise the else-if-tree case bails if `GetElseIfParent(ifInst) != null` (an else-if tree is reduced as a single group from the root IfInstruction), walks DOWN the else-if chain (`while (Block.Unwrap(ifInst.FalseInst) is IfInstruction elseIfInst) { UpdateStats(elseIfInst.TrueInst, ...); ifInst = elseIfInst; }`) tallying each else-if's then, bails if the leaf's `FalseInst` is not a Block (no trailing else -- a bare Nop, guarded per #3891) or `!ShouldReduceNesting(falseBlock, maxStatements, maxDepth)`, then a `do { ... } while (ifInst != null)` loop walks LEAF-TO-ROOT calling `EnsureEndPointUnreachable(ifInst.TrueInst, exitInst)` (make the then exit), checking `ifInst.FalseInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)` and `block.Instructions.RemoveRange(...)` (drop the now-dead trailing exitInst when the else exits), and `ExtractElseBlock(ifInst)` (inline the else content into the parent block). KEY BLOCK-MODEL ADAPTATION (the recurring D73/D75 divergence, the crux D160's deferral flagged): the C# `ExtractElseBlock` INLINES the else content into the PARENT BLOCK (which can be a nested else block), so the else-if chain flattens into a single block `[ifRoot, ifInner, ..., elseContent]`. This port's if-as-final model makes each if a block's FinalInstruction, so the else content CANNOT be inlined into a nested else block (it would precede the if-as-final). The faithful adaptation is to PROMOTE each else block to the CONTAINER (Block A's parent) as a NEW SIBLING block after Block A's position: after the fold the container is `[Block A (ifRoot), Block C (ifInner's holder), ..., Block E (else content), Block B (exit)]`, which renders the same as the C#'s single-block structure (each block falls through positionally to the next -- the C# output visitor would emit `if (c1) {...; exit;} if (c2) {...; exit;} elseBlock; exit;` either way). The KEY ORDERING difference from the C#: the C# does `ExtractElseBlock` LEAF-TO-ROOT (inlining into the parent block, which always exists). This port MUST do `ExtractElseBlock` ROOT-TO-LEAF, because `ExtractElseBlock` (D159) moves the else block to the CONTAINER of the if's parent block, and an intermediate else-if's parent block is another if's `FalseInst` (NOT a container) until its own parent if's else block has been promoted. After `ExtractElseBlock(ifRoot)` the next else-if's holder block is in the container, so `ExtractElseBlock` on the next if can promote its else; the if pointers stay valid across the moves (`ExtractElseBlock` does not destroy ifs, it moves else blocks and clears `FalseInst` to a Nop). The `EnsureEndPointUnreachable` calls (the then-exit duplication) are independent of the `FalseInst` moves (different slots), so they all precede the `ExtractElseBlock` calls. The dead-exit removal (the C# `RemoveRange`): the C# checks `ifInst.FalseInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)` per iteration and removes the trailing `exitInst` from `block` when the else exits. This port promotes the else content to the container (its end point is invariant across the moves -- `ExtractElseBlock` moves the whole Block, preserving its `FinalInstruction`), so a single check on the promoted else content (`BlockExitsReal` -- a Leave/Throw final, the same opcode check `EnsureEndPointUnreachable` uses, faithful to the C# `HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)` which this port's Block-container `Flags()` does not replicate per the D157 divergence) drops `Block B` via `RemoveEmptyExitBlock` (only when Block B has no non-terminal Instructions -- a conservative faithfulness gap for the Block-B-with-falseCode case that does not arise in the else-if-tree shape, where the exit is directly after the if). Two new file-local helpers: `BlockExitsReal` (a block's end point is unreachable -- its `FinalInstruction` is a Leave/Throw, not a Branch/Nop fall-through or an IfInstruction if-as-final) and `RemoveEmptyExitBlock` (erase a bare-exit Block B from its container and re-parent/re-number the remaining blocks). The plain if-else case (`ifRoot.FalseInst` is a Block not wrapping an if) is handled by the same code path: the walk-down does not descend (the else block does not `UnwrapElseIf`), `leaf == ifRoot`, and the else content is `ifRoot.FalseInst` directly. KEY FINDING (a corpus sweep, `MscorlibReduceNestingElseIfTreeSweep`): the else-if-tree fold is FAITHFULNESS-ONLY on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus -- running the full pre-pipeline + `ReduceNestingTransform` (so the wired ImproveILOrdering fold has re-inverted the early-return ifs) then firing `ReduceNesting` on every root if-final (not an else-if -- `GetElseIfParent` null) whose `FalseInst` is a Block (has an else) and whose next-block exit is a duplicable keyword exit, counted `candidates=716` / `fired=0` across 3000 methods (the invariant held; no crash / tree corruption). The 716 candidates are root if-finals with an else; of those, only 1 had a duplicable next-block exit and it bailed on `bailNoElseBlock` (the leaf's `FalseInst` is not a Block -- a no-trailing-else chain), and 0 bailed on `bailShallowElse` (`ShouldReduceNesting` false). So the fold never fires on this corpus (matching the D146/D154 faithfulness-only precedent -- the ReduceNesting heuristics fire on Roslyn-compiled/modern .NET, not the legacy-csc mscorlib); the no-else case (D160) fired 1 real fire, the else-if-tree case fires 0. The hand-built tests exercise the fire path (the deep-else else-if tree, the deep-else plain if-else) and the bail paths (the root-else-if bail, the no-trailing-else bail, the shallow-else bail via the renamed `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsOnShallowElse`). 6 new gtest cases (`ReduceNestingElseIfTreeFoldsDeepElse` [the fire case: a 2-level else-if tree with a deep exiting else; both ifs' else cleared to Nop, the else-if holder block and the else content block promoted to the container as siblings after Block A, Block B dropped because the else exits], `ReduceNestingElseIfTreeKeepsExitWhenElseFallsThrough` [the fire case where the else content falls through (a Branch-to-next final, not a Leave); Block B is kept -- it is not dead], `ReduceNestingElseIfTreeBailsOnRootElseIf` [a non-root else-if is not a reduction candidate -- `GetElseIfParent` non-null bails], `ReduceNestingElseIfTreeBailsOnNoTrailingElse` [a chain whose leaf has no else Block (a null `FalseInst`) bails], `ReduceNestingPlainIfElseFoldsDeepElse` [the plain if-else case -- no else-if chain, the else block is promoted directly], `MscorlibReduceNestingElseIfTreeSweep` [the corpus sweep + invariant sweep, with bail-reason diagnostics]). The existing `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsOnElse` test was renamed to `ReduceNestingNoElseBailsOnShallowElse` and its comment updated: it now bails because the shallow else block does not meet the `ShouldReduceNesting` heuristic (not because the else-if-tree case is deferred -- it is now handled, but the fold still bails on a shallow else). 1162/1162 gtest cases pass (6 new; was 1156 at D160); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 517 `lock` / 314 `using` / 79 `??` / 421408 lines, the deterministic counts match the D160 baseline exactly; the fold is not wired so the output is byte-identical to D160 modulo the D30 run-to-run non-determinism). Deferred vs the C#: the wired Visit walk (calling `ReduceNesting` from the `VisitContainer` walk after `ImproveILOrdering` + the `RemoveRedundantExit` call -- `ReduceNesting` now handles both the no-else and else-if-tree cases, so the wiring is the remaining piece; it also needs the content-block recursion `Visit(trueBlock)` / `Visit(falseBlock)` and the separate `ExtractElseBlock` call in the `ifInst.FalseInst is Block falseBlock` + `ifInst.TrueInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)` branch), `ReduceSwitchNesting` (needs the D39 dominator analysis), the `ExpressionTransforms.RunOnSingleStatement` re-visit (the wired fold's condition re-fold), the bare-Leave TrueInst ILRange propagation (the remaining ~28 port-specific LoopDetection sites), the `BlockContainer.ComputeFlags` LeaveCount-based `EndPointUnreachable` divergence (replicated inline in `CanDuplicateExit` for now), the falling-through-then case (the InvertIf single-pred adaptation bails where the C# fires -- a documented faithfulness gap that does not arise on this corpus), and the post-`StatementTransform` `GetILTransforms()` targets (`ProxyCallReplacer` / `DelegateConstruction` full / `LocalFunctionDecompiler` / `TransformDisplayClassUsage` / `IntroduceDynamicTypeOnLocals` / `IntroduceNativeIntTypeOnLocals`) are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D162 | ReduceNesting wired into the Visit walk (the no-else and else-if-tree folds now fire from `Run`), Phase 4 next-in-order after D161 | port | Wires `ReduceNestingTransform.ReduceNesting` (the no-else case [D160] + the else-if-tree case [D161]) into the `Run` Visit walk -- the `VisitContainer` file-local function now calls `CanDuplicateExit` + `ReduceNesting` + `RemoveRedundantExit` after `ImproveILOrdering` on each if-as-FinalInstruction, matching the C# `Visit` (`if (CanDuplicateExit(NextInsn(), continueTarget, out var keywordExit2) && ReduceNesting(block, ifInst, keywordExit2)) RemoveRedundantExit(block, nextInstruction)`). The C# `NextInsn()` (`block.Instructions.ElementAtOrDefault(i + 1) ?? nextInstruction`, the instruction after the if) maps to this port's next block's first instruction -- Block B's `FinalInstruction` when Block B has no non-terminal `Instructions` (the exit directly after the if, the no-else/else-if-tree shape), or Block B's first non-terminal when it has content. KEY BLOCK-MODEL ADAPTATION (the recurring D73/D75 divergence): the C# `Visit(BlockContainer)` iterates `container.Blocks` by index with a `container.Blocks[i] == block` assert, and the C# `ExtractElseBlock` inlines the else content into the SAME block (the container's block list is unchanged -- only appends are possible per the C# comment). This port's else-if-tree fold (D161) PROMOTES else blocks to the CONTAINER (inserts after the current block) and DROPS the dead exit block (removes after the current block), so a range-for over `container->Blocks` would be invalidated (std::vector iterator invalidation on insert/erase). The faithful adaptation is the index-based loop (matching the C#): the fold only inserts/removes blocks AFTER the current index (Block A is unchanged at index i), so the `assert(container->Blocks[i].get() == block)` holds and the loop re-reads the (possibly grown/shrunk) block list each iteration. The `RemoveRedundantExit` call: the C# passes `nextInstruction` (the fall-through after the block); for container blocks the C# passes null (a container block's end point is unreachable, so the `Debug.Assert(block.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable) || nextInstruction != null)` holds), and after the fold Block A's `FinalInstruction` is the if (not a keyword exit), so `RemoveRedundantExit(block, nullptr)` is a no-op here (the if is not a Leave/Branch, so `ExitsStructurallyEqual` returns false; and nullptr never matches). The content-block recursion (the C# `Visit(trueBlock, continueTarget, NextInsn())` / `Visit(falseBlock, continueTarget, NextInsn())` for single-Block then/else arms, where `RemoveRedundantExit` would fire with a real `nextInstruction`) and the separate `ExtractElseBlock` branch (the C# `if (ifInst.TrueInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)) { ExtractElseBlock(ifInst); break; }` in the `ifInst.FalseInst is Block falseBlock` case) are deferred -- the current `VisitContainers` recursion into the if's arms processes nested BlockContainers but not single-Block if-as-final arms, so nested ifs in a Block then/else are not reduced (a subset of the full behavior, safe but incomplete; the content-block recursion is the subsequent iteration). KEY FINDING: the wired fold fires on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus -- the `MscorlibReduceNestingNoElseSweep` (which runs `ReduceNestingTransform().Run(*fn, ctx)` -- now including the wired ReduceNesting -- then walks and fires ReduceNesting again) shows the walk's `fired=0` (was 1 at D160) because the wired `Run` now fires the 1 corpus fire BEFORE the sweep's walk (the walk sees the post-`Run` shapes, where the 1 deep-then candidate was already folded by `Run`); the sweep's `candidates=2794` (was 2787) reflects the post-`Run` candidate set. The `MscorlibReduceNestingElseIfTreeSweep` shows `candidates=726` / `fired=0` (was 716/0 at D161 -- the wired `Run`'s else-if-tree fold fires 0 times, matching the D161 faithfulness-only finding). So the total fires are unchanged (1 no-else fire, 0 else-if-tree fires), now occurring in the wired `Run` rather than the sweep's direct call. 1 new gtest case (`ReduceNestingWiredRunFoldsNoElse` [the same no-else deep-then shape as `ReduceNestingNoElseFoldsDeeplyNestedThen`, but exercised via the wired `Run` walk rather than a direct `ReduceNesting` call; asserts the if is inverted, its TrueInst is the return (Block B's exit), and the deep then moved into Block B -- verifying the wiring, not just the static]). 1163/1163 gtest cases pass (1 new; was 1162 at D161); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 517 `lock` / 314 `using` / 79 `??` / 421432 lines, the deterministic counts match the D160/D161 baseline exactly; the no-else fold is a nesting-reduction that operates on if/return/break/continue structures, not lock/using/??, so the coarse statement counts are unchanged). The wired fold's 1 corpus fire changes the IL structure of 1 method (the deep-then no-else shape is inverted), which is MORE faithful to the C# (the C# does the same ReduceNesting fold from its `Visit` walk). Deferred vs the C#: the content-block recursion (`Visit(trueBlock, continueTarget, NextInsn())` / `Visit(falseBlock, continueTarget, NextInsn())` for single-Block then/else arms -- where `RemoveRedundantExit` fires with a real `nextInstruction` and nested ifs in a Block then/else get reduced; needs the content-block `nextInstruction` plumbing), the separate `ExtractElseBlock` branch (the C# `if (ifInst.TrueInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)) { ExtractElseBlock(ifInst); break; }` in the `ifInst.FalseInst is Block falseBlock` case -- a post-ConditionDetection else-block extraction that fires when the then exits and there is an else), `ReduceSwitchNesting` (needs the D39 dominator analysis), the `ExpressionTransforms.RunOnSingleStatement` re-visit (the wired fold's condition re-fold), the bare-Leave TrueInst ILRange propagation (the remaining ~28 port-specific LoopDetection sites), the `BlockContainer.ComputeFlags` LeaveCount-based `EndPointUnreachable` divergence (replicated inline in `CanDuplicateExit` for now), the falling-through-then case (the InvertIf single-pred adaptation bails where the C# fires -- a documented faithfulness gap that does not arise on this corpus), and the post-`StatementTransform` `GetILTransforms()` targets (`ProxyCallReplacer` / `DelegateConstruction` full / `LocalFunctionDecompiler` / `TransformDisplayClassUsage` / `IntroduceDynamicTypeOnLocals` / `IntroduceNativeIntTypeOnLocals`) are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D163 | ReduceNestingTransform wired ExtractElseBlock branch (the C# `Visit(Block)` if-case `if (TrueInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)) { ExtractElseBlock(ifInst); break; }` branch, Phase 4 next-in-order after D162) | port | Wires the ExtractElseBlock branch of the C# `ReduceNestingTransform.Visit(Block)` if-case into the C++ `VisitContainer` walk (the C# runs it after `Visit(trueBlock)` and the ReduceNesting fold, before `Visit(falseBlock)`). When the if's then exits (`EndPointUnreachable`) and the else is a single Block, extract the else -- the else content becomes the fall-through after the if (the then exits, so the else is the only fall-through path): `if (cond) { ...; return; } else { elseContent }` => `if (cond) { ...; return; } elseContent`. This is the `if (ifInst.TrueInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)) { ExtractElseBlock(ifInst); break; }` branch, a NEW fold distinct from the ReduceNesting else-if-tree case (D161): ReduceNesting else-if-tree requires a duplicable exit AFTER the if + the ShouldReduceNesting heuristic; the ExtractElseBlock branch fires when ReduceNesting did NOT fire (no duplicable exit after the if, or the else is too shallow for ShouldReduceNesting) but the then exits and there's a plain else Block. ExtractElseBlock (D159) promotes the else to the container as a new sibling block after Block A and clears the if's FalseInst to a Nop; the new sibling is visited by the container loop's next iteration (i+1). The C# `break` exits the block's instruction loop; this port's if-as-final is the block's last child (no further non-terminals), so no break is needed. KEY block-model divergence handled (the recurring D157 divergence): the C# uses `ifInst.TrueInst.HasFlag(EndPointUnreachable)`. This port's `Block::Flags()` unions ALL children's flags (the D157 divergence -- the C# Block.HasFlag is just the last instruction's flags), so `HasFlag(block->Flags(), EndPointUnreachable)` over-fires when a nested child exits but the block falls through. A new file-local `ThenExits` helper uses `BlockExitsReal` (the structural final-is-Leave/Throw check, faithful to the C# Block.HasFlag) for a Block then, `HasFlag` for a bare instruction then (a Leave/Throw, which carries EndPointUnreachable in its DirectFlags), and returns false for a BlockContainer then (deferred -- `HasFlag` over-fires badly for a container, and the container end-point check needs the unported `BlockContainer.ComputeFlags` LeaveCount semantics). ImproveILOrdering bails safely for this shape (it requires no else -- `if (ifInst->FalseInst) return;`), and ReduceNesting bails when there's no duplicable exit after the if (the then-exits-else shape with no trailing exit), so the ExtractElseBlock branch fires cleanly. KEY FINDING: the `if (cond) { ...; return; } else { ... }` (then-exits-WITH-else) shape is RARE on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus -- ConditionDetection inverts early-returns to `if (!cond) { rest }` (no else) or `if (cond) return; rest` (no else), so the then-exits-else shape rarely arises. The wired ExtractElseBlock branch is faithfulness-only on this corpus (matching the D161 else-if-tree precedent: candidates=716, fired=0); the hand-built `WiredExtractElseBlockFoldsWhenThenExitsAndElseIsBlock` test verifies the fold fires (the else Block is promoted to the container as a sibling, the if's FalseInst becomes a Nop), the two negatives (then falls through, else is not a Block) verify the gates, and the `MscorlibWiredExtractElseBlockSweep` verifies the ILAst invariant holds across the corpus (asserts `totalFolds == 0`, the faithfulness-only contract) and reports the candidate/fold counts. The branch fires on Roslyn-compiled / modern .NET corpora (the then-exits-else shape is more common there). 4 new gtest cases (WiredExtractElseBlockFoldsWhenThenExitsAndElseIsBlock; WiredExtractElseBlockBailsWhenThenFallsThrough; WiredExtractElseBlockBailsWhenElseIsNotBlock; MscorlibWiredExtractElseBlockSweep). 1167/1167 gtest cases pass (4 new; was 1163); the CLI decompiles the full mscorlib module end-to-end (exit 0, no crash, no regression -- 517 `lock` / 314 `using` / 79 `??` unchanged; the branch fires 0 on this corpus so the output is byte-identical to D162). Deferred vs the C#: the BlockContainer-then case of the ExtractElseBlock branch (the container end-point check, needs the unported `BlockContainer.ComputeFlags` LeaveCount-based `EndPointUnreachable` semantics -- approximated as `false` for now), the content-block recursion (`Visit(trueBlock)`/`Visit(falseBlock)` for single-Block then/else arms -- a no-op for content-block ifs in this port's model: ReduceNesting/ImproveILOrdering bail for content-block ifs because there is no Block B / next-block-in-container, so nested ifs in Block arms cannot be reduced; the recursion would only visit nested containers VisitContainers already handles), ReduceSwitchNesting (needs the D39 dominator analysis), the `ExpressionTransforms.RunOnSingleStatement` re-visit (the wired fold's condition re-fold), the bare-Leave TrueInst ILRange propagation (the remaining ~28 port-specific LoopDetection sites), the `BlockContainer.ComputeFlags` LeaveCount-based `EndPointUnreachable` divergence (replicated inline in `CanDuplicateExit`/`ThenExits` for now), the falling-through-then case (the InvertIf single-pred adaptation bails where the C# fires -- a documented faithfulness gap that does not arise on this corpus), and the post-`StatementTransform` `GetILTransforms()` targets (`ProxyCallReplacer` / `DelegateConstruction` full / `LocalFunctionDecompiler` / `TransformDisplayClassUsage` / `IntroduceDynamicTypeOnLocals` / `IntroduceNativeIntTypeOnLocals` -- each needs Phase 5 resolver/type-system infrastructure) are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D164 | LoopDetection determinism fix (ConstructLoop block-move order + FindExitPoint exit pick) | fix | Ports no new C# transform; fixes a blocking-grade determinism defect in the already-ported `LoopDetection.cs`. Two `std::set<ControlFlowNode*>` iteration points leaked raw pointer-address order into the ILAst, so `ilspycmd --csharp` was a NON-deterministic function of its input (two identical runs on mscorlib differed by ~36543 lines: block reordering, goto-vs-empty-body, if-inversion, if/else presence, label placement; even the `??`/goto counts varied 80/79, 22025/22092, destabilizing the verify signature). Root cause 1: `ConstructLoop` moved loop-member blocks into the new loop container by iterating the `loop` set (address order), so member block order (and downstream label/goto naming) varied run-to-run. Root cause 2: `FindExitPoint` returned the first out-of-loop successor found in address order, so a multi-exit loop picked a run-to-run-varying exit block. Fix 1 moves member blocks by scanning `parent->Blocks` in the enclosing container's existing order (a membership `unordered_set<Block*>` for O(1)); Fix 2 iterates the loop members ordered by block `StartILOffset` and picks among all out-of-loop successor blocks the earliest one (min StartILOffset, the natural layout-next block), keeping the simplified single-exit model (the C# picks via a post-dominance analysis; deferred) but making the choice stable. Verified at the level the bug manifests: the mscorlib `--csharp` double-run went from always-different (red) to byte-identical (green); exit 0; signature unchanged at the known-good 517 lock / 314 using / 79 ??; gotos even improved 22k -> 20124. 1171/1171 gtest pass (+1, `LoopDetection.PicksEarliestOutOfLoopExitDeterministically`, a guard asserting a two-exit loop exits to the earliest-offset block, not the later one). `ilast-all` (decode only, no transforms) was already deterministic, confirming the defect lived in the transform pipeline, not the reader or the seed emitter. This determinism is a precondition for trusting the runtime verify gate (the 517/314/79 signature is only meaningful on a stable output). Deferred (next nondeterminism candidates if any resurface): SwitchDetection `unordered_set`/`unordered_map` iteration (externalSet / breakTargets / primaryByTarget / toRemove), ControlFlowSimplification `std::set<Branch*> destroyed`, VariableUsage `unordered_set`s -- none currently observed to diverge after this fix. The remaining Phase-4 in-order tail after ReduceNestingTransform (D163) is effectively exhausted for productive porting: RemoveRedundantReturn's recursive descent is emitter-bound Phase-5 work (the seed pins non-body leaves to `break;` / body leaves to `return;`, and retargeting would trade a valid redundant `return;` for an invalid `break;`, breaking pinned emitter tests), and the post-StatementTransform GetILTransforms() targets (ProxyCallReplacer / IntroduceDynamicTypeOnLocals / IntroduceNativeIntTypeOnLocals / full DelegateConstruction / LocalFunctionDecompiler / TransformDisplayClassUsage) all need the Phase-5 resolver/type-system. |
| D165 | LoopDetection.FindExitPoint prefers the loop-exit convergence over min-StartILOffset (follow-up to D164) | fix | Corrects a latent exit mis-selection in the D164 deterministic pick. D164 chose the lowest-StartILOffset out-of-loop successor among all candidates; but a multi-exit loop's match/break path block often has a LOWER offset than the true post-loop convergence (e.g. mscorlib OAVariantLib.GetCVTypeFromClass: break-path block at IL_0015, true convergence at IL_0027), so min-offset exits into the break path rather than the block every exit flows into. FindExitPoint now collects the distinct out-of-loop successor candidates in deterministic offset order and, when there is more than one, prefers the unique candidate that every other candidate REACHES without re-entering the loop (`ReachesOutsideLoop` DFS, visited-set bounded; a fixed graph property, order-independent) -- the deterministic subset of the C# reverse-CFG post-dominator analysis (the full analysis stays deferred). Divergent exits (or a single candidate) fall back to the D164 min-offset pick, so D164's PicksEarliest guard and the byte-identical mscorlib determinism are preserved (the convergence branch fires 0 times on the mscorlib corpus -- single-exit/divergent or coincident -- so --csharp output is unchanged at 423460 lines, 517 lock / 314 using / 79 ??, exit 0, deterministic). TDD: new LoopDetection.PrefersConvergenceExitOverEarlyBreakPath builds the GetCVTypeFromClass block graph (loop {cond, equals-test, increment} with a lower-offset match path and a higher-offset convergence) and was RED under min-offset (picked the break path) before the fix, GREEN after; full suite 1172/1172. NOT fixed (deferred, Phase 5 seed rendering): the GetCVTypeFromClass emitted text remains jumbled (a dangling `goto IL_001D` entry to the absorbed condition block, an early-break rendered as a backward `goto IL_0015` after the `while`, the break-to-non-designated-exit lost) -- the ILAst loop structure is now correct, but the seed cannot yet render break/continue to a non-designated exit (its documented approximation: "other leaves (switch/try) are break for now (the real back end disambiguates)"); that is emitter/rendering work, not a transform-correctness gap. |

The seed's `GotoText`/`IsFallThroughGoto` only dropped the plain goto-to-next-sibling-block case; a pre-header branch into a nested loop's front block isn't a container sibling, so it fell through to a dangling `goto`. | D170 | FlattenMetadataName strips generic type-arity before the type-argument list | fix | Doubles down on D167's generic-name work, which only covered type/variable declarations via `CSharpTypeName` and the `newobj` path via `CallText`. Remaining references -- static fields/properties/method calls on generic types, `typeof(...)`, and any member-ref rendered through the string-based `FlattenMetadataName` -- still leaked the ECMA `` `N `` arity suffix (`EqualityComparer`1<System.Byte>`, `List`1<System.String>`). `FlattenMetadataName` now runs `StripGenericArity`: scanning for `<` preceded by `` `Ndigits` (and that preceded by a backtick) and erasing the `` `N `` marker, recursing naturally into nested args by continuing from the erased position. The guard (must be `` `Ndigits` `` immediately before `<`) keeps compiler-generated names that merely *start* with `<` (`<>c`, `<Foo>d__0`) and comparison/pointer operator text unaffected -- only ECMA arity encodings match. Concrete-arg generic member refs on mscorlib drop 628 -> 178 (the remaining 178 are all `<!0>`/`<!!0>` *type-parameter* placeholders -- the CLR's VAR/MVAR index encoding -- whose names require reading the GenericParam metadata table per declaring type, a Phase-2 type-system task, deferred). Deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 ??), gotos still 18505. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GenericMemberRefMetadataNameRendersCSharpForm (a `typeof(List`1<System.String>)` emission) was RED (`typeof(System.Collections.Generic.List`1<System.String>)`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1179/1179. |
| D171 | Render a `StLoc` used as an expression value as a chained assignment | fix | The C# seed fell back to `(default)/*op=34*/` whenever a `StLoc` appeared where an expression value is expected. That shape is a real ILAst idiom -- an inline assignment whose value IS another store (`stloc dup_N, stloc V, call(...)`, produced by ILInlining/CopyPropagation folding the C# `(hr = Marshal.GetLastWin32Error())` style test into a temp), so on mscorlib it printed 346 `var dup_N = (default)/*op=34*/;` broken declarations. `Expr` now handles `OpCode::StLoc` by rendering `name = Expr(value)`; chained assignment is right-associative so no parentheses are needed (`dup_34 = num_2 = Marshal.GetLastWin32Error()`) -- matching what the C# back end's inlining produces for the same pattern. All 346 occurrences now render as valid C#. Verified: mscorlib --csharp deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged at 517 lock / 314 using / 79 ??, 18505 gotos. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.NestedInlineAssignmentRendersChained was RED (`var dup_0 = (default)/*op=34*/`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1180/1180. LEFT-NOTE: the other `(default)/*op=N*/` fallbacks remaining in the seed are the ExpressionTransforms placeholder paths plus truly unrecognized ops (ldobj with nested IL-tree-class that can't express `--` quite right, NullableRewrap, RefAnyType / typedrefs) -- each is a decode, not a rendering, gap worth its own D-block. |
| D172 | Name MethodDef VAR/MVAR generic params from owner TypeDef/MethodDef GenericParam rows (`GetMethodSignature` passes a GenericParamNames to `DecodeMethodSignatureBlob`); member-ref/local/TypeSpec sites unchanged | 1181/1181; VAR-labeled lines 3471→2028; deterministic |
| D173 | Extend generic-param naming to local sigs, field sigs, and TypeSpec operands | fix | D172 only named VAR/MVAR in method-signature decode (GetMethodSignature). The remaining VAR/MVAR placeholder text came from three more decode surfaces, each with its own scoping rule now resolved: (1) LOCAL_SIG decodes in the owning method body's scope -- GetLocalTypes/GetLocalTypesWithPinned take an optional ownerMethodToken (both ILReader call sites pass it), so `T[] V_1` locals in generic methods come back authored-named; (2) a field sig's VAR scopes to the field's own declaring TypeDef, resolvable from the FieldDef row alone -- GetFieldSignature collects the parent TypeDef's GenericParam rows; (3) TypeSpec blobs decode in the scope of the method body the operand appears in -- ResolveTypeToken (newarr/castclass/isinst/box/...) and ResolveMethodDeclaringType (MemberRef-parent TypeSpec) take an optional ownerMethodToken threaded through a new ReaderState.ownerMethodToken in the IL reader, so `new T[newSize]`, `new List<T>()`, and `ArraySortHelper<T>.Default` call sites resolve their instantiation arg names. Shared build logic factored into one BuildGenericParamNames(db, methodRow) helper (also re-used by GetMethodSignature, replacing the inline D172 lambda). The inner TypeSpec-blob reader in the decoder now inherits the outer reader's name context (a TypeSpec wraps one type of the same signature). Remaining: `EqualityComparer`1<!0>.Default`-style static-member reference TEXT built through the string-level FlattenMetadataName path (the member-ref name renderer keeps no IType, so it cannot consult the name context) and MemberRef-signature parameter naming (the MemberRef's own sig decodes in the referenced method's scope, a separate pairing). | D174 | Name VAR/MVAR in member-reference strings; strip arity on static property-accessor prefixes | fix | The last generic-placeholder class: static calls/fields on generic types whose declaring type is a TypeSpec render through ResolveTokenToString (Call::MethodName, LdFld/LdFtn/LdVirtFtn/SizeOf operands) -- a STRING path, so D173's IType-level naming never reached it. ResolveTokenToString gains the same optional ownerMethodToken and feeds its TypeSpec branches (MemberRef-parent, MethodSpec unwrap recursion); the IL reader passes ReaderState.ownerMethodToken at all 8 string-resolution sites. A second bug surfaced under it: the static property-accessor emitter extracts its short type name via rfind('.') without going through FlattenMetadataName, so `EqualityComparer`1<T1>` kept its ECMA arity marker even after the name resolved -- the accessor path now runs StripGenericArity on the extracted segment, so `EqualityComparer`1<T1>.Default.GetHashCode(...)` becomes `EqualityComparer<T1>.Default.GetHashCode(...)`.
