| D176 | MatchForLoop (dedicated-increment-block case) + For container emission | new | Phase 4's HighLevelLoopTransform gains the for-loop recognition: after a Loop container is marked While, if exactly one counted edge enters the loop header (the pre-header "falls into" the container in this port's model, so C#'s entry.IncomingEdgeCount == 2 becomes our == 1 -- anything more is a second back-edge that would skip the increment) and a non-entry block of all-simple statements ends in a Branch to the header (the `continue`-target increment block), that block is moved to the container's end and the kind is marked For. The C#'s other sub-case (splitting a trailing `stloc V(add(ldloc V, k)); br entry` tail off a body block, plus condition-splitting with LogicAnd) is deferred -- the seed's while emission needs no condition relocation for the common csc lowering. The emitter renders a For container as `for (; cond; incr) { body }`: locating the increment block BY SHAPE (non-empty simple statements + Branch-to-header final) rather than position because post-pipeline transforms (ReduceNesting's ordering folds run after HighLevelLoopTransform in GetILTransforms order) can leave a trailing empty block behind the moved increment; the increment clause renders each simple statement (StLoc via the shared AssignmentText so `V = V + 1` emits `V++`) comma-joined; branches to the increment block emit `continue` (the increment block joins the label-free loopHeaders set -- C# `continue` runs the for-update); an empty trailing block branching to the increment block is dropped as dead layout. The pre-header `V = init` stays outside the loop as the C# back end does for separately-declared loop variables. On the mscorlib corpus the match fires exactly once (System.Text.StringBuilder::ReplaceInPlaceAtChunk: `for (; indexInChunk < chunk.m_ChunkLength; )` -- the .NET Framework source's shape, rendered as `while (...)` before); all other loops keep their while/do-while rendering because their header edges or increment block shapes do not satisfy the strict gates, which exist so over-permissive matches cannot misuse a `continue` to skip an increment. Deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??` / 18505 gotos). TDD: new HighLevelLoopTransform.RunTransformsLoopWithIncrementBlockToFor was RED (kind stayed While -- 1-byte <02> vs <04>) before, GREEN after; new ILAstToCSharp.ForLoopContainerRendersForWithIncrementClause was RED (no `for (; num < 5; num++)` text) before, GREEN after; full suite 1184 -> 1186/1186. KNOWN-HOLE (pre-existing, not this change): loop-header blocks that carry preamble statements (the increment consumed into the entry block by ReduceNesting's ImproveILOrdering pass) are not rendered by either the While or For paths -- a separate seed-emission limitation worth its own D-block. |
| D177 | MatchForLoop no-dedicated-block split (trailing stloc-increment + br entry) + For trailing-continue drop | new | Complements D176's dedicated-increment-block case with the C#'s other MatchForLoop branch: a While loop whose last body block ends `stloc V(add(ldloc V, k)); br entry` (the common csc way of keeping the increment inline in the body) has the trailing pair split into a new increment block appended to the container, the body block rewired to branch to it (not the old head), and the kind marked For. Gated on the load-use / no-assignment condition checks (TreeLoadsVariable / TreeHasAssignment, ported gates for the C# SplitConditions loop) and this port's own strict shape limits: a single comparison Comp (or LdLoc) condition only -- a compound `&&`/`||` condition needs the three-valued condition nodes (deferred, matching D139's ThreeValuedBool prerequisite note), a While head whose true-arm does NOT branch into the body block definitively bails (a separate 2-block body condition shape), and a body split off a 2-block loop whose body is JUST the increment stays While (a 1-instruction body with just stloc+br entry would otherwise loop-restore, producing `for (;; x++; ;)` -- the stloc/:2 brigade). The seed now drops the body's trailing Branch-to-the-new-increment as the iteration itself (not a `continue` -- the loop header's for-update runs the increment), keeping the mid-body Branch-to-increment as `continue` (the update still runs, the C# `continue` semantic). No corpus While-on-For change: the mscorlib For fire remains exactly one (StringBuilder.ReplaceInPlaceAtChunk, D176's shape) -- the corpus's `for` loops mostly keep the increment in the ENTRY block (this port's While preamble), which this iteration conservatively does not split (high-precision, low-recall, matching the D152/D153 gate philosophy). Deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 79 `??` / 18505 gotos; 314 using unchanged at D174's count). TDD: new HighLevelLoopTransform.RunSplitsTrailingIncrementIntoForBlock was RED (Kind stayed While -- <02> vs <04>) before, GREEN after; new ILAstToCSharp.ForSplitIncrementEmitsNoTrailingContinue was RED (`continue;` printed before the loop close) before, GREEN after; full suite 1186 -> 1188/1188. |
| D178 | Render While/DoWhile/For header preamble statements inside the loop body | fix | A While/DoWhile/For container's header block (the first block -- the guard then the condition if) may carry non-final Instructions between the guard and the final If: the do-while-like `x = expr` a csc 2-block for body packs into the entry, or a refreshed local, or the guard's own checked local, or a `for (i = init; ...; )` loop-init lowered to an entry statement. The emission previously read only the block's FinalInstruction for the condition and dropped the preamble silently, producing a syntactically plausible but semantically wrong loop body -- the preamble runs at the top of every iteration, so omitting it both loses a real statement and misplaces its effect out of order. The fix renders the header's non-final Instructions at the loop body's open, one per line at body indent, before the body blocks emit (for (;;) blocks the guard). This restores the corpus's While/DoWhile/For renderings to their source-faithful shape -- specifically the StringBuilder.ReplaceInPlaceAtChunk for loop now reads `for (; indexInChunk < chunk.m_ChunkLength; ) { int num = Math.Min(...); ThreadSafeCopy(...); indexInChunk = (indexInChunk + num); ... }` where the num computation and ThreadSafeCopy were silently lost. Deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 79 `??` / 18505 gotos). The corpus line count rose 400148 -> 400510 (+362 restored preamble statements across the corpus). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.WhileLoopHeaderPreambleStatementsRenderInsideBody was RED (`other = 42` absent from the body) before, GREEN after; full suite 1188 -> 1189/1189. |
| D179 | DoWhile multi-condition fold (AnalyzeDoWhileConditions-lite) + body-before-condition soundness gate | fix | Completes the port's HighLevelLoopTransform do-while handling: the Run formerly marked a loop DoWhile only when its last block was a single-condition `if(cond) br entry` guard; trailing additional `if(cond) br entry` guards (non-final on the same trailing block) now fold into the final condition as the C# IfInstruction.LogicAnd if-expression (`if (c1) c2 else 0`, NOT ThreeValuedBoolAnd: the && short-circuit must not evaluate its rhs when lhs is false -- a faithful-choice discovery, the initial ThreeValuedBoolAnd abuse broke CheckInvariant in emissive contexts). Two more soundness fixes: (1) the Run's While-shape short-circuit `if (!iff) continue;` previously SKIPPED the do-while check for loops whose entry carried no condition if -- the entry-if-null case now falls through to a goto'd doWhileCheck label (while-gating semantics preserved); (2) a structural gate rejects do-while marking when the loop's entry does not reach a BODY block first (entry's final Branch targets a block that is NOT Blocks[1], or the entry falls through into the trailing condition block in a 2-block loop) -- this fixes the mis-folding the internal corpus measurement uncovered on System.IO.File::InternalReadAllLines (the csc lowers `while ((line = reader.ReadLine()) != null) list.Add(line);` with the condition block last; a do-while render would have executed the add once unconditionally, then re-assigned on each pre-check -- a reordering bug the initial marking). Corpus: one do-while flip was the observed mis-fold this prevents; mscorlib's do-while counts stay at genuine shapes (the port previously folded ~90 extra `while (true) { ...; if(cond) continue; }` methods into `do { ... } while (!(cond));` -- internal run analysis -- but the structural gate rejects the unsafe subset; net corpus do count is 1 with the actual header-bits-working condition block). Deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??` / 18506 gotos at D178 restore level, -1 from the gate). TDD: new HighLevelLoopTransform.RunCompoundsDoWhileConditions (3-block entry/body/cond layout) was RED initially on the restricted topology, GREEN after; full suite 1189 -> 1190/1190. |
| D180 | Drop redundant gotos that fall through construct boundaries (using/lock/try) via TextuallyNextEmittedBlock | fix | `IsFallThroughGoto` previously recognized only same-container `goto next;`-to-`next:` drops (a block-final or final-if-true-arm branch whose target is the NEXT block in its own container). The common `using/lock/try { ...; br after }; after:` construct-exit shape -- 579 gotos on the mscorlib corpus whose whole control role is the pipe-out-of-construct pipe -- kept emitting those gotos because the branch's enclosing block reaches its container's end inside a UsingInstruction/TryCatch node, not a container sibling. `IsFallThroughGoto` now resolves the fall-through via a new static `TextuallyNextEmittedBlock(node)`: inside a container it is the next block (the old answer); at a container's end the walk continues up first through non-Block construct-node owners (a UsingInstruction owning its body container, say) and then through the enclosing BLOCK when the construct occupies its last emitted statement (the last pb.Instructions element with no remaining pb-final, or one that is itself a fall-through Branch to pb's textual next -- the recursive+gated consistency condition that keeps the drops strictly equivalent); anything else (in-line statements after the construct, a switch arm, the function end) returns nullptr and the goto stands. Corpus: mscorlib `--csharp` line count 400521->399669, gotos 18506->17927, exit 0, deterministic; the flagship System.IO.File::InternalReadAllLines now reads
using (new System.IO.StreamReader(...)) { while (true) { ... } }
return list.ToArray();
(without the trailing `goto IL_002D;` and its IL_002D: label). lock/using/?? signature unchanged (517/314/79). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GotoFallingOutOfUsingConstructToFollowingBlockIsDropped was RED (`goto IL_0000;` printed inside the using) before, GREEN after; full suite 1190->1191/1191. The pipeline-emission emits a spurious `IL_` label iff a non-dropped (elsewhere-referenced) goto still targets `after` -- CollectLabels only labels emitted gotos, so a completely dropped unique reference removes the label, matching the guaranteed-same-target invariant. |
| D181 | Inline switch-section body thunks under their case labels (AnalyzeSwitchInline + break replacement) | new | The switch-family transforms leave each SwitchSection's body as a bare Branch thunk to a real body block laid out after the switch-host block in the same outer container (the seed rendered `case N: goto IL_XXXX;` per section plus the bodies as labeled blocks below -- the largest single family of remaining gotos). The emitter now computes a per-switch `SwitchInlinePlan` (cached in `switchInlinePlans_` and shared by the label-collection and emission passes, so registration order is stable) and, when every section is a Body-is-one-Branch thunk to a distinct block in the same outer container AND every target's trailing is a `br exit` (convergent on ONE exit by the relaxation -- replaces the initial over-rigid positional rule "exit directly after the last target", which rejected the far more common unordered and fall-through-chain layouts) or a Leave (return/throw), AND no Branch anywhere in the function besides the switch's own per-section thunks targets a body block (the foreign-reference safety walk), it renders the case labels with the real bodies inline: the Body's instructions skip trailing/Nop entries, inner `br exit` and the trailing `br exit` both render as `break;`, a Leave stays a `return`/`throw`, and the outer block iteration skips the inlined blocks via the centralized `inlinedBodyBlocks_` guard in EmitBlock. The corpus effect: 26 switch methods gain real case bodies (the early Win32Error-class `case N:`/`case range:` arms hand back their Win32ErrorStatic-throw/RegistryKeyOpenRemoteBaseKey bodies), gotos 17927 -> 17781 (-146), lines 399669 -> 399497, deterministic, exit 0, lock/using/?? signature unchanged (517/314/79). The bail-profile measurement that drove the relaxation (a temporary env-gated SWBAIL/SWOK stderr dump, since removed) reported: 26 eligible, sw-signature bails split 190 not-thunk (real case bodies already inlined by a better-shaped seed lowering), 163 final-kind (throw/if finals beyond the `br exit`/Leave shapes -- the next eligible class), 27 brk-not-exit, 25 no-exit, 23 target-outside, 9 exit-outside, 8 no-outer, 12 foreign-branch -- the deferred family is dominated by `if`-shaped finals that ChainCondition into the exit path (a follow-up iteration, guarded to keep the noexcept + single-target guarantees the current code encodes). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyThunksInlineIntoCaseSections was RED (`goto IL_0030;` etc. printed under the cases) before, GREEN after; full suite 1191->1192/1192. |
| D182 | Switch-body conditional-exit inlining + fall-through positional integrity gate | fix | Extends D181's switch-body inlining from trailing `br exit`/Leave trailing exit paths to a body final `if (cond) br exit` (no else): such bodies render `if (cond) break;` inline (the false path falls positionally, gated as below). The analysis accepts the trailing if's true-arm Branch into the exit convergence union (same single-exit rule as the plain branch case). It also closes a positional-integrity gap the D181 order-gate removal exposed: any body whose trailing lets control continue positionally (a null FinalInstruction, or this conditional-exit form) must see its next OUTER block equal to the NEXT SECTION's body (mid sections) or the discovered exit (the last section), otherwise the section-order inlining would mis-route execution for block-order-vs-section-order divergence. Corpus: the new conditional-exit fires 0 times on the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus (the `final-kind` bails profiled in D181 are throw- and else-arm finals, not this form) -- a faithfulness-only construction per the D59/NullCoalescing precedent; the 26 D181 SWOK switches survive the positional-integrity gate unchanged. Deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??` / 17781 gotos). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithConditionalExitInlineAsIfBreak was RED (`goto IL_0030;`-style thunks printed, no `if (num) break;`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1192->1193/1193. |
| D183 | Switch bodies terminating in throw are inlined | fix | Follows D181/D182: a case body that always throws (`throw new ArgumentException(...)` -- the Win32Error guarding-call shape) has a Throw block-final, which the D181 analysis classified as `final-kind` bail (its corpus profile was 51 throws). The exit-convergence now treats a Throw final as contributing no exit (alongside Leave), and the inline emission keeps the body with the throw in place (`throw ...;` as the case's last line; no break needed). Corpus: gotos 17781 -> 17731 (-50), lines 399497 -> 399430, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The remaining `final-kind` profile (a temporary env-gated FK dump, removed) is: 71 if-final whose true arm is not Branch(exit), 60 if-else finals whose two arm targets must be profiled against the exit/next-body before any inlining (the natural next-family candidates -- shape profiling, not guessed), 4 opcode-17 (~rare). The Win32Error switch (the D181 reference case) remains a thunk because its `case 0` body is a throw-following if-final with a non-exit true arm (into the arg-throw side block) and a positionally-false false-arm into the exit block -- the exact if-final-other shape still out. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithThrowExitIsInlined was RED (bail class `final-kind`, thunks printed) before, GREEN after; full suite 1193 -> 1194/1194. |
| D184 | Switch-body inlining: exiting true arms + no-convergence switches | new | Broadens D181-D183's switch-body inlining in three ways. (1) A body whose trailing is `if (cond) { return; }` or `if (cond) throw ...` (a no-else if whose true arm is a Block with a Leave/Throw final, or a bare Leave/Throw) now joins the fold: the true arm exits, contributing no exit branch; the false path falls positionally (the D182 integrity gate enforces the fall goes to the next section body or the exit). (2) A switch with NO convergence exit (every body self-terminates via throw/return or falls positionally -- no body branches to a shared exit) now accepts by using the block after the last target as the implicit exit (the post-switch continuation); no `break;` lines render since no body branches to it. (3) Fixes a code-ordering bug where the positional integrity gate ran before the no-convergence exit was set (the `fall-no-target` bail fired spuriously). Updated the pre-D181 `SwitchEmitsCaseLabelsWithGotos` test (now `SwitchInlinesLeaveFinalBodies`) to reflect the inlined rendering its shape now produces. Corpus: mscorlib `--csharp` SWOK 26->56 (the bail profile: 190 not-thunk, 106 final-kind [if-else + non-exiting true-arm shapes, the next family], 28 brk-not-exit, 23 target-outside, 22 no-post-exit, 20 exit-is-target, 12 fall-order, 10 exit-outside, 8 no-outer); gotos 17731->17665, lines 399430->399299, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithConditionalReturnInlineAsIfReturn (if(cond){return;} body) and ILAstToCSharp.SwitchAllBodiesExitOrFallThroughNoConvergenceExit (no-convergence all-self-terminating/fall-through switch) were RED before, GREEN after; full suite 1195->1196/1196. |
| D185 | Switch-body inlining: falling-through true arms | new | Follows D184. A case body whose trailing is `if (cond) { work; }` (no else, the true arm a Block with real instructions but no final, or a nested no-else if, that does work then falls through) now joins the fold. The `armFallsThrough` recursive predicate (Block with no final -> true; Block -> recurse on final; IfInstruction no-else -> recurse on true arm, if-else -> both arms; Branch/Leave/Throw/SwitchInstruction -> false; bare statement -> true) accepts such a true arm: the body contributes no exit branch -- both the true path (after the work) and the false path fall positionally to the same place -- so the analysis `continue`s (no exit contribution) and the positional integrity gate checks the fall goes to the next section's body or the exit. Emission needs no change: the body's trailing if hits the inline emitter's `else { EmitStatement(*fin); }` branch and renders `if (cond) { work; }` in place. The foreign-reference check (whole-function recursive walk) catches any hidden Branch to a body block. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp SWOK 56->59, final-kind bails 106->86 (-20 falling-through bodies accepted); 9 of those then hit `fall-order` (a non-adjacent fall-through, which correctly bails -- a non-adjacent fall is a `goto case` in C#, not a natural fall-through, so the goto form is faithful); net gotos 17665->17656 (-9), lines 399299->399281, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The remaining `final-kind` profile: 66 if-else-final (`if (cond) br A else br B`, two-destination -- the next family), 4 SwitchInstruction-final, and ~16 if-final-other whose true arm branches (Block ending in a Branch/Switch). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithFallingThroughTrueArmInlines (case 0: `if (num) { num = 1; }` then fall to exit) was RED (bail `final-kind`, thunks/IL_ labels printed) before, GREEN after; full suite 1196->1197/1197. |
| D186 | Switch-body inlining: Nop else arm = no-else | fix | A case body whose trailing is `if (cond) br A else <Nop>` (a conditional branch with a redundant Nop else arm) used to bail as `final-kind` because the convergence loop gated the conditional-exit / exiting-true-arm / falling-through-true-arm paths on `!iif->FalseInst` -- a Nop FalseInst is non-null, so the gate rejected it, even though a Nop else is semantically fall-through (no-op) and the emitter's `isEmptyArm` already treated a Nop arm as empty. The analysis was inconsistent with the emitter about what "no else" means. Relaxed the three `!iif->FalseInst` checks (the convergence-loop conditional-exit gate, the positional-integrity `fallsThrough` flag, and the emission special case that renders `if (cond) break;`) to also accept a Nop FalseInst. `armFallsThrough` already handled Nop (Nop is not Block/If/Branch/Leave/Throw/Switch, so it hits the `default: return true`). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp is net-neutral on goto count (17656 unchanged, SWOK 59 unchanged) -- the 51 Nop-else bodies that left `final-kind` redistributed to `brk-not-exit` (+34, the true-arm Branch targets a non-exit block, so the body breaks convergence and correctly stays a goto) and `fall-order` (+14, the true-arm Branch targets the exit but the false path's fall is not positionally adjacent to the next section, so the inline ordering constraint correctly keeps it a goto); deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The fix is a faithfulness/correctness improvement (analysis now agrees with the emitter) backed by a RED->GREEN test, not a goto-count mover on this corpus. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithConditionalExitAndNopElseInlines (case 0: `if (num) br exit else nop`) was RED (bail `final-kind`, thunks/IL_ labels printed) before, GREEN after; full suite 1197->1198/1198. |
| D187 | Switch-body inlining: nested conditional-exit recognition + GotoText break centralization | new | Follows D186. A case body whose trailing is a NESTED conditional exit -- `if (cond) { if (cond2) br exit }` or `if (cond) { work; br exit }` (the body's final is a no-else if whose true arm is a Block ending in a `br exit`, possibly under further conditions) -- used to bail as `final-kind` because the convergence loop's single-level check only recognized a DIRECT true-arm Branch (`if (cond) br exit`, the D182 case); a true arm that was a Block (or a nested if) fell through to the `trueArmExits`/`armFallsThrough` checks, both of which returned false for a Block ending in a Branch, so it bailed. Added `collectExitBranches` (recurses through Blocks and nested no-else/if-else ifs, gathering every Branch terminator; Leave/Throw/bare-statement paths contribute no branch): in the no-else-if true-arm branch, after the existing exits/falls-through checks, it collects the true arm's branches; if any, they must all target the SAME block (else multi-exit `final-kind` bail), the representative becomes the body's exit branch (conditionalExit), and all collected branches are pushed to bodyExit so they reach breakBranches_. The positional integrity gate already saw a no-else outer if as falling through, so it needs no change. The EMISSION needed a companion fix: the switch-inline emission special-cases a DIRECT `if (cond) br exit` final as `if (cond) break;`, but a NESTED br-exit (inside a Block inside the if) falls to the general `EmitStatement(*fin)` path, whose `GotoText` returned `goto IL_exit;` (not break). Centralized the rule: `GotoText` now returns `break;` for any `breakBranches_` member (consistent with `CollectLabels`, which already skipped label creation for them), placed before the loop-header/continue check -- `break;` exits the switch, not the loop, even if the exit block is a loop header. This also makes the switch emission's explicit `Line("break;")` special cases redundant (harmless). The `conditionalExit` local is now set in two places but remains read-nowhere (dead; left to avoid churn). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp is net-neutral (SWOK 59 unchanged, gotos 17656 unchanged, lines 399281 unchanged, deterministic, exit 0, signature 517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`) -- the 15 nested cases that left `final-kind` redistributed to `brk-not-exit` (+10, the inner br targets a non-exit block, a genuine `goto case`/forward goto C# requires) and `fall-order` (+2, the body's positional fall is non-adjacent, a `goto case` C# requires) and `exit-outside` (+1); both correct bails. The fix is a faithfulness/generalization improvement (the construct inlines per the RED->GREEN test; the GotoText centralization is a cleanup) but does not move mscorlib's goto count -- the switch-inlining arc has plateaued on mscorlib: the remaining bails (190 not-thunk [real case bodies already inline], 74 brk-not-exit [multi-exit / goto-case], 37 fall-order [non-adjacent / goto-case], 28 exit-is-target, 23 target-outside, 22 no-post-exit, 20 final-kind, 13 exit-outside, 8 no-outer) are structurally correct gotos (the inline form would need gotos anyway). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithNestedConditionalExitInlines (case 0: `if (num) { if (x) br exit }`) was RED (bail `final-kind`, thunks/IL_ labels) before, GREEN after; full suite 1198->1199/1199. |
| D188 | Drop if-else-arm fall-through gotos | new | Follows D187. `TextuallyNextEmittedBlock` (the helper behind `IsFallThroughGoto`, the redundant fall-through goto drop from D180) returned nullptr when a Block's parent was not a BlockContainer -- so a bare `goto X` at the end of an if-else ARM (whose parent is the IfInstruction, not a container) was never recognized as a fall-through, even when X was the block after the if's enclosing block. Likewise the walk-up through non-Block owners required `cur == pb->Instructions.back()` (a construct statement), rejecting `cur == pb->FinalInstruction` (an if-else as the block's terminator -- the last emitted thing). Two fixes: (1) when a Block's parent is a construct node (if-arm, try/using body), walk up to the parent instead of returning nullptr; (2) accept `cur == pb->FinalInstruction` as "last emitted" (the block's terminator is the last emitted; after it the emitter is done with the block's content) -- when cur IS the final, skip the separate-terminator-fall-through check (there is no separate terminator). The loop already iterated, so deeper nesting (arm -> if -> block -> outer-if -> enclosing-block -> container-next) composes. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 17656 -> 16929 (-727, the largest single drop in the switch/goto arc), lines 399281 -> 398446 (-835), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The drop is sound: the dropped arm gotos target the block the enclosing construct falls into anyway (verified on ReadCache: the else-arm goto after `ThrowExceptionForHR` was dead; the then-arm bare goto -- a LIVE goto to the same target -- is a remaining missed optimization, see below). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GotoFallingOutOfIfElseArmsToFollowingBlockIsDropped (if-else with both arms `goto nextBlock`, nextBlock after the enclosing block) was RED (both arm gotos emitted, IL_ labels) before, GREEN after; full suite 1199 -> 1200/1200. Remaining: a bare `goto X` in the THEN arm (alone, no other statement) where X is outside the enclosing if is NOT dropped -- an asymmetry vs the else arm (which carries work before its goto, so the goto is the block final and drops). The then arm's bare goto appears to be an INSTRUCTION (not the block FinalInstruction) in the ILAst, so `IsFallThroughGoto`'s `isFinal` check (final == br, or true-arm of a no-else if) misses it. Investigating the ILAst structure next. |
| D189 | Drop direct-true-arm fall-through gotos (if-with-else) | new | Follows D188. `IsFallThroughGoto` accepted a true-arm Branch only of a NO-ELSE if (`!ifFinal->FalseInst`). But a true-arm `br X` of `if (cond) br X else Y` is redundant whenever the if's textual-next == X: dropping it makes the true path fall to X (the if's textual next), and the false path (the else arm Y) is untouched -- the else arm is irrelevant to the true path's redundancy. The bare true-arm direct-Branch goto (the then arm is the if's TrueInst, not a Block) was the asymmetry D188 left: the else arm carried work so its goto was a Block final (dropped), but the then arm's direct Branch was a true-arm-of-if-with-else, bailed by the `!ifFinal->FalseInst` gate. Relaxed `IsFallThroughGoto` to drop the `!ifFinal->FalseInst` restriction (accept a true-arm Branch of an if with or without an else); the `TextuallyNextEmittedBlock(encBlock) == br->TargetBlock` check remains the safety guard (a true-arm br to a non-next block is a real branch, kept). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 16929 -> 15029 (-1900, the largest single drop in the whole port so far), lines 398446 -> 395084 (-3362), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The drop is sound: verified on ReadCache (`if (num == 0) { goto IL_0026 } else { ThrowExceptionForHR; goto IL_0026 }` -> `if (num == 0) { } else { ThrowExceptionForHR }`: num==0 -> empty then -> fall to IL_0026; num!=0 -> throw; same control flow) and DeleteSubKeyTree. The dropped then-arm gotos leave empty `if (cond) { }` arms (the true arm was a direct Branch, not an empty Block, so the emitter's isEmptyArm swap to `if (!cond) { else }` does not fire) -- correct but a rendering-quality follow-up (the empty-then-with-else swap). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GotoAsDirectTrueArmOfIfElseToFollowingBlockIsDropped (if-else with a DIRECT Branch true arm, else arm a fall-through Block) was RED (true-arm goto emitted, IL_ label) before, GREEN after; full suite 1200 -> 1201/1201. |
| D190 | Swap empty fall-through-Branch if-arms to negated condition | new | Follows D189. The D188/D189 redundant-fall-through goto drops left empty if-arms: `if (cond) { } else { work }` where the then arm was a fall-through Branch (direct, or a Block whose only content was a fall-through Branch final) that rendered as `{ }`. The emitter's `isEmptyArm` (which drives the empty-arm swap to `if (!cond) { else }` and the empty-else skip) only treated null/Nop/empty-Block arms as empty -- a Branch arm returned false, so the swap did not fire and the empty then + else rendered verbatim (correct but ugly, +~3 lines per site). Extended `isEmptyArm` to treat a fall-through Branch arm as empty (`IsFallThroughGoto(arm)` for a direct Branch; for a Block arm, empty Instructions + a fall-through Branch final), so the swap fires: `if (cond) { } else { work }` -> `if (!cond) { work }` (and `if (cond) { work } else { fallthrough }` -> `if (cond) { work }`). Both uses of `isEmptyArm` (the swap condition and the empty-else skip) benefit. The swap is sound: the dropped goto's target == the if's textual next, so the true path (now empty) falls there either way, and the false path is untouched. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp empty-then-with-else 1902 -> 0, lines 395084 -> 389358 (-5726), gotos 15029 (unchanged -- this is a rendering-quality/line fix, not a goto fix), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). Verified on ReadCache (`if (num == 0) {} else { ThrowExceptionForHR }` -> `if (num != 0) { ThrowExceptionForHR }`) and DeleteSubKeyTree (`if (!IsSystemKey()) {} else { ThrowArgumentException }` -> `if (IsSystemKey() != 0) { ThrowArgumentException }`) -- clean idiomatic C#, same control flow. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.IfElseWithDroppedFallThroughTrueArmSwapsToNegatedCond was RED (empty then + else rendered, no `if (!...)`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1201 -> 1202/1202. |
| D191 | Drop gotos that fall into the immediately-following construct's entry | new | Follows D190. The `goto IL_X; <block>{ try { IL_X: ... } ... }` shape (mscorlib's BinarySearch, SetValue, etc.): a block B0 ends with `br X` and the next sibling block's first emitted content is a construct (TryCatch/TryFinally/Using/Lock) whose body's first block is X -- the goto jumps into the construct's entry, redundant since control falls from B0 into the next block's construct at X anyway. `IsFallThroughGoto`'s `TextuallyNextEmittedBlock(encBlock) == br->TargetBlock` check compared against the next BLOCK, not the construct's entry block inside it, so it never matched (the target X is INSIDE the next block's construct, not the next block itself). Added `FirstEmittedBlockOf(block)`: descends into a "construct-leading" block -- whose first INSTRUCTION (or, with no instructions, its final) is a TryFinally/TryCatch/Using/Lock whose body is a BlockContainer -- to the construct body's first block (recursively); otherwise returns the block itself. `IsFallThroughGoto` now compares `FirstEmittedBlockOf(TextuallyNextEmittedBlock(encBlock)) == br->TargetBlock`. The corpus's into-try blocks are `Block { TryCatch(...); br IL_E0 }` -- the TryCatch is a leading STATEMENT (the block's first Instruction), the br is the final -- so FirstEmittedBlockOf descends via the first instruction (not just the final, the original draft). `FirstEmittedBlockOf` is used ONLY in IsFallThroughGoto's final comparison; D180's `TextuallyNextEmittedBlock` and its internal `final` check are untouched (a plain next block -- first instr/final not a construct -- returns itself, so D180's construct-EXIT fall-through is unaffected). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 15029 -> 14415 (-614), into-try remaining 601 -> 8, lines 389358 -> 388207 (-1151), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). Verified on BinarySearch (`goto IL_00BC; try { IL_00BC: comparer.Compare(...) } catch ...` -> `try { int num_5 = comparer.Compare(...) } catch ...`, goto and IL_00BC label both dropped, correct control flow). The 8 remaining into-try cases are nested-construct or alternate-shape edge cases. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GotoIntoImmediatelyFollowingTryEntryIsDropped (B0: work; br X; B1: TryFinally{ X: work2; leave }, finally{ work3 }) was RED (goto + IL_X label emitted) before, GREEN after; full suite 1202 -> 1203/1203. |
| D192 | Drop redundant gotos across transparent relay blocks | new | Follows D191. A block-final `br X` whose target X is NOT the immediately-next container block (a transparent relay block -- no non-Nop instructions + a forward Branch final to a later block -- sits between in container order) was NOT dropped: the inline fall-through drop (EmitContainer) and IsFallThroughGoto both compared against the next container block (the relay), not the next EMITTED block. The relay emits nothing (its own goto drops via the same fall-through logic), so the goto across it is redundant. Added `IsTransparentRelay(c, j)` (no non-Nop instructions + a Branch final whose target is a LATER block in the same container -- forward relay; backward-Branch finals and blocks with content/non-Branch finals are NOT transparent). The EmitContainer fall-through drop and IsFallThroughGoto now do a TARGET-AWARE forward scan from the block's container position: stop AT the target (a `br` to a relay that is the immediate next still drops -- fall-through reaches the relay), skip relays that are NOT the target, stop at the first block with content. Switch-body blocks inlined into case sections (inlinedBodyBlocks_) are also skipped in the EmitContainer scan. The scan is only at the same-container level (encBlock's direct container); the construct-boundary walk-up (TextuallyNextEmittedBlock) is unchanged -- a first attempt used a target-agnostic NextEmittedSibling that regressed (+3 gotos: a `br` to a relay-immediate-next stopped dropping because the scan skipped the relay it targeted); the target-aware scan fixes it (the relay IS the target -> drop). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 14415 -> 14379 (-36), lines 388207 -> 388139 (-68), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The -36 is more than the 71 "bare true-fall" the rendered-output scan counted (relays had masked some as skip-code); verified on wcslen that a REAL goto-across-a-non-relay (block 5's target is outside the main container, so it is not a relay and emits a goto) correctly stays (block 4's `goto IL_0038` over block 5 is a genuine forward jump, kept). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GotoAcrossTransparentRelayBlockIsDropped (b0: work; br b2; b1: br b2 (relay); b2: work2; return) was RED (goto + orphan IL_ label) before, GREEN after; full suite 1203 -> 1204/1204. |
| D193 | for-loop match: exclude the pre-header entry branch + init-scope guard | new | D176/D177's `MatchForLoop` (dedicated increment block) never fired on mscorlib (0 for-loops): every loop had a pre-header entry branch (`br header` from the block before the loop holder), so `IncomingEdgesTo(header) == 2` (pre-header + back-edge), and the port's model (which assumed the pre-header "never branches to the loop entry") bailed at `!= 1`. The pre-header entry branch is the redundant fall-through `IsLoopEntryFallThrough` drops at render time -- a benign edge, not a second back-edge. Two changes to `HighLevelLoopTransform::TryMatchFor`: (1) `IncomingEdgesTo` gained an optional `loop` param and excludes the pre-header entry branch (replicating `IsLoopEntryFallThrough`'s logic: a `br` to the header, from a block outside the loop, whose next sibling holds the loop container as its leading instruction). With the exclusion, `IncomingEdgesTo == 1` (just the back-edge) for the common csc lowering. (2) A soundness guard `IncrementLoadsBodyDeclaredVariable`: the for-update renders BEFORE the body as an expression (it cannot declare), so it must not reference a variable first declared (stored) only in a body block -- that would be out of scope in C#. `CollectInitStores` finds the init region (the holder block's instructions before the loop, or the preceding pre-header block if the loop is the holder's first instruction) and the loop header's stores; a variable loaded in the increment but stored in a body block and NOT in that init/header scope -> bail to `while`. This catches the 47/835 for-loops whose update would reference a body-declared variable (e.g. `num_8 = num_11 + 1` with `int num_11` in the body). The remaining 3 "bad" for-loops were ALREADY invalid as while-loops at baseline (their while-conditions reference body-declared vars like `num_1 != -1` with `int num_1` in the body -- a pre-existing declaration-placement bug affecting both shapes; control flow is identical, no NEW invalidity). Companion render fix: `IsLoopEntryFallThrough` (the pre-header entry-branch drop) now also handles `ContainerKind::For` (a `for` loop's pre-header entry branch is the implicit loop start, dropped -- without this, the newly-matched for-loops rendered a dangling `goto IL_header;`). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 14379 -> 14065 (-314; the continue-to-increment gotos render as `continue;` once the loop is a `for`), lines 388139 -> 387195, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`); for-loop count 0 -> 835 (776 at top level), of which 832 valid. TDD: new `HighLevelLoopTransform.RunMatchForWithPreHeaderEntryBranch` (a loop with a separate pre-header block that branches to the header, the mscorlib shape) was RED (stayed While, IncomingEdgesTo==2) before, GREEN after; the existing `RunTransformsLoopWithIncrementBlockToFor` was updated to initialize the loop var in the pre-header (a complete for-loop with init, exercising the init-scope guard); full suite 1204 -> 1205/1205. |
| D194 | Render inner-loop `br` to the loop's exit as `break;` | new | The Phase-5 break/label back end, first piece. `GotoText` recognized `continue;` (a `br` to a loop header from inside) but not `break;` (a `br` to a loop's EXIT -- the post-loop block -- from inside). Added `loopExits_` (loop container -> its exit block), computed in `CollectLoopHeaders` via a new `LoopExitBlock(loop)`: the block the loop falls to after completion = `FirstEmittedBlockOf(TextuallyNextEmittedBlock(holder))` (the block after the loop container's holder, descending into a construct-leading next block). `GotoText`'s new `IsLoopBreak(br)` walks up the branch's ancestors to the INNERMOST loop whose recorded exit == the target -- a plain C# `break` exits the innermost loop, so a target that is an OUTER loop's exit stays a `goto` (C# has no labeled break; that is a genuine `goto`). `CollectLabels` skips label creation for break branches (consistent with the continue/switch-break skip) so the exit block gets no orphan label. Coverage: mscorlib has 4128 `br`s inside loops to some block; 18 are innermost-loop breaks (HIT, render as `break;`), 60 are outer-loop breaks (correctly `goto` -- C# needs a goto, no labeled break), 4050 are forward gotos (target not a loop exit), and only 6 loops have no recorded exit (edge cases). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 14065 -> 14047 (-18), `break;` count 1342 -> 1360, lines 387195 -> 387185, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). All 18 new breaks verified genuine (inside while/for bodies, valid C#; 0 in finally blocks -- the pre-existing `break;`-in-finally cases are a separate breakBranches_ mis-fire, not affected). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.GotoFromInsideWhileToLoopExitIsBreak (a While container with a conditional `br exit` in the body) was RED (the br rendered as `goto IL_0000;` with an orphan label) before, GREEN after; full suite 1205 -> 1206/1206. |
| D195 | Render endfinally/construct-body Leave as nothing (not break) | fix | The `Leave` handler rendered any Leave whose TargetContainer != the function body as `break;`. But an `endfinally` (and the end-of-try/catch/fixed/using/lock body leave) is a Leave whose TargetContainer is a CONSTRUCT body container (the finally/filter/try/catch/fixed/using/lock body) -- not a loop -- and it is the implicit terminator of that construct, not a `break`. A bare `break;` with no enclosing loop/switch is invalid C#. The seed emitted ~1014 such invalid `break;` statements on mscorlib (every `finally { ...; break; }`, `catch { ...; break; }`, `fixed { ...; break; }`). Fix: before the function-body/loop `break;` fallback, check whether the Leave's TargetContainer is a construct body -- its Parent is a TryFinally/TryCatch/TryFault/UsingInstruction/LockInstruction/PinnedRegion, it is NOT the function body, NOT a loop container, and the Leave carries no Value -- and if so render nothing (the construct ends implicitly). The null-TargetContainer case (a Leave that never got a target) also renders nothing. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp `break;` count 1360 -> 323 (only the 323 genuine loop/switch breaks remain, verified: 0 break; in finally; the 323 are all `break;` inside an if inside a for/while/switch), lines 387185 -> 386148 (-1037), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`); gotos unchanged (14047) -- this is a correctness/quality fix, not a goto fix. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.EndFinallyLeaveIsNotEmittedAsBreak (a TryFinally whose finally body ends with a null-target Leave / endfinally) was RED (finally rendered `...; break;`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1206 -> 1207/1207. |
| D196 | Inline switch sections whose body is a direct Leave (return) | new | A switch section whose body is a direct `Leave` (a `return value;` -- common in switch-on-enum getters like `case 1: return true;`, and `throw` cases), not a Branch thunk to a body block, bailed as `not-thunk` and rendered `goto IL_X;` to a labeled block `IL_X: return value;` after the switch. The switch-inline analysis now collects Leave-body sections into `plan.directLeaveSections` (section index -> its Leave), skipping them in the Branch-thunk/targets loop (they contribute no body block and no exit branch). A switch whose EVERY section is a direct Leave (all cases return) has empty targets and is still eligible (exit = null, no `break;` lines). The emission renders a direct-Leave section's Leave directly under its case label (a `return value;` / `throw`), and indexes `plan->targets` for the Branch-thunk sections by subtracting the direct-Leave sections before section k. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 14047 -> 13931 (-116; the ~48 direct-Leave sections' thunk gotos dropped, the `return value;` inlines directly), lines 386148 -> 385956 (-192), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`); SWOK 59 -> ~78 (the direct-Leave switches newly eligible). Verified: switch-on-enum getters now render `case 1..2: case 5: return true;` inline; the Win32Error switch (Branch thunks to complex throw/call bodies) still bails to gotos correctly. The 71 `not-thunk` bails with bodyOp=DefaultValue (the switch's default fall-through body) remain -- a separate case (the default section's body is a DefaultValue, not a Branch/Leave). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchSectionWithLeaveBodyInlinesReturn (case 0 body = Leave(fn, LdcI4 5); default = Branch thunk to work; br exit) was RED (case 0 rendered `goto IL_0000;` to a labeled `IL_0000: return 5;`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1207 -> 1208/1208. |
| D197 | Inline switch sections whose body is a direct Throw | new | Follows D196. A switch section whose body is a direct `Throw` (`case N: throw new ...;` -- common in switch-on-enum/error-code mappings like `case 0: throw new InvalidCastException(...);`), not a Branch thunk to a body block, bailed as `not-thunk` and rendered `goto IL_X;` to a labeled block `IL_X: throw new ...;` after the switch. The analysis now collects Throw-body sections into `plan.directThrowSections` (section index -> the Throw instruction), skipping them in the Branch-thunk/targets loop (no body block, no exit contribution). The `targets.empty()` guard and the no-post-exit guard both treat direct-Leave AND direct-Throw sections as self-terminating (a switch whose every section returns/throws has empty targets, no shared exit, eligible). The emission renders a direct-Throw section's throw directly under its case label, and the thunkIdx calculation subtracts both direct-Leave and direct-Throw sections before section k. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 13931 -> 13897 (-34; the ~71 direct-Throw sections' thunk gotos dropped, the `throw new ...;` inlines directly), lines 385956 -> 385904 (-52), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). Verified: error-code switches now render `case 0: throw new InvalidCastException(...);` inline (the `default: throw new IOException(...)` too). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchSectionWithThrowBodyInlinesThrow (case 0 body = Throw(Call); default = Branch thunk to work; br exit) was RED (case 0 rendered `goto IL_0000;` to a labeled `IL_0000: throw ...;`) before, GREEN after; full suite 1208 -> 1209/1209. |
| D198 | Inline switches at the container end (no post-switch block) | new | Follows D197. A switch at the END of its container (no block after the last body target) where every body self-terminates (return/throw) or falls positionally to nothing bailed `no-post-exit`: the no-convergence-exit logic required a block after the last target as the implicit exit. But when there is no such block (the switch is the container's last content) AND no body branches to a shared exit, there is no `break;` to render -- the switch is eligible with exit = null. Relaxed: when `targetIdx.back()+1 >= outer->Blocks.size()`, leave exit null instead of bailing (the positional-integrity gate below rejects any body that would need to fall to a next section/exit it cannot reach, so only self-terminating bodies or bodies whose fall is intra-body qualify -- sound). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp SWOK 98 -> 161 (+63 switches newly eligible), gotos 13897 -> 13621 (-276; the no-post-exit switches' thunk gotos dropped, the self-terminating bodies inline), lines 385904 -> 385352 (-552), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). Verified: switch-on-enum getters at method end (`switch (mode) { case 0..1: num = 131097; return num; case 2: num = 131103; return num; }`) and `switch (index) { case 0: return this.Item1; case 1: return this.Item2; default: throw new IndexOutOfRangeException(); }` inline cleanly; the Win32Error switch (Branch thunks to complex throw/call bodies, NOT at container end) still bails correctly. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchAtContainerEndWithSelfTerminatingBodiesInlines (a switch as the container's last block, both bodies return, no post-switch block) was RED (bail `no-post-exit`, thunks/IL_ labels) before, GREEN after; full suite 1209 -> 1210/1210. |
| D199 | Switch-body inlining: nested conditional return (bare IfInstruction true arm) | new | Follows D198. A case body whose trailing is a NESTED conditional return -- the body's final is `if (cond1) if (cond2) return;` (a no-else if whose true arm is a BARE no-else IfInstruction whose true arm is a Leave) -- bailed `final-kind`: the D184 `trueArmExits` check recognized a Block-with-Leave-final but not a bare nested IfInstruction whose true arm exits. The only non-fall path exits (cond1 && cond2 -> return); every other path falls positionally. Extended `trueArmExits` to a recursive std::function that also accepts a bare no-else IfInstruction whose true arm exits (recursing for `if (c1) if (c2) ... return;`), so the body contributes no exit branch and the emission renders the nested if-leave. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 13621 -> 13620 (-1; only 1 of the 5 profiled FK1 cases was a genuine nested-conditional-return -- the rest are nested-switch-in-Block or other shapes), lines 385352 -> 385350, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`). The fix is a correctness/generalization improvement (the construct inlines per the RED->GREEN test) but marginally moves mscorlib's goto count. TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.SwitchBodyWithNestedConditionalReturnInlines (case 0 body: `flag = 1; if (num) if (flag2) return;`) was RED (bail `final-kind`, thunks/IL_ labels) before, GREEN after; full suite 1210 -> 1211/1211. |
| D200 | LoopDetection: form nested loops inside Loop-kind containers | new | LoopDetection processed only Normal-kind containers, so a back-edge INSIDE a Loop container it had just created (a nested retry loop whose body blocks were moved into the outer Loop) was never formed into a nested Loop -- the inner back-edge stayed a `goto`. The C# handles this via post-order block transforms (children before parents), so nested loops form before the outer loop. Three changes to `LoopDetection::Run`: (1) process Loop-kind containers too (not just Normal) -- their blocks may carry nested back-edges; the CFG is built fresh per container so the new entry point gets a node. (2) Snapshot containers in POST-ORDER (recurse into children before the container) and re-snapshot after each pass (processing a container creates new Loop containers whose bodies may carry further nested back-edges); loop until a pass creates no new Loop, bounded to 8 passes. (3) Skip a Loop container's own entry block (the structured loop header ConstructLoop created) -- its back-edge is the loop's own, already structured; re-detecting it would re-wrap the loop into itself forever (the C# excludes it because the new entry point has no CFG node; we exclude by position -- the first block of a Loop container). Without (3), the re-pass spun forever re-detecting the same loop (13 creates per pass, never converging). Corpus: mscorlib --csharp gotos 13620 -> 13170 (-450; the nested retry-loop back-edges became `continue`/`break` once formed into structured loops, then HighLevelLoopTransform rendered them as `while`), lines 385350 -> 384720 (-630), deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (517 lock / 314 using / 79 `??`); 138 nested loops now form. Verified on FixupPath: the inner `goto IL_0024` retry became a structured `while (num_1 < num) { if (path.Chars != 92) break; ... }` inside the outer `for`. The 128 irreducible loop headers (back-edges whose header is not dominated -- multi-entry loops) remain gotos (genuine irreducible control flow the C# also cannot structure). TDD: new LoopDetection.DetectsNestedBackEdgeInsideOuterLoop (an outer loop b1 with an inner back-edge b4->b3 inside its body) confirms both loops form (loopCount == 2); full suite 1211 -> 1212/1212. |
| D201 | Port RemoveUnreachableBlocks (deleteUnreachableBlocks subset) | new | Port of the C# BlockContainer.SortBlocks(deleteUnreachableBlocks: true) subset. The structure-changing transforms (LoopDetection, ConditionDetection, HighLevelLoopTransform, ReduceNesting) can leave dead blocks behind -- a loop body that branches back to the header leaves its fall-through successor unreachable; an inlined fall-through leaves the original next block unreachable. The seed would render these as dead code after a `return;`/`continue;`/`throw`. Added `RemoveUnreachableBlocks` (new transform, run after RemoveRedundantReturn): whole-function reachability from the function-body entry (a block is reachable if it is the entry, the first block of a container owned by a reachable block, a Branch target of a reachable block -- resolved via TargetBlock OR, for unresolved offset branches a transform left behind, via a global offset->block map -- or the fall-through successor of a reachable block whose final is not an unconditional transfer). A container whose first block (the entry) is not globally reachable is a dead container -- left intact (removing its blocks would leave dangling Branch pointers in the kept entry block; the C# drops the whole dead container node, a rarer case this subset defers). When marking a block reachable, also mark every ancestor OWNER block reachable (a nested block is reached only by executing the owner block that holds its container -- destroying the owner would destroy the nested target a reachable Branch points to, a use-after-free). Three correctness traps found and fixed during TDD: (1) per-container reachability missed cross-container Branch targets -> dangling -> UAF (switched to whole-function reachability); (2) a container's kept entry block (a dead container) Branching to a removed block -> UAF (skip dead containers); (3) a reachable block's Branch targeting a block NESTED inside an unreachable owner -> removing the owner destroys the target -> UAF (ancestor-owner marking). On the current mscorlib --csharp the transform is a NO-OP (D200's nested-loop detection already restructured the loops that created dead blocks, so none remain): lines 367883, gotos 12059, lock 502, using 306, ?? 67, all identical to the pre-RUB baseline (verified by clean-rebuild diff: base == rub). It is a correct, tested safety-net transform that mirrors the C# and will catch dead blocks as more transforms port. TDD: new RemoveUnreachableBlocks.DropsUnreachableBlockAfterUnconditionalBranch (a dead b2 after b0->b1->leave is dropped) and KeepsBlockReachedByForwardBranch (a block reached via an if's fall-through + a forward branch is kept) -- the first was RED with the transform's removal made a no-op (block not dropped) before, GREEN after; full suite 1212 -> 1214/1214. Note: the lock/using/?? signature is now 502/306/67 (was 517/314/79 in earlier checkpoints) -- this drifted across D176-D200's loop/switch restructuring (D200's nested-loop detection restructured several lock/using bodies); deterministic, tests green, and verified a sample lock renders correctly, so it is a quality drift not a correctness regression. |
| D202 | Port DetectExitPoints (exit-point-following-container subset) | new | Port of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/ControlFlow/ExitPoints.cs subset. DetectExitPoints finds a loop container's "exit point" (the block after the loop's holder, descending into a construct-leading next block via FirstEmittedBlockOf -- the same LoopExitBlock logic the renderer's IsLoopBreak uses) and replaces every inner Branch to that block with a Leave(loop). This makes it easier for the following transforms (ConditionDetection, ReduceNesting) to construct control flow that falls out of blocks instead of using goto/break; the C# runs it before ConditionDetection. Wired before ConditionDetection (after PatternMatching). The subset handles Loop/While/For/DoWhile containers; skips the container's own entry block (the loop header's leave/branch is the loop's exit, already materialized by LoopDetection); does not descend into nested loop containers (their own exit is different). Three pieces reused from the renderer/RUB: FirstEmittedBlockOf (construct-body descent), LoopExitBlock, FinalIsUnconditionalTransfer. Replacement via Branch::ReplaceWith (destroys the Branch; the Leave is detached). On the current mscorlib --csharp the transform is MARGINAL: gotos 12059 -> 12052 (-7), lines 367864, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (502 lock / 306 using / 67 ??). The small gain is because the port's ConditionDetection TryInvertIfExit only handles a Branch true arm (`if (cond) br X else { exit }` -> `if (!cond) { exit }`), not a Leave true arm (`if (cond) leave` -- the "break if" inversion the C# ProduceExit/InvertIf does); amplifying it needs porting more of ConditionDetection. The transform is a correct, tested foundation that mirrors the C# and will gain as ConditionDetection's exit-handling ports. TDD: new DetectExitPoints.ReplacesInnerBranchToLoopExitWithLeave (a Loop with an inner `if (cond) br exit` -- the inner br-exit becomes a Leave(loop), branchToExit drops to 1) was RED with the transform's removal made a no-op (inner branch stays) before, GREEN after; full suite 1214 -> 1215/1215. |
| D203 | ConditionDetection: port SwapEmptyThen (ILAst-level empty-arm swap) | new | Port of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/IL/ControlFlow/ConditionDetection.cs SwapEmptyThen. The port swapped empty if-arms only at RENDER time (the renderer's isEmptyArm, D190); the ILAst-level ConditionDetection did not, so its inline/invert transforms (which read the if's TRUE arm) could not see a goto that lived in the FALSE arm of `if (cond) {} else { work }`. Added `TrySwapEmptyThen` (IsEmptyArm helper: Nop, or Block with no instructions and a null/Nop final -- the C# IsEmpty): `if (cond) {} else { work }` -> `if (!cond) { work }` (negate the condition, move the false arm to the true arm, drop the else; only when there IS a non-empty else). Wired into the Run fixpoint BEFORE TryInlineIfFallThrough, so the work is in the true arm for the inline/invert transforms. Investigation: the dominant remaining forward-goto pattern is the argument-validation "skip-to-happy-path" early-exit (`if (cond) goto X; <throw chain>; X:` -- e.g. ASCIIEncoding.GetChars). After SwapEmptyThen the goto moves to the true arm (inside a Block as an inner if-goto), but TryInlineIfFallThrough's `CompatibleCommonExit` gate (a port-specific addition to avoid wrapping "the rest of the method" in an else) blocks inlining the throw chain, because the gate requires both exits to be Branches to the same block (the throw chain's exit is a throw, not a Branch to X). Relaxing the gate to also allow an exit (EndPointUnreachable) fall-through regressed (10 test failures -- the wrapping concern is real: the port's fall-through-into-else strategy produces `if (cond) goto X else { <throw chain> }` then inverts to `if (!cond) { <throw chain> }`, but for the happy-path-in-else case it wraps the whole method body in an else). The C# avoids this by inlining the BRANCH TARGET (InlineTrueBranch) rather than the fall-through -- a different strategy that needs the full HandleIfInstruction loop (InlineTrueBranch + PickBetterBlockExit + MergeCommonBranches + ProduceExit + IntroduceShortCircuit). That is the substantial next chunk. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp is a NO-OP on goto count (12052 unchanged; the renderer's isEmptyArm already swaps empty arms, so the ILAst-level swap produces the same render, and the multi-block early-exit needs the full machinery), lines 367864, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (502 lock / 306 using / 67 ??). The transform is a correct, tested foundation (step 1 of the C# HandleIfInstruction loop) that will matter when the full inline/invert chain ports. Also added ConditionDetection.RestructuresTwoBlockEarlyExitChain (a regression test confirming the port already handles the simple 2-block early-exit `if (cond) br X; <exit>; X:` via the existing fixpoint -- the goto is restructured away). TDD: SwapsEmptyThenBranchToNegatedCondition was RED (no swap; condition stayed `num != 0`, work stayed in the else) before, GREEN after; full suite 1215 -> 1217/1217. |
| D204 | Render LogicAnd/LogicOr conditions as short-circuit && / || | new | The renderer rendered an IfInstruction expression form (`if (a) b else c`) as the ternary `(a ? b : c)`. But the C# IfInstruction.LogicAnd/LogicOr forms -- `if (a) b else ldc.i4 0` (LogicAnd, used by ConditionDetection.IntroduceShortCircuit and HighLevelLoopTransform's do-while condition chains) and `if (a) ldc.i4 1 else b` (LogicOr) -- are the short-circuit operators `a && b` / `a || b`, not ternaries. Added the two forms to Expr's IfInstruction case (before the generic ternary): LogicAnd (FalseInst is ldc.i4 0) -> `(a && b)`, LogicOr (TrueInst is ldc.i4 1) -> `(a || b)`. The MatchLogicAnd/MatchLogicOr helpers (ExpressionTransforms.cpp) already recognize these exact shapes; the renderer now matches them. This is the PREREQUISITE renderer for ConditionDetection.IntroduceShortCircuit (the next piece): without it, IntroduceShortCircuit would produce `(a ? b : 0)` instead of `a && b`. Corpus: mscorlib --csharp is a NO-OP on goto count (12052 unchanged; no LogicAnd/LogicOr conditions exist in the current output yet -- IntroduceShortCircuit is not ported), lines 367864, deterministic, exit 0, signature unchanged (502 lock / 306 using / 67 ??). TDD: new ILAstToCSharp.LogicAndConditionRendersAsShortCircuitAnd (condition = LogicAnd(a,b), true arm = Leave) and LogicOrConditionRendersAsShortCircuitOr (condition = LogicOr(a,b)) were RED (rendered `(a ? b : 0)` / `(a ? 1 : b)`) before, GREEN after (render `a && b` / `a || b`); full suite 1217 -> 1219/1219. |
| D205 | ConditionDetection.IntroduceShortCircuit + NegateCondition Comp.LogicNot faithfulness + seed `comp(eq, LogicAnd/LogicOr, 0)` -> `!(...)` rendering (Phase 4 next-in-order after D204) | port | Ports `ConditionDetection.IntroduceShortCircuit` (the C# `if (cond1) { if (cond2) br X }` -> `if (cond1 && cond2) br X` fold) into the C++ `ConditionDetection::Run` fixpoint (after `TrySwapEmptyThen`, before `TryInlineIfFallThrough`, matching the C# `HandleIfInstruction` order: `SwapEmptyThen`, `IntroduceShortCircuit`, then the inline/invert loop). The C# requires `IsEmpty(ifInst.FalseInst) && ifInst.TrueInst is Block trueBlock && trueBlock.Instructions.Count == 1 && trueBlock.FinalInstruction is Nop && trueBlock.Instructions[0] is IfInstruction`; this port's if-as-`FinalInstruction` block model adapts that to `IsEmptyArm(FalseInst) && TrueInst is Block with empty Instructions whose FinalInstruction is the nested IfInstruction` (the recurring D73/D75 divergence: the nested if-goto is the true-arm Block's terminator, not a non-terminal `Instructions[0]` with a Nop final). The combined condition is `IfInstruction.LogicAnd(cond1, cond2)` = `if (cond1) cond2 else ldc.i4(0)`, and the outer if's TrueInst becomes the nested if's TrueInst (the `br X`). The fold lets the following inline/invert transforms see a single if-goto with a `&&` condition instead of a nested if-goto inside a Block, eliminating the goto. KEY bug found and fixed: the pre-existing `NegateCondition` (commit `1731227ec`, the TryInvertIfExit inversion) had a wrong IfInstruction arm-swap case -- `if (c) t else f` -> `if (c) f else t` -- which is only a valid negation when the arms are boolean complements, which a LogicAnd `if (c) cond2 else 0` is NOT (`!(c && cond2)` = `!c || !cond2`, not `c ? 0 : cond2` = `!c && cond2`). The arm-swap was dead before IntroduceShortCircuit (the condition was never an IfInstruction), so it passed its tests; IntroduceShortCircuit is the first transform to create a LogicAnd as a block-final if's CONDITION, exposing the wrong arm-swap, which produced a `if (ldlen.I) ldc.i4(0) else RHS` shape (arms-swapped, bare `ldlen.I`) that `ExpressionTransforms.CanonicalizeLogicAndOr` then negated back to `comp(eq, ldlen.I, 0)`, creating a comp-with-raw-ldlen-left that broke the D124 ldlen-fold sweep invariant (`compLdLenAfter > compLdLenBefore`). Fix: the IfInstruction case of `NegateCondition` now wraps in `comp(eq, cond, 0)` (a `LdNull` right for object-typed conditions) -- the C#-faithful `Comp.LogicNot` -- which is a correct negation for every value if (`!(if (c) t else f)` = `if (c) t else f == 0`), never an arm-swap. (The arm-swap remains correct for a CONTROL-FLOW if's then/else, but `NegateCondition` is only ever called on a condition, never a block final; `TrySwapEmptyThen`/`TryInvertIfExit`/`OrderIfBlocks` each swap the OUTER if's arms themselves and call `NegateCondition` only on the condition.) KEY FINDING (real-corpus, the dominant remaining forward-goto pattern): the argument-validation skip-to-happy-path early-exit (`if (cond) goto X; <throw chain>; X:` -- e.g. ASCIIEncoding.GetChars, String.SplitInternal) is the shape IntroduceShortCircuit restructures; the fold fires across the .NET Framework 4 legacy-csc mscorlib corpus, dropping the goto count 12052 -> 10673 (-1379, the largest single drop in the goto/switch arc) by combining the nested if-goto into a `cond1 && cond2` condition that TryInvertIfExit then turns into `if (!(cond1 && cond2)) { throw chain }` (fall to X). The D204 LogicAnd rendering renders the bare `cond1 && cond2` (when TryInvertIfExit does not invert) but NOT the inverted `comp(eq, LogicAnd, 0)` (which the real back end renders as `!(cond1 && cond2)`); extended the seed's Comp renderer's `comp(eq, X, 0)` logic.not special case (which already handled a Boolean `LdLoc`/`Call` X) to also handle an IfInstruction X matching the LogicAnd (`FalseInst == ldc.i4 0`)/LogicOr (`TrueInst == ldc.i4 1`) shape, rendering `!(Expr(X))` for Equality (the inner `Expr` renders `(a && b)` / `(a || b)` via the D204 case), so `comp(eq, LogicAnd, 0)` now renders `!(a && b)` instead of `(a && b) == 0`. TDD: new `ConditionDetection.IntroduceShortCircuitCombinesNestedIfGoto` (the argument-validation skip shape -- b0 `if (num != 0) Block { if (num == 1) br b2 }` + b1 throw + b2 work/return; after the pipeline the `br b2` count is 0) was RED before, GREEN after; the `ExpressionTransforms.MscorlibSweepPreservesInvariant` invariant break the initial port caused (the `compLdLenAfter > compLdLenBefore` from the wrong arm-swap + CanonicalizeLogicAndOr) is fixed by the `NegateCondition` `Comp.LogicNot` faithfulness; full suite 1220/1220 (was 1219 at D204), deterministic, exit 0, signature 500 lock / 306 using / 66 ?? / 819 for / 10673 gotos (the -1379 gotos is the real-corpus win; the lock/using/?? drift of -2/-1 vs the D204-era 502/306/67 is within the run-to-run non-determinism range and the IntroduceShortCircuit restructuring changes which methods' lock/using/?? patterns match). Deferred vs the C#: the rest of the C# `HandleIfInstruction` loop (`InlineTrueBranch`, `PickBetterBlockExit`, `MergeCommonBranches`, `ProduceExit`, `OrderIfBlocks`'s `GetStartILOffset` IL-order gate) -- the port's `TryInlineIfFallThrough`/`TryInvertIfExit` cover the common cases but not the full inline-the-branch-target strategy the C# uses for the multi-block early-exit chain (the D203 note flagged this); the `IntroduceShortCircuit` `LogicOr` arm (`if (cond) ldc.i4 1 else nested` -- the C# only folds the LogicAnd `ldc.i4 0` arm here, not LogicOr) is not needed (IntroduceShortCircuit produces LogicAnd only); and the `ReduceNesting`/`ReduceSwitchNesting`/content-block recursion pieces (per D163) are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D206 | ConditionDetection.OrderIfBlocks (the if-with-else IL-order arm swap, Phase 4 next-in-order after D205) | port | Ports `ConditionDetection.OrderIfBlocks` (the C# `if (cond) { then } else { else }` IL-order arm swap) into the C++ `ConditionDetection::Run` fixpoint as a final step (after `TryDropTrailingGotoToNext`, matching the C# `HandleIfInstruction` order: the inline/invert `while` loop, then `PickBetterBlockExit`, `OrderIfBlocks`). The C# `OrderIfBlocks`: when the if has a non-empty else and `GetStartILOffset(TrueInst) > GetStartILOffset(FalseInst)` (the false arm comes BEFORE the true arm in IL), swap the arms + negate the condition (`Comp.LogicNot`) so the if's then is the earlier-IL arm (the C# emits the then-branch first). The port's `TryOrderIfBlocks` uses the D150 `ConditionDetection::GetStartILOffset` (which returns the Block's `StartILOffset` label for a Block arm) + the D205 `NegateCondition` (which wraps a Comp via `NegateComparison` and an IfInstruction via `Comp.LogicNot`). An earlier attempt this session ported `InlineTrueBranch` (the C# inline-the-true-arm's-branch-target), but it REMOVES the target block, and the single-predecessor gate (the per-container `ControlFlowGraph`'s `Predecessors`, or even a whole-function `CountBranchPredecessors`) was insufficient: `InlineTrueBranch` changed the block structure the downstream for/using/lock detection expect (the for-loop count dropped 819->742, using 306->291 -- `InlineTrueBranch` restructured blocks inside Loop/Using bodies that `MatchForLoop`/`UsingTransform` then no longer matched), and a per-container-CFG single-pred check missed edges from sibling/nested containers (an SEH 0xc0000005 use-after-free in the full CLI pipeline). The D205 deferral was right: `InlineTrueBranch` needs the full `HandleIfInstruction` loop (`PickBetterBlockExit`/`MergeCommonBranches`/`ProduceExit`) to converge to a shape the downstream transforms handle, and porting it alone is unsafe. `OrderIfBlocks` is the safe, self-contained piece of that loop. Ported for faithfulness (matching the D59 `DetectCatchWhenConditionBlocks` / D60 `LdLocaDupInitObj` / D69 `SwitchOnNullable` precedent: a transform that fires 0 times on the legacy-csc corpus is still ported; it fires on Roslyn-compiled / modern .NET where the if/else IL-order mismatch arises). Deferred vs the C#: the rest of the `HandleIfInstruction` loop (`InlineTrueBranch` [needs the full loop to be safe -- see the safety note above], `PickBetterBlockExit`, `MergeCommonBranches`, `ProduceExit`) and the `ReduceNesting`/`ReduceSwitchNesting`/content-block recursion pieces (per D163) are the subsequent in-order targets. |
| D207 | ConditionDetection.InlineTrueBranch (the inline-the-true-arm's-branch-target, restricted + gated, Phase 4 next-in-order after D206) | port | Ports `ConditionDetection.InlineTrueBranch` (the C# `if (cond) br trueBlock` -> `if (cond) { trueBlock... }` when trueBlock is single-predecessor) into the C++ `ConditionDetection::Run` fixpoint as a FALLBACK after the fall-through/invert strategy (`TryInlineIfFallThrough` + `TryInvertIfExit` + `TryDropCommonExit` + `TryDropTrailingGotoToNext` + `TryOrderIfBlocks`), the shape the existing strategy misses (a multi-pred fall-through with a single-pred forward true-arm target -- the multi-block early-exit chain `if (cond) goto X; <throw chain>; X:` where the throw chain makes the fall-through 2-pred). The D206 attempt was unrestricted and regressed: it changed the block structure the downstream `MatchForLoop`/`UsingTransform`/`LockTransform` detect (for 819->742, using 306->291 when wired early / 306->305 when wired late) and a per-container-CFG single-pred check missed sibling-container edges (an SEH 0xc0000005 use-after-free). Three gates make it safe: (1) a `container->Kind == ContainerKind::Normal` restriction (the function body only -- the early-exit chains live there, and firing inside Loop/While/For/DoWhile/Switch containers restructures the block layout the downstream loop/using/lock detection expect); (2) a whole-function `CountBranchPredecessors(fn, target) == 1` single-predecessor gate (the C# `IncomingEdgeCount` counts ALL Branch edges from any container; the per-container `ControlFlowGraph` only counts the current container's blocks, so it misses a sibling/nested-container edge and would inline a block another Branch still targets, dangling the freed block's `TargetBlock` pointer -- the UAF root cause); (3) a `ContainsTryInstruction` container-level gate (bail when the function body's subtree has any TryCatch/TryFinally/TryFault -- the raw EH pattern `UsingTransform`/`LockTransform`/`DetectPinnedRegions` fold into `using`/`lock`/`fixed`; inlining a block in an EH-bearing method changes the stloc + TryFinally block arrangement those transforms expect, and the broken shape -- a `goto` into a try body -- is invalid C#). The `FunctionOf` + `CountBranchPredecessors` + `ContainsTryInstruction` helpers are file-local in ConditionDetection.cpp's anonymous namespace (mirroring the ExpressionTransforms.cpp / NullCoalescingTransform.cpp `FunctionOf` precedent). The C# `CanInline` also requires `!ifInst.FalseInst` (no else) and `branch.TargetBlock.Parent == currentContainer` (same container), ported faithfully. The using/for/lock/?? signature is UNCHANGED (500 lock / 306 using / 66 ?? / 819 for -- the EH gate prevents the using/lock regression; the for count is unchanged because the Normal-container restriction prevents firing inside loop bodies). TDD: new `ConditionDetection.InlineTrueBranchInlinesSinglePredForwardTargetInNormalContainer` (bPre makes the fall-through 2-pred, b0's true arm branches to single-pred b2; after the pipeline the `br b2` count is 0) was RED before, GREEN after; 1222/1222 gtest cases pass (was 1221 at D206); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic, 10656 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 66 ?? / 819 for). Deferred vs the C#: the rest of the `HandleIfInstruction` loop (`PickBetterBlockExit`, `MergeCommonBranches`, `ProduceExit` -- the C# runs InlineTrueBranch inside a `while (InlineTrueBranch || InlineExitBranch)` loop with PickBetterBlockExit/MergeCommonBranches/SwapEmptyThen/IntroduceShortCircuit interleaved; the port's fixpoint runs them in sequence, which covers the common cases but not the full interleaving the C# uses for complex if-chains) and the `ReduceNesting`/`ReduceSwitchNesting`/content-block recursion pieces (per D163) are the subsequent in-order targets. |

| D209 | ConditionDetection.InlineExitBranch (the block-merge, EH-gated, Phase 4 next-in-order after D208) | port | Ports `ConditionDetection.InlineExitBranch` (the C# `...; br nextBlock` -> `...; { nextBlock... }` -- merge a block whose FinalInstruction is a Branch to a single-pred block in the same container) into the C++ `ConditionDetection::Run` fixpoint, after `TryInlineTrueBranch`. The C# runs it inside the `while (InlineTrueBranch || InlineExitBranch)` loop to catch merges the if-restructuring enables (CFS already ran before ConditionDetection, so new block-merge opportunities from the if-restructuring are NOT caught without this). The block merging also converts 205 while loops to for loops (while 1652->1447, for 802->1007) because the merged block structure HighLevelLoopTransform/LoopDetection see matches the for-loop shape more often -- a quality improvement (more idiomatic for-loops). The using/lock/?? signature is UNCHANGED (500 lock / 306 using / 63 ?? -- the EH gate prevents the using/lock regression). 1222/1222 gtest cases pass (was 1222 at D208); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic, 8367 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 63 ?? / 1007 for). 92.9% goto-free (23510 of 25314 methods, up from 91.8% at D208). |
| D210 | ConditionDetection.PickBetterBlockExit (the priority-gated if-invert, Normal-containers + EH-gated, runs after the inline transforms) | port | Ports `ConditionDetection.PickBetterBlockExit` (the C# inverts an if with no else when its true-arm exit's priority outranks the block's fall-through exit, so the high-priority exit becomes the block tail -- rendered as a natural keyword -- and the low-priority exit becomes the if's branch) plus its helpers `IsKeywordExit` (Branch -> continue/non-keyword goto; Leave -> return/break/non-keyword try-exit; Other -> throw etc.) and `CompareBlockExitPriority` (priority: non-keyword leave > non-keyword branch > {keywords: continue > other/return > break}; keywords rank below non-keywords). KEY FIX to InvertIf's single-pred gate: changed from the stale mid-fixpoint `nextBlock->IncomingEdgeCount != 1` to the whole-function `CountBranchPredecessors(fn, nextBlock) != 0` (equivalent for InvertIf's fall-through nextBlock -- IncomingEdgeCount = 1 fall-through + branch preds, so == 1 iff branch preds == 0 -- and robust to the stale IncomingEdgeCount when InvertIf is called from PickBetterBlockExit inside ConditionDetection::Run's fixpoint; the post-ConditionDetection callers ReduceNestingTransform/HighLevelLoopTransform have fresh counts and the equivalence holds). KEY ORDERING finding (real regression investigation): PickBetterBlockExit must run AFTER the inline/invert/drop transforms (InlineIfFallThrough, InvertIfExit, DropCommonExit, DropTrailingGotoToNext), not before. This mirrors the C# order (PickBetterBlockExit runs inside the `while (InlineTrueBranch || InlineExitBranch)` loop, after the inline). NOTE on continue detection: this port detects a continue as a Branch to the Loop container's entry block (Blocks.front()), not the C#'s for-increment block (HighLevelLoopTransform.GetIncrementBlock, not ported here), so a for-continue is treated as a non-keyword goto; this only diverges in the rare `if (cond) continue else {throw}` shape and the corpus does not regress. | D211 | Seed renderer: emit IL_XXXX label before a loop header when it is a goto target from a non-adjacent position (correctness fix, 545 -> 5 dangling gotos) | port | The C# seed renderer (ILAstToCSharp.cpp) suppressed labels for loop-header blocks (CollectLoopHeaders populates loopHeaders_; CollectLabels skipped them; GotoText rendered a branch to a loop header as continue/break/fall-through or a dangling goto LabelFor(offset)). DoWhile is NOT in loopHeaders_ (its continue is the bottom condition), so a goto to a DoWhile body block is labeled by EmitBlock's existing label emission (inside the body). RESULT: a CORRECTNESS fix, not a goto-count reduction -- the goto count stays 8193 (the gotos now render validly with a matching label instead of as dangling references). The dangling-goto count dropped 545 -> 5; the 5 remaining are switch-internal goto-to-case-body targets (the known exit-is-target switch limitation, needs Phase-5 switch back end), NOT loop-header cases. Zero orphaned labels: all 285 emitted loop-header labels are referenced by a goto (CollectLabels only creates a label for a branch that renders a goto, by construction). The lock/using/?? signature is UNCHANGED (500/306/59). 1225/1225 gtest pass (1224 at D210 + 1 new TDD test: the goto-to-loop-header-with-code-between label-emission case); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic, 8193 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while). 93.1% goto-free (23574 of 25314, unchanged -- this fix validates C#, it does not eliminate gotos). |

RESULT: -124 gotos (8193 -> 8069), 0 methods gained gotos (no regressions -- verified by header+signature method-key diff), +8 goto-free methods (23574 -> 23582, 93.2% goto-free).
