| D213 | Seed renderer: emit IL_XXXX label before try/catch/lock/using entry when it is a goto target from outside (correctness fix, 176 -> 8 goto-into-construct, 19 -> 3 within-method duplicate labels) | port | The seed (ILAstToCSharp.cpp) emitted a construct-body entry block's IL_xxxx: label INSIDE the construct (EmitBlock), so a goto to the entry from OUTSIDE rendered as a goto INTO the construct body -- invalid C# (a goto cannot jump into a try/catch/finally/lock/using body). The early-exit-guard-into-try shape (e.g. Microsoft.Win32.Registry.GetValue: `if (registryKey != null) goto IL_0016; return null; try { IL_0016: ... } finally { registryKey.Close(); }` -- the goto jumps over the `return null` and into the try's entry) had 176 instances on the legacy-csc mscorlib corpus. FIX (generalizes D211's loop-header label from loops to try/lock/using): (1) EmitHeaderLabel(header, bodyContainer) emits the entry block's label BEFORE the construct keyword (so the goto targets the construct statement -- `IL_0016: try { ... }` is valid) and records the block in emittedHeaderLabels_; (2) EmitBodyHeaderLabel(bodyInst) casts the ILInstruction body to BlockContainer and calls EmitHeaderLabel for the TryCatch/TryFinally/Lock/Using emission; (3) EmitBlock suppresses the label for a block in emittedHeaderLabels_ so it is not emitted a second time inside (fixes D211's latent double-emission for Loop while(true) headers and the new constructs); (4) the loop EmitHeaderLabel calls now pass the loop container as the body. KEY SAFETY GATE (EntryTargetedFromInside): the label moves before the construct only when NO goto-rendering branch to the entry is from INSIDE the construct (a goto from inside to the construct's own entry re-enters it; moving the label would make it jump OUT of the construct, running a finally/leave, and back in -- wrong). Branches that render as continue/break/a dropped fall-through do not reference the label (CollectLabels skipped them) and do not block the move; the loop back-edge (a continue) is correctly ignored, so D211's loop test still passes. RESULT: a CORRECTNESS fix, not a goto-count reduction -- the goto count stays 8069 (the gotos now render validly with a matching label before the construct). The goto-into-construct-entry count dropped 176 -> 8 (168 fixed); the 8 remaining are nested-try cases (a goto from inside an inner try to the outer try's entry -- EntryTargetedFromInside correctly bails; genuinely needs restructuring). BONUS: the EmitBlock suppression fixed D211's latent double-emission -- within-method duplicate labels dropped 19 -> 3 (the 3 remaining are pre-existing iterator state machines `<>d__`, YieldReturnDecompiler not ported). The lock/using/?? signature is UNCHANGED (500/306/59); 0 methods gained gotos (no regressions, verified by header+signature diff); 93.2% goto-free unchanged (23582 of 25314). 1227/1227 gtest pass (1226 at D212 + 1 new TDD test: the goto-to-try-entry-with-code-between label-before-try case); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic, 8069 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while). |
| D214 | Run RemoveUnreachableBlocks before RemoveRedundantReturn; gate RemoveRedundantReturn against switch case bodies (-391 redundant return;, -43 gotos, +6 goto-free) | port | The port's RemoveRedundantReturn (only the function body's last block's value-less Leave) bailed when a trailing EMPTY dead block shadowed the real last reachable block's `return;` (e.g. Microsoft.Win32.RegistryKey.Dispose: a `try/finally` that always returns leaves its fall-through successor unreachable and empty, so the literal last block is empty, not the return block). The structure-changing transforms leave such trailing dead blocks; RemoveUnreachableBlocks (which removes them) ran AFTER RemoveRedundantReturn, so RemoveRedundantReturn saw the dead block and bailed, leaving a redundant `return;` (391 instances on the legacy-csc mscorlib corpus). FIX PART 1 (pipeline order): swap RemoveUnreachableBlocks to run BEFORE RemoveRedundantReturn so the dead trailing block is dropped first, making the real last reachable block last so RemoveRedundantReturn fires on it. FIX PART 2 (switch case body gate): the crude swap regressed 3 methods whose last reachable block was a SWITCH CASE BODY (e.g. System.Reflection.Emit.CustomAttributeBuilder.EmitType: `if (type.IsPrimitive) { switch (...) { case 5: ...; return; } }` -- the case body block is the function body's last block). Removing the case body's `return;` changed it from self-terminating to fall-through, and the seed's AnalyzeSwitchInline bailed (fall-order), rendering `goto IL_XXXX` thunks (+26 gotos). The C# RemoveRedundantReturn avoids this via ConvertReturnToFallthrough, which recurses into try/lock/using/if bodies ONLY (NOT switch), so it never touches a case body's return. The port's structural equivalent: a gate IsSwitchCaseBody that checks whether the block is a switch case body (some SwitchInstruction in the container subtree has a section whose Body is a Branch to the block) -- if so, keep the return. The walk is recursive (a switch may be nested in an if-arm -- the D212 `no-outer` shape -- with its case bodies in the ancestor container), so the gate walks the whole container subtree for SwitchInstructions. RESULT: -391 redundant `return;` (3656 -> 3265; the trailing returns after try/finally/construct-end are now dropped) AND -43 gotos (8069 -> 8026; the RemoveUnreachable-first ordering and the gate let some methods restructure further, a bonus beyond the return cleanup) AND +6 goto-free methods (23582 -> 23588, 93.2% unchanged ratio). 0 methods gained gotos (no regressions, verified by header+signature diff -- the gate fully protects switch case bodies including nested switches). The lock/using/?? signature is UNCHANGED (500/306/59). The C# ConvertReturnToFallthrough (recurse into construct bodies, convert a try-body/lock-body/using-body/if-arm `return;` to a fallthrough) is deferred -- the port's last-block removal + the switch gate cover the dominant trailing-return cases without the construct-body recursion's block-model complexity. 1229/1229 gtest pass (1227 at D213 + 2 new TDD tests: the trailing-dead-block old-order-bug + new-order-fix case, and the switch-case-body-keep-return gate case); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic, 8026 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while). |
| D215 | Port RemoveRedundantReturn.ConvertReturnToFallthrough: recurse into try/catch/lock/using/if bodies to convert a trailing return to a fallthrough (-720 redundant return;, 0 regressions) | port | D214 ported RemoveRedundantReturn's last-block trailing-return removal but deferred the C# ConvertReturnToFallthrough recursion (recurse into construct/if bodies, convert a trailing `return;` to a fallthrough). A `return;` at the end of a try/lock/using body (the construct is the method's last statement) is redundant: the body falls through to the finally/dispose/end, then the method falls through to its implicit exit. 720 such redundant `return;` on the legacy-csc mscorlib corpus (e.g. Microsoft.Win32.Registry.SetValue: `try { registryKey.SetValue(...); return; } finally { registryKey.Close(); }` -- the `return;` in the try body is redundant). PORT (the C# ConvertReturnToFallthrough + case Block/BlockContainer, adapted to the port's block model): (1) ConvertBlockTrailingReturn(block, fnBody, switchGateContainer) handles a block's trailing return -- drops a value-less Leave of `fnBody` (a `return;`), gated by IsSwitchCaseBody for container last-blocks (switchGateContainer non-null; null for if-arms); then recurses into the block's "last instruction" -- the construct/if FINAL, OR (when the return was the final and got dropped) the last NON-TERMINAL. (2) ConvertReturnToFallthrough(inst, fnBody) recurses into BlockContainer (handle its last block), TryFinally (TryBlock), TryCatch (TryBlock + each handler Body), LockInstruction/UsingInstruction (Body), IfInstruction (both arms -- the if is the last statement, so a trailing return in either arm is redundant), and a Block arm (handle its trailing return, no switch gate). (3) Run calls ConvertBlockTrailingReturn on the method body's last block (unifies D214's last-block removal + the recursion). KEY BLOCK-MODEL FINDING (D73/D75 divergence, the crux): a method body's last block carries the TryFinally as a NON-TERMINAL with a Leave final (the `[TryFinally]; Leave(fnBody)` shape -- `try {...; return;} finally {...}`), NOT as the block's FinalInstruction. D214 removes the Leave final (the method-level return), but the TryFinally non-terminal was not recursed (D214 only read the FinalInstruction). The fix: after dropping the return final, recurse into the block's last NON-TERMINAL when it is a construct (IsConstructOrIf). The construct-as-final case (the synthetic test shape, TryFinally IS the final) is also handled (recurse into the construct final). KEY GATE: IsSwitchCaseBody (D214, recursive -- a switch may nest in an if-arm) is applied to container last-blocks (the method body / nested containers) so a switch case body's terminator `return;` is kept (removing it breaks AnalyzeSwitchInline); if-arms have no gate (an arm is not a switch case body). Only a value-less Leave of `fnBody` (a void `return;`) is removed; value returns and leaves of other containers (break) are kept. RESULT: -720 redundant `return;` (3265 -> 2545; the trailing returns inside try/lock/using/if bodies are now dropped, e.g. SetValue renders `try { SetValue(...); } finally { Close(); }` with no redundant return). 0 methods gained gotos (no regressions, verified by header+signature diff -- the recursion only removes redundant returns, no goto impact); the goto count stays 8026; 93.2% goto-free unchanged (23588 of 25314). The lock/using/?? signature is UNCHANGED (500/306/59). 1230/1230 gtest pass (1229 at D214 + 1 new TDD test: the try-body trailing-return-to-fallthrough case); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic, 8026 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while). |

| D219 | PatternMatching core (Match + BacktrackingInfo + INode + Pattern, the Phase-5 C# AST pattern-match foundation, second piece) | port | Ports the PatternMatching core (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/PatternMatching/{Match,BacktrackingInfo,INode,Pattern}.hpp, mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/PatternMatching/{Match,BacktrackingInfo,INode,Pattern}.cs) -- the third in-order Phase-5 piece per the D218 plan (AstNode base -> SlotInfo/Role -> PatternMatching infrastructure). The core is the self-contained, RTTI-free foundation the generated node hierarchy's `DoMatch`/`DoMatchCollection` and the `Match...` helpers consult: `Match` (the result container -- a shared capture vector plus a Success flag), `BacktrackingInfo` (the backtracking stack of alternative continuations), `INode` (the pattern-match interface -- `DoMatch` for a single candidate, `DoMatchCollection` for a collection position), and `Pattern` (the abstract base of the pattern nodes -- the `$any$` string-wildcard, the `MatchString` helper, and the `DoMatchCollection` backtracking algorithm). KEY DESIGN (the C# `Match` is a struct holding a `List` reference, passed by value through the recursion so the copy shares the underlying list and captures/checkpoints propagate back): ported as a `shared_ptr<vector<pair<string, INode*>>>` -- a default-constructed `Match` holds a null shared_ptr (the failure sentinel, Success=false, matching the C# `default(Match)` whose `results == null`), `CreateNew()` allocates the vector (Success=true), and every copy aliases the one capture vector (matching the C# struct-by-value sharing of the reference-type List), so `Match` may be passed by value here too. The C# `internal int CheckPoint()` / `RestoreCheckPoint(int)` (Count / RemoveRange-to-truncate) port as size() / resize(). The C# `Add(string?, INode?)` / `AddNull(string?)` (no-op on a null group name) and `Get<T>` (a checked `(T)` downcast) port with `optional<string_view>` for the nullable group names and `dynamic_cast<T*>` for the checked downcast (INode is polymorphic via its virtual dtor). KEY STRUCTURE (the C# `Pattern.PossibleMatch` is a nested struct, but C++ cannot forward-declare a nested type, and `BacktrackingInfo` holds `Stack<Pattern.PossibleMatch>` while `Pattern` uses `BacktrackingInfo` -- a mutual include): `PossibleMatch` is ported as a free struct in the `PatternMatching` namespace (the C# member is `internal`, used only by Pattern/BacktrackingInfo), breaking the cycle cleanly (BacktrackingInfo.hpp defines it; Pattern.hpp includes BacktrackingInfo.hpp). The `Pattern.DoMatchCollection` static backtracking algorithm (the patternStack mirrors the backtracking stack; each pushed alternative is paired with the pattern index to resume at; the `stack.size() == patternStack.size()` invariant is restored each iteration) is ported inline verbatim, with `Debug.Assert` -> `assert`. The C# `PatternExtensions` (Match/IsMatch/ToType/ToExpression/ToStatement/WithName in INode.cs) and the concrete pattern nodes (AnyNode, OptionalNode, Repeat, NamedNode, ...) are NOT ported: the extension methods reference the generated AST node types (AstType, Expression, Statement) and NamedNode, none of which exist yet -- they land with the generated node hierarchy; the concrete nodes land as the transforms that use them arrive. Namespace `ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax::PatternMatching` (the convention, `ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.Syntax.PatternMatching` -> `ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax::PatternMatching`). All four headers are header-only (all methods inline): no CMake source listing (the TextLocation.hpp header-only precedent). KEY DESIGN (the C# `ChildType` is a `System.Type` and the is-a test is `ChildType.IsInstanceOfType(child)`; C++ has no `System.Type`): the declared child type is captured at the generic `CSharpSlotInfoT<T>` ctor as a type-erased `bool(*)(const AstNode*)` predicate -- a captureless lambda doing `dynamic_cast<const T*>` -- so the is-a check is faithful to the CLR `IsInstanceOfType` (accepts `T` and any subtype of `T`). That needs the `AstNode` hierarchy to be polymorphic, which is why `CSharpSlotInfo` lands alongside the start of the `AstNode` base: `AstNode : PatternMatching::INode` gives the virtual destructor `dynamic_cast` requires. The C# generic `CSharpSlotInfo<T>` cannot reuse the base name in C++ (a class template may not share a name with a non-template class), so the generic is `CSharpSlotInfoT<T>` deriving from the non-template `CSharpSlotInfo` base. Slots are singletons compared by ADDRESS (the C# `==` on the reference-type `CSharpSlotInfo` is reference equality), so a node-type header must define each slot static as a C++17 `inline` variable (one address across translation units); a plain `static` would give each TU its own copy and break the pointer-identity comparison. THE MINIMAL AstNode BASE ports the stable, self-contained core: the source-location pair (`StartLocation`/`EndLocation` virtual getters + `StorePrintStart`/`StorePrintEnd`, reusing the ported `TextLocation` -- locations are assigned at print time, overridable by single-token leaves); the parent / flattened-child-index / lazy-reindex machinery (`Parent()`, `ChildIndex`, `ChildIndicesValid()`, `InvalidateChildIndices()`, `EnsureChildIndices()`); the slot this node occupies in its parent (`Slot()` -> the parent's `GetChildSlotInfo(ChildIndex)`); the slot-storage contract the generated concrete nodes override (`GetChildCount`/`GetChild`/`SetChild`/`GetChildSlotInfo`/`GetCollectionByKind`/`CloneChildrenInto`) with the zero-child defaults a childless node (and the pattern placeholder) keep; sibling/child navigation (`NextSibling`/`PrevSibling`/`FirstChild`/`LastChild`/`HasChildren`); and the `INode` pattern-match hooks (`DoMatch`/`DoMatchCollection` delegating to the abstract `DoMatch(AstNode*, Match)` the concrete nodes supply). FIELD-ACCESS CRUX (C++ [class.access.derived]): the C# `internal int childIndex` would naively port to a protected field, but a derived concrete node's `SetChildNode` helper writes the CHILD's index directly (`value->childIndex = index` where `value` is `AstNode*`), and C++ forbids a derived class from writing a protected base member through a base-class pointer (only through its own type or a class derived from it). So `ChildIndex` is a PUBLIC field (the `ILInstruction::ChildIndex` precedent in the ported IL AST), while `Parent` stays faithful (private `parent_` + read-only `Parent()` + `SetParent`/`ClearParentAndIndex` accessors -- the C# generated code writes `parent` only via `SetParent`, never directly). The `internal` slot-storage-contract virtuals and helpers are public (the port's internal-to-public convention, the `Match` precedent). NAME-HIDING CRUX: a derived concrete node's `DoMatch(AstNode*, Match)` override HIDES the base `DoMatch(INode*, Match)` (the INode explicit-interface delegation), so the INode interface method must be invoked through an `INode*` -- the C++ equivalent of the C# `((INode)node).DoMatch(...)` explicit-interface call; calling it through the concrete/AstNode type resolves to the hidden typed overload and fails to compile. The ported pattern matcher already calls `DoMatch` via `INode*` (`Pattern.DoMatchCollection` uses `INode*`), so this fits naturally. DEFERRED to later Phase-5 slices (each a separately testable unit): `AbstractAnnotatable` + the `NodeTrivia` trivia it carries, `AstNodeCollection<T>` collection slots, the `ChildrenCollection`/`ChildEnumerator` enumerator, ancestor/descendant walks, the mutation API (`AddChild`/`InsertChild*`/`Remove`/`ReplaceWith`/`Clone` with its `ValidateNewSingleChild` tree invariants), `IAstVisitor`/`AcceptVisitor`, `ToString`/`CSharpOutputVisitor` rendering, and the `Contains`/`IsInside`/`GetNextNode`/`GetPrevNode` queries; the `Trivia` branch of the sibling/slot accessors is dropped with trivia itself. All self-contained on the already-ported `Parent`/`FirstChild`/`NextSibling`/`PrevSibling`/`GetChildCount`/`StartLocation`/`EndLocation` machinery, so this slice lands without touching the engine/CLI. PORTED: (1) `Children()` -> `ChildrenCollection` + `ChildEnumerator` (the C# `AstNode.ChildrenCollection` readonly struct + `ChildEnumerator` struct, nested in `AstNode`): a view over a node's children in document order with an enumerator that captures each child's successor before handing it out (`next_ = current_->NextSibling()` before the yield), so the loop body may remove or replace the current child mid-traversal without losing the place -- the hand-over-hand guarantee the transforms rely on. `Count`/`At(i)`/`operator[]` over the present (non-null) children, `GetEnumerator()` for the explicit MoveNext/Current loop, and `begin()`/`end()` for range-for (`for (AstNode* child : node.Children())`). (2) `Ancestors`/`AncestorsAndSelf` -- the parent-chain walk. (3) `Descendants`/`DescendantsAndSelf`/`DescendantNodes(pred)`/`DescendantNodesAndSelf(pred)` -- the pre-order DFS (`GetDescendantsImpl`, a private member: at each node remember its next sibling on a null-seeded stack, yield the node, then descend into the first child unless `descendIntoChildren` vetoes it, else resume from the stacked sibling). (4) `GetParent<T>()` (template, `dynamic_cast<T*>` is-a) and `GetParent(pred)` (first ancestor matching the predicate, or the first ancestor when `pred` is empty). (5) `GetNextNode`/`GetPrevNode` -- the document-order walk (next/prev sibling, else the parent's next/prev). (6) `Contains`/`IsInside` -- the half-open / closed location-range queries. KEY DESIGN (C# `IEnumerable<AstNode>` with `yield return` -> C++): the lazy sequences port to EAGER `std::vector<AstNode*>` (C++ has no `yield`; the document order is preserved), and the C# `Func<AstNode,bool>?` predicate ports to `std::function<bool(AstNode*)>` with an empty (default-constructed) function meaning "descend into all / match the first ancestor" (`!pred` discriminates empty). The `ChildEnumerator` ports verbatim (the successor-capture is the load-bearing invariant); for range-for it doubles as a C++17 input iterator -- `begin()` is a `MoveNext`'d enumerator (at the first child or exhausted), `end()` is the default sentinel (`current_ == nullptr`), and `operator!=` discriminates by `current_`, so a non-empty enumerator is not equal to the sentinel until it is advanced past its last child. `GetParent<T>()` (template, no params) and `GetParent(pred)` (non-template, default arg) overload without ambiguity: the template requires explicit `<T>` (so `GetParent()` resolves to the non-template), and `GetParent<StubBinary>()` selects the template. `ChildrenCollection`/`ChildEnumerator` are FREE types (not nested in `AstNode`) defined AFTER the `AstNode` class -- their method bodies call `AstNode` members (`FirstChild`/`NextSibling`), so they need the complete class; `Children()` is declared inside `AstNode` (forward-declared return type) and defined `inline` after the helper types, all in the one header (no circular include). The C# `GetNextNode`/`GetPrevNode` `Trivia` branch is dropped with trivia itself (a trivia node's next is its owning list, not the owner's sibling space). DEFERRED to later Phase-5 slices: the `AbstractAnnotatable` annotation channel (+ `NodeTrivia` trivia), the `AstNodeCollection<T>` collection slots, the mutation API (`AddChild`/`InsertChild*`/`Remove`/`ReplaceWith`/`Clone` with `SetChildNode`/`ValidateNewSingleChild`), `IAstVisitor`/`AcceptVisitor`, `ToString`/`CSharpOutputVisitor` rendering, and the `GetNextNode`/`GetPrevNode`/`GetNextSibling`/`GetPrevSibling` predicate overloads (the no-pred `GetNextNode`/`GetPrevNode` land here; the `pred` variants are a trivial follow-up). The `Type`-based overloads (`Annotation(Type)`, `RemoveAnnotations(Type)`) are DROPPED: they would need a `type_info`-to-`dynamic_cast` bridge C++ does not provide, and the engine uses only the generic `Annotation<T>()`/`RemoveAnnotations<T>()` (verified by grep -- every call uses a static type). The C# thread-safety (`Interlocked`/`lock` on the lazily-promoted single-vs-list) is DROPPED (the decompiler is single-threaded); a lazily-allocated `unique_ptr<vector<shared_ptr<AnnotationBase>>>` (null until the first `AddAnnotation`) matches the C# "no storage when no annotations" profile (the overwhelmingly common case for an AST node). Renaming the base to `AnnotationBase` (keeping the method `Annotation<T>()` -- the C# API name) fixes it; the isolated-compile repro (`cl /c` on a minimal file including only the header) confirmed the fix. KEY DESIGN (the C# `MemberwiseClone`+`CloneAnnotations`+`ReparentTrivia` `Clone` combo): the port has no `MemberwiseClone` (each concrete node's `Clone` copies its fields and deep-clones its children itself, per D223), so the concrete node's `Clone` calls `CloneAnnotationsFrom(*this)` (a `protected` helper on `AbstractAnnotatable` that copies the source's annotations onto the fresh clone: clonable -> deep copy, non-clonable -> shared via the same `shared_ptr`) + `ReparentTrivia()` (a `protected` helper on `AstNode`; the C# `private` -> C++ `protected` deviation, the `SetChildNode` precedent -- the per-concrete-node `Clone` needs it) to re-point the cloned `NodeTrivia`'s deep-copied trivia at the clone. `CloneAnnotationsFrom` replaces the C# `MemberwiseClone`+`CloneAnnotations` combo for the annotation channel. KEY DESIGN (trivia ownership): the C# `NodeTrivia.Leading`/`Trailing` (`List<Trivia>?`, GC-owned) port to an always-present `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Trivia>>` (empty until the first add -- the D222 always-present-vector precedent); `NodeTrivia` OWNS its trivia (the C# GC owns them; the port transfers ownership on `AddLeadingTrivia`/`AddTrailingTrivia`/`CopyTriviaFrom`, which clone the source trivia onto the target). `AddLeadingTrivia(Trivia*)` takes ownership (the holder owns the trivia); the engine's call sites (`AddLeadingTrivia(new Comment(...))`) map 1:1. DEFERRED to later Phase-5 slices: the sibling/slot/remove navigation trivia branches (the C# `this is Trivia { triviaSiblings: ... }` tests in `NextSibling`/`PrevSibling`/`Slot`/`Remove`/`GetNextNode`/`GetPrevNode`/`ClearParentAndIndex`) -- kept DROPPED (as D223): trivia is reached through the `LeadingTrivia`/`TrailingTrivia` lists (not the sibling/slot space), and the engine never calls `Remove()` on trivia (verified by grep); they land when a transform walks trivia via sibling links (would need either a `dynamic_cast<Trivia*>` in each method (needs the complete `Trivia` type inline -- a circular include with `Trivia.hpp`) or a virtual `IsTriviaNode()`/`TriviaNextSibling()`/... dispatch on `AstNode`). The concrete trivia (`Comment`/`PreProcessorDirective`) land with the generated node hierarchy (port-the-output per D1). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 (port the generated *output* by hand), the concrete nodes are hand-translated from the generated/hand-written source rather than the Roslyn source generator. The three concrete leaf expressions (`NullReferenceExpression`, `ThisReferenceExpression`, `BaseReferenceExpression` -- `null`/`this`/`base`) are the simplest generated nodes: no `[Slot]` children, no match members, just an `EndLocation` override (the keyword spans 4 chars from the print-time `StartLocation`). Each is a `final` (C# `sealed`) `Expression` subclass overriding `AcceptVisitor(IAstVisitor&)` to call `visitor.Visit<NodeName>(this)` (the generated visitor override), supplying the generated type-only `DoMatch` (`return other is <NodeName>` -> `dynamic_cast<<NodeName>*>(other) != nullptr`, since a no-slot no-member node matches by type only), and overriding `Clone` (the C# inherits `MemberwiseClone`+`CloneChildrenInto`; C++ has no `MemberwiseClone`, so each concrete node overrides it per the D223 pattern -- copy the print-time `StartLocation` via `StorePrintStart`, then `CloneAnnotationsFrom(*this)`+`ReparentTrivia()` for the annotation channel; no children to deep-copy). The `Expression` abstract base is thin: the C# `public abstract partial class Expression : AstNode` carries `[DecompilerAstNode(hasPatternPlaceholder: true)]` and adds only a typed `Clone` (`new Expression Clone()` downcasting `base.Clone()`) and a typed `ReplaceWith`. The typed `Clone` ports as a COVARIANT PURE-VIRTUAL OVERRIDE: `AstNode::Clone()` returns `AstNode*` (its base body throws, since C++ has no `MemberwiseClone`); `Expression` re-declares it `virtual Expression* Clone() const override = 0`, so a call through an `Expression*` returns an `Expression*` (the typed return the C# `new` gives) and a concrete expression MUST override it (the redeclaration makes it pure, so the base throwing body is unreachable through the expression hierarchy -- matching the C# where every concrete `Expression` overrides the virtual `Clone`). Covariant returns (`Expression*` derives from `AstNode*`, and `NullReferenceExpression*` derives from `Expression*`) make this a valid override chain. The pattern placeholder (`hasPatternPlaceholder: true` -> the generated `implicit operator Expression(Pattern)` + a sealed `PatternPlaceholder : Expression, INode, IPatternPlaceholder` wrapping a `Pattern`) is DEFERRED: it needs the concrete pattern nodes (`AnyNode`/`NamedNode`/...) and `VisitPatternPlaceholder` on `IAstVisitor`, neither ported yet (the D219 deferral -- the concrete pattern nodes land as the transforms that use them arrive); the abstract base and the concrete leaf nodes do not depend on it. The typed `ReplaceWith(Func<Expression,Expression>)` is DEFERRED: the C# `new` hides the `AstNode` overloads, but a C++ member of the same name would hide the inherited `ReplaceWith(AstNode*)` and `ReplaceWith(std::function<AstNode*(AstNode*)>)` (a `using`-declaration would re-introduce them), churn not needed for the dispatch slice; the `AstNode` overloads work for expressions (an `Expression` IS an `AstNode`), and the typed convenience lands with the engine's expression-level `ReplaceWith` call sites. `IAstVisitor.hpp` gains the three `Visit<Name>(<Name>*)` pure-virtuals (forward-declaring the concrete types so the header need not include them -- the D225 convention); `DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp` gains the matching `Visit` overrides defaulting to `VisitChildren(node)` (the C# generator's one-liner), including the three concrete node headers so the implicit `ConcreteNode* -> AstNode*` upcast in `VisitChildren(node)` has the complete derived type. The new Visit pure-virtuals on `IAstVisitor` are satisfied for every existing `IAstVisitor` subclass by the `DepthFirstAstVisitor` defaults (the only one is the D225 `RecordingVisitor : DepthFirstAstVisitor` in `IAstVisitor_Test.cpp`, which inherits the new defaults -- no breakage). TDD: 17 gtest cases in a new `CSharp_Expression` suite (cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Expressions/Expression_Test.cpp) -- `Expression` is abstract (covariant pure-virtual Clone), concrete expressions are Expression+AstNode (dynamic_cast is-a), the three EndLocation keyword spans, AcceptVisitor dispatches to the matching Visit + is virtual through AstNode*/Expression*, DepthFirstAstVisitor walks a tree of the new expressions in document order, DoMatch matches same-type/rejects-different-type/rejects-null (via the public INode delegation -- the protected typed DoMatch is hidden in the derived class, the D220 pattern), Clone copies StartLocation+detaches + is covariant through Expression* + virtual through AstNode*, inherited CheckInvariant passes on the no-child leaves, and the zero-child slot-storage defaults (no children, no First/Last, empty Children range-for). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled `Expression_Test.cpp` + relinked `ilspy_tests.exe` cleanly; the new headers are header-only (no CMake source listing -- the TextLocation.hpp/AbstractAnnotatable.hpp header-only precedent). RESULT: 17 new gtest cases, all pass; the full suite is 1432 -> 1449 (109 test suites, was 108) with 0 regressions (the 1432 prior tests pass unchanged -- the IAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the DepthFirstAstVisitor defaults); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0) with the engine UNAFFECTED (the new headers are not in the CLI's include graph -- confirmed by grep: `ILAstToCSharp.cpp` and `ILSpyCmd/` include none of them; the engine uses the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy). The next in-order Phase-5 pieces are the rest of the generated Expression hierarchy (the expressions with children/slots -- `PrimitiveExpression` (Value+Format scalars, no children), `IdentifierExpression`, `MemberReferenceExpression`, `InvocationExpression`, `BinaryOperatorExpression`, ... each adding its `[Slot]` child accessors, `Role`/`CSharpSlotInfo` statics, the generated `DoMatch` over its members, and `Clone`), then the Statement/TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies (each the same slot/visitor/match/clone shape), then the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage (`CSharpOutputVisitor : IAstVisitor`); the resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the AST. |

C++ has no boxed `object`, so the value is a `std::variant` (`PrimitiveValue`) whose alternatives are the faithful C++ equivalents: `std::monostate` is the C# null, `AnyValueTag` is the pattern wildcard, `char16_t` is the C# `char` (a UTF-16 code unit), `std::string`, `DecimalValue`, `float`, `double`, `std::int32_t`/`std::uint32_t`/`std::int64_t`/`std::uint64_t`. `operator==` on `std::variant` compares the index (the type) first then the held value, reproducing `object.Equals(a, b)` semantics exactly: same type + value equality, different types never equal (even when numerically equal -- a boxed `int` 0 and a boxed `long` 0 are not equal), two nulls equal. KEY DESIGN (the `AnyValue` sentinel): the C# `public static readonly object AnyValue = new object()` is a unique instance a pattern `PrimitiveExpression`'s `Value` is set to so its `DoMatch` matches any candidate; C++ has no single `object` root, so it is a distinct empty-struct alternative `AnyValueTag` (a tag) -- `std::holds_alternative<AnyValueTag>` is the "Value is AnyValue" test, and the `DoMatch` short-circuits on it. `AnyValueTag` needs `operator==`/`operator!=` (a no-state empty struct, always equal) because `std::variant::operator==` requires every alternative to be equality-comparable -- the first build failed on this (MSVC C2676 "binary operator== not defined for AnyValueTag") and the fix added the friend operators. KEY DESIGN (the 128-bit `decimal` alternative): the C# `decimal` alternative is the faithful `System.Decimal` model `DecimalValue` already ported in the IL layer (`Decompiler/IL/Instructions/LdcDecimal.hpp` -- a 96-bit unsigned mantissa lo/mid/hi, a sign, a scale, with `ToString` and the `FromInt32`/.../`FromBits` factories). It is REUSED here via a `using DecimalValue = ILSpy::Decompiler::IL::DecimalValue` alias rather than duplicated -- the 96-bit-mantissa + scale arithmetic (the divmod-by-1e9 digit formatting) is non-trivial and a second copy would be a drift hazard. The CSharp back end already depends on the IL layer (`ILAstToCSharp.cpp` consumes IL types); a Syntax header pulling in one IL value-type header is a minimal, contained cross-reference (the include weight is modest -- the IL instruction headers pull only `InstructionFlags`/`OpCode`/`StackType` + the standard `<cstdint>`/`<memory>`/`<string>`). The new pure-virtual is satisfied for every existing `IAstVisitor` subclass by the `DepthFirstAstVisitor` default (the D225 `RecordingVisitor` and the D226 `RecordingVisitor` both inherit it -- no breakage); the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op `AcceptVisitor` do not call any `Visit` method, so adding `VisitPrimitiveExpression` does not affect them. KEY DESIGN (the `Slots.hpp` shared kind holder): the C# generated `public static class Slots` (Slots.g.cs) is the shared set of canonical slot-kind constants -- one typed `CSharpSlotInfo<T>` per distinct child position across all node types, each its own canonical kind (null `Kind`); a node's per-node slot points back at it, and consumers compare `node.Slot.Kind == Slots.X` by object identity to identify a position polymorphically. The C# `public static class Slots` ports as a NAMESPACE (`ILSpy::...::Syntax::Slots`) holding C++17 `inline` variables: `inline` variables at namespace scope have external linkage and one address across translation units, so the pointer-identity comparison the slot system relies on is preserved. Each constant is `CSharpSlotInfoT<T>` whose ctor captures a `dynamic_cast<const T*>` is-a test, so the concrete child type must be complete where `Slots.hpp` is included -- hence the `Expression.hpp` include (the type of the `Left`/`Right` positions ported so far). `Slots.hpp` GROWS MONOTONICALLY: each new slot kind (a `[Slot]` name not yet seen) adds one `inline` constant. Ported as a `protected static` on `AstNode` (the generated `DoMatch` of a node with a nullable single-child slot calls it). KEY DESIGN (the `MatchRequired` helper on `AstNode`): the C# generator's direct `this.{member}.DoMatch(o.{member}, match)` for a non-nullable recursive child cannot be ported as a literal `expression_->DoMatch(...)` in the derived node -- C++ `[class.access.derived]` forbids a derived class from calling a protected base member through a pointer of a DIFFERENT type (the operand is an `Expression*`, a base of `UnaryOperatorExpression`, not `UnaryOperatorExpression*` itself); the build failed on MSVC C2244 "cannot access protected member declared in class AstNode". The `MatchOptional` precedent (D229) already routes the protected `DoMatch` through a same-class static on `AstNode` (a static member of `AstNode` may call the protected `DoMatch` through any `AstNode*`, same-class access). The port adds the matching `MatchRequired` protected static on `AstNode`: it guards a null PATTERN-side child defensively (the C# would null-deref `this.{member}` since the getter is null-forgiving `field!`; the port returns false rather than crashing -- a malformed required child fails to match) and lets a null CANDIDATE-side child flow through the operand's `DoMatch(nullptr)`, which returns false, matching the C#. For well-formed nodes (the operand always set) the behavior is identical to the C#. This helper will be reused by every node with a non-nullable recursive child (CastExpression's Expression, ConditionalExpression's children when non-nullable, ...). KEY DESIGN (the `class Expression` elaborated-type-specifier crux): the C# property is `Expression` of type `Expression` (a property named the same as its type -- legal in C#, which keeps property and type names in separate spaces). The faithful port names the accessor `Expression()`, but a member function named `Expression` SHADOWS the `Expression` base type within `UnaryOperatorExpression`'s class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member function and stops, even though it is not a type -- the D224 `Annotation<T>()`-shadows-the-`Annotation`-type crux). The ctor parameter and the getter return type precede the getter's declaration, so they use the plain `Expression`; every type usage AFTER the `Expression()` getter is declared (the setter parameter, the `ExpressionSlot` element type, the `static_cast`s in `SetChild`/`Clone`, and the backing field) uses the ELABORATED-TYPE-SPECIFIER `class Expression` (basic.lookup.elab: an elaborated specifier ignores non-type names and finds the hidden class). The build confirmed the elaborated specifier works in every one of these positions (a template argument, a `static_cast`, a member-field declaration). This is a recurring crux: every node with an `Expression`-typed `Expression` slot (ParenthesizedExpression, CastExpression, AsExpression, IsExpression, ...) will use the same `class Expression` elaboration in the shadowed spots. The constant name collides with the `Expression` class in the parent `Syntax` namespace; the template argument in the constant's own definition resolves to the class (the constant being declared is not yet in scope at the point its type is parsed, so unqualified lookup falls through to the parent namespace). RESULT: 29 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered `CSharp_UnaryOperatorExpression.*` run is green); the full suite is 1580 -> 1609 (114 test suites, was 113) with 0 regressions (the 1580 prior tests pass unchanged -- the `IAstVisitor`/`DepthFirstAstVisitor` additions are additive, satisfied by the new default, and `AstNode`'s `MatchRequired` is a new static that no prior code calls); the CLI decompiles mscorlib end-to-end (exit 0, deterministic) with the engine signature UNCHANGED from D230 (8026 gotos / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while / 2543 return -- verified by precise `grep -c` statement counts on the whole-mscorlib stdout: `ilspy_cli --csharp mscorlib.dll` with no `-t` filter) since `UnaryOperatorExpression.hpp`/`IAstVisitor.hpp`/`DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp`/`AstNode.hpp`/`Slots.hpp` are NOT in the CLI's include graph (the engine/CLI use the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy -- confirmed by the unchanged engine signature). The next in-order Phase-5 pieces are the remaining single-slot-only Expression nodes that do not need the `AstType` hierarchy: `ConditionalExpression` (Condition + TrueExpression + FalseExpression, three single `Expression` slots -- all non-nullable in the C# source, so it exercises the `MatchRequired` direct-dispatch pattern three times), `CheckedExpression`/`UncheckedExpression` (a single `Expression` operand, the same one-single-slot shape as `UnaryOperatorExpression` -- may share the `Expression` kind or declare its own), `ParenthesizedExpression` (a single `Expression` operand, hits the `class Expression` elaborated-specifier crux), ... then the `AstType` hierarchy (`SimpleType`/`MemberType`/`ComposedType`/`PrimitiveType`/...) which unblocks the `AstType`-bearing nodes (`CastExpression` an `Expression` + an `AstType`, `IdentifierExpression`'s `TypeArguments` `AstNodeCollection<AstType>`, `AsExpression`/`IsExpression`, `TypeOfExpression`, `TypeReferenceExpression`, ...), then the collection-slot nodes (`MemberReferenceExpression` target + name, `InvocationExpression` target + arguments `AstNodeCollection<Expression>`, `IndexerExpression` target + arguments), then the Statement/TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies, then the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage (`CSharpOutputVisitor : IAstVisitor`); the resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the AST. |

The FOURTH slot-bearing C# AST node (after BinaryOperatorExpression D229, AssignmentExpression D230, UnaryOperatorExpression D231) and the FIRST with MORE THAN ONE required (non-nullable) child slot, so it is the first real node to exercise the generator's non-nullable recursive DoMatch term THREE times in one node (the direct dispatch this.{member}.DoMatch(o.{member}, match), NOT MatchOptional, which the generator emits only for a nullable recursive child). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. `conditional_expression ::= expression '?' expression ':' expression` (C# grammar 12.21): an Expression with three single, REQUIRED (non-nullable) [Slot] Expression children (Condition/TrueExpression/FalseExpression) and NO scalar enum. PORTED: (1) the three slot accessors -- the generated [Slot("Condition")] Expression Condition, [Slot("True")] Expression TrueExpression, [Slot("False")] Expression FalseExpression as single REQUIRED (non-nullable) Expression* backing fields, each set through the CONST-INDEX SetChildNode(field, value, index) (no collection precedes any slot, so each flattened index is the constant slot position 0/1/2), (2) the per-node slot statics ConditionSlot/TrueExpressionSlot/FalseExpressionSlot (C++17 inline CSharpSlotInfoT<Expression> pointing at the shared Slots::Condition/Slots::True/Slots::False kinds; IsOptional = false since each slot is required; the static is named {PropertyName}Slot so TrueExpression's static is TrueExpressionSlot and FalseExpression's is FalseExpressionSlot, while the kind names are True/False), (3) the AcceptVisitor override calling visitor.VisitConditionalExpression(this), (4) the slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount = 3, GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo as a flat three-case index switch), (5) the generated DoMatch -- return other is ConditionalExpression o && this.Condition.DoMatch(o.Condition, match) && this.TrueExpression.DoMatch(o.TrueExpression, match) && this.FalseExpression.DoMatch(o.FalseExpression, match) (all three children non-nullable recursive -> the direct dispatch, routed through the D231 MatchRequired helper; NO scalar enum, so there is NO Any-wildcard term -- the simplest multi-child DoMatch shape), and (6) the per-concrete-node Clone (the D223 pattern -- no scalar member, so CloneAnnotationsFrom(*this) + deep-clone the three children through the setters + ReparentTrivia(); each child skipped if absent). KEY DESIGN (no name-shadowing crux): unlike UnaryOperatorExpression (D231) whose Expression() accessor shadows the Expression base type and forces the class Expression elaborated-type-specifier, ConditionalExpression's accessors are Condition/TrueExpression/FalseExpression (NONE named Expression), so the Expression base type is unshadowed in this class scope and the plain Expression (the base type) is used throughout -- the elaborated specifier is needed ONLY when a member function shares the base type's name (the D224 Annotation<T>() / D231 Expression() discriminator). KEY DESIGN (three new Slots kinds, qualified element type): the Condition/True/False operand positions are NEW slot kinds (distinct from Left/Right/Expression), so Slots.hpp gains three inline CSharpSlotInfoT constants. They are defined AFTER the Slots::Expression constant, so the D231 collision note's prediction applies: unqualified Expression would resolve to the Expression *variable* (the Slots::Expression constant), so each new constant's element type is qualified ::ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax::Expression. This is the first Slots addition after Expression and confirms the D231 note as the established pattern for every new Expression-typed Slots kind. Condition is a kind SHARED with several statement nodes (IfElseStatement/WhileStatement/DoWhileStatement/ForStatement/TryCatchStatement/QueryExpression, all Expression-typed -- TryCatchStatement's is nullable but the kind is the same) -- the first ported kind shared across an Expression node and Statement nodes (which land later); True/False are unique to ConditionalExpression (True/False are PascalCase, not the lowercase true/false C++ keywords, so the identifiers are safe and no macro collision was found in the include graph). KEY DESIGN (the all-required, no-collection ctor shape): the generator emits only the empty ctor plus the FULL all-params ctor for a node whose every slot is required and which has no collection slot (RequiredConstructorPrefixLength == count, ConstructorPrefixLengths = {count}, no shorter prefix and no params overload) -- so ConditionalExpression gets the empty ctor and the (condition, trueExpression, falseExpression) full ctor only, no intermediate prefix ctor. KEY DESIGN (the required-slot CheckInvariant): an empty ConditionalExpression (any slot null) violates the required-slot invariant, so the test suite exercises CheckInvariant ONLY on a node with all three slots filled (the BinaryOperatorExpression/AssignmentExpression nullable-slot precedent let CheckInvariant pass on an empty node; the UnaryOperatorExpression required-slot precedent exercises it on a filled node only -- ConditionalExpression follows the required-slot precedent). The DepthFirst walk and Clone tolerate absent children (the walk records just the conditional node; Clone skips a child clone when the child is null). DEFERRED: the hand-written QuestionMarkToken/ColonToken const-string fields (the ?/: token strings the output visitor emits) -- they are output-visitor concerns, not AST structure; they land when the output visitor consumes them (the D229/D230/D231 token-string/GetOperatorToken precedent). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitConditionalExpression(ConditionalExpression*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring ConditionalExpression -- the D225 convention); DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching override defaulting to VisitChildren(node) and includes ConditionalExpression.hpp for the upcast. The new pure-virtual is satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default (the D225-D231 RecordingVisitors all inherit it -- no breakage); the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding VisitConditionalExpression does not affect them. The slot kind is `Expression` (the `[Slot]` argument), so the per-node `ExpressionSlot` REUSES the already-ported `Slots::Expression` kind (the same kind `UnaryOperatorExpression` registered in D231) -- no new `Slots.hpp` constant (the first slot-bearing node since `AssignmentExpression` D230 to reuse an existing kind rather than add one; `AssignmentExpression` reused `Slots::Left`/`Slots::Right`, this reuses `Slots::Expression`). PORTED: the `Expression` slot accessor (the const-index `SetChildNode(field, value, 0)` setter, since the single slot is the first and only slot, no collection precedes it), the per-node `ExpressionSlot` static (C++17 `inline CSharpSlotInfoT<class Expression>` pointing at `Slots::Expression`, `IsOptional = false`), the `AcceptVisitor` override calling `visitor.VisitParenthesizedExpression(this)`, the slot-storage overrides (`GetChildCount = 1`, `GetChild`/`SetChild`/`GetChildSlotInfo` as a flat single-case index switch), the generated `DoMatch` (`return other is ParenthesizedExpression o && this.Expression.DoMatch(o.Expression, match)` -- one non-nullable recursive term routed through the D231 `MatchRequired` helper, no `Any`-wildcard), the per-concrete-node `Clone` (the D223 pattern -- no scalar, so `CloneAnnotationsFrom(*this)` + deep-clone the child through the setter + `ReparentTrivia()`; the child is skipped if absent), and the empty + all-params (`expression`) ctors (the generator emits only those two -- all slots are required and there is no collection, so `RequiredConstructorPrefixLength == count` and the full ctor is the only prefix). KEY DESIGN (the `class Expression` elaborated-type-specifier crux, the D231 precedent): the C# property is `Expression` of type `Expression` (a property named the same as its type). The faithful port names the accessor `Expression()`, which SHADOWS the `Expression` base type in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member function and stops, even though it is not a type -- the D224 `Annotation<T>()` crux). Every type usage AFTER the `Expression()` getter is declared (the setter parameter, the slot static, the `static_cast`, the backing field) uses the elaborated specifier `class Expression` (basic.lookup.elab ignores non-type names and finds the hidden class); the ctor parameter and the getter return type precede the getter so they use the plain `Expression`. KEY DESIGN (reusing `Slots::Expression`, no new constant): the C# generator's `Slots` holder has one typed `CSharpSlotInfo<T>` constant per distinct slot KIND NAME (verified in DecompilerSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs `WriteSlotKinds`/`CollectSlotKinds` -- kinds collapse to one name, so `node.Slot.Kind` is shared and consumers compare against `Slots.X`), so `[Slot("Expression")]` on `ParenthesizedExpression` shares the `Slots::Expression` kind `UnaryOperatorExpression` already registered. The per-node `ExpressionSlot` points at `&Slots::Expression`, and the pointer-identity comparison `node.Slot().Kind() == &Slots::Expression` is preserved across the two node types. This is the established reuse pattern (`AssignmentExpression` D230 reused `Slots::Left`/`Slots::Right`); `Slots.hpp` is unchanged. KEY DESIGN (the required-slot `CheckInvariant`): an empty `ParenthesizedExpression` (operand null) violates the required-slot invariant, so the test suite exercises `CheckInvariant` ONLY on a filled node (the `UnaryOperatorExpression` D231 / `ConditionalExpression` D232 required-slot precedent). The `DepthFirst` walk and `Clone` tolerate an absent operand (the walk records just the parenthesized node; `Clone` skips the child clone when the operand is null). DEFERRED: the hand-written `LParToken`/`RParToken` const-string fields (the `(`/`)` token strings the output visitor emits) -- they are pretty-printer concerns, not the AST structure; they land when the output visitor consumes them (the D229/D230/D231/D232 token-string / `GetOperatorToken` precedent deferred the same helpers). `IAstVisitor.hpp` gains the `VisitParenthesizedExpression(ParenthesizedExpression*)` pure-virtual (forward-declaring `ParenthesizedExpression` -- the D225 convention); `DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp` gains the matching override defaulting to `VisitChildren(node)` and includes `ParenthesizedExpression.hpp` for the upcast. The new pure-virtual is satisfied for every existing `IAstVisitor` subclass by the `DepthFirstAstVisitor` default (the D225-D232 `RecordingVisitor`s all inherit it -- no breakage); the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op `AcceptVisitor` do not call any `Visit` method, so adding `VisitParenthesizedExpression` does not affect them. ArraySpecifier is the first in-order piece of the ComposedType dependency: ComposedType.ArraySpecifiers is an AstNodeCollection<ArraySpecifier>, so ArraySpecifier must exist before ComposedType can port its collection slot; it is a self-contained leaf with no dependencies, so it lands first (the PrimitiveType-before-SimpleType leaf-first precedent). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. ArraySpecifier has [DecompilerAstNode] (no hasPatternPlaceholder), so no pattern placeholder is emitted. It declares NO [Slot] children: Dimensions is a hand-written int property (NOT a [Slot]), so the generator sees no slots and emits no slot properties, no name accessors, and no generated constructors (the WriteConstructors step returns early when slots.Count == 0); the two hand-written ctors (the empty ctor defaulting Dimensions to 1, and the (int dimensions) ctor) stand, and the inherited zero-child GetChildCount/GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo defaults apply (the NullReferenceExpression/Identifier leaf precedent). The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitArraySpecifier(this) (the class name does not end in "AstType", so the visit-method-name default yields VisitArraySpecifier). The generated DoMatch is `return other is ArraySpecifier o && this.Dimensions == o.Dimensions` -- a type check plus a plain-equality term on the int Dimensions: a non-[Slot] public int property goes to MembersToMatch (the generator adds every non-[Slot] instance property), and the DoMatchTerm fall-through (after the MatchAttributesAndModifiers/recursive/hasAny/String branches) emits `this.Dimensions == o.Dimensions` -- an int is not an AstNode (not recursive), not an enum (no Any wildcard), and not a string, so it hits the final `this.{member} == o.{member}` term. This is the first ported node to exercise an int-scalar DoMatch term (the Operator nodes are enums with Any; the FieldDirection node is an enum without Any; PrimitiveType.Keyword is a string; MemberType.IsDoubleColon is a bool -- ArraySpecifier.Dimensions is the first int). Dimensions is NOT a ctor param (the generator adds only settable ENUM-typed scalars to CtorParams, and an int is not an enum), so it is set via the property setter or the hand-written (int) ctor. Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): a fresh node with the same Dimensions plus CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia (the D223 concrete-clone pattern). No children to deep-copy (a leaf); the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not derived (the node stores them at print time, no own location fields), so they are NOT copied (the ConditionalExpression/SimpleType precedent for nodes without derived locations -- the discriminator is whether the node derives EndLocation: Identifier/PrimitiveType/NullReferenceExpression derive it and copy StartLocation; ConditionalExpression/SimpleType/MemberType/ArraySpecifier do not and copy no locations). The hand-written CheckInvariant override asserts Dimensions >= 1 (a rank specifier always has at least one dimension -- [] is rank 1) after the inherited base check -- the FIRST ported concrete node to add its own scalar invariant beyond the inherited base; AstNode::CheckInvariant is a no-op in NDEBUG (its body is #ifndef NDEBUG-guarded) and assert is a no-op in NDEBUG, so the whole override is a no-op in release builds without an explicit #ifndef NDEBUG wrap (mirrors the C# [Conditional("DEBUG")]). ToString(CSharpFormattingOptions) is DEFERRED (output stage; the ported AstNode base does not declare it, so there is nothing to override). KEY DESIGN (the first int-scalar DoMatch term): the generator's DoMatchTerm fall-through emits `this.{member} == o.{member}` for any non-recursive, non-enum, non-string scalar -- a plain C++ `==` on the int reproduces the C# `==` exactly (value equality, no boxing, no type distinction since both sides are int). This is the recurring pattern for every int/long/byte scalar member (ComposedType.PointerRank is the next int-scalar DoMatch term, landing with ComposedType). KEY DESIGN (the first scalar-invariant CheckInvariant override): the C# hand-written CheckInvariant override (base.CheckInvariant() + Debug.Assert) ports as `void CheckInvariant() override { AstNode::CheckInvariant(); assert(...); }` -- the base call is a no-op in NDEBUG (guarded body) and the assert is a no-op in NDEBUG, so the override is a no-op in release without an explicit #ifndef NDEBUG wrap (cleaner than wrapping). This is the pattern for every node with a hand-written scalar invariant (ComposedType's PointerRank >= 0 is the next, landing with ComposedType). KEY DESIGN (the no-location-copy Clone discriminator): a node that does NOT derive EndLocation (it stores the print-time span on the inherited base fields, no own location fields) does NOT copy StartLocation/EndLocation in Clone -- the locations are transient print-time artifacts re-set on the next output pass; a node that DERIVES EndLocation (Identifier/PrimitiveType/NullReferenceExpression) copies StartLocation so the derived EndLocation is correct. ArraySpecifier does not derive EndLocation, so its Clone copies no locations (the ConditionalExpression/SimpleType/MemberType precedent). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitArraySpecifier(ArraySpecifier*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring ArraySpecifier -- the D225 convention); DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching override defaulting to VisitChildren(node) plus the ArraySpecifier.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding VisitArraySpecifier does not affect them). (C# grammar 23.3): an attribute is a Type reference (the attribute class) plus an optional argument list; the Type is a REQUIRED AstType child slot, the Arguments is an AstNodeCollection<Expression> (zero or more argument expressions), and HasArgumentList is a plain bool distinguishing [Foo] (no argument list, false) from [Foo()] (an empty argument list, true). It is the first concrete AstNode that lives in the GeneralScope sub-namespace of the C# source; the port keeps it in the flat Syntax directory (the established convention -- no ported file uses the C# subfolder layout, all .hpp files are flat in Syntax/). It derives DIRECTLY from AstNode (not AstType and not Expression): an attribute is a structural node attached to an AttributeSection, not a type reference or an expression. It is the second ported node to combine a REQUIRED AstType child (Type) with a collection slot (Arguments) -- the MemberType shape (Target AstType + TypeArguments collection), but SIMPLER: Attribute has NO string-name [Slot] (no backing Identifier token), so there is no MemberName/MemberNameToken pair and no MatchString term. It is the second ported node with a plain (non-[Slot], non-enum) bool scalar (MemberType.IsDoubleColon was the first). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitAttribute(this) (the class name does not end in "AstType", so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitAttribute). The generated slot statics are TypeSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots.Type, required -- the Type AstType is non-nullable) and ArgumentsSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Expression> pointing at Slots.Argument, collection). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): copies the HasArgumentList scalar, deep-clones the Type through the setter (which re-parents; AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override), and deep-clones every Arguments element through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; Expression::Clone() returns Expression*, which Add(Expression*) accepts directly). No own location fields (StartLocation/EndLocation are the print-time base fields set by the unported output visitor), so they are not copied (the ConditionalExpression/SimpleType/MemberType/ArraySpecifier precedent for nodes without derived locations). PORTED: (1) the HasArgumentList bool scalar -- a plain property (no [Slot], not a ctor param since the generator adds only settable ENUM-typed scalars to CtorParams, and a bool is not an enum); it IS in MembersToMatch (the generator adds every non-[Slot] instance property), and a bool (not an enum, no Any member) emits the fall-through plain-equality DoMatch term (this.HasArgumentList == o.HasArgumentList); set via the property setter (object initializer). (2) the Type slot -- a single REQUIRED (non-nullable) AstType child at flattened index 0, const-index SetChildNode(field, value, 0) (no collection precedes it). (3) the Arguments collection slot -- an AstNodeCollectionT<Expression> member at flattened index 1, baseIndex=1 (the Type single slot precedes it), supportsIncremental=true (the node's only collection and last slot, so an element's flattened ChildIndex is 1 + its local position). (4) the per-node slot statics (TypeSlot pointing at Slots.Type required; ArgumentsSlot pointing at Slots.Argument collection). (5) the AcceptVisitor override (visitor.VisitAttribute(this)). (6) the collection-aware slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount = 1 + Count; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo walk the slots subtracting each one's width -- a single case then a collection step; GetCollectionByKind returns the Arguments collection for the Argument kind). (7) the generated DoMatch in MembersToMatch declaration order (Type, Arguments, HasArgumentList): the Type non-nullable recursive term dispatched via MatchRequired + the Arguments collection DoMatch term + the HasArgumentList plain-equality term. (8) the per-concrete-node Clone (copies HasArgumentList + CloneAnnotationsFrom + deep-clone Type via the setter + deep-clone each argument via Add + ReparentTrivia). (9) the ctors -- the empty ctor (collection member initialized with baseIndex=1, supportsIncremental=true) + the generated required-prefix (AstType) ctor; the collection ctors (AstType, IEnumerable<Expression>) and the params Expression[] form are DEFERRED (they use AddRange, the D222 deferral); Attribute.cs declares NO hand-written ctors (unlike SimpleType), so the port carries only the generated ctors. | D241 | AttributeSection (the second GeneralScope-sub-namespace concrete node: a sealed AstNode with an optional Identifier AttributeTargetToken slot + an Attribute Attributes collection -- the bracketed group of attributes, needed by ComposedType's Attributes collection and by every Statement/TypeMember/GeneralScope/ParameterDeclaration node) + Slots.Attribute (defined in Attribute.hpp, the cycle-breaking resolution) + IAstVisitor VisitAttributeSection + DepthFirstAstVisitor VisitAttributeSection (Phase 5: the third ComposedType-dependency piece, twenty-sixth piece) | port | Ports the AttributeSection concrete node (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/AttributeSection.hpp, mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/GeneralScope/AttributeSection.cs -- the generated AttributeSection.g.cs + the hand-written partial, which declares the AttributeTarget string convenience accessor, the AttributeTargetToken token slot, the Attributes collection, and the (Attribute) hand-written ctor) -- the twenty-sixth in-order Phase-5 piece per the D240 plan ("AttributeSection (an optional Identifier AttributeTargetToken + an Attribute Attributes collection ... needed by ComposedType's Attributes collection and by every Statement/TypeMember/GeneralScope/ParameterDeclaration node)"). attribute_section ::= '[' ( identifier ':' )? attribute* ']' (C# grammar 23.3): a bracketed group of attributes, optionally carrying a target ([return:...]/[assembly:...]/...). The AttributeTargetToken is an OPTIONAL (nullable) Identifier token slot (absent for the common [Foo] case, present only for [target:...]); the Attributes is an AstNodeCollection<Attribute> (one or more Attribute nodes). It is the second concrete AstNode that lives in the GeneralScope sub-namespace of the C# source; the port keeps it in the flat Syntax directory (the Attribute D240 precedent). It derives DIRECTLY from AstNode (not AstType and not Expression): an attribute section is a structural container, not a type reference or an expression. It is the first ported node to combine an OPTIONAL (nullable) single Identifier child slot with a collection slot -- the SimpleType shape (a nullable Identifier token + a collection), but with an Attribute collection instead of AstType type arguments. Its generated DoMatch has two terms in MembersToMatch order: a MatchString on the AttributeTarget string (the hand-written string convenience accessor -- a non-[Slot] instance string property, so the generator adds it as a String term; the backing AttributeTargetToken is [ExcludeFromMatch] so the token is not matched twice) and a collection recursive Attributes term (this.Attributes.DoMatch, the generator emits the collection-typed recursive term directly, NOT MatchOptional which it emits only for a nullable non-collection child -- the token is [ExcludeFromMatch] so it never appears in MembersToMatch). NO MatchRequired (no required child), NO plain-equality scalar. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitAttributeSection(this) (the class name does not end in "AstType", so the visit-method-name default yields VisitAttributeSection). The generated slot statics are AttributeTargetTokenSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Identifier> pointing at Slots.Identifier, optional -- the target may be absent) and AttributesSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Attribute> pointing at Slots.Attribute, collection). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): deep-clones the AttributeTargetToken (if present) and every Attributes element through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes). PORTED: (1) the AttributeTargetToken slot -- a single OPTIONAL (nullable) Identifier child at flattened index 0, const-index SetChildNode(field, value, 0) (no collection precedes it), reusing Slots.Identifier (no new Slots constant). (2) the AttributeTarget hand-written string convenience accessor -- the C# get => GetChild(Slots.Identifier)?.Name ?? string.Empty; set => SetChild(Slots.Identifier, Identifier.Create(value)); implemented directly over the attributeTargetToken_ field (the token is the only Identifier-kind slot, so reading/writing it directly is the faithful kind-scan equivalent, the SimpleType Identifier() precedent). The getter returns an empty std::string when the token is absent (the C# ?? string.Empty); the setter creates the token via Identifier::Create (NOT CreateIfNotEmpty -- the C# uses Identifier.Create, so an empty target still creates a token with an empty Name, not a null token, faithful to the C#). AttributeTarget is a non-[Slot], non-[ExcludeFromMatch] string property, so it IS in MembersToMatch (a String term). (3) the Attributes collection slot -- an AstNodeCollectionT<Attribute> member at flattened index 1, baseIndex=1 (the AttributeTargetToken single slot precedes it), supportsIncremental=true (the node's only collection and last slot). (4) the per-node slot statics (AttributeTargetTokenSlot pointing at Slots.Identifier optional; AttributesSlot pointing at Slots.Attribute collection). (5) the AcceptVisitor override (visitor.VisitAttributeSection(this)). (6) the collection-aware slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount = 1 + Count; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo walk the slots subtracting each one's width -- a single case then a collection step; GetCollectionByKind returns the Attributes collection for the Attribute kind). (7) the generated DoMatch in MembersToMatch declaration order (AttributeTarget, Attributes): the AttributeTarget MatchString term + the Attributes collection DoMatch term. (8) the per-concrete-node Clone (CloneAnnotationsFrom + deep-clone AttributeTargetToken via the setter + deep-clone each attribute via Add + ReparentTrivia). (9) the ctors -- the empty ctor (collection member initialized with baseIndex=1, supportsIncremental=true) + the hand-written (Attribute) ctor (adds the attribute via Add); the collection ctors (Identifier?, IEnumerable<Attribute>) and the params Attribute[] form are DEFERRED (they use AddRange, the D222 deferral). KEY DESIGN (the Slots.Attribute cycle-breaking resolution): Attribute is the first concrete node that is BOTH a Slots element type AND a node with per-node slot statics (its TypeSlot/ArgumentsSlot reference &Slots::Type/&Slots::Argument, so Attribute.hpp includes Slots.hpp). CSharpSlotInfoT<Attribute> needs Attribute complete (the dynamic_cast<const Attribute*> is-a test in the ctor), so the Slots::Attribute kind cannot live in Slots.hpp: placing it there would force Slots.hpp to include Attribute.hpp (for the complete Attribute), but Attribute.hpp includes Slots.hpp (for Slots::Type/Slots::Argument), and with Slots.hpp's include guard set the Slots::Type/Slots::Argument definitions would not be visible where Attribute.hpp's class body needs them -- a circular include. The resolution: define Slots::Attribute in Attribute.hpp ITSELF, after the Attribute class (where both CSharpSlotInfoT (visible via the Slots.hpp include) and Attribute (just defined) are complete). The inline variable still has external linkage and one address across TUs (the C++17 inline guarantee), preserving the pointer-identity comparison node.Slot.Kind == &Slots::Attribute. This is the resolution for every future concrete-node element kind whose node header includes Slots.hpp (the collection-element kinds whose element type is a concrete node with per-node slot statics). KEY DESIGN (NO name-shadowing crux, unlike SimpleType/UnaryOperatorExpression): the AttributeTarget and AttributeTargetToken accessors are not named Identifier/Expression/AstType, so no class in the Syntax namespace is shadowed, no elaborated-type-specifier is needed, and the Identifier::Create factory call in the AttributeTarget setter is unqualified (the Identifier class is found in the enclosing namespace). The discriminator is property-name vs class-name for the recurring Identifier/Expression shadowing (the MemberType D238 lesson). KEY DESIGN (the optional-slot CheckInvariant passes on empty): the AttributeTargetToken is an OPTIONAL (nullable) slot, so CheckInvariant does NOT assert it is filled -- an empty AttributeSection (no token, no attributes) passes the inherited CheckInvariant (unlike Attribute whose Type is required). KEY DESIGN (the AttributeTarget is a non-nullable string): the C# AttributeTarget is string (not string?), returning string.Empty when the token is absent, so the port returns std::string (non-optional) -- the MatchString passes optional<string_view>(string_view(AttributeTarget())) per side (the temporary std::string lives until the end of the full return expression, keeping the views valid for the MatchString call). The AnyString wildcard: a pattern AttributeSection whose AttributeTarget is "$any$" (set via AttributeTarget("$any$") which creates a token with Name "$any$") matches any candidate's AttributeTarget (the MatchString short-circuit when pattern == AnyString). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitAttributeSection(AttributeSection*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring AttributeSection -- the D225 convention); DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching override defaulting to VisitChildren(node) plus the AttributeSection.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding VisitAttributeSection does not affect them). TDD: 31 gtest cases in a new CSharp_AttributeSection suite (cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/AttributeSection_Test.cpp, wired into tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering is-a (AstNode not Expression not AstType), construction (the empty ctor -- AttributeTargetToken null, AttributeTarget empty, Attributes empty, GetChildCount 1; the (Attribute) ctor -- adds the attribute, parented, incremental ChildIndex baseIndex 1), the AttributeTargetToken setter (re-parents + detaches + clears on null), the AttributeTarget string accessor (round-trips via the token, empty creates an empty-Name token -- the Create-vs-CreateIfNotEmpty discriminator, replaces the token), the Attributes collection (empty, Add appends + parents + incremental ChildIndex baseIndex 1, GetCollectionByKind for the Attribute kind vs the Identifier/Type single-slot kinds vs null), the collection-aware slot-storage (GetChildCount = 1 + Count, GetChild dispatches token + attributes + throws out of range, GetChildSlotInfo dispatches + the kind identities for Identifier/Attribute, SetChild dispatches + throws), AcceptVisitor dispatch + virtuality through AstNode* (the depth-first walk visits the AttributeTargetToken, then the Attributes, each recursing into the attribute's Type SimpleType + its Identifier token, in document order), DoMatch (same-all matches, different-AttributeTarget rejects -- the MatchString term, the AnyString wildcard matches any + asymmetric, different-Attributes-count rejects, different-Attributes-value rejects, different-type rejects vs Attribute, null-candidate rejects), Clone (deep-copies token + attributes + re-parents + detaches, empty clone, virtual through AstNode*), CheckInvariant (passes on EMPTY -- the optional token, AND on filled), and the slot-static distinctness. BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled AttributeSection_Test.cpp + the recompiled IAstVisitor_Test.cpp/Identifier_Test.cpp/Expression_Test.cpp/PrimitiveExpression_Test.cpp/BinaryOperatorExpression_Test.cpp/AssignmentExpression_Test.cpp/UnaryOperatorExpression_Test.cpp/ConditionalExpression_Test.cpp/ParenthesizedExpression_Test.cpp/CheckedUncheckedExpression_Test.cpp/DirectionThrowExpression_Test.cpp/PrimitiveType_Test.cpp/SimpleType_Test.cpp/MemberType_Test.cpp/ArraySpecifier_Test.cpp/Attribute_Test.cpp (the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default) + relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe; the FIRST build hit a C2248 (Identifier's 2-arg ctor is private -- the tests must use the public Identifier::Create factory, not std::make_unique<Identifier>(name, location)), fixed by constructing the target tokens via Identifier::Create; the SECOND build hit SEH 0xc0000005 access violations in 4 tests (the MakeFooAttribute helper returned a unique_ptr<Attribute> whose Type SimpleType was a local that died when the helper returned -- a use-after-free, since the Attribute's Type slot is a non-owning raw pointer and the test's unique_ptrs own the nodes), fixed by returning a FooAttr struct holding BOTH the SimpleType type and the Attribute attr alive (with get()/operator-> exposing the Attribute*); the THIRD build compiled and the full filtered run is green. RESULT: 31 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_AttributeSection.* run is 31/31 green; the filtered CSharp_* run is 736/736 green across 30 suites); the full suite is 1937 -> 1968 (126 test suites, was 125) with 0 regressions (the 1937 prior tests pass unchanged -- the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly (the engine/CLI use the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy -- confirmed by grep: ILAstToCSharp.cpp and ILSpyCmd/ include none of the C# AST Syntax node headers, including the new AttributeSection.hpp and the changed Attribute.hpp), so the engine signature is byte-identical to D240 (no mscorlib.dll present in this environment to run the full 8026/500/306/59/999/1454/2543 baseline, but the include-graph isolation -- the D224-D240 precedent, re-confirmed by grep -- guarantees the CLI is unaffected; the Attribute.hpp/AttributeSection.hpp/IAstVisitor.hpp/DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp changes are header-only so no ilspy.lib .cpp symbol the CLI links changed, and the only .cpp change is the new test file which is in the tests target not ilspy.lib).
