| D242 | ComposedType (the third concrete AstType with a collection slot and the FIRST ported node with TWO collection slots: an Attributes collection of AttributeSection + a required BaseType AstType single slot + an ArraySpecifiers collection, plus HasRefSpecifier/HasReadOnlySpecifier/HasNullableSpecifier bools and a PointerRank int -- the next in-order Phase-5 piece per the D241 plan) + Slots.ArraySpecifier (in Slots.hpp) + Slots.AttributeSection (in AttributeSection.hpp, cycle-breaking) + IAstVisitor VisitComposedType + DepthFirstAstVisitor VisitComposedType (Phase 5: the first two-collection-slot node, twenty-seventh piece) | port | Ports the ComposedType concrete node (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/ComposedType.hpp, mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/ComposedType.cs -- the generated ComposedType.g.cs + the hand-written partial, which declares the const keyword tokens, the scalar properties, the slot properties, ToString, the Make* builders, and CheckInvariant; no hand-written ctors) -- the twenty-seventh in-order Phase-5 piece per the D241 plan ("ComposedType itself (Attributes collection + BaseType AstType + ArraySpecifiers collection + HasRefSpecifier/HasReadOnlySpecifier/HasNullableSpecifier bools + PointerRank int -- the first node with TWO collection slots, so the first whose second collection's baseIndex is dynamic and supportsIncremental is false for both)"). array_type ::= non_array_type rank_specifier+ (C# grammar 8.2.1), pointer_type ::= dataptr_type | funcptr_type | voidptr_type (24.3.1), nullable_reference_type/nullable_value_type (8.2.1/8.3.1): a ComposedType wraps a BaseType AstType with optional modifiers -- a leading ref/readonly (HasRefSpecifier/HasReadOnlySpecifier), a trailing ? (HasNullableSpecifier), a trailing *-run (PointerRank), and trailing rank specifiers (ArraySpecifiers, one ArraySpecifier per [...]); it also carries an Attributes collection of AttributeSections (the [Foo]/[return: Foo] groups attached to the type). It is the FIRST ported node with TWO collection slots (Attributes at slot 0 + ArraySpecifiers at slot 2, with the required BaseType single slot at slot 1 between them). The generator's supportsIncremental flag is `collectionCount == 1 && slotIndex == slots.Count - 1`; with two collections that is FALSE for BOTH, so neither maintains its elements' flattened ChildIndex incrementally -- every Add/Insert/Remove/single-slot-set invalidates the parent's indices for a lazy rebuild (EnsureChildIndices), and IndexOf falls back to a linear identity search. This is the first ported node where a single slot (BaseType) FOLLOWS a collection, so its setter uses the index-less SetChildNode(ref field, value) (the generator's constIndex = !slots.Take(slotIndex).Any(IsCollection) is false when a collection precedes the slot), which invalidates on a set/clear (the flattened index is dynamic -- the Attributes count can change); the SetChild override still passes the known flattened index to the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, index). The baseIndex passed to each collection is its SLOT INDEX (0 for Attributes, 2 for ArraySpecifiers), not the dynamic flattened index -- the generator passes slotIndex, and since supportsIncremental is false it is unused on the fast path (the lazy EnsureChildIndices rebuilds the actual flattened indices by walking GetChild(i)). The dynamic flattened layout is: Attributes occupies [0, attrCount), BaseType is at index attrCount, ArraySpecifiers occupies [attrCount + 1, attrCount + 1 + arrCount) -- the second collection's flattened start is dynamic (it depends on the first collection's count), the property the D241 plan flagged. Its generated DoMatch has SEVEN terms in MembersToMatch (source declaration) order: a collection recursive Attributes term, a plain-equality HasRefSpecifier bool term, a plain-equality HasReadOnlySpecifier bool term, a non-nullable recursive BaseType term (dispatched through MatchRequired -- the D231 [class.access.derived] workaround), a plain-equality HasNullableSpecifier bool term, a plain-equality PointerRank int term (the second ported int-scalar DoMatch term, the ArraySpecifier.Dimensions precedent), and a collection recursive ArraySpecifiers term. It is the first ported node to interleave two collections, three bool scalars, an int scalar, and a single AstType child across one DoMatch, and the first whose DoMatch term order is NOT the pure slot order (the scalars declared between the slots appear between their recursive terms). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitComposedType(this) (the class name does not end in "AstType", so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitComposedType; the EndsWith("AstType") rewriting to "...Type" applies only to FunctionPointerAstType/InvocationAstType/TupleAstType). The generated slot statics are AttributesSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AttributeSection> pointing at Slots.AttributeSection, collection), BaseTypeSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots.Type, required -- the BaseType AstType is non-nullable so IsCollection||IsNullable is false), and ArraySpecifiersSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<ArraySpecifier> pointing at Slots.ArraySpecifier, collection). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): copies the four scalars, deep-clones the BaseType through the setter (which re-parents; AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override), and deep-clones every Attributes/ArraySpecifiers element through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; AttributeSection::Clone() returns AttributeSection* and ArraySpecifier::Clone() returns ArraySpecifier*, which the typed Adds accept directly), in slot declaration order matching the generated CloneChildrenInto. No own location fields (ComposedType does not derive EndLocation), so no location copy (the ConditionalExpression/SimpleType/MemberType/ArraySpecifier/Attribute precedent). The four const keyword tokens (RefKeyword/ReadonlyKeyword/NullableToken/PointerToken) port as static constexpr const char* (the CheckedExpression.CheckedKeyword precedent); the generator excludes const string fields from MembersToMatch (it iterates only instance IPropertySymbols), so they never appear in the generated DoMatch. NO C++ name-shadowing crux (unlike SimpleType/UnaryOperatorExpression): the Attributes/BaseType/ArraySpecifiers accessors do not collide with any class in the Syntax namespace (there is AstType, not Type or BaseType), and no member is named AstType/Identifier/Expression/AttributeSection/ArraySpecifier, so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed anywhere and the Slots.Type/Slots.AttributeSection/Slots.ArraySpecifier references are unqualified. The generated ctors are DEFERRED except the empty ctor: every parametrized ctor takes the Attributes collection as its FIRST param (it precedes the required BaseType single slot, so the required-prefix ctor is (IEnumerable<AttributeSection>, AstType) and includes a collection param), and the generator's ctor body calls this.Attributes.AddRange(...) for it -- AddRange is the D222-deferred collection convenience mutator, so the whole parametrized-ctor surface (the required-prefix (attributes, baseType) ctor, the all-params (attributes, baseType, arraySpecifiers) ctor, and the params ArraySpecifier[] overload) is deferred until AddRange lands. This is the first ported node whose required-prefix ctor includes a collection param (because a collection precedes the required single slot), so the empty ctor is the only portable ctor; a node is built via the empty ctor + Attributes().Add / BaseType(...) / ArraySpecifiers().Add. ComposedType.cs declares NO hand-written ctors. ToString(CSharpFormattingOptions) and the Make* builders (MakePointerType/MakeArrayType/MakeRefType) are DEFERRED (output/resolver stage; the ported AstType base does not declare them, so there is nothing to override). The hand-written CheckInvariant override (asserts PointerRank >= 0 after the inherited base check) is PORTED -- the second ported scalar-invariant override (the ArraySpecifier.Dimensions >= 1 precedent); AstType::CheckInvariant (inherited from AstNode) is a no-op in NDEBUG and assert is a no-op in NDEBUG, so the whole override is a release no-op without an explicit #ifndef NDEBUG wrap. KEY DESIGN (the first two-collection-slot node, supportsIncremental false for both): the generator's supportsIncremental is true ONLY when the collection is the node's sole collection AND its last slot; with two collections it is false for both, so every mutation invalidates and the flattened indices are rebuilt lazily by EnsureChildIndices (the dynamic layout the D241 plan flagged -- the second collection's start depends on the first collection's count). This is the first ported node whose Add does NOT maintain ChildIndex incrementally, so a test that asserts an element's ChildIndex immediately after Add would see a stale value; the reindex is triggered by Slot()/NextSibling()/PrevSibling() (the methods that call EnsureChildIndices), after which each child's ChildIndex is its correct flattened index. KEY DESIGN (the first single slot that FOLLOWS a collection): the BaseType setter uses the index-less SetChildNode(ref field, value) (invalidates) because a collection precedes it -- the generator's constIndex = !slots.Take(slotIndex).Any(IsCollection) is false, unlike every prior single-slot node whose single slot had no collection before it (so it used the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, slotIndex)). The SetChild override still passes the known flattened index (the method argument) to the const-index SetChildNode, since the caller computed it by walking the slots. KEY DESIGN (the first DoMatch whose term order interleaves scalars between recursive terms): MembersToMatch is the source declaration order of non-excluded instance properties, so the scalars declared between the slots (HasRefSpecifier/HasReadOnlySpecifier before BaseType, HasNullableSpecifier/PointerRank before ArraySpecifiers) appear between their recursive terms -- the DoMatch is NOT pure slot order. KEY DESIGN (Slots.ArraySpecifier in Slots.hpp, Slots.AttributeSection in AttributeSection.hpp -- the cycle-breaking discriminator): a Slots kind whose element-type node header does NOT include Slots.hpp (the element type has no per-node slot statics) lives in Slots.hpp (Slots.Identifier/Type/Target/TypeArgument/Argument and now Slots.ArraySpecifier -- ArraySpecifier.hpp does not include Slots.hpp since it is a leaf with no [Slot] children); a Slots kind whose element-type node header DOES include Slots.hpp (the element type has per-node slot statics referencing Slots::X) is cycle-broken into its own header after the class (Slots.Attribute in Attribute.hpp, Slots.AttributeSection in AttributeSection.hpp -- both Attribute.hpp and AttributeSection.hpp include Slots.hpp for their per-node slot statics). Slots.hpp gained an ArraySpecifier.hpp include (ArraySpecifier.hpp does not include Slots.hpp, so no cycle). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitComposedType(ComposedType*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring ComposedType -- the D225 convention); DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching override defaulting to VisitChildren(node) plus the ComposedType.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding VisitComposedType does not affect them). TDD: 33 gtest cases in a new CSharp_ComposedType suite (cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/ComposedType_Test.cpp, wired into tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering is-a (AstType and AstNode not Expression), construction (the empty ctor -- no base type, no attributes, no array specifiers, scalars default, GetChildCount 1), the const keyword tokens, the four scalar round-trips, the BaseType setter (re-parents + detaches + clears on null -- the first single-slot-after-a-collection setter), the Attributes collection (empty, Add appends + parents + INVALIDATES -- the non-incremental path, GetCollectionByKind), the ArraySpecifiers collection (empty, Add appends + parents + invalidates, GetCollectionByKind), the dynamic flattened-index layout (sec at 0, baseType at attrCount, arr at attrCount+1 after a Slot()-triggered reindex), the three-slot collection-aware slot-storage (GetChildCount = 1 + attrCount + arrCount, GetChild dispatches collection -> single -> collection, GetChildSlotInfo dispatches + the kind identities, SetChild dispatches + throws), AcceptVisitor dispatch + virtuality through AstNode*/AstType* + the two-collection depth-first walk (Attributes' sections recursing into their attributes + the attribute Type, then BaseType, then ArraySpecifiers, in document order), DoMatch (same-all matches, different-BaseType rejects -- MatchRequired, different-ArraySpecifiers-count/value rejects, different-Attributes-count rejects, different-HasRefSpecifier/PointerRank reject -- the plain-equality terms, different-type rejects vs SimpleType, null-candidate rejects), Clone (deep-copies BaseType + both collections + four scalars + re-parents + detaches, virtual through AstNode*/AstType*), CheckInvariant (passes on the filled node with PointerRank >= 0), and the slot-static distinctness (three slots). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled ComposedType_Test.cpp + the recompiled IAstVisitor_Test.cpp/Identifier_Test.cpp/Expression_Test.cpp/PrimitiveExpression_Test.cpp/BinaryOperatorExpression_Test.cpp/AssignmentExpression_Test.cpp/UnaryOperatorExpression_Test.cpp/ConditionalExpression_Test.cpp/ParenthesizedExpression_Test.cpp/CheckedUncheckedExpression_Test.cpp/DirectionThrowExpression_Test.cpp/PrimitiveType_Test.cpp/SimpleType_Test.cpp/MemberType_Test.cpp/ArraySpecifier_Test.cpp/Attribute_Test.cpp/AttributeSection_Test.cpp (the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default) + relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe cleanly on the FIRST build (no crux -- the MemberType shape without the string-name [Slot], no name-shadowing since no member is named AstType/Identifier/Expression/AttributeSection/ArraySpecifier, no new AstNode helper -- MatchRequired already exists from D231 and the collection-DoMatch surface already exists from D237); the new headers are header-only (no CMake source listing -- the MemberType/Attribute header-only precedent). RESULT: 33 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_ComposedType.* run is 33/33 green; the filtered CSharp_* run is 769/769 green across 31 suites); the full suite is 1968 -> 2001 (127 test suites, was 126) with 0 regressions (the 1968 prior tests pass unchanged -- the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly (the engine/CLI use the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy -- confirmed by grep: ILAstToCSharp.cpp and ILSpyCmd/ include none of the C# AST Syntax node headers, including the new ComposedType.hpp and the changed Slots.hpp/AttributeSection.hpp), so the engine signature is byte-identical to D241 (no mscorlib.dll present in this environment to run the full 8026/500/306/59/999/1454/2543 baseline, but the include-graph isolation -- the D224-D241 precedent, re-confirmed by grep -- guarantees the CLI is unaffected; the ComposedType.hpp/Slots.hpp/AttributeSection.hpp/IAstVisitor.hpp/DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp changes are header-only so no ilspy.lib .cpp symbol the CLI links changed, and the only .cpp change is the new test file which is in the tests target not ilspy.lib). The next in-order Phase-5 pieces are the remaining AstType-bearing Expression nodes (CastExpression an Expression + an AstType, IdentifierExpression's TypeArguments AstNodeCollection<AstType> + its Identifier string-name [Slot], AsExpression/IsExpression, TypeOfExpression, TypeReferenceExpression, DefaultValueExpression/SizeOfExpression whose single slot is [Slot("Type")] AstType -- all reusing the now-ported Slots.Type kind), then the collection-slot Expression nodes (MemberReferenceExpression target + name, InvocationExpression target + arguments AstNodeCollection<Expression> -- reusing the now-ported Slots.Argument kind, IndexerExpression target + arguments), then the Statement/TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies, then the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage (CSharpOutputVisitor : IAstVisitor); the resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the AST. |
| D243 | CastExpression (the first AstType-bearing Expression node: a sealed Expression with a required AstType Type slot at flattened index 0 + a required Expression Expression slot at flattened index 1 -- the cast (type)expression, reusing the already-ported Slots.Type/Slots.Expression kinds) + IAstVisitor VisitCastExpression + DepthFirstAstVisitor VisitCastExpression (Phase 5: the first AstType-bearing Expression node, twenty-eighth piece) | port | Ports the CastExpression concrete node (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Expressions/CastExpression.hpp, mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Expressions/CastExpression.cs -- the generated CastExpression.g.cs; the hand-written partial declares ONLY the two slot properties, no ctors, no helpers) -- the twenty-eighth in-order Phase-5 piece per the D242 plan ("the remaining AstType-bearing Expression nodes: CastExpression an Expression + an AstType"). cast_expression ::= '(' type ')' expression (C# grammar 12.9.8): an Expression with two single, REQUIRED (non-nullable) [Slot] children -- a Type AstType (the target type) and an Expression (the operand being cast) -- and NO scalar enum. It is the FIRST ported AstType-bearing Expression node: the two-slot all-required shape of ConditionalExpression (D232) but with an AstType Type child instead of a third Expression child, and with the Expression accessor name-shadowing crux of UnaryOperatorExpression (D231). The generator emits two typed slot statics (TypeSlot pointing at the shared Slots::Type kind, ExpressionSlot pointing at the shared Slots::Expression kind -- both ALREADY ported, by Attribute D240 and UnaryOperatorExpression D231 respectively, so NO new Slots constant is added), the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, index) setters (no collection precedes either slot, so each flattened index is the constant slot position 0/1), the GetChildCount/GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo overrides over the two single slots (the WriteReturnDispatchSwitch shape, two cases), and the DoMatch 'return other is CastExpression o and this.Type.DoMatch(o.Type, match) and this.Expression.DoMatch(o.Expression, match)'. Both children are NON-NULLABLE recursive, so the generator emits the direct this.{member}.DoMatch(o.{member}, match) term for each (NOT MatchOptional, which the generator emits only for a nullable recursive child); there is no scalar enum, so there is no Any-wildcard term. Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): there is no scalar member, so Clone copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern) and deep-clones the two children through the setters (which re-parent and re-index via SetChildNode). No own location fields (StartLocation/EndLocation are the print-time base fields set by the unported output visitor), so they are not copied (the ConditionalExpression/SimpleType/MemberType/Attribute precedent for nodes without derived locations). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitCastExpression(this) (the class name does not end in 'AstType', so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitCastExpression). The generated slot statics are TypeSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots::Type, required) and ExpressionSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Expression> pointing at Slots::Expression, required). PORTED: (1) the Type slot -- a single REQUIRED (non-nullable) AstType child at flattened index 0, const-index SetChildNode(field, value, 0) (no collection precedes it); the Type() accessor does not collide with the AstType base type (no class named Type lives in the Syntax namespace -- the Attribute D240 lesson), so the operand type is the plain AstType (no elaborated specifier). (2) the Expression slot -- a single REQUIRED (non-nullable) Expression child at flattened index 1, const-index SetChildNode(field, value, 1); the Expression() accessor SHADOWS the Expression base type in this class scope (the D231 UnaryOperatorExpression crux), so every type usage AFTER the getter uses the elaborated-type-specifier class Expression (the setter parameter, the slot static's element type, the static_cast in SetChild/Clone, and the backing field); the ctor parameter and the getter return type precede the getter's declaration, so they use the plain Expression. (3) the per-node slot statics (TypeSlot pointing at Slots::Type required; ExpressionSlot pointing at Slots::Expression required, element type the elaborated class Expression). (4) the AcceptVisitor override (visitor.VisitCastExpression(this)). (5) the slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount is the constant 2; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo are a flat two-case index switch). (6) the generated DoMatch in MembersToMatch declaration order (Type, Expression): two non-nullable recursive terms, each dispatched via AstNode::MatchRequired (the D231 [class.access.derived] workaround -- a derived node may not call the protected DoMatch through a base AstType*/Expression*, but a static member of AstNode may via same-class access; MatchRequired guards a missing pattern-side child defensively and lets a null candidate child flow through the child's DoMatch(nullptr) which returns false). (7) the per-concrete-node Clone (CloneAnnotationsFrom + deep-clone Type via the setter -- AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override, which Type(AstType*) accepts directly + deep-clone Expression via the setter cast to class Expression* + ReparentTrivia; each child skipped if absent). (8) the ctors -- the empty ctor + the generated all-params (AstType, Expression) ctor (both slots required, so the required prefix IS the full set; no shorter prefix ctor and no params overload, since no collection slot is present); CastExpression.cs declares NO hand-written ctors. KEY DESIGN (the first AstType-bearing Expression node): the two-slot all-required shape is the ConditionalExpression shape with an AstType child -- confirming the const-index SetChildNode path and the flat-index-switch slot storage generalize from the all-Expression case to a mixed AstType+Expression case with no new machinery (MatchRequired already exists from D231 and accepts any AstNode*). The AstType child deep-clones through AstType::Clone() (the covariant override returning AstType*) which the Type(AstType*) setter accepts directly, the same shape Attribute's Type deep-clone uses (D240). KEY DESIGN (the class Expression elaborated-type-specifier crux, the D231 precedent): the C# property Expression of type Expression (a property named the same as its type -- legal in C#) ports as an accessor Expression() that shadows the Expression base type in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops -- the D224 Annotation<T>() crux); every type usage after the getter uses the elaborated specifier class Expression (basic.lookup.elab ignores non-type names and finds the hidden class). This is the recurring crux for every node with an Expression-typed Expression slot (UnaryOperatorExpression D231, ParenthesizedExpression D233, CheckedExpression/UncheckedExpression D234, DirectionExpression/ThrowExpression D235, and now CastExpression); the discriminator is whether a member is NAMED Expression (the accessor), not whether the element type is Expression. KEY DESIGN (NO new Slots constant): both slot kinds are already ported (Slots::Type by Attribute D240, Slots::Expression by UnaryOperatorExpression D231), so Slots.hpp is unchanged -- CastExpression is the first AstType-bearing Expression node to reuse two existing Slots kinds without adding any, confirming the D240 'Slots::Type unblocks many nodes at once' note came due. IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitCastExpression(CastExpression*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring CastExpression -- the D225 convention); DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching override defaulting to VisitChildren(node) plus the CastExpression.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding VisitCastExpression does not affect them). TDD: 31 gtest cases in a new CSharp_CastExpression suite (cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Expressions/CastExpression_Test.cpp, wired into tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering is-a (AstNode and Expression, NOT AstType -- it derives from Expression not AstType), construction (the empty ctor -- both slots null, GetChildCount 2; the all-params ctor -- both children set + parented at indices 0/1), the Type setter (re-parents + detaches + clears on null), the Expression setter (re-parents + detaches + clears on null), GetChildCount is 2, GetChild returns slots + throws out of range, SetChild routes to slots + throws, GetChildSlotInfo returns slot statics + throws, the slot kinds point at Slots::Type/Slots::Expression, the slot-static element-type cross-check (TypeSlot accepts a PrimitiveType not a NullReferenceExpression; ExpressionSlot accepts a NullReferenceExpression not a PrimitiveType -- the two slots' element types are distinct and faithful), AcceptVisitor dispatch + virtuality through AstNode*/Expression*, the depth-first walk (cast, then the PrimitiveType Type, then the Expression operand, in document order; an empty node records just the cast), DoMatch (same children match, different-Type rejects -- the first term, different-Expression rejects -- the second term, null-pattern-Type rejects, null-candidate-Type rejects, all-children-null rejects, delegates-to-child-DoMatch -- an int Type vs a long Type rejects via the PrimitiveType child's MatchString on Keyword, non-Cast candidate rejects, null candidate rejects), Clone (deep-clones both children + re-parents + the cloned Type keeps its keyword, empty-node null slots, virtual through AstNode*/covariant through Expression*, does-not-detach-source), and CheckInvariant on the FILLED node only (both slots required, so an empty node violates the invariant). They are structurally identical to CastExpression (D243) -- the two-slot all-required shape -- but with the slot order REVERSED: the C# source declares Expression BEFORE Type (CastExpression declares Type first), so Expression is at flattened index 0 and Type at flattened index 1 (the reverse of CastExpression's Type-0/Expression-1). TypeReferenceExpression has no C# spec grammar production (an ILSpy wrapper that lets an AstType appear in expression position, e.g. the int in int.Parse(...)); type_of_expression ::= 'typeof' '(' type ')' (12.8.18); default_value_expression ::= 'default' ( '(' type ')' )? All four share the EXACT same shape: an Expression with a single, REQUIRED (non-nullable) [Slot] child -- a Type AstType -- and NO scalar; TypeReferenceExpression has no const string, the other three each carry a public const string (TypeofKeyword/DefaultKeyword/SizeofKeyword). They are the simplest ported AstType-bearing Expression nodes (one required single slot, no scalar, no name shadowing), simpler than CastExpression/AsExpression/IsExpression (two slots) and simpler than UnaryOperatorExpression (one slot + a scalar enum). The generator emits one typed slot static (TypeSlot pointing at the shared Slots::Type kind -- already ported by Attribute D240, so NO new Slots constant is added), the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, 0) setter (the single slot is the first and only slot, no collection precedes it, so the flattened index is the constant 0), the GetChildCount/GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo overrides over the one single slot (the WriteReturnDispatchSwitch shape, single case), and the DoMatch 'return other is <Node> o && this.Type.DoMatch(o.Type, match)'. The child is NON-NULLABLE recursive, so the generator emits the direct this.Type.DoMatch(o.Type, match) term (NOT MatchOptional, which the generator emits only for a nullable recursive child); there is no scalar enum, so there is no Any-wildcard term. Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): there is no scalar instance member (the keyword const string is a static literal, not instance state), so Clone copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern) and deep-clones the child through the setter (which re-parents and re-indexes via SetChildNode). The print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not stored on these nodes (no own location fields -- the base fields hold the print-time span), so only the child + annotation channel are copied. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.Visit<TypeName>(this) (the class names do not end in 'AstType', so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitTypeReferenceExpression/VisitTypeOfExpression/VisitDefaultValueExpression/VisitSizeOfExpression; the EndsWith('AstType') rewriting to '...Type' applies only to FunctionPointerAstType/InvocationAstType/TupleAstType). The generated slot static is TypeSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots::Type, required) for each. PORTED per node: (1) the Type slot -- a single REQUIRED (non-nullable) AstType child at flattened index 0, const-index SetChildNode(field, value, 0) (no collection precedes it). (2) the per-node slot static (TypeSlot pointing at Slots::Type required, element type the plain AstType). (3) the AcceptVisitor override. (4) the slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount is the constant 1; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo are a flat single-case index switch). (5) the generated DoMatch: one non-nullable recursive term, dispatched via AstNode::MatchRequired (the D231 [class.access.derived] workaround -- a derived node may not call the protected DoMatch through a base AstType*; a static member of AstNode may via same-class access; MatchRequired guards a missing pattern-side child defensively and lets a null candidate child flow through the child's DoMatch(nullptr) which returns false). (6) the per-concrete-node Clone (CloneAnnotationsFrom + deep-clone Type via the setter -- AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override, which Type(AstType*) accepts directly + ReparentTrivia; the child skipped if absent). (7) the ctors -- the empty ctor + the generated all-params (AstType) ctor (the one slot is required, so the required prefix IS the full set; no shorter prefix ctor and no params overload, since no collection slot is present; the ctor is explicit since it takes one argument); all four .cs files declare NO hand-written ctors. (8) the keyword const string for the three keyword nodes (TypeofKeyword/DefaultKeyword/SizeofKeyword = "typeof"/"default"/"sizeof", a static constexpr const char* -- the CheckedExpression D234 precedent, a compile-time literal, not instance state, so NOT part of MembersToMatch/DoMatch). This is the cleanest slot-bearing AstType-bearing Expression port so far: unlike CastExpression/AsExpression/IsExpression (whose Expression() accessor shadows the Expression base type and forces the class Expression elaborated specifier), the Type() accessor shadows nothing, so all four nodes compiled on the FIRST build with no crux -- no name shadowing, no new Slots constant, no new AstNode helper (MatchRequired already exists from D231), no new enum. KEY DESIGN (NO new Slots constant): the single slot kind is already ported (Slots::Type by Attribute D240), so Slots.hpp is unchanged -- all four nodes reuse the existing Slots::Type kind, confirming the D240 'Slots::Type unblocks many nodes at once' note came due for the fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh times (CastExpression D243, AsExpression/IsExpression D244, and now these four). TypeReferenceExpression carries no const keyword (its C# source declares none). KEY DESIGN (the natural quartet): the four nodes share the EXACT same one-required-single-slot shape, so they form a natural quartet (the D234 natural-pair framing extended from two to four); the four suites are kept in one shared test file (the D234 multi-suite pattern) with a single RecordingVisitor and a single DoMatchAgainst helper, and each suite is independently --gtest_filter-selectable. IAstVisitor.hpp gains the four Visit pure-virtuals (forward-declaring all four -- the D225 convention); DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching overrides defaulting to VisitChildren(node) plus the four concrete includes for the upcasts (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding the four Visits does not affect them). (C# grammar 12.8.4): an Expression consisting of an Identifier name plus zero or more TypeArguments (AstType children). It is STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to SimpleType (D237) -- the first ported node with a collection slot (TypeArguments: AstNodeCollection<AstType>) and a string-name [Slot] (the Identifier, over a backing IdentifierToken) -- but with two divergences: (1) it derives from Expression (parallel to AstType, not under it), so it is the first AstType-bearing EXPRESSION node with a collection (the CastExpression D243 / TypeReferenceExpression D245 single-AstType-slot Expression nodes have no collection); and (2) the Identifier is a NON-nullable string (the C# source declares 'public partial string Identifier', not 'string?'), so the backing token is a REQUIRED (non-nullable) slot (unlike SimpleType.IdentifierToken which is optional), the string getter DEREFS the token (returning std::string, not std::optional<std::string> -- a null token is a half-constructed node that would NullReferenceException in C#), and the string setter uses Identifier.Create (NOT CreateIfNotEmpty -- a non-nullable name creates a token even for an empty string, so an empty name yields a token with an empty Name, not a null token -- the MemberType.MemberName D238 precedent). The generator emits one typed slot static for the token (IdentifierTokenSlot, a CSharpSlotInfo<Identifier> pointing at Slots.Identifier, required) and one for the collection (TypeArgumentsSlot, a CSharpSlotInfo<AstType> pointing at Slots.TypeArgument, collection), the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, 0) token setter (no collection precedes it), the collection-aware slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount is 1 + Count; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo walk the token slot then the collection -- the generator's WriteReturnDispatchWithCollections/WriteSetChildWithCollections shape, the SimpleType precedent), and the DoMatch 'return other is IdentifierExpression o && MatchString(this.Identifier, o.Identifier) && this.TypeArguments.DoMatch(o.TypeArguments, match)' (the Identifier term is a String MatchString with the $any$ wildcard; the TypeArguments term is a recursive collection match -- the generator emits the AstNodeCollection-typed recursive term directly, NOT MatchOptional, which the generator emits only for a nullable non-collection child). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): a fresh node, the annotation channel copied (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), the IdentifierToken deep-cloned through the setter (which re-parents; the cloned token carries its own Name and StartLocation), and every TypeArguments element deep-cloned through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes). No scalar to copy (the Identifier string is derived from the token). The print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not stored on this node (no own location fields -- the base fields hold the print-time span), so they are not copied (the ConditionalExpression/SimpleType precedent). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output rather than regenerated. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitIdentifierExpression(this) (the class name does not end in 'AstType', so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitIdentifierExpression). The generated slot statics are IdentifierTokenSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Identifier> pointing at Slots::Identifier, required -- the name is non-nullable so the token is a required slot) and TypeArgumentsSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots::TypeArgument, collection). PORTED: (1) the IdentifierToken slot -- a single NON-nullable (required) Identifier child at flattened index 0, const-index SetChildNode(field, value, 0) (no collection precedes it). (2) the Identifier string-name accessor (over the token) -- a NON-optional name (the C# string, not string?): get returns IdentifierToken.Name (derefs the token -- a null token is a half-constructed node, NRE in C#); set creates the token via Identifier.Create(value) (NOT CreateIfNotEmpty -- a non-nullable name creates a token even for an empty string). Identifier() returns std::string (a copy of the token's name); the Identifier::Create factory call is fully-qualified (::ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax::Identifier::Create). (3) the TypeArguments collection slot -- AstNodeCollectionT<AstType> at flattened index 1, baseIndex=1, supportsIncremental=true (the node's only collection and last slot); an always-present stack member (the D222 design). (4) the per-node slot statics (IdentifierTokenSlot pointing at Slots::Identifier required, element type the elaborated class Identifier; TypeArgumentsSlot pointing at Slots::TypeArgument collection, element type the plain AstType). (5) the AcceptVisitor override (visitor.VisitIdentifierExpression(this)). (6) the slot-storage overrides (GetChildCount is 1 + Count; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo walk the token slot then the collection; GetCollectionByKind returns the TypeArguments collection for the TypeArgument kind). (7) the generated DoMatch (a MatchString on Identifier + a collection DoMatch on TypeArguments); the Identifier() calls are inlined in the MatchString arguments (not pre-computed in locals) to preserve the C# && short-circuit (o->Identifier() derefs the candidate's token only when the type check passed -- the MemberName D238 precedent; a nameless candidate is UB/NRE in both languages, so the tests never pass one). (8) the ctors -- the empty ctor + the generated (string) required-prefix ctor (Identifier is the only required ctor param; the body calls the string setter, which creates the token via Identifier.Create) + the hand-written (string, TextLocation) ctor (creates the token via the fully-qualified factory and sets it through SetChildByKindUntyped); the collection ctors ((string, IEnumerable<AstType>) and the params AstType[] overload) are DEFERRED (they use AddRange, the D222 collection-convenience-mutator deferral). KEY DESIGN (the SimpleType structural shape + the Expression base): IdentifierExpression is the first node to combine the SimpleType collection-slot shape (token at 0 + TypeArguments at 1) with the Expression base -- confirming the collection-aware slot-storage dispatch, the const-index SetChildNode token setter, and the MatchString + collection-DoMatch generalize from the AstType hierarchy (SimpleType) to the Expression hierarchy with no new machinery. The covariant Clone returns IdentifierExpression* (through Expression*, the Expression::Clone pure-virtual); the TypeArguments elements deep-clone through AstType::Clone() (returns AstType*, the covariant override) which the collection's Add(AstType*) accepts directly. KEY DESIGN (the non-nullable Identifier string, the MemberType D238 precedent): the C# 'string' (not 'string?') makes the backing token a REQUIRED slot (IsOptional=false), the getter derefs (returns std::string, not std::optional<std::string>), and the setter uses Identifier.Create (not CreateIfNotEmpty), so an empty name yields a token with an empty Name (not a null token). CheckInvariant therefore passes only on a FILLED node (the token is a required slot, so an empty node violates the required-slot invariant -- the assert fires in debug), unlike SimpleType whose optional token passes CheckInvariant on a nameless node. A nameless IdentifierExpression is a half-constructed node (UB to deref the Identifier getter or pass to DoMatch), so the tests exercise the empty-name case as a token-with-an-empty-Name (a real '' match), not a nameless case. KEY DESIGN (the class Identifier elaborated-type-specifier name-shadowing crux, the D237 SimpleType precedent): the string accessor Identifier() (a member function) shadows the Identifier CLASS in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops, even though it is not a type -- the D224 Annotation<T>() crux), so the token type is the elaborated-type-specifier class Identifier (basic.lookup.elab ignores non-type names) in every type position AFTER the accessor (the backing field, the slot static's element type, the SetChild static_cast, the token accessor's signature, and the ctor parameter), and the Identifier::Create factory calls in the setter and the hand-written ctor are fully-qualified (::ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax::Identifier::...) -- the C# generator's global:: qualification for the same shadowing case; the hand-written IdentifierExpression.cs ctor likewise fully-qualifies as Decompiler.CSharp.Syntax.Identifier.Create. KEY DESIGN (NO new Slots constant): both slot kinds are already ported (Slots::Identifier by SimpleType D237, Slots::TypeArgument by SimpleType D237), so Slots.hpp is unchanged -- IdentifierExpression is the first collection-slot Expression node to reuse two existing Slots kinds without adding any. The hand-written Add(Statement)/Add(Expression) convenience overloads (the C# forwards to AddChild(statement, Slots.Statement) / wraps the expression in a new ExpressionStatement(expression)) are DEFERRED: thin wrappers consumed by the unported output-visitor/resolver stage (the D235 hand-written-helper deferral), and the Statements().Add(...) collection API is the equivalent for building a block. The IEnumerable<Statement> enumeration (the C# explicit interface forwarding to Statements.GetEnumerator()) is DEFERRED (the D222 lazy-sequence-surface deferral; the ported Statements() collection exposes begin()/end() range-for and Count/At/operator[] instead). KEY DESIGN (the cross-hierarchy structural-twin DoMatch rejection): a BlockStatement pattern does not match an ArrayInitializerExpression candidate and vice versa -- the two are both collection-only nodes (a single Expression/Statement collection) but in DISJOINT hierarchies (Statement vs Expression), so the other is BlockStatement type-check gate rejects (the D237 disjoint-hierarchy discriminator applied to two collection-only nodes). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitBlockStatement(BlockStatement*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring BlockStatement -- the D225 convention) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the BlockStatement.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding VisitBlockStatement does not affect them). TDD: 29 gtest cases in a new CSharp_BlockStatement suite (cpp/tests/.../Statements/BlockStatement_Test.cpp, wired into cpp/tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering is-a (Statement and AstNode, NOT Expression -- the disjoint-hierarchy check), is-concrete-and-not-final, construction (the empty ctor -- no statements, GetChildCount 0), the Statements collection (empty by default; Add appends + parents + incremental flattened index; GetCollectionByKind returns Statements for the Statement kind), the collection-only slot-storage (GetChild/GetChildSlotInfo/SetChild dispatch the statements at 0..Count; an empty node throws for any index; the slot kind points at Slots::Statement), AcceptVisitor dispatch + virtuality through AstNode*/Statement*, the depth-first walk (block then its statements in document order, recursing into a ReturnStatement's operand; the empty block records just self), DoMatch (same-statements match, two-empties match, different-count reject, different-value reject via the leaf-statement type-only DoMatch, cross-hierarchy ArrayInitializerExpression rejection, cross-type ReturnStatement rejection, null-candidate rejection), Clone (deep-copy statements + re-parent + detach; deep-copy nested statements incl. a ReturnStatement operand; virtual through AstNode*; covariant through Statement*; empty clone), CheckInvariant (passes on the filled node AND on the empty node -- the collection-only shape where the empty node is invariant-valid), and the StatementsSlot identity (points at Slots::Statement, IsCollection). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled BlockStatement_Test.cpp + the recompiled prior 30 C# AST test files (the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new defaults) + relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe cleanly on the FIRST build (no crux -- the collection-only ArrayInitializerExpression D250 shape applied to the Statement hierarchy: no new machinery since the collection-aware slot-storage dispatch, the collection-only GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo walk, the single collection-recursive DoMatch, and the per-concrete-node Clone all already exist from ArrayInitializerExpression; no name shadowing since no member is named Statement; the new Slots::Statement kind lives in Slots.hpp with no cycle since Statement.hpp does not include Slots.hpp); the new header is header-only (no CMake source listing -- the collection-only-node header-only precedent). RESULT: 29 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_BlockStatement.* run is 29/29 green); the full suite is 2609 -> 2638 (147 test suites, was 146) with 0 regressions (the 2609 prior tests pass unchanged -- the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly (the engine/CLI use the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy -- confirmed by grep: ILAstToCSharp.cpp and ILSpyCmd/*.cpp reference none of the new BlockStatement.hpp header, and AstNode.cpp -- the only ilspy.lib .cpp touching CSharp/Syntax/ -- includes only AstNode.hpp/AstNodeCollection.hpp/CSharpSlotInfo.hpp/Trivia.hpp, none of which include the new BlockStatement header since AstNode.hpp only forward-declares IAstVisitor, so the engine signature is byte-identical to D255; no mscorlib.dll present in this environment to run the full 8026/500/306/59/999/1454/2543 baseline, but the include-graph isolation -- the D224-D255 precedent, re-confirmed by grep -- guarantees the CLI is unaffected). The next-in-order Phase-5 pieces are the remaining collection-bearing statements (IfElseStatement/WhileStatement/DoWhileStatement with a Condition + an embedded statement, YieldReturnStatement with a nullable Expression, the EmptyStatement/GotoStatement/LabelStatement leaves, then VariableDeclarationStatement/ForStatement/ForeachStatement/FixedStatement/UsingStatement/LockStatement/UnsafeStatement/CheckedStatement/UncheckedStatement/SwitchStatement/TryCatchStatement/LocalFunctionDeclarationStatement), then the TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies, then the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage (CSharpOutputVisitor : IAstVisitor); the resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the AST. |

LabelStatement applies the MemberType.MemberName D238 / GotoStatement D257 differently-named-property precedent: the [Slot('Identifier')] argument names the slot KIND 'Identifier' but the PROPERTY is 'Label', so the string accessor is Label() (NOT Identifier()) and the backing token accessor is LabelToken() (NOT IdentifierToken()); neither shadows the Identifier CLASS in this class scope (no member is named Identifier), so no elaborated class Identifier is needed anywhere and the Identifier::Create factory call is unqualified. KEY DESIGN (EmptyStatement reuses the inherited startLocation_, the Identifier D227 precedent): the C# declares its OWN Location field and overrides StartLocation to return it; the port stores Location in the INHERITED startLocation_ field via StorePrintStart, so the base StartLocation() returns it WITHOUT an override (the C# override is purely because it has its own field, the semantics are identical -- the Identifier D227 precedent applied to a statement leaf). The EndLocation override returns TextLocation(StartLocation().Line, StartLocation().Column + 1) (one column past the ';'). This avoids a redundant shadowing location_ field. KEY DESIGN (EmptyStatement derives EndLocation so its Clone copies StartLocation, the Identifier/PrimitiveType D236 precedent): a node that derives EndLocation copies StartLocation so the derived end is correct; EmptyStatement is the first ported statement leaf whose Clone copies StartLocation (StorePrintStart(StartLocation()) + CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia), unlike the BreakStatement D254 / GotoStatement D257 leaf precedents whose Clones copy no locations (they do not derive EndLocation). CheckInvariant therefore passes only on a FILLED node (the token is required), unlike GotoStatement whose optional token passes CheckInvariant on a nameless node. A nameless LabelStatement is a half-constructed node (UB to deref or pass to DoMatch), so the tests exercise the empty-name case as a real '' match (two empty names match; empty does not match non-empty), not a nameless/nullopt case. The DoMatch wraps the non-nullable std::string in std::optional<std::string_view> always engaged (a real name, never nullopt -- the MemberType D238 precedent); the std::string temporaries live until the end of the full return expression keeping the std::string_view views valid for the MatchString call. This is the cleanest slot-bearing-statement-with-a-concrete-child port so far: no name shadowing, no new enum, no new AstNode helper (MatchRequired from D231), the only recurring work being the mechanical const-index SetChildNode + flat-index-switch slot storage + per-concrete-node Clone. KEY DESIGN (the NEW Slots::Body kind, cycle-broken into BlockStatement.hpp): the [Slot("Body")] argument names a NEW slot kind "Body" not yet ported, a CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement> (the element type is the concrete BlockStatement node). BlockStatement.hpp INCLUDES Slots.hpp (its StatementsSlot references &Slots::Statement), so the kind CANNOT live in Slots.hpp: CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement> needs BlockStatement complete (the dynamic_cast<const BlockStatement*> is-a test in the ctor), and placing it in Slots.hpp would require Slots.hpp to include BlockStatement.hpp, forming a circular include (Slots.hpp would include BlockStatement.hpp for the complete BlockStatement, but BlockStatement.hpp includes Slots.hpp for Slots::Statement, and with Slots.hpp's guard set those definitions would not be visible where BlockStatement.hpp's class body needs them). The resolution is the Slots::Attribute D241 / Slots::AttributeSection D242 cycle-breaking precedent: define Slots::Body in BlockStatement.hpp AFTER the BlockStatement class (where both CSharpSlotInfoT -- visible via the Slots.hpp include -- and BlockStatement are complete), in a namespace Slots { inline const CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement> Body{...}; } block; the C++17 inline variable still has external linkage and one address across translation units, preserving the pointer-identity comparison node.Slot.Kind == &Slots::Body the slot system relies on. CheckedStatement adds the kind (the cycle-broken definition); UncheckedStatement and UnsafeStatement REUSE the already-cycle-broken Slots::Body kind (no new Slots constant, no cycle to break again -- the D230 Slots-kind-reuse precedent). KEY DESIGN (the generated ctors): each node gets the empty ctor (Body defaults to null, a required slot so a default-constructed node is only valid until Body is set -- the UnaryOperatorExpression D231 required-slot behaviour, CheckInvariant asserts 'required slot must not be empty' on an empty node) plus the explicit (BlockStatement) all-params ctor (reqLen 1 == count, the ExpressionStatement D255 single-required-slot precedent; explicit because a single-argument ctor is a converting ctor by default -- the D237/D248/D255 precedent); the (BlockStatement) ctor body calls the Body setter which re-parents and re-indexes via SetChildNode. KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone, no location copy): each Clone makes a fresh node, copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), and deep-clones the Body child through the Body setter (which re-parents and re-indexes); BlockStatement::Clone() returns BlockStatement* (the covariant override), which the Body(BlockStatement*) setter accepts directly; no own location fields (none of the three derives EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the BreakStatement D254 no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is <NodeName>* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). LockStatement ...'). lock_statement ::= 'lock' '(' expression ')' statement (C# grammar 13.13): a Statement with two single, REQUIRED (non-nullable) [Slot] children -- an Expression (the lock object) at flattened index 0 and an EmbeddedStatement Statement (the lock body) at index 1 -- and NO scalar enum. It is the WhileStatement D258 two-required-single-slot shape (the Condition+EmbeddedStatement loop shape) with the loop test slot renamed Expression: the simplest remaining statement, and the cleanest re-port of an already-established shape (a positional/type rename, not a structural change). The generator emits two typed slot statics (ExpressionSlot pointing at the shared Slots::Expression kind and EmbeddedStatementSlot pointing at the shared Slots::EmbeddedStatement kind), the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, index) setters (no collection precedes either slot, so each flattened index is the constant slot position 0/1), the GetChildCount/GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo overrides over the two single slots, and the DoMatch return other is LockStatement o and this.Expression.DoMatch(o.Expression, match) and this.EmbeddedStatement.DoMatch(o.EmbeddedStatement, match). Both children are NON-NULLABLE recursive, so the generator emits the direct this.{member}.DoMatch(o.{member}, match) term for each (the MatchRequired same-class static in the port); there is no scalar enum, so there is no Any-wildcard term. Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): deep-clones the two children through the setters (which re-parent) and copies the annotation channel. The LockKeyword const string ports as a static constexpr const char* (a static field, not instance state), so the generator's MembersToMatch (which iterates only instance IPropertySymbols) excludes it from the DoMatch (the BreakStatement.BreakKeyword D254 / IfElseStatement D258 precedent applied to the lock statement). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete nodes are hand-translated from the generated output. KEY DESIGN (the C++ name-shadowing crux on the Expression slot, the UnaryOperatorExpression D231 / ExpressionStatement D255 precedent): the C# property is Expression of type Expression (a property named the same as its type). The faithful port names the accessor Expression(), which SHADOWS the Expression class in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops, even though it is not a type). Every type usage AFTER the Expression() getter is declared therefore uses the elaborated-type-specifier class Expression: the setter parameter, the ExpressionSlot element type (a CSharpSlotInfoT template argument), the SetChild static_cast at index 0, the Clone static_cast for the Expression deep-clone, and the backing field; the ctor parameter and the getter return type precede the getter so they use the plain Expression. The EmbeddedStatement() accessor does NOT shadow the Statement base type (a member named EmbeddedStatement is not the name Statement), so the plain Statement is used throughout the EmbeddedStatement slot -- the WhileStatement D258 no-shadowing-on-EmbeddedStatement precedent applied to LockStatement. This is the discriminator (a member shadows a class in the same namespace only when the member's name IS that class's name), and it is the only recurring crux on this node (the rest is the mechanical WhileStatement two-required-slot machinery). KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant): LockStatement reuses two already-ported Slots kinds -- Slots::Expression (ported by UnaryOperatorExpression D231 as the single-Expression operand position) for the lock-object Expression slot, and Slots::EmbeddedStatement (ported by WhileStatement D258 as the loop-body Statement position) for the EmbeddedStatement slot; Slots.hpp is unchanged. The per-node ExpressionSlot points at &Slots::Expression (with the elaborated class Expression element type for the shadowing crux), and the per-node EmbeddedStatementSlot points at &Slots::EmbeddedStatement (with the plain Statement element type, no shadowing). This confirms the Slots kind-collapsing design (one kind per [Slot] name, shared across single and collection positions across disjoint hierarchies): LockStatement's Expression slot is the same kind as UnaryOperatorExpression's operand, and its EmbeddedStatement slot is the same kind as WhileStatement's body. KEY DESIGN (the generated ctors): the empty ctor (both slots default to null; null slots violate the required-slot invariant, so a default-constructed node is only valid until the slots are set -- the WhileStatement D258 required-slot behavior) plus the (Expression*, Statement*) all-params ctor. RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 2 (both required) and there is no collection, so the single full ctor IS the required-prefix ctor (no shorter prefix ctor and no params overload); the ctor parameter types precede the Expression() accessor declaration so they use the plain Expression/Statement, and the body resolves the Expression(expression) call to the setter declared below. KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone, no location copy): the Clone makes a fresh node, copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), and deep-clones the two children through the setters (which re-parent and re-index via SetChildNode); each child is skipped if absent (Clone tolerates a missing child even though the slots are required -- the invariant is enforced by CheckInvariant, not by Clone). Expression::Clone() returns Expression* and Statement::Clone() returns Statement* (the covariant overrides), which the setters accept directly; the Expression setter takes the elaborated class Expression* (the shadowing crux), so the deep-clone cast uses the elaborated specifier, and the EmbeddedStatement setter takes the plain Statement* (no shadowing). No own location fields (LockStatement does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the WhileStatement D258 / BreakStatement D254 no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is LockStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitLockStatement(LockStatement*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring the concrete type -- the D225 convention; pointer params need only a forward declaration, so no include; the forward declaration precedes the IAstVisitor class body per the D260 forward-declaration-must-precede-pure-virtual crux) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the LockStatement.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage; the existing test stub concrete nodes' no-op AcceptVisitor do not call any Visit method, so adding the new Visit does not affect them). TDD: 32 gtest cases in a single CSharp_LockStatement suite (cpp/tests/.../Statements/LockStatement_Test.cpp, wired into cpp/tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering is-a (Statement and AstNode, NOT Expression -- the disjoint-hierarchy check), the LockKeyword const, construction (the empty + the (Expression, Statement) all-params ctor + the ctor-transfers-ownership-Parent/ChildIndex), the Expression/EmbeddedStatement slot accessors/setters (re-parent and re-index; the null-Expression-clears-slot), the slot-storage contract (GetChildCount 2; GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo flat switch; out-of-range throw), the shared-Slots-kind identity (ExpressionSlot -> Slots::Expression, EmbeddedStatementSlot -> Slots::EmbeddedStatement), the IsInstanceOfType is-a cross-check (ExpressionSlot accepts an Expression not a Statement; EmbeddedStatementSlot accepts a Statement not an Expression), AcceptVisitor dispatch + virtuality through AstNode*/Statement*, the depth-first walk (lock then Expression then EmbeddedStatement in source order; the empty node records just self), DoMatch (same-values match, different-Expression/different-EmbeddedStatement reject, null-Expression reject, cross-structural-twin WhileStatement rejection BOTH directions -- LockStatement and WhileStatement share the exact two-required-single-slot shape but are distinct concrete types, so the other-is-LockStatement / other-is-WhileStatement type-check gates reject, generalizing the D234 cross-sibling rejection to a structural twin, cross-type NullReferenceExpression rejection, null-candidate rejection), Clone (deep-copy children distinct from source + re-parent + re-index + ChildIndex; the empty clone has no children; virtual through AstNode*; covariant through Statement*; does not detach source), CheckInvariant on the filled node (both slots required), and the slot-static distinctness + the shared-EmbeddedStatement-kind-across-Lock-and-While identity + the shared-Expression-kind-with-Slots::Expression identity. It is the first ported node with a collection -> single -> collection -> single slot layout. The generator's supportsIncremental flag is collectionCount == 1 && slotIndex == slots.Count - 1; here collectionCount == 2, so it is FALSE for BOTH collections: every Add/Insert/Remove/single-slot-set INVALIDATES the parent's indices for a lazy rebuild (EnsureChildIndices), and IndexOf falls back to a linear identity search. The Condition single slot FOLLOWS a collection (Initializers), so the generator's constIndex = !slots.Take(1).Any(IsCollection) is false, and the Condition setter uses the index-less SetChildNode(ref field, value) (which invalidates on a set/clear, since the flattened index is dynamic -- the Initializers count can change). The EmbeddedStatement single slot FOLLOWS TWO collections (Initializers + Iterators) plus a single (Condition), so constIndex is likewise false, and the EmbeddedStatement setter uses the index-less SetChildNode(ref field, value). The SetChild override still passes the known flattened index to the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, index) for each single slot. The flattened layout is Initializers [0, initCount), Condition at initCount, Iterators [initCount+1, initCount+1+iterCount), EmbeddedStatement at initCount+1+iterCount; GetChildCount is 2 + initCount + iterCount (the two single slots always occupy a flattened index each, even when the Condition is null and the collections are empty). It is the first ported node to combine TWO collection-DoMatch terms with a MatchOptional and a MatchRequired interleaved across one DoMatch. KEY DESIGN (NO C++ name-shadowing crux): the Initializers/Condition/Iterators/EmbeddedStatement accessors are member functions, but NO class named any of them lives in the Syntax namespace, and NO member is named Expression/Statement/AstType, so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed anywhere and the plain Statement/Expression resolve to the classes in every type position (the ComposedType/ArrayCreateExpression differently-named-property precedent). KEY DESIGN (two NEW Slots kinds, two reused): the [Slot('ForInitializer')] and [Slot('Iterator')] arguments name two NEW slot kinds not yet ported, both CSharpSlotInfoT<Statement> (the element type is the Statement abstract base, complete via the Statements/Statement.hpp include; Statement.hpp does NOT include Slots.hpp so both kinds live in Slots.hpp with no include cycle -- the Slots.Statement/Slots.EmbeddedStatement precedent). Both are defined AFTER the Slots::Statement variable, so the element type is qualified (::ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax::Statement) to avoid resolving to that variable (the Expression/Condition/AdditionalArraySpecifier collision precedent: an unqualified name shared with a prior Slots variable resolves to the variable, not the class). The [Slot('Condition')] and [Slot('EmbeddedStatement')] single slots REUSE the already-ported Slots::Condition (by ConditionalExpression D232) and Slots::EmbeddedStatement (by WhileStatement D258) kinds with no new Slots constant; the per-node ConditionSlot carries IsOptional=true (the Condition is nullable) while the shared Slots::Condition kind is constructed non-optional (the per-position optionality lives on the per-node slot -- the IfElseStatement.FalseStatement D258 precedent applied across two nodes sharing one kind with different optionality, confirming the Slots kind-collapsing design is by [Slot] name regardless of per-position optionality). KEY DESIGN (the generated ctors, only the empty): ForStatement.cs declares NO hand-written ctors (only the ForKeyword const and the four slot properties), so the port carries only the generated ctors. The generated collection ctors use AddRange, which lands with the collection convenience mutators (the D222 deferral), so they are DEFERRED; the RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 0 (the first slot is a collection, not required, so the required prefix stops before it), so the empty ctor is the only portable ctor. An initializer list is built via Initializers().Add(...), a condition via Condition(...), iterators via Iterators().Add(...), and a body via EmbeddedStatement(...) until AddRange lands. KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone, no location copy): the Clone makes a fresh node, copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), deep-clones every Initializers/Iterators element through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; Statement::Clone() returns Statement*, which the typed Adds accept directly), the Condition deep-cloned through the setter when present, and the EmbeddedStatement deep-cloned through the setter when present. The deep-copy order follows the slot declaration order (Initializers, Condition, Iterators, EmbeddedStatement) matching the generated CloneChildrenInto; with both collections non-incremental every mutation invalidates, so the order does not affect the final rebuilt state. No own location fields (ForStatement does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the WhileStatement/ComposedType no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is ForStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitForStatement(ForStatement*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring the concrete type -- the D225 convention; the forward declaration precedes the IAstVisitor class body per the D260 forward-declaration-must-precede-pure-virtual crux, handled proactively) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the ForStatement.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage). 'foreach' '(' type variable_designation 'in' expression ')' statement (C# grammar 13.9.5.1): a Statement with four [Slot] children in source declaration order -- a REQUIRED (non-nullable) AstType VariableType (the element type, e.g. int in foreach (int x in c)), a REQUIRED (non-nullable) VariableDesignation VariableDesignation (the loop variable or deconstruction, e.g. x or (x, y) -- the VariableDesignation hierarchy just ported in D264), a REQUIRED (non-nullable) Expression InExpression (the collection, the expression after in), and a REQUIRED (non-nullable) Statement EmbeddedStatement (the loop body) -- plus an IsAsync bool scalar (the leading await) and NO scalar enum. It is the first ported STATEMENT with FOUR required single [Slot] children (the ConditionalExpression D232 three-required-slot Expression shape plus one more, spanning three disjoint child hierarchies AstType/VariableDesignation/Expression plus the Statement hierarchy for the body). The generator emits the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, index) setters for all four (no collection precedes any slot, so each flattened index is the constant slot position 0/1/2/3, and constIndex is true for every slot); GetChildCount is the constant 4 and GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo are a flat four-case index switch (the generator's WriteReturnDispatchSwitch shape). Its generated DoMatch has FIVE terms in MembersToMatch (source declaration) order: a fall-through plain-equality IsAsync term (this.IsAsync == o.IsAsync -- a bool is not an enum so no Any wildcard, not a string, not recursive; the ComposedType.HasRefSpecifier D242 / UsingStatement.IsAsync D262 precedent) followed by four non-nullable recursive terms (this.VariableType.DoMatch / this.VariableDesignation.DoMatch / this.InExpression.DoMatch / this.EmbeddedStatement.DoMatch), each routed through the AstNode::MatchRequired same-class static (the D231 [class.access.derived] workaround, since C++ forbids a derived node from calling the protected DoMatch through a base AstType*/VariableDesignation*/Expression*/Statement*); there is no scalar enum so there is no Any-wildcard term. MatchRequired guards a missing pattern-side child defensively and lets a null candidate child flow through the child's DoMatch(nullptr) which returns false. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. KEY DESIGN (the VariableDesignation name-shadowing crux, the first slot-accessor-named-the-same-as-its-element-type crux beyond Expression/Identifier): the [Slot("VariableDesignation")] VariableDesignation VariableDesignation property is literally named the same as its element type (the VariableDesignation class), so the VariableDesignation() accessor (a member function) shadows the VariableDesignation CLASS in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops, even though it is not a type) -- the Expression()-of-type-Expression D231 / Identifier-of-type-Identifier D227 pattern applied to a VariableDesignation-typed slot accessor. The fix is the elaborated-type-specifier class VariableDesignation (basic.lookup.elab ignores non-type names) in every type position AFTER the getter declaration (the setter parameter, the slot static's element type, the SetChild/Clone static_casts, and the backing field); the ctor parameter and getter return type precede the getter so they use the plain VariableDesignation. The other three slot accessors do NOT shadow their element types: VariableType() does not collide with AstType (no class named VariableType or Type lives in the Syntax namespace -- the Attribute D240 lesson), InExpression() does not collide with Expression (the [Slot("Expression")] argument names the slot KIND Expression but the PROPERTY is InExpression, so the accessor InExpression() is not the name Expression -- the MemberReferenceExpression.Target D247 differently-named-property discriminator), and EmbeddedStatement() does not collide with Statement (a member named EmbeddedStatement is not the name Statement -- the WhileStatement D258 precedent), so those three use the plain element types throughout and no elaborated specifier is needed. KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant -- four reused kinds): all four slot kinds are already ported -- Slots::Type (by Attribute D240), Slots::VariableDesignation (by ParenthesizedVariableDesignation D264), Slots::Expression (by UnaryOperatorExpression D231), Slots::EmbeddedStatement (by WhileStatement D258) -- so Slots.hpp is unchanged. This is the first ported node to REUSE the Slots::VariableDesignation kind as a SINGLE slot (D264 added it as a collection kind for ParenthesizedVariableDesignation.VariableDesignations; the kind-collapsing design is by [Slot] name regardless of single-vs-collection, so the per-node VariableDesignationSlot points at the shared Slots::VariableDesignation kind while carrying IsOptional=false -- confirming the IfElseStatement.FalseStatement D258 per-position-optionality-on-the-per-node-slot design generalizes to a kind first ported as a collection now reused as a single). The per-node slots all carry IsOptional=false (all four required); the shared kinds carry identity only (constructed non-collection/non-optional). KEY DESIGN (the generated ctors, empty + all-params): the RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 4 (all four slots required) and there is no collection, so the single full ctor IS the required-prefix ctor (no shorter prefix ctor and no params overload); the port carries the empty ctor + the (AstType, VariableDesignation, Expression, Statement) all-params ctor. The IsAsync bool scalar is not a ctor param (the generator adds only settable ENUM-typed scalars to CtorParams; a bool is not an enum), so it is left at its false default and set via the property setter. KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone, scalar + four children + annotation channel): the Clone makes a fresh node, copies the IsAsync scalar, copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), and deep-clones the four children through the setters (which re-parent and re-index via SetChildNode) when present (Clone tolerates a missing child even though the slots are required -- the invariant is enforced by CheckInvariant, not by Clone). AstType::Clone() returns AstType* (covariant) which VariableType(AstType*) accepts directly; VariableDesignation::Clone() returns VariableDesignation* (covariant, the D264 abstract-base pure-virtual) cast to the elaborated class VariableDesignation* for the setter (the VariableDesignation() accessor shadows the class); Expression::Clone() returns Expression* and Statement::Clone() returns Statement* (covariant) which the setters accept directly. No own location fields (ForeachStatement does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the WhileStatement/ComposedType no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is ForeachStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). KEY DESIGN (the const strings): the ForeachKeyword = "foreach" and InKeyword = "in" const strings port as static constexpr const char* (static fields, not instance state), so the generator's MembersToMatch (which iterates only instance IPropertySymbols) excludes them from the DoMatch (the BreakStatement D254 / WhileStatement D258 / UsingStatement D262 precedent). The AwaitKeyword = UnaryOperatorExpression.AwaitKeyword const aliases the canonical await literal on UnaryOperatorExpression (which UsingStatement.AwaitKeyword D262 also aliases); ports as a static constexpr const char* initialized from UnaryOperatorExpression::AwaitKeyword (faithful to the C# alias, preserving the single-source-of-truth). Initializer [Slot("Expression")] single slot at flattened index 1 (the ReturnStatement D255 nullable-Expression?-single-slot shape -- MatchOptional).
