NO C++ name-shadowing crux (unlike SingleVariableDesignation D264 / SimpleType D237 whose Identifier() accessor shadows the Identifier class): the [Slot("Identifier")] argument names the slot KIND Identifier but the PROPERTY is Name, so the string accessor is Name() (NOT Identifier()) and the backing token accessor is NameToken() (NOT IdentifierToken()); neither shadows the Identifier CLASS in this class scope (no member is named Identifier), so NO elaborated-type-specifier (class Identifier) is needed anywhere, and the Identifier::Create factory call in the Name setter is unqualified -- the LabelStatement D259 / MemberType.MemberName D238 / AttributeSection D241 differently-named-property precedent. The Initializer() accessor likewise does NOT collide with the Expression class (no member is named Expression -- the MemberReferenceExpression.Target D247 differently-named-property precedent), so no class Expression elaboration is needed either. The NON-nullable string Name (vs GotoStatement's nullable string?): the backing NameToken is a REQUIRED (non-nullable) slot (IsOptional=false), the Name() getter DEREFS the token (returning std::string, NOT std::optional<std::string> -- a null token is a half-constructed node that would NullReferenceException in C#), and the Name setter uses Identifier::Create (NOT CreateIfNotEmpty -- a non-nullable name creates a token even for an empty string, so an empty name yields a token with an empty Name, not a null token -- the MemberType.MemberName D238 / LabelStatement.Label D259 / SingleVariableDesignation.Identifier D264 precedent). CheckInvariant therefore passes only on a node whose NameToken is filled (the token is a required slot, so a default-constructed node violates the required-slot invariant -- the assert fires in debug), though the Initializer slot is nullable so its absence is invariant-valid. A nameless VariableInitializer is a half-constructed node (UB to deref or pass to DoMatch), so the tests exercise the empty-name case as a real '' match (two empty names match; empty does not match non-empty), not a nameless/nullopt case. KEY DESIGN (the generated ctors, empty + required-prefix + all-params): a string-name [Slot] is a required ctor param regardless of optionality (the generator's line-168 rule), and the Initializer is nullable so it is NOT in the required prefix -- RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 1, ConstructorPrefixLengths is {1, 2} (the required prefix then the full count), and there is no collection so no params overload. The generated ctors are the empty ctor + the (string name) required-prefix ctor + the (string name, Expression? initializer) all-params ctor. The (string name) ctor body is this.Name = name; (it calls the string setter, which creates the token via Identifier::Create); the all-params ctor chains to the prefix via : this(name) then sets this.Initializer = initializer;. The (std::string) single-arg ctor is explicit (a single-argument ctor is a converting ctor by default -- the SimpleType D237 / LabelStatement D259 / SingleVariableDesignation D264 precedent); the two-arg all-params ctor is NOT explicit (a multi-arg ctor is not a converting ctor). The delegation to the explicit (std::string) prefix ctor is fine (delegating ctor calls may invoke explicit ctors; explicit only blocks implicit conversion sequences, not ctor delegation). The next-in-order Phase-5 pieces are FixedStatement (now unblocked -- it needs the VariableInitializer just ported plus a NEW Slots::Variable kind for its Variables AstNodeCollection<VariableInitializer> collection, plus the already-ported Slots::Type/Slots::EmbeddedStatement kinds), then SwitchStatement, TryCatchStatement, LocalFunctionDeclarationStatement, VariableDeclarationStatement (also now unblocked -- it needs VariableInitializer for its Variables collection), then the remaining TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies, then the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage (CSharpOutputVisitor : IAstVisitor); the resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the AST. |
| D267 | FixedStatement (the fixed_statement ::= 'fixed' '(' type variable_initializer* ')' statement node, C# grammar 24.7 -- a sealed Statement with a single REQUIRED AstType Type slot + a Variables AstNodeCollection<VariableInitializer> collection + a single REQUIRED Statement EmbeddedStatement, the ObjectCreateExpression D251 single + collection + trailing-single shape with a Statement base and a REQUIRED trailing single) + the NEW cycle-broken Slots::Variable kind + IAstVisitor VisitFixedStatement + DepthFirstAstVisitor Visit* (Phase 5: the fixed pin statement -- the first single + collection + required-trailing-single statement, fifty-sixth piece) | port | Ports the FixedStatement concrete C# AST node (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Statements/FixedStatement.hpp mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Statements/FixedStatement.cs -- the generated .g.cs + the hand-written partial, which declares only the FixedKeyword const and the three slot properties, no ctors, no helpers) -- the fifty-sixth in-order Phase-5 piece, the next-in-order target per the D266 plan ('FixedStatement (now unblocked -- it needs the VariableInitializer just ported plus a NEW Slots::Variable kind for its Variables AstNodeCollection<VariableInitializer> collection, plus the already-ported Slots::Type/Slots::EmbeddedStatement kinds)'). fixed_statement ::= 'fixed' '(' type variable_initializer* ')' statement (C# grammar 24.7): a Statement with three [Slot] children in source declaration order -- a REQUIRED (non-nullable) AstType Type (the pinned pointer element type, e.g. int in fixed (int* p = &x) body), a Variables AstNodeCollection<VariableInitializer> collection (the comma-separated name = initializer declarators, each a VariableInitializer, the D266 dependency), and a REQUIRED (non-nullable) Statement EmbeddedStatement (the body whose scope pins the pointers). It is the ObjectCreateExpression D251 shape (a single + a collection + a trailing single) applied to the Statement hierarchy with the trailing single REQUIRED (not nullable, unlike ObjectCreateExpression.Initializer). The generator's supportsIncremental flag is collectionCount == 1 && slotIndex == slots.Count - 1; here collectionCount == 1 but the Variables collection is at slotIndex 1, NOT the last slot (slots.Count - 1 == 2 -- the EmbeddedStatement single slot follows), so supportsIncremental is FALSE: every Add/Insert/Remove/single-slot-set INVALIDATES the parent's indices for a lazy rebuild (EnsureChildIndices). The EmbeddedStatement single slot FOLLOWS a collection, so the generator's constIndex = !slots.Take(slotIndex).Any(IsCollection) is false, and the EmbeddedStatement property setter uses the index-less SetChildNode(ref field, value) (which invalidates on a set/clear, since the flattened index is dynamic -- the Variables count can change); the SetChild override still passes the known flattened index to the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, index). The Type single slot PRECEDES the collection, so its setter uses the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, 0). GetChildCount is 2 + Count (the two single slots plus the collection length); GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo walk the slots subtracting each one's width from a running index (a single step, a collection step, then a single step); GetCollectionByKind returns the Variables collection for the Variable kind. Its generated DoMatch has THREE terms in MembersToMatch (source declaration) order: a non-nullable recursive Type term (dispatched through MatchRequired -- the D231 [class.access.derived] workaround), a collection recursive Variables term (this.Variables.DoMatch -- the generator emits the collection-typed recursive term directly, NOT MatchOptional, which it emits only for a nullable non-collection child), and a non-nullable recursive EmbeddedStatement term (dispatched through MatchRequired). Both recursive single terms are REQUIRED (non-nullable), so neither uses MatchOptional (unlike ObjectCreateExpression whose trailing Initializer is nullable). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. KEY DESIGN (no name-shadowing crux -- the ObjectCreateExpression D251 differently-named-property precedent): the Type()/Variables()/EmbeddedStatement() accessors are member functions, but no class named Type/Variables/EmbeddedStatement lives in the Syntax namespace (there is AstType, not Type), and no member is named AstType/VariableInitializer/Statement, so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed anywhere, and the plain AstType/VariableInitializer/Statement resolve to the classes in every type position (the MemberReferenceExpression/InvocationExpression differently-named-property precedent). KEY DESIGN (the NEW cycle-broken Slots::Variable kind): the [Slot("Variable")] argument on FixedStatement.Variables names a NEW slot kind not yet ported, a CSharpSlotInfoT<VariableInitializer> (the element type is the concrete VariableInitializer node). VariableInitializer.hpp INCLUDES Slots.hpp (it has per-node slot statics NameTokenSlot/InitializerSlot referencing &Slots::Identifier/&Slots::Expression), so the kind cannot live in Slots.hpp -- a circular include (Slots.hpp would have to include VariableInitializer.hpp for the complete VariableInitializer, but VariableInitializer.hpp includes Slots.hpp, and with Slots.hpp's guard set those definitions would not be visible where VariableInitializer's class body needs them) -- so the kind is cycle-broken into VariableInitializer.hpp after the VariableInitializer class where both CSharpSlotInfoT and VariableInitializer are complete (the Slots::Attribute D241 / Slots::AttributeSection D242 / Slots::Initializer D251 precedent applied to a collection kind). The inline variable still has external linkage and one address across TUs (the C++17 inline guarantee), preserving the pointer-identity comparison node.Slot.Kind == &Slots::Variable the slot system relies on. The kind name Variable collides with no class in the Syntax namespace (there is VariableInitializer/VariableDesignation, not Variable), so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed. The shared constant is constructed non-collection/non-optional ({"Variable", false, nullptr, false}); the per-node VariablesSlot on FixedStatement carries the IsCollection flag (the collection [Slot] makes the per-node slot a collection). KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant for Type/EmbeddedStatement -- two reused kinds): both are already ported -- Slots::Type by Attribute D240, Slots::EmbeddedStatement by WhileStatement D258 -- so Slots.hpp is unchanged. KEY DESIGN (the generated ctors, empty + required-prefix): FixedStatement.cs declares NO hand-written ctors (only the FixedKeyword const and the three slot properties), so the port carries only the generated ctors. The generated collection ctors (the (AstType, IEnumerable<VariableInitializer>), the params VariableInitializer[] form, and the (AstType, IEnumerable<VariableInitializer>, Statement) all-params ctor) use AddRange, which lands with the collection convenience mutators (the D222 deferral), so they are DEFERRED; the empty + the (AstType) required-prefix ctors cover the construction API (the Type is the only required ctor param before the Variables collection -- Variables is an optional collection and EmbeddedStatement is a required single that follows a collection, so it goes into the deferred all-params ctor). A variables list is built via Variables().Add(...) and the body is set via EmbeddedStatement(...) until AddRange lands. The (AstType) ctor is explicit (a single-argument ctor is a converting ctor by default), matching the generator's public ctor but avoiding an implicit AstType -> FixedStatement conversion. KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone, type + variables + body + annotation channel): the Clone makes a fresh node, copies the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), deep-clones the Type through the setter (AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override), deep-clones every Variables element through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; VariableInitializer::Clone() returns VariableInitializer*, which Add(VariableInitializer*) accepts directly), and deep-clones the EmbeddedStatement through the setter when present (Statement::Clone() returns Statement*, which EmbeddedStatement(Statement*) accepts directly; Clone tolerates a missing body even though the slot is required -- the invariant is enforced by CheckInvariant, not by Clone). No own location fields (FixedStatement does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the ObjectCreateExpression/WhileStatement no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is FixedStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). KEY DESIGN (the const string): the FixedKeyword = "fixed" const string ports as a static constexpr const char* (a static field, not instance state), so the generator's MembersToMatch (which iterates only instance IPropertySymbols) excludes it from the DoMatch (the BreakStatement D254 / WhileStatement D258 precedent). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitFixedStatement(FixedStatement*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring the concrete type -- the D225 convention; the forward declaration precedes the IAstVisitor class body per the D260 forward-declaration-must-precede-pure-virtual crux, handled proactively by adding class FixedStatement; before the class body) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the FixedStatement.hpp include for the upcast (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the DepthFirstAstVisitor default -- no breakage). It is the ComposedType D242 two-collection shape but with NO single slot between (a collection -> collection layout): supportsIncremental is collectionCount == 1 && slotIndex == slots.Count - 1, FALSE for BOTH collections (collectionCount == 2), so every Add/Insert/Remove INVALIDATES the parent's indices for a lazy rebuild (EnsureChildIndices), and IndexOf falls back to a linear identity search. KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant in Slots.hpp -- two NEW cycle-broken kinds): CaseLabel reuses the already-ported Slots::Expression (by UnaryOperatorExpression D231); SwitchSection adds the NEW Slots::CaseLabel kind (CSharpSlotInfoT<CaseLabel>) cycle-broken into CaseLabel.hpp after the class (CaseLabel.hpp includes Slots.hpp for its per-node ExpressionSlot, so the kind cannot live in Slots.hpp -- a circular include -- and is defined in CaseLabel.hpp where both CSharpSlotInfoT and CaseLabel are complete; the Slots::Attribute D241 / Slots::AttributeSection D242 / Slots::Initializer D251 / Slots::Variable D267 precedent applied to a collection kind) and reuses Slots::EmbeddedStatement; SwitchStatement adds the NEW Slots::SwitchSection kind (CSharpSlotInfoT<SwitchSection>) cycle-broken into SwitchSection.hpp after the class (SwitchSection.hpp includes Slots.hpp for its per-node slot statics) and reuses Slots::Expression. So Slots.hpp is UNCHANGED (the two new kinds are cycle-broken into their element-type headers). KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone): CaseLabel deep-clones the Expression when present + the annotation channel (a default: label with a null Expression clones to a null-Expression clone); SwitchSection deep-clones both collections via Add (CaseLabel::Clone returns CaseLabel* and Statement::Clone returns Statement*, which the typed Adds accept directly) + the annotation channel; SwitchStatement deep-clones the Expression via the setter + every SwitchSections element via Add + the annotation channel. No own location fields on any of the three (none derives EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the no-location-copy precedent). The covariant returns are CaseLabel* (through AstNode*), SwitchSection* (through AstNode*), and SwitchStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). The generator's supportsIncremental flag is collectionCount == 1 && slotIndex == slots.Count - 1; here collectionCount == 1 but the CatchClauses collection is at slotIndex == 1, NOT the last slot (slots.Count - 1 == 2 -- the FinallyBlock single slot follows), so supportsIncremental is FALSE: every Add/Insert/Remove/single-slot-set INVALIDATES the parent's indices for a lazy rebuild (EnsureChildIndices), and IndexOf falls back to a linear identity search. The TryBlock single slot PRECEDES the collection, so its setter uses the const-index SetChildNode(ref field, value, 0). The (BlockStatement) ctor is explicit (a single-argument ctor is a converting ctor by default). KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant in Slots.hpp -- three NEW cycle-broken kinds): CatchClause reuses the already-ported Slots::Type/Slots::Identifier/Slots::Condition/Slots::Body; the NEW Slots::CatchClause kind (CSharpSlotInfoT<CatchClause>) is cycle-broken into CatchClause.hpp after the class (CatchClause.hpp includes Slots.hpp for its per-node slot statics, so the kind cannot live in Slots.hpp -- a circular include -- and is defined in CatchClause.hpp where both CSharpSlotInfoT and CatchClause are complete; the Slots::Attribute D241 / Slots::CaseLabel D268 precedent applied to a collection kind). TryCatchStatement adds the NEW Slots::TryBlock and Slots::FinallyBlock kinds (both CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement>) cycle-broken into BlockStatement.hpp after the Slots::Body kind (BlockStatement.hpp includes Slots.hpp for its StatementsSlot, so a CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement> kind cannot live in Slots.hpp -- the Slots::Body D260 cycle-breaking precedent applied to two more BlockStatement-typed kinds); TryCatchStatement reuses Slots::CatchClause for the CatchClauses collection. So Slots.hpp is UNCHANGED (all three new kinds are cycle-broken into their element-type headers). The shared kind constants are constructed non-collection/non-optional; the per-node TryBlockSlot carries IsOptional=false (required), the per-node CatchClausesSlot carries IsCollection=true, the per-node FinallyBlockSlot carries IsOptional=true (nullable -- the shared kind is constructed non-optional, the per-node slot carries the optionality, the IfElseStatement.FalseStatement D258 precedent). KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone): CatchClause deep-clones the four children when present (the Type/Condition via the setters, the VariableNameToken via the token setter, the Body via the setter) + the annotation channel (a bare catch with only the Body clones to a bare clone with only the Body); TryCatchStatement deep-clones the TryBlock via the setter (BlockStatement::Clone returns BlockStatement*, the covariant override), every CatchClauses element via Add (CatchClause::Clone returns CatchClause*, which Add(CatchClause*) accepts directly), and the FinallyBlock via the setter when present + the annotation channel. No own location fields on either (neither derives EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the no-location-copy precedent). The covariant returns are CatchClause* (through AstNode*, the AstNode::Clone virtual -- CatchClause has no hand-written typed Clone, faithful to the hasPatternPlaceholder:true non-sealed form) and TryCatchStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). KEY DESIGN (the const strings): the CatchKeyword/WhenKeyword/CondLPar/CondRPar/TryKeyword/FinallyKeyword const strings port as static constexpr const char* (static fields, not instance state), so the generator's MembersToMatch (which iterates only instance IPropertySymbols) excludes them from the DoMatch (the BreakStatement D254 / IfElseStatement D258 / SwitchStatement D268 precedent). The all-params and the params forms call this.Variables.AddRange(...), which lands with the collection convenience mutators (the D222 deferral), so they are DEFERRED; the empty + the (Modifiers, AstType) required-prefix ctors cover the generated construction API. The (Modifiers, AstType) ctor is NOT explicit (a multi-arg ctor is not a converting ctor -- the IfElseStatement D258 (Expression, Statement) 2-arg precedent). The HAND-WRITTEN convenience ctor VariableDeclarationStatement(AstType type, string name, Expression? initializer = null) (declared in the C# partial) creates a single VariableInitializer(name, initializer) and adds it via this.Variables.Add(...) -- it uses Add (already ported), NOT AddRange (deferred), and the VariableInitializer(string, Expression*) 2-arg ctor is already ported (D266), so the convenience ctor ports now. The 3-arg form with the default initializer = nullptr matches the C# Expression? initializer = null; the default covers the bare 'type name;' form. The hand-written GetVariable(string name) helper (a VariableInitializer? lookup by name) is DEFERRED: it is a behaviour helper (Variables.FirstOrNull(...)) consumed by the resolver/output stage, not part of the node structure, and FirstOrNull is itself a deferred collection convenience. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. KEY DESIGN (the Modifiers [Flags] enum port): the first ported [Flags] enum and the first ported enum used as a non-[Slot] scalar. The C# default underlying type is int; the Any member is unchecked((int)0x80000000) -- the sign bit, a negative int. The port uses an UNSIGNED std::uint32_t underlying type so Any's 0x80000000 fits as a plain value rather than relying on implementation-defined signed overflow. The VisibilityMask = Private|Internal|Protected|Public == 0x000F. The [Flags] bitwise operators (|, &, ^, ~) are defined on the enum class (C++ enum class does NOT have them implicitly, unlike the C# enum); they are part of the value type's core semantics (constructing a combined mask, testing a bit), NOT an output-stage helper, so they land now. The CSharpModifiers static helper (GetModifierName/AllModifiers, the output-order lookup table consumed by the output visitor) is DEFERRED. KEY DESIGN (the Modifiers name-shadowing crux -- the D235 DirectionExpression.FieldDirection precedent applied to a [Flags] enum): the Modifiers() getter (a member function) shadows the Modifiers enum class in C++ class scope (unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops, even though it is not a type), so the setter parameter type uses the elaborated enum specifier enum Modifiers, the DoMatch Any-wildcard term uses the fully-qualified ::ILSpy::...::Modifiers::Any (the elaborated specifier cannot apply in a qualified-name position), and the backing-field declaration/initializer use enum Modifiers and the fully-qualified ::ILSpy::...::Modifiers::None. The (Modifiers, AstType) ctor body assigns the Modifiers scalar DIRECTLY to the backing field (not via the ambiguous Modifiers(modifiers) setter call -- the D235 FieldDirection(fieldDirection) ambiguity precedent: the call could parse as a functional cast of the enum). The Type()/Variables() accessors do NOT collide with their element types (AstType/VariableInitializer -- no member is named those, the ObjectCreateExpression D251 / FixedStatement D267 differently-named-property precedent), so the plain AstType/VariableInitializer resolve to the classes there. KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant): Slots::Type is already ported (by Attribute D240), and Slots::Variable is already cycle-broken into VariableInitializer.hpp (by FixedStatement D267), so Slots.hpp is UNCHANGED. The Modifiers enum lives in its own Modifiers.hpp header (a shared enum used by VariableDeclarationStatement and the future TypeMember/EntityDeclaration hierarchy). KEY DESIGN (the per-concrete-node Clone): copies the Modifiers scalar, the annotation channel (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), the Type deep-cloned through the setter (AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override), and every Variables element deep-cloned through Add (VariableInitializer::Clone() returns VariableInitializer*, which Add(VariableInitializer*) accepts directly). No own location fields (does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the FixedStatement D267 no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is VariableDeclarationStatement* (through Statement*, the Statement::Clone pure-virtual). The port's non-owning model means the hand-written convenience ctor's internally-created VariableInitializer is not deleted on the parent's destruction (the Clone-produced-subtree leak profile -- consistent with the established D223 non-owning model). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitVariableDeclarationStatement pure-virtual (forward-declaring VariableDeclarationStatement; the forward declaration precedes the IAstVisitor class body per the D260 crux, handled proactively) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the VariableDeclarationStatement.hpp include (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the default -- no breakage). TDD: 40 gtest cases in the CSharp_VariableDeclarationStatement suite (cpp/tests/.../Statements/VariableDeclarationStatement_Test.cpp, wired into cpp/tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering is-a (Statement + AstNode, NOT Expression), is-concrete-and-final, the Modifiers scalar (None default, setter round-trips a combined Static|Public mask, the [Flags] bitwise operators), the Type slot (required single, re-parent/detach/clear-with-null), the Variables collection (empty-by-default, Add appends/parents/INCREMENTAL -- ChildIndex == 1 + local position, unlike FixedStatement), GetCollectionByKind, the shared Slots::Variable kind identity with FixedStatement, the single->collection slot storage (GetChild/SetChild/GetChildSlotInfo, SetChild replaces in place), the shared Slots::Type kind, the IsInstanceOfType is-a cross-checks, AcceptVisitor dispatch + virtuality, the depth-first walk (Type -> its Identifier -> Variables per element -> its NameToken Identifier -> its Initializer), DoMatch (same match, Any-wildcard matches any, different-modifiers reject, the [Flags] == is exact-value-NOT-bitmask test -- Static|Public does NOT match Static alone but matches Static|Public, different-Type reject, null-pattern/candidate-Type reject, different-Variables-count reject, different-Variables-name reject, cross-structural-twin FixedStatement rejection, null), Clone (deep-copy/virtual/covariant/non-detach, no-variables-stays-empty), CheckInvariant (filled passes, empty REJECTED via EXPECT_DEBUG_DEATH -- the Type required-slot), and the slot-static distinctness (the cross-element-type EXPECT_NE crux -- cast both to the common const CSharpSlotInfo* base). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled VariableDeclarationStatement_Test.cpp + the recompiled prior C# AST test files (the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new defaults) + relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe cleanly; the node header hit the D235 Modifiers name-shadowing crux on the first build (the Modifiers() getter shadows the Modifiers enum class -- the setter parameter type, the DoMatch Any term, and the field declaration/initializer all failed to resolve the plain Modifiers to the enum), fixed by the elaborated enum Modifiers specifier (type positions) + the fully-qualified ::ILSpy::...::Modifiers::Any/::None (qualified-name positions) + the direct field assignment in the (Modifiers, AstType) ctor body (the D235 FieldDirection(fieldDirection) ambiguity precedent); the test then hit a second crux -- several tests called a single-arg VariableDeclarationStatement(AstType*) ctor that does NOT exist (the generated required-prefix is (Modifiers, AstType) since Modifiers is the first required ctor param, NOT (AstType) as for FixedStatement whose only required param is Type), fixed by using the (Modifiers::None, type.get()) 2-arg generated ctor. After both fixes the node header and the test compiled cleanly. RESULT: 40 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_VariableDeclarationStatement.* run is 40/40 green); the full suite is 3431 -> 3471 (176 test suites, was 175) with 0 regressions (the 3431 prior tests pass unchanged -- the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new defaults); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly (the engine/CLI use the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy -- confirmed by grep: the new VariableDeclarationStatement.hpp/Modifiers.hpp are included ONLY by DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp, IAstVisitor.hpp (the forward declaration), the header itself, and the test file, NOT by any engine/CLI .cpp; ILAstToCSharp.cpp has NO CSharp/Syntax includes; AstNode.cpp -- the only ilspy.lib .cpp touching CSharp/Syntax -- includes only AstNode.hpp/AstNodeCollection.hpp/CSharpSlotInfo.hpp/Trivia.hpp, none of which include the new headers since AstNode.hpp only forward-declares IAstVisitor; so the engine signature is byte-identical to D269; no mscorlib.dll present in this environment to run the full 8026/500/306/59/999/1454/2543 baseline, but the include-graph isolation -- the D224-D269 precedent, re-confirmed by grep -- guarantees the CLI is unaffected). The next-in-order Phase-5 pieces are the remaining TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies (MethodDeclaration -- which unblocks LocalFunctionDeclarationStatement; FieldDeclaration; PropertyDeclaration; ...), then the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage (CSharpOutputVisitor : IAstVisitor); the resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the AST. |
| D271 | The kind-based slot-kind accessors on the AstNode base (GetChildByKind<T>(CSharpSlotInfoT<T>*) / SetChildByKind<T>(CSharpSlotInfoT<T>*, T*), the port of the C# public T? GetChild<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T>) / protected void SetChild<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T>, T?) -- the single-slot read/write by canonical Slots kind that the hand-written Name/NameToken/ReturnType virtuals on EntityDeclaration and the output/resolver stage build on, walking the slot storage by Kind() and downcasting via dynamic_cast (faithful to the C# GetChild(i) as T) or delegating to SetChildByKindUntyped) + the SymbolKind enum (cpp/Decompiler/TypeSystem/SymbolKind.hpp, the port of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/TypeSystem/ISymbol.cs's SymbolKind, a Phase-2 TypeSystem dependency: a byte-based enum class, 18 members None..ReturnType mirroring the C# declaration order, the underlying type the EntityDeclaration.SymbolKind abstract property -- the next in-order TypeMember piece -- needs) (Phase 5: the TypeMember foundation -- the kind-based slot API on AstNode plus the SymbolKind TypeSystem dependency, sixty-third piece) | port | Ports the kind-based single-slot read/write accessors on the AstNode base (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/AstNode.hpp -- two new public template members added next to the existing SetChildByKindUntyped non-template, mirroring the C# AstNode.cs public T? GetChild<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T> slot) and protected void SetChild<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T> slot, T? newChild)) plus the SymbolKind enum (cpp/Decompiler/TypeSystem/SymbolKind.hpp, mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/TypeSystem/ISymbol.cs) -- the sixty-third in-order Phase-5 piece, the foundation for the TypeMember hierarchy (the next in-order target per the D270 plan: 'the remaining TypeMember/GeneralScope hierarchies (MethodDeclaration -- which unblocks LocalFunctionDeclarationStatement; FieldDeclaration; PropertyDeclaration; ...)'). The kind-based GetChild<T> walks GetChildSlotInfo finding the slot whose Kind() is the passed canonical Slots constant and returns its child downcast to T (dynamic_cast<T*>(GetChild(i)), faithful to the C# GetChild(i) as T) or null when this node declares no slot of that kind (the C# returns the default T? == null); SetChild<T> delegates to SetChildByKindUntyped (which finds the matching-kind slot and writes the child, throwing std::logic_error when this node declares no slot of the kind). Both are templated on the slot's element type (the C# GetChild<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T>) generic), so a caller writes node.GetChildByKind(&Slots.Identifier) and gets an Identifier*; the element type is deduced from the slot's CSharpSlotInfoT<T> argument (matching the C# generic inference), so a call passing an Expression slot can only ask for Expression (not a more-derived type). KEY DESIGN (the MSVC permissive-mode template-disambiguation crux -- a NEW C++-porting crux): the C# GetChild<T>/SetChild<T> are OVERLOADED with the non-generic internal AstNode? GetChild(int) / SetChild(int, AstNode?) slot-storage virtuals (which the generator overrides and the port keeps as the non-template GetChild(int)/SetChild(int,...)). A C++ member template sharing that name with the non-template GetChild(int) makes MSVC's permissive-mode parser (the project builds without /permissive-) treat obj.GetChild<T>(...) as a less-than (GetChild < T(...)) rather than a template-id: the first build failed MSVC C2275 ('Identifier: expected an expression instead of a type') cascading into C2660 ('EqHelper::Compare does not take 3 arguments', the EXPECT_EQ macro split on the misparsed commas). The C++ standard template disambiguator obj.template GetChild<T>(...) is ALSO rejected on a non-dependent object (MSVC C2187 'syntax error: template was unexpected here') -- the .template disambiguator is only accepted for a DEPENDENT object expression, and the call sites (and the future EntityDeclaration hand-written virtuals) are non-dependent. The resolution is to NAME the kind-based templates GetChildByKind<T>/SetChildByKind<T> (template-ONLY names with NO non-template overload of those exact names, paralleling the already-ported GetCollectionByKind(CSharpSlotInfo*) non-template): a template-only member name parses obj.GetChildByKind<T>(...) as a template-id in MSVC permissive mode (the less-than interpretation requires the name to resolve to a single non-template function as an operand, which a template-only name cannot), so the C# GetChild<T>/SetChild<T> port to C++ takes template-only ByKind-suffixed names (a C++ porting divergence from the C# overloaded name, recorded here as the established pattern for every C# generic/non-generic-overloaded AstNode API the port exposes). The non-template GetChild(int)/SetChild(int,...) slot-storage virtuals keep their C# names (every concrete node overrides them by name; renaming would touch every ported concrete node). The existing GetParent<T>()/GetParent(pred) overload pair (D221) compiles with explicit <T> at a non-dependent site (AstNode_Test.cpp:627 L1.GetParent<StubBinary>()) because its non-template overload GetParent(pred) takes a std::function with a default arg callable as GetParent() (the less-than interpretation GetParent < StubBinary() is grammatically ill-formed since the 0-arg call leaves the < operand unbalanced), distinct from the GetChild(int)/GetChild<T>(slot) case where the 1-arg call makes the less-than interpretation grammatically viable -- the discriminator is whether the less-than interpretation is grammatically constructible at the call site, which is why GetParent<T>() survives the permissive parser but a same-named GetChild<T>(slot) does not. KEY DESIGN (the SymbolKind port): the first ported TypeSystem enum beyond the TypeKind/KnownTypeCode precedent is a faithful header-only enum class with std::uint8_t underlying (the C# ': byte') and 18 members in C# declaration order (None=0, Module=1, TypeDefinition=2, Field=3, Property=4, Indexer=5, Event=6, Method=7, Operator=8, Constructor=9, Destructor=10, Accessor=11, Namespace=12, Variable=13, Parameter=14, TypeParameter=15, Constraint=16, ReturnType=17), living in its own SymbolKind.hpp in the ILSpy::Decompiler::TypeSystem namespace (the TypeKind.hpp precedent); the C# underlying is byte so the port keeps std::uint8_t (sizeof == 1) and the values fit as plain unsigned. EntityDeclaration.SymbolKind is the abstract property returning one of these (each concrete declaration overrides it -- MethodDeclaration returns SymbolKind::Method, FieldDeclaration Field, DestructorDeclaration Destructor, etc.), the consumption that lands with the EntityDeclaration base next iteration. KEY DESIGN (GetChildren<T> deferred): the C# public AstNodeCollection<T> GetChildren<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T> slot) (the kind-based COLLECTION read, returning the collection occupying the slot or a detached empty new AstNodeCollection<T>(this, slot) when the node declares no collection of that kind) is DEFERRED -- the ported AstNodeCollectionT<T> is a value type holding its own std::vector<T*> list (not a reference type as in C#), so the detached-empty-collection return needs a stable reference or a by-value copy whose return type conflicts with the concrete nodes' by-reference Attributes() accessors; the EntityDeclaration base's virtual Attributes (the only GetChildren consumer) is overridden by every concrete EntityDeclaration, so the base body is dead for real nodes. GetChildren<T> and the EntityDeclaration virtual Attributes land with the EntityDeclaration base next iteration, where the detached-empty case is resolved. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete nodes are hand-translated from the generated output. KEY DESIGN (no new Slots constant, no IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor change): the kind-based accessors are AstNode base members (not a concrete node), so no Slots constant, no IAstVisitor Visit, and no DepthFirstAstVisitor override is added -- the additions are purely the two AstNode template members + the SymbolKind enum header. TDD: 14 gtest cases across two suites (CSharp_SlotKindAccessors 10, CSharp_SymbolKind 4) in a single test file (cpp/tests/.../CSharp/Syntax/AstNodeSlotKind_Test.cpp, wired into cpp/tests/CMakeLists.txt) covering, for the kind-based accessors, GetChildByKind returns the single-slot child by kind (a SimpleType IdentifierToken via Slots::Identifier), returns null for a kind the node declares no slot of (SimpleType has no Expression slot; UnaryOperatorExpression has no Identifier slot), downcasts the stored child to the slot's element type (the NullReferenceExpression operand via Slots::Expression, recovered by a further dynamic_cast), returns null for an empty slot (an operand-less UnaryOperatorExpression), distinguishes the Left vs Right kinds on a BinaryOperatorExpression, returns the first element of a collection slot by kind (a SimpleType TypeArguments element via Slots::TypeArgument) and null for an empty collection, SetChildByKind writes a single slot by kind (replaces the UnaryOperatorExpression operand, detaches the old child, re-parents the new), clears a slot by kind (null), and throws std::logic_error for a kind with no slot (SetChildByKindUntyped throws rather than silently no-op'ing); and for SymbolKind, None==0, ReturnType==17 (the last of 18), sizeof==1 with std::uint8_t underlying, and the distinct ordered values (Field==3, Method==7, Destructor==10, Parameter==14, TypeParameter==15, Constraint==16). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled AstNodeSlotKind_Test.cpp + the recompiled prior C# AST test files (the AstNode.hpp additions are header-only template members, satisfied inline) + relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe cleanly; the test hit two build cruxes and was fixed: (1) the MSVC C2275 permissive-mode less-than misparse of obj.GetChild<T>(slot) (the kind-based template sharing the GetChild name with the non-template GetChild(int)), fixed by renaming to the template-only GetChildByKind<T>/SetChildByKind<T> (the .template disambiguator obj.template GetChild<T> was first tried and rejected C2187 on the non-dependent object); (2) two test cases passed a CSharpSlotInfoT<Expression>* (&Slots::Expression) to GetChildByKind<NullReferenceExpression>/GetChildByKind<Identifier> and a CSharpSlotInfoT<Identifier>* stray to SetChildByKind<Expression>, which are MSVC C2664 type errors because GetChildByKind<T>/SetChildByKind<T> deduce T from the slot's element type (faithful to the C# GetChild<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T>)) -- a call passing an Expression slot can only ask for Expression, and SetChildByKind<Expression> takes an Expression* not an Identifier*; fixed by testing the downcast via the Expression element type (a further dynamic_cast<NullReferenceExpression*> recovers the concrete type) and using a NullReferenceExpression stray for the absent-kind SetChildByKind test. After both fixes the test compiled cleanly. EntityDeclaration is the common base of every type-member declaration node (MethodDeclaration/FieldDeclaration/PropertyDeclaration/ConstructorDeclaration/DestructorDeclaration/...), an abstract partial class : AstNode (a type member is a structural container, not a Statement/Expression/AstType, so it derives DIRECTLY from AstNode -- the VariableInitializer D266 precedent for a direct-AstNode-rooted TypeMembers node). The abstract base carries the shared virtual surface every member declaration reuses: the abstract SymbolKind (each concrete declaration overrides it to report which kind of member it is -- MethodDeclaration returns SymbolKind.Method, DestructorDeclaration SymbolKind.Destructor; the SymbolKind enum is the D271 port); the virtual Attributes (the C# base body returns GetChildren(Slots.AttributeSection); the port returns GetChildren(&Slots::AttributeSection); every concrete EntityDeclaration overrides Attributes to return its real collection, so the base body is dead for real nodes -- the D271 note); the Modifiers scalar (a plain settable Modifiers-typed property, NOT virtual, NOT a [Slot] -- the [Flags] Modifiers enum was ported by D270) plus the HasModifier(mod) bitmask helper; the virtual Name/NameToken/ReturnType (convenience accessors over the Identifier/Type slot positions by canonical Slots kind, read/written via the D271 GetChildByKind/SetChildByKind; Name is a string over the Identifier token, NameToken is the Identifier slot, ReturnType is the nullable AstType slot -- a destructor/constructor/operator has no return type, so the slot may be absent; a concrete declaration that declares its own [Slot("Identifier")]/[Slot("Type")] overrides the matching virtual to use its backing field directly, one that does not inherits the base kind-walk which returns null for a kind the node declares no slot of); and the protected MatchAttributesAndModifiers(EntityDeclaration, Match) helper (the generated DoMatch of every concrete EntityDeclaration calls this to match the Modifiers Any-wildcard AND the Attributes collection together -- the generator adds a MatchAttributesAndModifiers term to MembersToMatch for every EntityDeclaration-derived node). The abstract base gets NO IAstVisitor Visit method (NeedsVisitor is false for an abstract base -- the Statement D254 / AstType D236 precedent), so this header does not touch IAstVisitor.hpp/DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp; the concrete EntityDeclaration subclasses each add their own Visit<NodeName> as they land. The Modifiers name-shadowing crux (the D270 VariableDeclarationStatement precedent applied to the base): the Modifiers() getter shadows the Modifiers enum class in this class scope, so the setter parameter type, the HasModifier parameter, and the backing-field declaration use the elaborated enum Modifiers specifier (type positions) and the MatchAttributesAndModifiers Any-wildcard term and the backing-field initializer use the fully-qualified ::ILSpy::...::Modifiers::Any/::None (qualified-name positions). The Name()/NameToken()/ReturnType() accessors do NOT collide with any class in the Syntax namespace, and the GetChildByKind<Identifier>/<AstType> template arguments are NOT shadowed (no member is named Identifier or AstType), so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed there. KEY DESIGN (GetChildren<T> + the detached-empty resolution, the D271-deferred piece now landed): the C# public AstNodeCollection<T> GetChildren<T>(CSharpSlotInfo<T> slot) returns the collection occupying the slot OR a detached empty new AstNodeCollection<T>(this, slot) when the node declares no collection of that kind. The ported AstNodeCollectionT<T> is a VALUE type holding its own std::vector<T*> list (not a C# reference type), so returning a detached empty by reference needs a stable object. The resolution: GetChildren<T> returns AstNodeCollectionT<T>& (by reference, so the concrete by-reference Attributes() override can covariantly return the same type); for the real-collection case it returns *static_cast<AstNodeCollectionT<T>*>(GetCollectionByKind(slot)) (the downcast is safe -- GetCollectionByKind returns the collection whose Kind() matches slot, which is the node's AstNodeCollectionT<T> member); for the no-collection case it returns a reference to a function-local static AstNodeCollectionT<T> empty (a stable per-<T> singleton, default-constructed as a detached empty). This needs a default-constructible detached-empty AstNodeCollectionT<T> -- a NEW default ctor (parent/kind null, baseIndex 0, supportsIncremental false, empty list) added to AstNodeCollectionT<T>, documented as read-only (the C# detached empty is a read-only view; the D271 note: writes go through AddChild/SetChild, which reject a missing slot -- no caller mutates a GetChildren-returned detached empty; read paths Count/iteration/AsNodeList/DoMatch are safe and never touch the null parent, but mutation Add/Insert/Remove/SetAt would deref the null parent and is UB). The C++ name keeps the C# GetChildren (no non-template overload shares it, unlike GetChild<T> which collides with GetChild(int) -- the D271 permissive-mode template-disambiguation crux does not apply). KEY DESIGN (DestructorDeclaration, the first concrete TypeMember): finalizer_declaration ::= attribute_section* modifier* '~' identifier '(' ')' ( block or ';' ) (C# grammar 15.13) -- a sealed EntityDeclaration (the [DecompilerAstNode] default hasPatternPlaceholder false, so final). Three [Slot] children in source declaration order: an Attributes AstNodeCollection<AttributeSection> collection at slot 0 (reusing the cycle-broken Slots::AttributeSection, NON-incremental -- the collection is the node's only collection but NOT its last slot, the NameToken and Body singles trail it, so supportsIncremental is false and Add/Insert/Remove/single-slot-set INVALIDATE the parent's indices for a lazy EnsureChildIndices rebuild, the ComposedType D242 / ObjectCreateExpression D251 non-incremental precedent); a [ExcludeFromMatch][Slot("Identifier")] Identifier NameToken single REQUIRED slot at slot 1 (non-nullable -- the property type is Identifier, no '?' annotation; index-less SetChildNode since it follows the collection; [ExcludeFromMatch] opts it out of DoMatch -- the finalizer's name is just the declaring type name; reusing Slots::Identifier); a [Slot("Body")] BlockStatement? Body single NULLABLE slot at slot 2 (index-less; reusing the cycle-broken Slots::Body). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (D13/D147) re-configured (the tests/CMakeLists.txt change triggers a cmake re-run) and compiled Accessor_Test.cpp + the recompiled prior C# AST test files (the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default) + relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe cleanly; the node header (Accessor.hpp) compiled with NO crux on the first build (no name shadowing, no new Slots constant, the MatchString/MatchOptional/MatchAttributesAndModifiers/Any-wildcard already exist); the test hit TWO build cruxes and both were fixed: (1) the MSVC C4002/C2059 'too many arguments for function-like macro invocation EXPECT_TRUE' on EXPECT_TRUE(std::is_constructible_v<Accessor, AccessorKind>) -- the comma in the two-arg type trait is split by the preprocessor as a macro-arg separator -- fixed by wrapping in outer parens EXPECT_TRUE((std::is_constructible_v<Accessor, AccessorKind>)) (the gtest workaround for type traits with template-arg commas; the one-arg std::is_final_v has no comma so it needs no wrap); (2) two test-expectation errors (not node bugs): GetChildWalksSlots expected GetChildCount 2 but it is attrCount + 1 == 1 (the single Body slot contributes 1 to the flattened count regardless of fill -- the formula is attributes_.Count() + 1, not + (body_ != nullptr ? 1 : 0)), and DepthFirstWalkWithAttribute expected a 6-entry trace but the Body BlockStatement holds a ReturnStatement so the walk is 7 entries (accessor, attrsec, attr, simple:Foo, id:Foo, block, return) -- both fixed by correcting the expectations. RESULT: 45 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_Accessor.* run is 45/45 green); the full suite is 3565 -> 3610 tests (182 test suites, was 181) with 0 regressions (the 3565 prior tests pass unchanged -- the IAstVisitor/DepthFirstAstVisitor additions are additive, satisfied by the new default); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly (the engine/CLI use the IL AST + the ILAstToCSharp seed, not the C# AST node hierarchy -- confirmed by grep: Accessor.hpp is included ONLY by DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp and the test file, NOT by any engine/CLI .cpp; ILAstToCSharp.cpp has no CSharp/Syntax includes; so the engine signature is byte-identical to D273; the include-graph isolation -- the D224-D273 precedent, re-confirmed by grep -- guarantees the CLI is unaffected). The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitOperatorDeclaration(this) (the class name does not end in "AstType", so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitOperatorDeclaration). The generated slot statics are AttributesSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AttributeSection> pointing at Slots.AttributeSection, collection), ReturnTypeSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots.Type, required), PrivateImplementationTypeSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots.PrivateImplementationType, nullable), ParametersSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<ParameterDeclaration> pointing at Slots.Parameter, collection), BodySlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement> pointing at Slots.Body, nullable). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): a fresh node, the Modifiers scalar copied via the public Modifiers() getter/setter (the base's private modifiers_ is not accessible from the derived Clone -- the C# MemberwiseClone copies the private backing; the port uses the public surface, the DestructorDeclaration D272 precedent), the OperatorType scalar copied directly to the backing field (the DirectionExpression.FieldDirection D235 scalar-copy precedent -- the field is private to this class, so accessible from the derived Clone), the annotation channel copied (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), the ReturnType deep-cloned through the setter (which re-parents; AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, which ReturnType(AstType*) accepts directly), every Attributes element deep-cloned through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; AttributeSection::Clone() returns AttributeSection*), every Parameters element deep-cloned through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; ParameterDeclaration::Clone() returns ParameterDeclaration*), and the PrivateImplementationType/Body deep-cloned through their setters (which re-parent; AstType::Clone()/BlockStatement::Clone() return the covariant concrete types the setters accept directly). No own location fields (does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the DestructorDeclaration D272 / IndexerDeclaration D279 no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is OperatorDeclaration* (through AstNode*, the AstNode::Clone virtual -- EntityDeclaration re-declares no typed Clone, faithful to its empty hand-written partial). C++ name-shadowing crux (the OperatorType property): the C# property is OperatorType of type OperatorType -- a property named the same as its enum type, the enum equivalent of the Expression-of-type-Expression D231 crux (the DirectionExpression.FieldDirection D235 precedent). The faithful port names the accessor OperatorType(), which SHADOWS the OperatorType enum in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops, even though it is not a type). The getter return type precedes the getter's own declaration, so the plain OperatorType (the enum) is unshadowed in the getter signature; every type usage AFTER the OperatorType() getter (the setter parameter, the backing field type) uses the ELABORATED enum specifier enum OperatorType (basic.lookup.elab ignores non-type names, the enum equivalent of class Expression), and the backing-field initializer uses the fully-qualified enum name (::ILSpy::...::OperatorType::LogicalNot) because the bare OperatorType::LogicalNot would resolve the unqualified OperatorType to the member function and reject ::LogicalNot on a non-type (the D235 precedent). The GetName parameter type is std::optional< ::ILSpy::...::OperatorType > (the fully-qualified name -- a qualified name is looked up in the named namespace, NOT class scope, so it ignores the member-function shadowing; a leading space after < dodges the <: digraph edge case). The DoMatch OperatorType term compares the backing fields directly (operatorType_ == o->operatorType_), so no type name appears and no elaborated specifier is needed there. The other slot accessors (Attributes/ReturnType/PrivateImplementationType/Parameters/Body) do NOT collide with any class in the Syntax namespace (no class named Attributes/ReturnType/PrivateImplementationType/Parameters/Body), so no elaborated specifier is needed for them. NO new Slots constant this iteration: Slots::AttributeSection (cycle-broken in AttributeSection.hpp D241), Slots::Type (D240), Slots::PrivateImplementationType (D276), Slots::Parameter (cycle-broken in ParameterDeclaration.hpp D279), and Slots::Body (cycle-broken in BlockStatement.hpp D260) are all already ported. This is the IndexerDeclaration D279 two-collection shape (the Attributes collection plus the Parameters collection, with three singles interleaved) MINUS the trailing Getter/Setter/ExpressionBody nullable singles and PLUS the OperatorType scalar (a positional/scalar change, not a structural one), so the collection-aware slot-storage dispatch, the MatchOptional/MatchRequired/collection-DoMatch/MatchAttributesAndModifiers machinery, and the covariant Clone all generalize with no new AstNode helper. IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitOperatorDeclaration(OperatorDeclaration*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring OperatorDeclaration before the IAstVisitor class body, the D260 forward-declaration-must-precede-pure-virtual crux) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the OperatorDeclaration.hpp include (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the default -- no breakage). The computed Name/FullName/Identifiers reads, the ConstructType/BuildQualifiedName helpers, and the hand-written (string name) ctor (which calls 'this.Name = name', whose setter uses ConstructType) are DEFERRED: the Name getter consumes the D289-deferred UsingDeclaration.ConstructNamespace (which consumes the D236-deferred AstType.Create factory); the helpers are output/resolver-stage behaviour. A NamespaceDeclaration is built via the empty or (AstType) ctor + IsFileScoped(...) + Members().Add(...) (or AddMember) until ConstructType/ConstructNamespace/AddRange land. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitNamespaceDeclaration(this) (the class name does not end in 'AstType', so the generator's visit-method-name default yields VisitNamespaceDeclaration). The generated slot statics are NamespaceNameSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> pointing at Slots.NamespaceName, required -- the NamespaceName is non-nullable) and MembersSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstNode> pointing at Slots.Member, collection). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): a fresh node, the IsFileScoped scalar copied, the annotation channel copied (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), the NamespaceName deep-cloned through the setter (which re-parents; AstType::Clone() returns AstType*, the covariant override, which NamespaceName(AstType*) accepts directly), and every Members element deep-cloned through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; the element type is the abstract AstNode root, which inherits AstNode::Clone returning AstNode*, so each element's Clone() returns AstNode* which Add(AstNode*) accepts directly -- NO static_cast needed, unlike the ExtensionDeclaration.Members D285 abstract-EntityDeclaration-collection path where EntityDeclaration redeclares no typed Clone; AstNode IS the root and its Clone returns AstNode*). No own location fields (does not derive EndLocation), so the print-time StartLocation/EndLocation are not copied (the Constraint D283 no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is NamespaceDeclaration* (through AstNode*, the AstNode::Clone virtual). NO C++ name-shadowing crux (the IsFileScoped()/NamespaceName()/Members() accessors do NOT collide with any class in the Syntax namespace -- no class named IsFileScoped/NamespaceName/Members; there is NamespaceDeclaration, not NamespaceName; there is MemberType/MemberReferenceExpression, not Member or Members; the AstType/AstNode element types do not collide with any member name), so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed anywhere. This is the cleanest AstNode-root-typed-collection port: no name shadowing, no new AstNode helper (MatchRequired from D231 + the collection DoMatch from D222 already exist). TWO new Slots constants land in Slots.hpp this iteration (no include cycle): Slots::NamespaceName (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType>, the single AstType of the namespace's dotted name) -- the AstType abstract base does NOT include Slots.hpp (the Slots.Type/Target/BaseType/Import precedent), so it lives in Slots.hpp; no Slots variable is named AstType and no class named NamespaceName lives in Syntax, so no elaborated specifier is needed. Slots::Member (a CSharpSlotInfoT<AstNode>, the collection of namespace-body members) -- the AstNode root base does NOT include Slots.hpp (the Slots.ResourceAcquisition D262 AstNode-typed-kind precedent, the only other CSharpSlotInfoT<AstNode>), so it lives in Slots.hpp; this is the FIRST AstNode-typed COLLECTION kind (Slots.ResourceAcquisition was a single slot); no Slots variable is named AstNode and no class named Member lives in Syntax, so no elaborated specifier is needed. The generated ctors: CtorParams in declaration order is [NamespaceName (required single), Members (collection, optional)] -- the IsFileScoped bool is NOT a ctor param (only settable ENUM-typed scalars are). RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 1 (through the last non-optional param NamespaceName at index 0); ConstructorPrefixLengths is {1, 2}. The (len=2) all-params ctor calls this.Members.AddRange(...) (the AddRange convenience, the D222 deferral), so it is DEFERRED; the empty + the (AstType) required-prefix ctors cover the construction API. The (AstType) ctor is explicit (a single-argument ctor is a converting ctor by default), matching the generator's public ctor but avoiding an implicit AstType-to-NamespaceDeclaration conversion (the Constraint D283 / SwitchStatement D268 precedent). IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitNamespaceDeclaration(NamespaceDeclaration*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring NamespaceDeclaration before the class body, the D260 forward-declaration-must-precede-pure-virtual crux handled proactively) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the NamespaceDeclaration.hpp include (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the default -- no breakage). (qualified lookup bypasses the class-scope SymbolKind() shadowing). The (len=5) ctor sets its five params via property setters (no AddRange), so it PORTS; the (len=6) and (len=7) ctors call AddRange for the collections, the D222 deferral, so they are DEFERRED; the empty + the (len=5) required-prefix ctors cover the construction API. The (len=5) ctor is NOT explicit (a multi-arg ctor is not a converting ctor); the two enum scalars are assigned DIRECTLY to the backing fields in the ctor body (not the ambiguous SymbolKind(symbolKind)/OperatorType(operatorType) setter calls that could parse as functional casts of the enums, the DirectionExpression.FieldDirection D235 / VariableDeclarationStatement.Modifiers D270 ambiguity precedent). The generated slot statics are DeclaringTypeSlot (CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> at Slots.DeclaringType, nullable), NameTokenSlot (CSharpSlotInfoT<Identifier> at Slots.Identifier, required), ConversionOperatorReturnTypeSlot (CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> at Slots.ConversionOperatorReturnType, required), TypeArgumentsSlot (CSharpSlotInfoT<AstType> at Slots.TypeArgument, collection), ParametersSlot (CSharpSlotInfoT<ParameterDeclaration> at Slots.Parameter, collection). The covariant return is DocumentationReference* (through AstNode*, the AstNode::Clone virtual). The UndocumentedExpressionType enum (ArgListAccess, ArgList, RefValue, RefType, MakeRef -- five values in C# declaration order, NO Any member) is declared in the same UndocumentedExpression.cs file (the ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.Syntax namespace), so it ports into this header at namespace scope BEFORE the class (the AccessorKind-in-Accessor.hpp D274 / ConstructorInitializerType-in-ConstructorInitializer.hpp D281 / CommentType-in-Comment.hpp D288 precedent). It declares NO Any member, so the generator's hasAny path does NOT fire and the generated DoMatch term is the PLAIN == value equality (the DirectionExpression.FieldDirection D235 / OperatorDeclaration.OperatorType D280 no-Any-enum precedent -- NOT a wildcard, NOT a bitmask test). The zero value ArgListAccess is a REAL kind (the bare __arglist form), NOT a wildcard -- distinct from the ConstructorInitializer D281 whose zero value Any IS the wildcard. The generated DoMatch (WriteDoMatch over MembersToMatch): the generator adds the per-property scan of non-override non-[ExcludeFromMatch] members in source declaration order (UndocumentedExpressionType the scalar, then Arguments the collection), so MembersToMatch is [UndocumentedExpressionType, Arguments], and the generated DoMatch is: return other is UndocumentedExpression o && this.UndocumentedExpressionType == o.UndocumentedExpressionType && this.Arguments.DoMatch(o.Arguments, match). The UndocumentedExpressionType term is the plain == (the enum declares NO Any member); the Arguments term is the collection recursive DoMatch (the generator emits a collection-typed recursive term directly, NOT MatchOptional -- the FieldDeclaration.Variables D273 / ConstructorInitializer.Arguments D281 precedent). A type-only mismatch (not an UndocumentedExpression) rejects early. The generated ctors (WriteConstructors): CtorParams is [UndocumentedExpressionType (enum, required), Arguments (collection, optional)], RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 1 (through the last non-optional param UndocumentedExpressionType), ConstructorPrefixLengths is {1, 2}. The (len=1) ctor (UndocumentedExpressionType) just sets this.UndocumentedExpressionType = type (a plain scalar assignment, no AddRange), so it PORTS (explicit, a single-arg ctor is a converting ctor by default). The (len=2) ctor (UndocumentedExpressionType, IEnumerable<Expression>) and its params overload both call this.Arguments.AddRange(...) (the AddRange convenience is the D222 deferral), so they are DEFERRED. The empty ctor + the (UndocumentedExpressionType) required-prefix ctor cover the generated construction API; an argument list is built via Arguments().Add(...) until AddRange lands. The four const-string keyword tokens (ArglistKeyword = "__arglist", RefvalueKeyword = "__refvalue", ReftypeKeyword = "__reftype", MakerefKeyword = "__makeref") are part of the node's public API (the output visitor emits them), ported as static constexpr const char* (static fields, not instance state, so they are NOT in MembersToMatch/DoMatch -- the CheckedExpression.CheckedKeyword D234 / ConstructorInitializer.BaseKeyword D281 precedent). Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitUndocumentedExpression(this) (the class name does not end in AstType, so the visit-method-name default yields VisitUndocumentedExpression). The generated slot static is ArgumentsSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Expression> pointing at Slots.Argument, collection). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): a fresh node, the UndocumentedExpressionType scalar copied directly to the backing field (the DirectionExpression.FieldDirection D235 / ConstructorInitializer.ConstructorInitializerType D281 scalar-copy precedent -- the field is private to this class, so accessible from the derived Clone), the annotation channel copied (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), and every Arguments element deep-cloned through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; Expression::Clone() returns Expression*, the covariant override, which Add(Expression*) accepts directly). No own location fields (StartLocation/EndLocation are the print-time base fields set by the unported output visitor -- UndocumentedExpression does not derive EndLocation), so they are not copied (the ConstructorInitializer D281 / DestructorDeclaration D272 no-location-copy precedent). The covariant return is UndocumentedExpression* (through Expression*, the Expression::Clone pure-virtual). C++ name-shadowing crux (the UndocumentedExpressionType property): the C# property is UndocumentedExpressionType of type UndocumentedExpressionType -- a property named the same as its enum type, the enum equivalent of the Expression-of-type-Expression D231 crux (the DirectionExpression.FieldDirection D235 / OperatorDeclaration.OperatorType D280 / Comment.CommentType D288 precedent). The faithful port names the accessor UndocumentedExpressionType(), which SHADOWS the UndocumentedExpressionType enum in this class scope (C++ unqualified name lookup finds the member and stops, even though it is not a type). The getter return type precedes the getter's own declaration, so the plain UndocumentedExpressionType (the enum) is unshadowed in the getter signature; every type usage AFTER the UndocumentedExpressionType() getter (the setter parameter, the backing field type) uses the ELABORATED enum specifier enum UndocumentedExpressionType (basic.lookup.elab ignores non-type names, the enum equivalent of class Expression), and the backing-field initializer uses the fully-qualified enum name (::ILSpy::...::UndocumentedExpressionType::ArgListAccess) because the bare UndocumentedExpressionType::ArgListAccess would resolve the unqualified UndocumentedExpressionType to the member function and reject ::ArgListAccess on a non-type (the D235 / D280 / D288 precedent). The DoMatch plain-== term compares the backing fields directly (undocumentedExpressionType_ == o->undocumentedExpressionType_), so no type name appears in the comparison body and no elaborated specifier is needed there. NO new Slots constant for the Arguments collection: Slots::Argument is already ported (by Attribute D240), so the collection reuses it. UndocumentedExpression is not referenced as a slot element type by any other node (it is a leaf expression), so no cycle-broken Slots::UndocumentedExpression kind is needed. The generated DoMatch (WriteDoMatch over MembersToMatch): AnonymousMethodExpression is NOT derived from EntityDeclaration so the explicit MatchAttributesAndModifiers/Name/ReturnType additions are skipped; the per-property scan adds IsAsync (a bool -- the fall-through plain-equality term), Parameters (a collection, RecursiveMatch true -- the collection recursive DoMatch term), Body (a BlockStatement, RecursiveMatch true, Nullable false -- the direct this.Body.DoMatch(o.Body, match) term, which the port routes through AstNode::MatchRequired, the [class.access.derived] workaround, the Accessor D274 / UnaryOperatorExpression Expression D231 precedent). A type-only mismatch (not an AnonymousMethodExpression) rejects early. The generated ctors (WriteConstructors): CtorParams is [Parameters (collection, optional), Body (single, required)] -- the IsAsync bool is NOT a ctor param. RequiredConstructorPrefixLength is 2 (through the last non-optional param Body). ConstructorPrefixLengths is {2} (reqLen 2, then no collection at-or-after reqLen since Parameters precedes the required Body (its index 0 + 1 = 1 < reqLen 2), then cp.Count 2). The (len=2) ctor body calls this.Parameters.AddRange(...) for the collection (the AddRange convenience is the D222 deferral), so it is DEFERRED; the empty ctor is the only portable ctor. An AnonymousMethodExpression is built via the empty ctor + Parameters().Add(...) + Body(...) + IsAsync(...) until AddRange lands. Per PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1 the concrete node is hand-translated from the generated output. The generated AcceptVisitor calls visitor.VisitAnonymousMethodExpression(this) (the class name does not end in AstType, so the visit-method-name default yields VisitAnonymousMethodExpression). The generated slot statics are ParametersSlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<ParameterDeclaration> pointing at Slots.Parameter, collection -- the node's only collection) and BodySlot (a CSharpSlotInfoT<BlockStatement> pointing at Slots.Body, required -- the Body BlockStatement is non-nullable). Clone is inherited in C# (MemberwiseClone + CloneChildrenInto); the port overrides it (no MemberwiseClone): a fresh node, the IsAsync scalar copied, the annotation channel copied (CloneAnnotationsFrom + ReparentTrivia, the D223 concrete-clone pattern), every Parameters element deep-cloned through Add (which re-parents and re-indexes; ParameterDeclaration::Clone() returns ParameterDeclaration*, which Add(ParameterDeclaration*) accepts directly), and the Body deep-cloned through the setter (which re-parents; BlockStatement::Clone() returns BlockStatement*, which Body(BlockStatement*) accepts directly -- the slot is typed the concrete BlockStatement so no cast, the Accessor D274 / MethodDeclaration D284 concrete-body precedent). The Body is skipped if absent (Clone tolerates a missing Body even though the slot is required -- the invariant is enforced by CheckInvariant, not by Clone, the LambdaExpression D305 / CastExpression D243 precedent). The covariant return is AnonymousMethodExpression* (through Expression*, the Expression::Clone pure-virtual). NO C++ name-shadowing crux (no member is named ParameterDeclaration/BlockStatement -- the Parameters()/Body()/IsAsync() accessors do not collide with any class in the Syntax namespace, and the Body accessor does not collide with the BlockStatement type -- a member named Body is not the name BlockStatement), so no elaborated-type-specifier is needed anywhere; the plain element types resolve to the classes. ONE new Slots constant in Slots.hpp: Slots::SubPattern (a CSharpSlotInfoT<Expression> collection kind, the SubPatterns position); Slots::Type (by Attribute D240) and Slots::VariableDesignation (by ParenthesizedVariableDesignation D264) are both already ported, so they are reused with no new constant. The Slots::SubPattern kind lives in Slots.hpp with no include cycle since Expression.hpp (the abstract base) does NOT include Slots.hpp (the Slots.Argument/Slots.Pattern precedent), and is defined AFTER the Slots::Expression variable so the element type is qualified to avoid resolving to that variable. IAstVisitor.hpp gains the VisitRecursivePatternExpression(RecursivePatternExpression*) pure-virtual (forward-declaring RecursivePatternExpression before the class body, the D260 forward-declaration-must-precede-pure-virtual crux handled proactively) and DepthFirstAstVisitor.hpp gains the matching VisitChildren-default override plus the RecursivePatternExpression.hpp include (additive, satisfied for every existing IAstVisitor subclass by the default -- no breakage). an empty node records just the node tag), the four-term DoMatch (matches same; rejects Type asymmetry; rejects Type mismatch; rejects SubPatterns count mismatch; rejects SubPatterns element mismatch; rejects Designation asymmetry; rejects Designation mismatch; rejects IsPositional mismatch; matches two bare patterns -- both MatchOptional terms true when both absent, empty collection matches, plain-bool matches; rejects a NullReferenceExpression candidate; rejects an ObjectCreateExpression cross-structural-twin candidate -- both share the single + non-incremental collection + trailing-nullable-single shape but distinct concrete types; rejects null candidate), Clone (deep-copies Type + SubPatterns + Designation + the IsPositional scalar; virtual through AstNode*/Expression*; covariant through RecursivePatternExpression*; non-detach-source;
