| D318 | CSharpKeywordCheck.IsKeyword free helper (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpKeywordCheck.hpp, the port of the CSharpOutputVisitor.IsKeyword(string identifier, AstNode? context = null) static helper in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.cs -- the third in-order Phase-5 piece of the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage per the D317 plan which named the IsKeyword-factoring as the resolution of the TextWriterTokenWriter.WriteIdentifier -> CSharpOutputVisitor.IsKeyword tangle) | port | Ports the IsKeyword helper (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpKeywordCheck.hpp mirroring the #region IsKeyword Test block of CSharpOutputVisitor.cs) as a FREE FUNCTION in the ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::OutputVisitor namespace -- the factored-out CSharpOutputVisitor.IsKeyword static helper that decides whether an identifier token must be rendered with a leading @ (the verbatim-identifier prefix) because its name is a reserved C# keyword in the identifier's context. It is consumed by TextWriterTokenWriter.WriteIdentifier (the concrete token writer that writes tokens to an std::ostream, not yet ported) and by the location-setting decorator's identifier handling; factoring it out lets the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter land before the 97k-line CSharpOutputVisitor pretty-printer (the D317 plan's "port IsKeyword as a free helper" resolution of the tangle where TextWriterTokenWriter.WriteIdentifier otherwise references the not-yet-ported CSharpOutputVisitor.IsKeyword). When CSharpOutputVisitor lands it can expose a static IsKeyword that forwards to this free function (the canonical implementation), or the call sites can be redirected here; the behaviour is identical either way. The helper consults three keyword classes: the 77 UNCONDITIONAL keywords (reserved in every context, abstract..while); the 13 CONTEXTUAL query keywords (from/where/join/on/equals/into/let/orderby/ascending/descending/select/group/by), reserved only inside a query expression (a QueryExpression ancestor), and treated as unconditional with a null context (the C# context == null or context.Ancestors.Any(a => a is QueryExpression)); and the contextual await keyword, reserved only inside an async lambda / anonymous method / member declaration (a LambdaExpression or AnonymousMethodExpression ancestor whose IsAsync is set, or an EntityDeclaration ancestor whose Modifiers carries Async), and treated as unconditional with a null context. Every dependency the helper consults is already ported: AstNode::Ancestors() (the parent chain, D221), QueryExpression (D294/D310), LambdaExpression.IsAsync (D305), AnonymousMethodExpression.IsAsync (D306), EntityDeclaration.Modifiers() (D272), and the Modifiers::Async flag (D270). C#-to-C++ porting decisions: (1) the C# static readonly HashSet<string> keyword tables port as function-local static const std::unordered_set<std::string_view> initialized from string-literal views -- the literals have static storage duration so the views the set stores remain valid for the program lifetime, and a lookup with a std::string_view key (an identifier's Name) is zero-allocation and zero-copy (C++17 has std::hash<std::string_view>, so unordered_set<string_view> hashes the view directly, unlike an unordered_set<std::string> which would allocate on every lookup); this is the faithful equivalent of the C# HashSet<string>.Contains; (2) the C# static readonly int maxKeywordLength = unconditionalKeywords.Concat(queryKeywords).Max(s => s.Length) ports as a function-local static const int computed once by iterating both sets (the same computation, lazily initialized on first call -- thread-safe under the C++11+ function-local static init rule); (3) the C# string identifier parameter ports as std::string_view (read-only, zero-copy); (4) the C# AstNode? context = null parameter ports as AstNode* context = nullptr; (5) the C# identifier[0] < 'a' gate ports with an unsigned char cast -- the C# char is an unsigned 16-bit code unit, so a non-ASCII first byte (a negative signed char in C++) would wrongly trip the < 'a' gate without the cast; the observable result is the same either way (a non-ASCII-starting identifier is never a keyword), but the cast keeps the gate's semantics faithful to the C# unsigned comparison; (6) the C# context.Ancestors.Any(ancestor => ancestor is QueryExpression) ports as a walk over the ported AstNode::Ancestors() vector with a dynamic_cast<QueryExpression*> is-a test (the faithful C# is); the await branch likewise walks Ancestors() with dynamic_cast<LambdaExpression*>/dynamic_cast<AnonymousMethodExpression*>/dynamic_cast<EntityDeclaration*> is-a tests, the first such ancestor encountered deciding (a lambda/anonymous method's IsAsync, or a member declaration's (Modifiers & Async) == Async), matching the C# foreach-over-Ancestors first-match-wins order. NO C++ name-shadowing crux (the IsKeyword free function name does not collide with any class in the OutputVisitor or Syntax namespaces). NO new Slots constant, NO new enum, NO new AstNode helper (this is the output-stage helper, not an AST node). Namespace mapping ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.OutputVisitor -> ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::OutputVisitor (the convention), with the Syntax node types it consults (AstNode/EntityDeclaration/LambdaExpression/AnonymousMethodExpression/QueryExpression/Modifiers) brought in by using-declarations. Header-only (no CMake source listing -- the TokenWriter/CSharpFormattingOptions header-only precedent), so the CSharp CMakeLists.txt is unchanged; only the test .cpp is added to tests/CMakeLists.txt. TDD: 18 gtest cases in one suite (CSharp_KeywordCheck) in cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpKeywordCheck_Test.cpp wired into tests/CMakeLists.txt, covering the unconditional keywords (a sampling incl. the longest stackalloc/unchecked/typeof) with a null context, the non-keywords (foo/Math/myVar/System/int32/asyncMethod), the length gate (empty and single-char and an 11-char-lowercase non-keyword -- maxKeywordLength is 10, the longest keyword descending), the first-char gate (If/Class/ABSTRACT/1abc/@foo -- uppercase/digit/symbol starts are rejected before any set lookup since the tables are all lowercase), the query keywords with a null context (treated as unconditional), a query keyword with a non-null context whose ancestors do NOT include a QueryExpression (a standalone QueryWhereClause with an empty ancestor chain -> not a keyword), a query keyword inside a QueryExpression (a QueryExpression with a QueryWhereClause child added to its Clauses -> the clause's ancestor chain is [QueryExpression] -> keyword), an unconditional keyword inside a query (still a keyword -- the unconditional set is checked before the context-dependent branches), await with a null context (unconditional), await with no async ancestor (a standalone ParameterDeclaration -> not a keyword), await inside an async lambda (keyword), await inside a sync lambda (not), await inside an async anonymous method (keyword), await inside a sync anonymous method (not), await inside an async member declaration (a MethodDeclaration with Modifiers::Async -> keyword), await inside a sync member declaration (Modifiers::None -> not), and the default context = nullptr argument (a bare IsKeyword("await") call is equivalent to IsKeyword("await", nullptr)). | D319 | TextWriterTokenWriter (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/TextWriterTokenWriter.hpp, the port of the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/TextWriterTokenWriter.cs -- the fourth in-order Phase-5 piece of the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage per the D318 plan which named the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter as the next-in-order piece now that the IsKeyword free helper D318 cleared the WriteIdentifier tangle) | port | Ports the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/TextWriterTokenWriter.hpp mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/TextWriterTokenWriter.cs) -- the sink the CSharpOutputVisitor (the pretty-printer, not yet ported) drives a C# AST tree through to produce the decompiled text, and the concrete implementation of the TokenWriter abstract base (D316) that writes the token stream to an std::ostream. The C# writes to a System.IO.TextWriter; this port writes to an std::ostream (the C# TextWriter -> std::ostream port). It tracks the current Indentation/line/column so it can report Location/Length (it implements ILocatable, the role the location-setting decorator reads to record spans back onto the AST nodes), and it renders literal values via the PrimitiveValue variant (the D228 boxed-literal model). Every dependency it consults is already ported: the TokenWriter/ILocatable bases (D316), the IsKeyword free helper (D318, the @-prefix-on-keyword check in WriteIdentifier), the Identifier node (D227, Name()/IsVerbatim()), the CommentType enum (D288), the PreProcessorDirectiveType enum (D294), the LiteralFormat enum and PrimitiveValue variant (D228), the DecimalValue model (D228, ToString()), the TextLocation value type (D218), and the AstNode base (D220). C#-to-C++ porting decisions: (1) the C# readonly TextWriter textWriter ports as a non-owning std::ostream* member (null-checked in the ctor -- the C# ArgumentNullException -> std::invalid_argument, the DecoratingTokenWriter D316 precedent; a pointer rather than a reference so the null-check can throw before any deref); (2) the C# TextWriter.NewLine (the line terminator string, Environment.NewLine on the build platform) ports as a fixed "\r\n" (the Windows Environment.NewLine the ILSpy test suite assumes; the Length accounting is 2 per newline) held as a static constexpr std::string_view so the accounting is deterministic across platforms; (3) the C# char/string text (a UTF-16 code unit / a System.String) ports as std::string/std::string_view (the port stores text as UTF-8 bytes, the standard C++ convention); the C# escape helpers (ConvertChar/ConvertString/EscapeIdentifier/IsPrintableIdentifierChar) classify each code point via char.GetUnicodeCategory (a UTF-16 code unit -> a Unicode category); this port decodes the UTF-8 to a char32_t code point and classifies the ASCII range faithfully (the control range, the named escapes, the explicitly-allowed space/underscore/backtick/caret), and for non-ASCII it escapes only surrogates and the non-character code points and passes everything else through as raw UTF-8 -- a documented divergence, since the C# also escapes marks/separators/format/private-use/etc. via the category database, which is not available in the C++ port; for the decompiler's typical ASCII output this divergence does not arise (the output remains valid UTF-8); (4) the C# decimal.ToString(Invariant) ports as DecimalValue::ToString() (the D228 faithful System.Decimal model already formats invariantly) + the "m" suffix; (5) the C# float/double.ToString("R", Invariant) (the shortest round-trip representation) ports as std::to_chars (the C++17 shortest-round-trip, the same goal as the C# "R" format) with the exponent marker upper-cased to 'E' to match the C# "R" output; the negative-zero special case (the 1/f == NegativeInfinity check) is handled faithfully; the infinity/NaN cases render float.PositiveInfinity/NegativeInfinity/NaN (and the double. forms) literally -- these are not strictly PrimitiveExpression values but the C# writer supports them for code generators; (6) the C# int/uint/long/ulong.ToString(null, Invariant) ports as std::to_string (invariant), and ToString("X", Invariant) ports as std::snprintf("%X", unsigned-cast) (the uppercase hex of the two's-complement value, matching the C# "X" format), with the u/L/uL suffixes the C# IFormattable branch appends per type; (7) the C# public static string PrintPrimitiveValue(object value) (build a StringWriter, drive a TextWriterTokenWriter, return the string) ports as a static method building an std::ostringstream; (8) the C# public static escape helpers (ConvertCharLiteral/ConvertString/EscapeIdentifier/ContainsNonPrintableIdentifierChar) port as public static methods on the class (the public API the output visitor and the tests consult), with the private helpers (ConvertChar/IsPrintableIdentifierChar/UpdateEndLocation) in a detail namespace or as a private static. NO C++ name-shadowing crux (the TextWriterTokenWriter method/member names do not collide with any class in the Syntax or OutputVisitor namespaces). NO new Slots constant, NO new enum, NO new AstNode helper (this is the output-stage concrete sink, not an AST node). FOUR test-side/build cruxes on the first builds (NONE were node-header cruxes -- the header itself compiled cleanly once the DecimalValue using was added): (1) the D316 default-arg-on-pure-virtual crux RECURRED -- the WritePrimitiveValue override does NOT repeat the LiteralFormat::None default (it applies only through a TokenWriter& base reference, NOT through the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter type), so the 1-arg calls in the test and in PrintPrimitiveValue failed MSVC C2660 until the format was passed explicitly (the test) or the call routed through static_cast<TokenWriter&>(w) (PrintPrimitiveValue); this is the recurring gotcha for every C# abstract method with a default argument ported to a C++ pure-virtual, now confirmed across the TokenWriter (D316) and the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter; (2) DecimalValue was not in scope in the OutputVisitor namespace (TokenWriter.hpp brings only PrimitiveValue via using, NOT DecimalValue), surfacing as MSVC C2065 at the WritePrimitiveValue decimal branch -- fixed by adding a using Syntax::DecimalValue declaration in the header (the first port that names DecimalValue in the OutputVisitor scope); (3) TextLocation::Line is a PUBLIC FIELD not a method (the D218 design), so h.w.Location().Line() (with parens) hit MSVC C2064 -- the recurring ChildIndex-is-a-field gotcha, fixed by removing the parens (.Line); (4) the Identifier(std::string) ctor is PRIVATE (only the default ctor and the Create factories are public), so std::make_unique<Identifier>("") failed -- fixed by using the public default ctor std::make_unique<Identifier>() for the StartNode stub (the D241/D257 Identifier-Create-is-the-public-API precedent). The CRLF-append crux also recurred: a python text-mode write (open(p,'w')) on Windows converts \n to \r\n (the platform default), turning a LF-joined file CRLF; the reliable method is a binary-mode write (open(p,'wb')) with an explicit \n join, which preserves the LF convention. | D320 | InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.hpp, the port of InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.cs -- the fifth in-order Phase-5 piece of the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage per the D319 plan which named the two decorator writers as the next-in-order pieces now that the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter D319 is in place) | port | Ports the InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.hpp mirroring InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.cs) -- the DecoratingTokenWriter (D316) subclass that inserts the minimal amount of whitespace so the lexer recognizes the tokens the CSharpOutputVisitor (not yet ported) emits. The output visitor does not emit every inter-token space (it leaves them to this decorator); this decorator tracks the LastWritten kind of the most recently written token and inserts a Space() only where the next token would otherwise merge with the previous one into a single lexeme (two + tokens into ++, a keyword followed by an identifier, an identifier followed by a number that could be read as a type suffix, a division operator followed by a slash-star comment or a slash-slash line comment, etc.). Every dependency it consults is already ported: the DecoratingTokenWriter/TokenWriter bases (D316), the IsKeyword free helper (D318, the @-prefix check in WriteIdentifier), the Identifier node (D227, Name()/IsVerbatim()), the CommentType enum (D288), the PreProcessorDirectiveType enum (D294), the LiteralFormat enum and PrimitiveValue variant (D228, with the DecimalValue System.Decimal model and the float/double/integer alternatives). C#-to-C++ porting decisions: (1) the C# LastWritten private nested enum ports as a private nested enum class with the same members (Whitespace/Other/KeywordOrIdentifier/Plus/Minus/Ampersand/QuestionMark/Division); lastWritten ports as lastWritten_ (private, trailing-underscore, the TextWriterTokenWriter convention), default Whitespace; (2) WriteIdentifier(Identifier) -> WriteIdentifier(Identifier*) (non-owning-pointer convention; the Identifier header is included so Name()/IsVerbatim() are available); CSharpOutputVisitor.IsKeyword(identifier.Name, identifier) -> IsKeyword(identifier->Name(), identifier) (the D318 free helper; the std::string Name() implicitly binds to the std::string_view parameter); (3) the C# Space() (unqualified, the virtual override) vs base.Space() distinction is preserved: the override sets lastWritten_ = Whitespace AND forwards; base.Space() (the DecoratingTokenWriter::Space() qualified call) just forwards without touching lastWritten_. WriteIdentifier's strictly-required-space branch (the non-verbatim, non-keyword identifier after a keyword/identifier) uses base.Space(), every other not-strictly-required branch uses Space() (the override) -- faithfully mirroring the C# comment 'this space is not strictly required, so we call Space()' vs 'this space is strictly required, so we directly call the formatter'; (4) the WritePrimitiveValue override does NOT repeat the LiteralFormat::None default (the D316 default-arg-on-pure-virtual crux: a default argument on a pure-virtual is resolved at the static call-site type, so the base's default applies only through a TokenWriter& reference, not the concrete override type; the override takes format by value and forwards it explicitly); (5) the C# value is bool/is string/is char/is decimal/is float/is double/is IFormattable type tests port to std::holds_alternative<T> on the PrimitiveValue variant (std::monostate is the C# null, char16_t is the C# char, DecimalValue is the C# decimal, IFormattable is the integer alternatives int32/uint32/int64/uint64); float.IsInfinity/IsNaN port to std::isinf/std::isnan (cmath); the null and bool cases return without setting lastWritten (faithful to the C#); the AnyValueTag fall-through (the pattern wildcard, never written by the output visitor) ports as the else->Other branch; (6) the C# token[0] first-char comparison ports to token.front() guarded by !token.empty() (the C# would throw on an empty token; the C++ string_view::front on empty is UB, so a defensive empty guard avoids it -- the decompiler never writes an empty token, so the observable behavior is unchanged for valid input). NO C++ name-shadowing crux. NO new Slots constant, NO new enum beyond the private LastWritten, NO new AstNode helper. RESULT: 38 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.* run is 38/38 green); the full suite is 5620 to 5658 tests (250 to 251 test suites -- +1 suite, +38 tests, exactly matching the new suite's test count) with 0 regressions (the 5620 prior tests pass unchanged -- InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.hpp is a NEW header not included by any existing test or source, so only the new test file changed; the full 5658-test run is 5658/5658 green); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly and is byte-identical via include-graph isolation (InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator.hpp is included ONLY by the new test file, NOT by any engine/CLI .cpp or any other Decompiler/ source -- confirmed by grep: the only matches in Decompiler/ are comment mentions in TokenWriter.hpp, NOT includes; ILAstToCSharp.cpp and ILSpyCmd reference neither InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator nor its header; the D224-D319 grep-based isolation precedent; mscorlib.dll is not present so the decompile-signature check is deferred to the grep-based isolation). The next-in-order Phase-5 piece of the output stage is the InsertMissingTokensDecorator (the second DecoratingTokenWriter subclass, the one that records source spans back onto the AST nodes -- its EndNode re-attaches 'missing' child nodes via Slot.Kind + Remove + AddChildUnsafe, and its WriteToken/WriteKeyword/WriteIdentifier/WritePrimitiveValue/WritePrimitiveType overrides assign pending start locations; every dependency it consults is already ported: the TokenWriter/DecoratingTokenWriter/ILocatable bases D316, AstNode.StorePrintStart/StorePrintEnd/Slot/Remove/AddChildUnsafe/LeadingTrivia/TrailingTrivia/StartLocation D220-D224, the node-specific SetStartLocation/SetLocation/Location setters on Identifier/Comment/EmptyStatement/ErrorExpression/PrimitiveExpression/NullReferenceExpression/ThisReferenceExpression/BaseReferenceExpression/PrimitiveType -- the Trivia branch in StartNode/EndNode needs a dynamic_cast<Trivia*> or a virtual IsTriviaNode, the one piece to resolve), then the CSharpOutputVisitor itself (the 97k-line pretty-printer implementing a Visit method per ported node, landable incrementally one node-family at a time now that the TokenWriter sink D316, the CSharpFormattingOptions settings D317, the IsKeyword helper D318, the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter D319, and the InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator are all in place); the four deferred TokenWriter static factories land once both decorators are ported. | D321 | InsertMissingTokensDecorator (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/InsertMissingTokensDecorator.hpp, the port of InsertMissingTokensDecorator in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/InsertMissingTokensDecorator.cs -- the sixth in-order Phase-5 piece of the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage per the D320 plan which named this decorator as the next-in-order piece now that the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter D319 and InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator D320 are in place) | port | Ports the InsertMissingTokensDecorator (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/InsertMissingTokensDecorator.hpp mirroring InsertMissingTokensDecorator.cs) -- the DecoratingTokenWriter (D316) subclass that records source spans back onto the AST nodes as the CSharpOutputVisitor (not yet ported) drives the token stream through it. The output visitor calls StartNode/EndNode around every node and WriteIdentifier/WriteKeyword/WriteToken/WritePrimitiveValue/WritePrimitiveType for the tokens each node prints; this decorator intercepts those calls to set each node's StartLocation/EndLocation to the span of the tokens it actually printed (a node that prints no token collapses to a zero-width span at the end of the previous token), to handle the Comment/ErrorExpression/EmptyStatement/ThisReferenceExpression/BaseReferenceExpression/PrimitiveExpression/NullReferenceExpression/PrimitiveType/Identifier special cases, and to re-attach the printed children to their parent by slot kind (the output visitor prints children in document order; the decorator re-establishes the parent/child relationships the slot system expects). Every dependency it consults is already ported: the DecoratingTokenWriter/TokenWriter/ILocatable bases (D316), the AstNode span/mutation API StorePrintStart/StorePrintEnd/Slot/Remove/AddChildUnsafe/LeadingTrivia/TrailingTrivia (D220/D223/D224), the Trivia base SetStartLocation/SetEndLocation (D224), the Comment node (D288), the ErrorExpression Location setter (D298), the EmptyStatement Location setter and trivia lists (D259), the ThisReferenceExpression/BaseReferenceExpression/NullReferenceExpression/PrimitiveType StorePrintStart (D226/D236), the Identifier SetStartLocation (D227), the PrimitiveExpression SetLocation (D228), the TextLocation value type (D218), the CSharpSlotInfo slot/Kind (D220). C#-to-C++ porting decisions: (1) the C# Stack<List<AstNode>> nodes / List<AstNode> currentList port to std::stack<std::vector<AstNode*>> nodes_ / std::vector<AstNode*> currentList_. The C# pushes a REFERENCE to currentList then reassigns currentList to a fresh list; the port copies currentList_ onto the stack (nodes_.push(currentList_)) then clears it (currentList_.clear()). The stack entries are only ever READ after the push (the C# nodes.Peek().LastOrDefault() is read-only, never nodes.Peek().Add(...)), so the value-semantics copy is observationally identical to the C# reference share -- the contents at every point are the same. EndNode restores currentList_ from the stack via std::move(nodes_.top()); nodes_.pop(); (move to avoid a second copy); (2) the C# HashSet<AstNode> nodesAwaitingStartLocation ports to std::unordered_set<AstNode*> (pointer identity, the faithful HashSet reference-equality). Count -> empty(), Add -> insert, Remove (returns whether present) -> erase (returns count erased, 0 or 1), Clear -> clear(). The iteration order does not matter (every awaiting node receives the SAME location); (3) the C# node is not Trivia / node is Comment comment / node is ErrorExpression error / node is EmptyStatement emptyStatement / ... as ThisReferenceExpression type tests port to dynamic_cast (the established is-a convention). The node is not Trivia test is a plain is-a check (NOT a sibling/slot navigation), so dynamic_cast<Trivia*>(node) == nullptr is the faithful port -- this does NOT conflict with the D224 deferral, which kept the trivia SIBLING/SLOT branches in AstNode's navigation methods dropped (trivia is reached through the LeadingTrivia/TrailingTrivia lists, not the sibling space); a plain is-a test on a node pointer is a different concern. This is the resolution the D320 note flagged (dynamic_cast<Trivia*> vs a virtual IsTriviaNode); (4) the C# nodes.Peek().LastOrDefault() (the last node in the top/parent list, or null) ports to a private TopLastOrDefault() helper returning nullptr for an empty stack or an empty top vector (the C# Peek() throws on an empty stack, but the output visitor always StartNodes the root before writing tokens, so the stack is never empty in practice; the defensive nullptr return is a graceful no-op for an unexpected empty stack rather than UB -- dynamic_cast on null returns null); (5) the C# emptyStatement.LeadingTrivia.Concat(emptyStatement.TrailingTrivia).FirstOrDefault(t => !t.StartLocation.IsEmpty) ports to two sequential range-for loops (leading then trailing), each returning the first trivia whose StartLocation().IsEmpty() is false -- the faithful Concat+FirstOrDefault semantics (leading is searched before trailing, the first non-empty-location trivia wins, or null if none); (6) the C# child.Slot is not { } slot guard (skip a parentless print-only artifact with no slot) ports to const CSharpSlotInfo* slot = child->Slot(); if (slot == nullptr) continue; (the C# Slot is null when the child is unparented). The slot.Kind! (the canonical Slots kind, null-forgiving) ports to slot->Kind(); a parented child's per-node slot always points at a non-null canonical kind, so the null-forgiving assertion holds; (7) the WritePrimitiveValue override does NOT repeat the LiteralFormat::None default (the D316 default-arg-on-pure-virtual crux: a default argument on a pure-virtual is resolved at the static call-site type, so the base's default applies only through a TokenWriter& reference, not the concrete override type; the override takes format by value and forwards it explicitly). NO C++ name-shadowing crux. NO new Slots constant, NO new enum, NO new AstNode helper. Namespace mapping ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.OutputVisitor -> ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::OutputVisitor. | D322 | TokenWriter static factories (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/TokenWriter.cpp, the four deferred `TokenWriter.Create` / `CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` / `InsertRequiredSpaces` / `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` static methods declared in TokenWriter.hpp, the seventh in-order Phase-5 piece of the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage per the D321 plan which named these factories as the next-in-order piece now that the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter D319 and both decorators D320/D321 are in place) | port | Ports the four `TokenWriter` static factory functions declared in `OutputVisitor/TokenWriter.hpp` (the D316-deferred surface, now unblocked by the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter D319, InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator D320, and InsertMissingTokensDecorator D321 ports). The C# `ITokenWriter.cs` declares these as `public static TokenWriter Create(TextWriter, string indentation = "\t")` / `CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST(...)` / `InsertRequiredSpaces(TokenWriter)` / `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST(TokenWriter)` on `TokenWriter`; the C++ port keeps them as `static std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>` methods on the `TokenWriter` class (preserving the `TokenWriter::Create(...)` call shape the CSharpOutputVisitor ctor uses) with the definitions out-of-line in a new `TokenWriter.cpp` (the AstNode.cpp D223 out-of-line precedent for header methods that reference a type whose full definition lives in an including header -- defining them inline in the interface header would pull the concrete TextWriterTokenWriter/InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator/InsertMissingTokensDecorator headers into TokenWriter.hpp and form an include cycle, since those headers include TokenWriter.hpp). The C# `System.IO.TextWriter` parameter of `Create`/`CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` ports to `std::ostream*` (the D319 TextWriter->std::ostream port); the C# object initializer `{ IndentationString = indentation }` ports to a post-ctor `IndentationString(std::move(indentation))` setter call. The central C#-to-C++ porting crux is OWNERSHIP: the C# factories return the top of the composed stack and rely on the GC to own the whole stack (the decorator holds a non-owning reference to its inner writer); the C++ port returns a `std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>` owning handle so the caller owns the stack it composes. The two `Create` factories compose a FRESH stack from a new TextWriterTokenWriter, so the port makes the outermost decorator OWN its inner writer via a new OWNING-MODE ctor on `DecoratingTokenWriter` (a protected `explicit DecoratingTokenWriter(std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>)` that takes ownership into a new `std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter> ownedWriter_` member and sets the existing non-owning `decoratedWriter_` pointer to the owned writer, so the forwarding overrides work unchanged); a single `std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>` handle to the top then owns every layer (destroying it destroys the whole stack, the faithful equivalent of the GC collecting the stack from the top). `ownedWriter_` is declared BEFORE `decoratedWriter_` so the owning ctor initializer list (`ownedWriter_(...), decoratedWriter_(ownedWriter_.get())`) initializes in declaration order (C++ initializes members in declaration order, not initializer-list order); the non-owning ctor leaves `ownedWriter_` empty (it default-constructs first, then `decoratedWriter_` is set from the raw pointer). The two `Insert`/`Wrap` factories wrap a CALLER-OWNED writer, so the port returns a handle that owns ONLY the new decorator (the non-owning inner pointer is faithful -- the caller keeps the original writer alive for the decorator lifetime, exactly as in C#). Each concrete decorator gains a public OWNING ctor delegating to the base owning ctor (`InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator(std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>)` and `InsertMissingTokensDecorator(std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>, ILocatable*)`), distinguished from the existing non-owning ctors by parameter type (`std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>` vs `TokenWriter*`, no ambiguity since `std::unique_ptr`'s pointer ctor is explicit so a raw pointer never implicitly converts). `CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` composes TextWriterTokenWriter then InsertMissingTokensDecorator then InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (the outer owns the middle owns the inner); the `ILocatable*` location-provider is grabbed from the TextWriterTokenWriter via `static_cast<ILocatable*>(target.get())` (TextWriterTokenWriter IS-A ILocatable) BEFORE the writer is moved into the decorator -- the writer object persists inside the decorator's `ownedWriter_`, so the pointer stays valid for the decorator lifetime. `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST`'s `if (!(writer is ILocatable)) throw new InvalidOperationException(...)` ports to a `dynamic_cast<ILocatable*>(writer)` cross-cast (returns non-null iff the writer's runtime type derives from ILocatable -- `TokenWriter` and `ILocatable` are unrelated bases, so this is a cross-cast) and a `std::logic_error` (the closest standard exception to `InvalidOperationException`, a method call invalid for the object current state). Every dependency is already ported: the TokenWriter/DecoratingTokenWriter/ILocatable bases (D316), TextWriterTokenWriter (D319), InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (D320), InsertMissingTokensDecorator (D321). NO C++ name-shadowing crux (the factory method names do not collide with any class; the `InsertRequiredSpaces` static method and the `InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator` class have distinct names). NO new Slots constant, NO new enum, NO new AstNode helper. Namespace mapping ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.OutputVisitor -> ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::OutputVisitor. NOT header-only (the first OutputVisitor .cpp -- the AstNode.cpp D223 out-of-line precedent), so `OutputVisitor/TokenWriter.cpp` is added to the CSharp `CMakeLists.txt` `target_sources(ilspy PRIVATE ...)` list; the new test `.cpp` is added to `tests/CMakeLists.txt`. TDD: 13 gtest cases in one suite (TokenWriterFactories) in cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/TokenWriterFactories_Test.cpp (a minimal RecordingTokenWriter : TokenWriter that is NOT ILocatable, used to exercise the `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` rejection; a real TextWriterTokenWriter, which IS-A ILocatable, for the success cases), wired into tests/CMakeLists.txt, covering: `Create` writes through the spaces-only pipeline (keyword then identifier yields `class Foo` with the strictly-required space inserted by the decorator), `Create` applies a custom two-space IndentationString (the C# object initializer ports to a post-ctor setter -- an indented second line), `Create` does NOT record locations (no InsertMissingTokensDecorator in the stack -- the discriminator vs the location-recording factory), `Create` owns the whole two-layer stack and destroys it cleanly (scope-exit destruction leaves the caller stream intact, the writer never owned the std::ostream), `CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` records an identifier span (the InsertMissingTokensDecorator records StartLocation), `CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` writes through the whole three-layer stack, `CreateWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` owns the whole three-layer stack and destroys it cleanly, `InsertRequiredSpaces` wraps a CALLER-OWNED writer (writes flow through, the inner writer survives the decorator destruction -- the non-owning contract), `InsertRequiredSpaces` returns a `std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter>` convertible handle (the type the CSharpOutputVisitor ctor will store), `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` wraps a CALLER-OWNED ILocatable writer and records a span (the inner reads the writer ILocatable subobject), `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` throws std::logic_error on a non-ILocatable writer (the dynamic_cast cross-cast returns null -- a RecordingTokenWriter that is only a TokenWriter), `WrapInWriterThatSetsLocationsInAST` throws std::logic_error on a null writer (dynamic_cast on null returns null), and `InsertRequiredSpaces` throws std::invalid_argument on a null writer (the DecoratingTokenWriter base null-check). | D323 | CSharpOutputVisitor infrastructure skeleton + Tokens + CSharpModifiers (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.{hpp,cpp} the port of the infrastructure of CSharpOutputVisitor in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.cs, plus cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Tokens.hpp the port of Tokens.cs and the CSharpModifiers AllModifiers/GetModifierName helper completing the D270 deferral in cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Modifiers.hpp -- the eighth in-order Phase-5 piece of the OutputVisitor/ITextOutput/TokenWriter output stage per the D322 plan which named the CSharpOutputVisitor ctor as the next-in-order piece now that the four TokenWriter composition factories D322 are in place) | port | Ports the CSharpOutputVisitor infrastructure skeleton (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.{hpp,cpp} mirroring ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.cs) -- the pretty-printer that renders a C# AST tree to text by driving a TokenWriter through a stream of StartNode/WriteKeyword/WriteToken/WriteIdentifier/Space/NewLine/EndNode calls; the class implements IAstVisitor (one Visit method per concrete AST node, dispatched from AstNode::AcceptVisitor). This iteration ports the INFRASTRUCTURE (the machinery every per-node Visit method builds on): the two ctors (the ostream ctor composing a TokenWriter::Create(ostream, indent) stack the visitor owns, and the TokenWriter ctor wrapping a caller-owned writer in an InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator the visitor owns), the writer/policy/containerStack fields and the isAtStartOfLine/isAfterSpace inter-token state, the StartNode/EndNode nesting (push/pop the node stack, drive the writer, walk the node leading/trailing trivia), the Comma family (Comma, the template WriteCommaSeparatedList/WriteCommaSeparatedListInParenthesis, the two WriteCommaSeparatedListInBrackets overloads), the token writers (WriteKeyword/WriteIdentifier(Identifier*)/WriteToken/LPar/RPar/Semicolon/Space/NewLine), the brace writers (OpenBrace/CloseBrace over every BraceStyle), the WriteBlock block writer, and the write-construct helpers (WriteTypeArguments/WriteTypeParameters/WriteModifiers/WriteQualifiedIdentifier/WriteEmbeddedStatement/WriteMethodBody/WriteAttributes/WritePrivateImplementationType). The 130 per-node Visit methods are DECLARED (so the class is a concrete, instantiable IAstVisitor) but DEFINED AS THROWING STUBS (NotImplemented() -> std::logic_error); they are implemented one node-family at a time in subsequent iterations, replacing the throwing stubs with real bodies (the incremental port-the-output strategy from PORT_PLAN.md section 5.2 / decision D1). Also ports Tokens.hpp (cpp/Decompiler/CSharp/Syntax/Tokens.hpp) the predefined punctuation/keyword const string literals the write methods emit (the C# public static class Tokens -> a namespace of inline constexpr const char* -- the FormattingOptionsFactory D317 static-class->namespace precedent), and completes the D270 deferral by porting the CSharpModifiers helper (AllModifiers the 20-entry output-order std::array<Modifiers>, and GetModifierName the lowercase-keyword const char* lookup) that WriteModifiers iterates. Every dependency the infrastructure consults is already ported: the IAstVisitor base + the 130 forward declarations (D225-D315), the TokenWriter/DecoratingTokenWriter/ILocatable bases + the four factories (D316/D319/D320/D321/D322), the InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (D320), the CSharpFormattingOptions + BraceStyle/NewLinePlacement/PropertyFormatting (D317), the Modifiers [Flags] enum (D270), the AstNode LeadingTrivia/TrailingTrivia/Slot/Parent/Children (D220/D221/D224), the CSharpSlotInfo Kind (D220), the Slots kinds ForInitializer/Iterator/ResourceAcquisition/Getter/Setter (D242/D247/D260/D258/D276), the Accessor Body/Attributes (D274), the BlockStatement Statements collection (D256), the Identifier Name (D227). C#-to-C++ porting decisions: (1) the C# readonly protected TokenWriter writer -> a non-owning TokenWriter* writer_ pointing at the top of the writer stack, plus a private std::unique_ptr<TokenWriter> writerOwner_ owning the stack (the two ctors compose a stack into writerOwner_; writer_ points at the top -- the D322 ownership design applied to the visitor own writer stack; the C# relies on the GC, the C++ owns the stack via the unique_ptr); (2) the C# readonly protected CSharpFormattingOptions policy -> a by-value CSharpFormattingOptions policy_ member (the data class is cheaply copyable, the D317 Clone()-via-copy-ctor precedent -- the visitor keeps its own copy, avoiding the lifetime coupling of a reference); the C# readonly protected Stack<AstNode> containerStack -> std::stack<AstNode*> containerStack_; (3) the C# TextWriter first-ctor param -> std::ostream* (the D319 TextWriter->std::ostream port); the C# ArgumentNullException on null -> std::invalid_argument (the D316 precedent); the policy is a value type (not nullable) so the C# policy null check is dropped; (4) string keyword/token parameters -> std::string_view (the established read-only-string convention; binds directly to the Tokens::LPar inline constexpr const char* literals without an allocation); (5) the C# IEnumerable<AstNode>/IEnumerable<AstType>/... collection parameters -> the typed std::vector<T*> the caller builds from the AstNodeCollection snapshot (the C# lazy IEnumerable ports to an eager vector, the established D221 tree-walk convention); the WriteCommaSeparatedList/WriteCommaSeparatedListInParenthesis helpers are TEMPLATES (defined inline in the header) so they accept any element type that upcasts to AstNode and dispatches via its virtual AcceptVisitor; the two WriteCommaSeparatedListInBrackets overloads are distinct typed-vector overloads (vector<ParameterDeclaration*> vs vector<Expression*>, the C# distinguishes them by element type); (6) the 130 Visit methods are THROWING stubs (NotImplemented() -> std::logic_error), NOT no-ops -- a no-op would silently produce no output and could mask a forgotten node, so the throw makes the unported state loud and explicit (each stub is replaced with a real body when that node-family lands). DEFERRED (land with the first Visit method that needs them): WriteIdentifier(string) -- it calls the D236-deferred AstType.Create, so the string overload lands when AstType.Create does; GetCallChainLengthLimited/ShouldInsertNewLineWhenInMethodCallChain/InsertNewLineWhenInMethodCallChain -- the method-call-chain new-line helpers consumed only by VisitMemberReferenceExpression; the IsKeyword static helper is already factored out to the free IsKeyword helper in CSharpKeywordCheck.hpp (the D318 factoring), so it is NOT a member here. NO new Slots constant, NO new enum (the Modifiers [Flags] enum D270 and the CSharpModifiers helper are the only additions). Namespace mapping ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.OutputVisitor -> ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::OutputVisitor, with the Syntax types it is expressed in qualified as Syntax::X. NOT header-only (the second OutputVisitor .cpp after TokenWriter.cpp D322 -- the infra methods are out-of-line), so OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp is added to the CSharp CMakeLists.txt target_sources(ilspy PRIVATE ...) list; the new test .cpp is added to tests/CMakeLists.txt. TDD: 28 gtest cases in one suite (CSharp_OutputVisitor) in cpp/tests/Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor_Test.cpp (a RecordingTokenWriter stub recording each call into a vector -- the inner sink the visitor InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator wraps; the decorator inserts a space only where two tokens would merge, so the recorded sequence for the punctuation/keyword/newline calls under test is exactly what the visitor wrote), wired into tests/CMakeLists.txt, covering: the two ctors reject null (ostream null, TokenWriter null) and construct a usable visitor; StartNode/EndNode on a trivia-free node push/pop the stack and drive the writer; Comma writes a comma (the default policy has no bracket-comma spaces); WriteKeyword/WriteIdentifier/WriteToken/LPar/RPar drive the writer and reset the inter-token state; Semicolon on a node with no slot kind writes a semicolon and a newline (the ForInitializer/Iterator/ResourceAcquisition skip and the auto-property accessor skip are exercised via the real Visit methods in later iterations); Space (addSpace=true writes, addSpace=false no-ops), NewLine; OpenBrace/CloseBrace per BraceStyle (EndOfLine, and the NextLineShifted early-return case); WriteBlock on an empty block (StartNode, OpenBrace, no statements, CloseBrace, EndNode); WriteTypeArguments/WriteTypeParameters empty (nothing -- the non-empty case recurses via the throwing stubs); WriteModifiers (Static|Public writes kw:public, space, kw:static, space in the AllModifiers output order; None writes nothing); WriteQualifiedIdentifier (id:System, tok:., id:Math); WriteEmbeddedStatement (nullptr -> newline; a block -> the block + a trailing newline); WriteMethodBody (nullptr -> Semicolon, needs a node on the stack as a real VisitMethodDeclaration would; a block -> the block + a trailing newline); WriteAttributes empty (nothing); WritePrivateImplementationType nullptr (nothing); WriteCommaSeparatedListInParenthesis empty (just the parens); and a representative Visit stub throws std::logic_error (VisitNullReferenceExpression, VisitBlockStatement). BUILD: the VS 2026 generator (Visual Studio 18 Insiders, MSVC 14.5x) re-configured (the CSharp CMakeLists.txt + tests/CMakeLists.txt changes trigger a cmake re-run) and compiled CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp into ilspy.lib plus CSharpOutputVisitor_Test.cpp and relinked ilspy.lib/ilspy_tests.exe/ilspy_cli.exe cleanly. THREE build cruxes on the first builds: (1) the OutputVisitor-namespace-vs-Syntax-namespace qualification crux -- the OutputVisitor-namespace types (CSharpFormattingOptions/TokenWriter/BraceStyle/NewLinePlacement/PropertyFormatting) were wrongly Syntax::-qualified in the header; the Syntax::-qualified lookups failed (BraceStyle is not a member of Syntax), surfacing as a cascade of C2352 'non-static member function requires an object' / C2511 'overloaded member function not found' / C2671 'static member functions do not have this pointers' errors in the .cpp definitions (the malformed header declarations made the .cpp definitions not match) -- the fix removes the Syntax:: prefix from the OutputVisitor-namespace types (they resolve unqualified within the OutputVisitor namespace); (2) the abstract-base-forward-declaration crux -- the infrastructure signatures name the abstract AST bases AstType/Statement/Expression by pointer, but IAstVisitor.hpp forward-declares only the 130 CONCRETE node types (the abstract bases are not among them); a first attempt to forward-declare them via a nested `namespace Syntax { class AstType; ... }` block INSIDE the OutputVisitor namespace created a nested OutputVisitor::Syntax that shadowed the real sibling Syntax (the Syntax::IAstVisitor base then failed to resolve), so the fix uses the fully-qualified `namespace ILSpy::Decompiler::CSharp::Syntax { ... }` re-declaration -- but even that did not resolve Syntax::AstType at the use site, so the robust fix is to INCLUDE the abstract base headers (AstType.hpp, Statement.hpp; Expression is already complete via TokenWriter.hpp -> PrimitiveExpression.hpp -> Expression.hpp) rather than forward-declare; (3) the test-side ambiguous-nullptr-ctor crux -- the two ctors (std::ostream*, CSharpFormattingOptions) and (TokenWriter*, CSharpFormattingOptions) make a `CSharpOutputVisitor v(nullptr, {})` call ambiguous (nullptr converts to both pointer types), so the null-arg tests use explicit `static_cast<std::ostream*>(nullptr)` / `static_cast<TokenWriter*>(nullptr)`; and a WriteMethodBody(nullptr) test crashed (deque back() on an empty stack) because Semicolon reads the current node from the container stack via containerStack_.top() (the C# containerStack.Peek(), unguarded -- the C# assumes a real Visit has the node StartNode'd), so the test StartNodes a node first as a real VisitMethodDeclaration would. RESULT: 28 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_OutputVisitor.* run is 28/28 green); the full suite is 5692 to 5720 tests (253 to 254 test suites per --gtest_list_tests -- +1 suite, +28 tests, exactly matching the new suite test count) with 0 regressions (the 5692 prior tests pass unchanged -- CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp is a NEW source whose infrastructure is not called by any existing test or engine code, and Tokens.hpp/CSharpModifiers are NEW/extended headers not referenced by the existing call graph; the full 5720-test run is 5720/5720 green); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly and is BYTE-IDENTICAL -- the whole-mscorlib decompile signature (ilspy_cli --csharp mscorlib.dll from C:/Windows/Microsoft.NET/Framework64/v4.0.30319/) is exactly 8026 goto / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while / 2543 return;, matching the D222-D322 baseline precisely (the FIRST iteration in the D224-D322 span to actually run the signature check rather than defer it to grep-based isolation, since a framework mscorlib.dll is now located), and the include-graph isolation is confirmed by grep (CSharpOutputVisitor.hpp and Tokens.hpp are included ONLY by CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp/.hpp and the test, NOT by any engine/CLI .cpp -- ILAstToCSharp.cpp and ILSpyCmd reference none of them; CSharpModifiers is not used by the CLI/ILAst sources). RESULT: 13 new gtest cases, all pass (the filtered CSharp_OutputVisitor.* run is 50/50 green -- the 37 D323/D324 tests + the 13 new Visit tests); the full suite is 5729 to 5742 tests (254 test suites per --gtest_list_tests -- +0 suites since the new tests join the existing CSharp_OutputVisitor suite, +13 tests, exactly matching the new test count) with 0 regressions (the 5729 prior tests pass unchanged -- the CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp changes replace 9 throwing stubs with real bodies but change no existing behaviour, and no existing test called those Visit methods; the full 5742-test run is 5742/5742 green); the CLI (ilspy_cli) compiles and links cleanly and is BYTE-IDENTICAL -- the whole-mscorlib decompile signature (ilspy_cli --csharp mscorlib.dll from C:/Windows/Microsoft.NET/Framework64/v4.0.30319/) is exactly 8026 goto / 500 lock / 306 using / 59 ?? / 999 for / 1454 while / 2543 return;, matching the D222-D324 baseline precisely (adding the 9 Visit bodies to CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp does not change the CLI output because the CLI decompile path uses ILAstToCSharp the seed, not CSharpOutputVisitor -- the new code paths are dead in the CLI call graph until a node is driven through AcceptVisitor), and the include-graph isolation is confirmed (the new concrete node headers are included by CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp which is dead in the CLI call graph -- ILAstToCSharp.cpp and ILSpyCmd reference none of them). The next-in-order Phase-5 pieces are the remaining per-node Visit methods (the simple statements ReturnStatement/ThrowStatement/ExpressionStatement/GotoStatement/GotoCaseStatement/GotoDefaultStatement/LabelStatement, then the slot-bearing expressions BinaryOperatorExpression/AssignmentExpression/UnaryOperatorExpression/ConditionalExpression/ParenthesizedExpression/CastExpression/AsExpression/IsExpression/TypeOfExpression/SizeOfExpression/DefaultValueExpression/IdentifierExpression/MemberReferenceExpression/InvocationExpression/IndexerExpression that recurse into children via AcceptVisitor, now unblocked by the AstType family landing this iteration), implemented one node-family at a time replacing the throwing stubs. The resolver (CSharp/Resolver, the embedded C# semantic engine, section 5.3) is the long pole that lands after the output stage. |

| D328 | CSharpOutputVisitor control-flow statement Visit methods (4 Visit method bodies: IfElseStatement/WhileStatement/DoWhileStatement/YieldReturnStatement) | port | Implemented the next in-order slice of the C# pretty-printer replacing the D323 throwing stubs, faithfully mirroring the C# source in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.cs: (1) VisitWhileStatement writes WriteKeyword(WhileKeyword) + Space(SpaceBeforeWhileParentheses) + LPar + Space(SpacesWithinWhileParentheses) + Condition()->AcceptVisitor(*this) + Space(SpacesWithinWhileParentheses) + RPar + WriteEmbeddedStatement(EmbeddedStatement()) -- the Condition is a required Expression and the body a required embedded Statement; (2) VisitDoWhileStatement is the WhileStatement shape with the slot order reversed (the body precedes the while clause): WriteKeyword(DoKeyword) + WriteEmbeddedStatement(EmbeddedStatement(), WhileNewLinePlacement) + WriteKeyword(WhileKeyword) + the parens+condition + Semicolon (a trailing semicolon closes the statement); (3) VisitIfElseStatement writes the if/condition/parens then branches on FalseStatement() being null: the single-branch path calls WriteEmbeddedStatement(TrueStatement()), the two-branch path calls WriteEmbeddedStatement(TrueStatement(), ElseNewLinePlacement) + WriteKeyword(ElseKeyword) then recurses DIRECTLY on the false branch when it is an IfElseStatement (the else-if special case -- no WriteEmbeddedStatement newline/indent so else and if stay on one line) or WriteEmbeddedStatement(FalseStatement()) otherwise -- the C# `is IfElseStatement` test ports to a dynamic_cast<IfElseStatement*> is-a check; (4) VisitYieldReturnStatement writes WriteKeyword(YieldKeyword) + WriteKeyword(ReturnKeyword) + Space() + Expression()->AcceptVisitor(*this) + Semicolon (yield return expr;). Added 4 statement-node includes (IfElseStatement/WhileStatement/DoWhileStatement/YieldReturnStatement) to CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp needed by the new Visit bodies to call their accessors (Condition/TrueStatement/FalseStatement/EmbeddedStatement/Expression -- the established D224/D258/D255 APIs). The InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (D320) the visitor wraps the inner writer in inserts the inter-keyword space the C# formatter relies on for `yield return` and `else if`: two consecutive WriteKeyword calls would merge into one lexeme without the decorator's WriteKeyword override (lastWritten == KeywordOrIdentifier -> Space() before forwarding), and the StartNode between `else` and the nested `if` does NOT reset lastWritten (the decorator's StartNode just forwards), so the `else if` gets a decorator-inserted space too -- the C# Visit methods never write these explicit spaces. The default CSharpFormattingOptions has SpaceBeforeIfParentheses/SpaceBeforeWhileParentheses/SpacesWithinIfParentheses/SpacesWithinWhileParentheses all false, so the parens hug the keyword and the condition with no inserted spaces. | D330 | CSharpOutputVisitor type-keyword expression Visit methods (6 Visit method bodies: CastExpression/AsExpression/IsExpression/TypeOfExpression/DefaultValueExpression/SizeOfExpression) | port | Implemented the next in-order slice of the C# pretty-printer replacing the D323 throwing stubs, faithfully mirroring the C# source in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/OutputVisitor/CSharpOutputVisitor.cs: (1) VisitCastExpression writes LPar + Space(SpacesWithinCastParentheses) + Type->AcceptVisitor + Space(SpacesWithinCastParentheses) + RPar + Space(SpaceAfterTypecast) + Expression->AcceptVisitor (the cast operator (T)e); (2) VisitAsExpression writes Expression->AcceptVisitor + Space() + WriteKeyword(AsExpression::AsKeyword) + Space() + Type->AcceptVisitor (the `as` operator with explicit spaces on both sides of the keyword); (3) VisitIsExpression writes Expression->AcceptVisitor + Space() + WriteKeyword(IsExpression::IsKeyword) + Type->AcceptVisitor (the `is` operator writes NO explicit space after the keyword -- the decorator inserts it); (4) VisitTypeOfExpression writes WriteKeyword(TypeofKeyword) + LPar + Space(SpacesWithinTypeOfParentheses) + Type->AcceptVisitor + Space(SpacesWithinTypeOfParentheses) + RPar (typeof(T)); (5) VisitDefaultValueExpression is structurally identical to typeof but with the DefaultKeyword and reusing the SpacesWithinTypeOfParentheses policy (default(T), faithful to the C# which uses the same policy field); (6) VisitSizeOfExpression is the typeof shape with the SizeofKeyword and the SpacesWithinSizeOfParentheses policy (sizeof(T)). All six reuse the already-ported D243/D244/D245 const-keyword strings (AsKeyword/IsKeyword/TypeofKeyword/DefaultKeyword/SizeofKeyword) and the already-ported D240/D317 policy fields (SpacesWithinCastParentheses/SpaceAfterTypecast/SpacesWithinTypeOfParentheses/SpacesWithinSizeOfParentheses) with no new helper, no new Slots constant, and no name-shadowing crux. Added 6 expression-node includes (AsExpression/IsExpression/CastExpression/TypeOfExpression/DefaultValueExpression/SizeOfExpression) to CSharpOutputVisitor.cpp needed by the new Visit bodies to call the Type()/Expression() accessors and the const keywords. The InsertRequiredSpacesDecorator (D320) is the load-bearing inter-token separator for VisitIsExpression: the C# writes NO explicit Space() after the `is` keyword, so a `42 is int` render would merge `is` and `int` into one lexeme without the decorator's WritePrimitiveType override (lastWritten == KeywordOrIdentifier after the `is` keyword -> insert a Space() before forwarding the primitive type), so the recorded sequence for `42 is int` carries a decorator-inserted space between kw:is and primtype:int -- distinct from VisitAsExpression where the C# writes BOTH explicit spaces (before and after `as`) so the decorator sees lastWritten == Whitespace at the type and inserts none. The default CSharpFormattingOptions has SpacesWithinCastParentheses/SpaceAfterTypecast/SpacesWithinTypeOfParentheses/SpacesWithinSizeOfParentheses all false, so `(int)42` and `typeof(int)`/`default(int)`/`sizeof(int)` render with the parens hugging the type and no space after the cast close paren. KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) the C# `enum KnownAttribute` has NO explicit backing type, so it defaults to `int`; the port keeps `int` (the values 0..ExtensionMarker fit), distinct from the D373 `Accessibility : byte` -> `std::uint8_t` and the D376 `TypeSystemOptions : int` (a `[Flags]` enum) -> `std::uint32_t` -- a plain ordinal enum with the C#-default `int` backing ports as `int`. (b) The `KnownAttributes` static class (C# extension methods) ports to free functions in the `TypeSystem` namespace (the D373 `AccessibilityExtensions` precedent): `KnownAttributeCount` (the C# `internal const int Count = (int)KnownAttribute.ExtensionMarker + 1` = 60), `GetTypeName(KnownAttribute) -> const TopLevelTypeName&` (the C# `public static ref readonly TopLevelTypeName GetTypeName(this KnownAttribute attr)`), `IsCustomAttribute(KnownAttribute) -> bool` (the C# `public static bool IsCustomAttribute(this KnownAttribute knownAttribute)`), plus the `typeNames` table exposed via `KnownAttributeTypeNames() -> const std::array<TopLevelTypeName, Count>&` (the C# `static readonly TopLevelTypeName[] typeNames`). (c) The `ref readonly TopLevelTypeName` return ports to `const TopLevelTypeName&` (the const-reference-return convention, the ITypeDefinitionOrUnknown::FullTypeName D377 precedent); the C# `Debug.Assert(attr != KnownAttribute.None)` ports to `assert(attr != KnownAttribute::None)` (debug-only, the D371/D373 precedent). (d) The `typeNames` table is a function-local `static const std::array<TopLevelTypeName, KnownAttributeCount>` inside an `inline` function (`KnownAttributeTypeNames`) -- `TopLevelTypeName` is a NON-literal type (it owns `std::string`), so the table CANNOT be `constexpr`, unlike the D376 `TypeSystemOptions::Default` bitwise-OR-in-initializer or the D373 relational operators; the function-local static is initialized once on first use (thread-safe under C++11+) and is ODR-safe because the enclosing function is `inline` (the standard "Meyers singleton" -- a single instance across the program, no `.cpp`/CMake entry needed, keeping the header-only leaf convention of D372/D373/D375/D376/D377). Index 0 (`None`) is default-constructed (`TopLevelTypeName{}`) mirroring the C# `default` entry, and a `static_assert(typeNames.size() == KnownAttributeCount)` pins the table extent at compile time. Exposing the table via a function (not just `GetTypeName`) lets the not-yet-ported `IsKnownAttributeType` iterate the same table it indexes. (e) `IsCustomAttribute` is the pure classifier: the C# `switch` with 16 `case`s returning `false` (Serializable/ComImport/StructLayout/DllImport/PreserveSig/MethodImpl/FieldOffset/NonSerialized/MarshalAs/PermissionSet/Optional/DefaultParameterValue/In/Out/IndexerName/SpecialName -- the pseudo-attributes the C# compiler folds into other metadata tables, NOT emitted as a real `CustomAttribute`) and a `default` returning `true`; the faithful port mirrors the switch verbatim, so `KnownAttribute::None` (and every value not in the false-list) classifies as a custom attribute -- the `default` arm IS the `None`/unknown case. KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) The C# `new string Name` REDECLARES `Name` (re-stating the same contract the `ISymbol` / `INamedElement` bases already expose). In C++ this DOES have a counterpart, REQUIRED here and NOT covered by the D374 `IVariable` single-inheritance "inherited virtual covers the `new`" precedent: `ISymbol` and `INamedElement` are TWO INDEPENDENT bases each declaring `virtual std::string Name() const = 0` with the SAME signature, so without a redeclaration `IEntity` would inherit both pure-virtuals and a name LOOKUP through an `IEntity*` (e.g. `entity->Name()`) is AMBIGUOUS (the two base `Name`s are both found, MSVC C2385) even though a concrete entity's single override IS the final overrider for both base subobjects. The faithful port therefore REDECLARES `Name()` in `IEntity` as a pure-virtual of the same signature -- this overrides BOTH base `Name`s (the standard C++ way one derived function overrides multiple matching base virtuals across independent subobjects), keeps `IEntity` abstract, and makes `Name` lookup through an `IEntity*` unambiguous (only `IEntity::Name` is found). A concrete entity then overrides `Name()` once, and dispatch through `ISymbol*` / `INamedElement*` / `IEntity*` all reach that single override. This is the documented multiple-inheritance-diamond resolution for the `IEntity` leaf, DISTINCT from the D374 single-inheritance "inherited virtual covers the `new`" precedent (verified by the RED-neuter: commenting out the `IEntity::Name()` redeclaration made the test fail to compile with C2385 at the `IEntity*` call sites -- lines 349/352/369/419 -- proving the redeclaration is load-bearing for name lookup, then restored to GREEN). The `MethodSemanticsLookup` (Metadata/MethodSemanticsLookup.cs) builds the accessor-to-association map from the metadata, and `MetadataMethod.AccessorKind` (MetadataMethod.cs line 75) stores the resolved flag; the metadata reader maps the raw ECMA flags directly, so the values are load-bearing for the accessor-to-association mapping and must match the ECMA-335 / BCL literals exactly. CONSUMERS: `TypeSystemAstBuilder.ConvertAccessor` (TypeSystemAstBuilder.cs lines 2207-2232) switches on the single-valued flag to map it to the AST `AccessorKind` (the `Syntax::AccessorKind` enum in `Accessor.hpp`, a DIFFERENT enum -- `Any`/`Getter`/`Setter`/`Init`/`Adder`/`Remover`, no `Other`/`Raiser`, no `[Flags]`; `MethodSemanticsAttributes.Getter`/`Setter`/`Adder`/`Remover` map to the matching `AccessorKind`, `Other`/`Raiser` fall through to default), and the IL transforms (`AssignVariableNames`, `ILInlining`, `IndexRangeTransform`, `NullPropagationTransform`, `PatternMatchingTransform`, `SwitchOnStringTransform`, `StatementBuilder`, `DeconstructInstruction`, `MatchInstruction`) compare `method.AccessorKind == MethodSemanticsAttributes.Getter`/`Setter`/... to detect accessors (single-valued equality, never a combined mask). The `MethodSemanticsLookup` ctor ALSO uses the enum as a real `[Flags]` mask: the `csharpAccessors = Getter OR-bitor Setter OR-bitor Adder OR-bitor Remover` composite filters which semantics to record, and `(filter & Other) != 0` (it throws if `Other` is requested) and `(semantics & filter) == 0` (skip an accessor whose semantics does not intersect the filter) are bit tests. The BCL `CustomAttributeTypedArgument<TType>` / `CustomAttributeNamedArgument<TType>` are the `System.Reflection.Metadata` readonly structs the `CustomAttributeDecoder.DecodeArgument` / `DecodeNamedArguments` builds from the attribute blob, and `IAttribute.FixedArguments` / `NamedArguments` hold the `ImmutableArray<...<IType>>`; `TypeSystemAstBuilder.ConvertAttribute` reads `arg.Type` / `arg.Value` (fixed) and `namedArg.Name` / `namedArg.Type` / `namedArg.Value` (named) to build the attribute's positional- and named-argument expressions (TypeSystemAstBuilder.cs lines 791-813). The `CustomAttributeNamedArgumentKind` is the one-byte ECMA-335 II.23.3 tag distinguishing a named argument that sets a field (0x53) from one that sets a property (0x54); the decoder casts a raw kind byte to it and rejects anything else (CustomAttributeDecoder.cs line 39). KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) BCL GENERIC ABSORBED AS A CONCRETE STRUCT: the BCL structs are generic (`CustomAttributeTypedArgument<TType>` / `CustomAttributeNamedArgument<TType>`) but the ILSpy type system uses only the `IType` instantiation (the `CustomAttributeDecoder<TType>` in the Metadata layer is generic, but that layer is not yet ported, and the TypeSystem surface -- `IAttribute` and its consumers -- needs only `IType`); the faithful port therefore absorbs the `<IType>` instantiation into the `TypeSystem` namespace as a CONCRETE (non-template) struct, the same convention the D384 `MethodSemanticsAttributes` / D381 `IEntity.MetadataToken` ports followed for BCL helper types, and the concrete-struct convention the `TypeConstraint` (D383) / `LifetimeAnnotation` (D382) / `FullTypeName` / `TopLevelTypeName` TypeSystem value types established. A future Metadata-layer port that needs the generic decoder can refactor or add a template then. (b) The C# `TType Type` (non-null for a decoded argument) ports to `ITypePtr` (the D271 `std::shared_ptr<IType>` shared, cached handle -- the `TypeConstraint.Type` D383 precedent); a null `shared_ptr` is the faithful representation of an argument whose type could not be decoded (the default-constructed value, the `ImmutableArray.CreateBuilder<T>(count)` zero-fill the decoder overwrites). (c) The C# `object? Value` ports to `std::any` (the D374 `IVariable::GetConstantValue` precedent -- `std::any` is the type-erased boxed value, empty for `null`); a `std::any` holds any copy-constructible value, so it models the full BCL `object?` range the decoder produces -- a primitive (`bool` / `int32_t` / ...), a `std::string`, an `ITypePtr`, an enum, a BOXED NESTED `CustomAttributeTypedArgument` (the `new CustomAttributeTypedArgument<TType>(outer.Type, new CustomAttributeTypedArgument<TType>(info.Type, value))` boxed-value case, CustomAttributeDecoder.cs line 196), or a `std::vector<CustomAttributeTypedArgument>` (the array case). Consumers retrieve a value with `std::any_cast` (the C# `object` cast) and test with `has_value` (the C# `null` test). (d) The C# `string? Name` (nullable -- the decoder reads it from `valueReader.ReadSerializedString()`, which returns null for a malformed blob) ports to `std::string` where the EMPTY string represents the null case (the D357 `AttributeTarget` `IsNullOrEmpty`-to-`.empty()` convention -- the consumer `TypeSystemAstBuilder` uses `namedArg.Name!` (null-forgiving), treating the name as non-null in practice for well-formed attributes, so the null and empty cases collapse to the empty string without loss for the consumer); the default-constructed value is the empty string. (e) The C# `readonly struct` (a value type with a ctor and readonly properties) ports to a `struct` with PRIVATE fields (the `_` suffix) and PUBLIC accessor member functions (the `TypeConstraint` D383 readonly-struct convention); the ctors store the members (the C# `CustomAttributeTypedArgument(TType type, object? value)` and `CustomAttributeNamedArgument(string? name, CustomAttributeNamedArgumentKind kind, TType type, object? value)`). A DEFAULTED default constructor is provided (the C# implicit parameterless struct ctor that zeroes the fields) so a `std::vector<CustomAttributeTypedArgument>` / `std::vector<CustomAttributeNamedArgument>` can default-construct its elements (the `ImmutableArray.CreateBuilder<T>(count)` zero-fill the decoder relies on); the MEMBER INITIALIZERS make the defaults safe -- a null `ITypePtr`, an empty `std::any`, an empty `std::string`, and `CustomAttributeNamedArgumentKind::Field` (the lower serialization code, a safe default the decoder overwrites before use; an explicit initializer is needed because `= default` on the ctor would zero-init the enum to 0, which is not a valid `CustomAttributeNamedArgumentKind`, so the member initializer pins `Field`). (f) The `CustomAttributeNamedArgumentKind` enum ports to a `std::uint8_t`-backed `enum class` (the C# `: byte` underlying type -- the kind is a single serialization byte); the member order and values mirror the ECMA-335 II.23.1.16 / BCL literals exactly (`Field = 0x53`, `Property = 0x54` -- each member's numeric value is its serialization code, so a raw byte read from the metadata blob casts directly to the enum). NO `[Flags]` bitwise operators are needed (the enum is a closed two-value tag, never combined or masked), so -- unlike `MethodSemanticsAttributes` (D384) / `TypeSystemOptions` (D376) -- only the `enum class` itself is ported; the C++ `enum class`'s built-in `==` / `!=` suffices for the consumer's `kind == Field` / `kind == Property` tests. (g) NAMESPACE: the BCL types live in `System.Reflection.Metadata`, but the C++ port has NO `System::Reflection::Metadata` namespace (no BCL-namespace fidelity for helper types), and the `IAttribute` that carries them lives in `ILSpy::Decompiler::TypeSystem`; the faithful port therefore places all three types in `ILSpy::Decompiler::TypeSystem` -- the same convention the D384 `MethodSemanticsAttributes` / D381 `IEntity.MetadataToken` ports followed (BCL helper types are absorbed into the `TypeSystem` namespace where their consumers live, not re-homed under a BCL-namespace mirror). (h) NO name-hiding qualification is needed (the three types and their members do not collide with any namespace-scope type in the `TypeSystem` namespace; `Type()` / `Value()` / `Name()` / `Kind()` as member functions of these structs do not hide any enum in their own struct scope -- none of these structs derives from `ISymbol`, so there is no inherited `SymbolKind()` to hide, the D383 `TypeConstraint` precedent), so the headers and the test compile unqualified -- the D375 `INamedElement` / D380 `Nullability` collision-free-accessor convention applies. | D386 | IAttribute (the resolved custom-attribute interface, carrying the `AttributeType` / `Constructor` / `HasDecodeErrors` / `FixedArguments` / `NamedArguments`; the next leaf after the D385 value-argument structs, landing the interface whose members those structs are, and unblocking `IMethod` / `IEvent` / `IField` / the member family on attribute accessors toward `TypeSystemAstBuilder` / `CSharpAmbience`) | port | Ported the `IAttribute` interface (cpp/Decompiler/TypeSystem/IAttribute.hpp, the port of ICSharpCode.Decompiler/TypeSystem/IAttribute.cs) -- the interface for a resolved custom attribute (a `[Attribute(...)]` applied to an entity). `IAttribute` carries the attribute's `AttributeType` (the `[...]` type), the resolved `Constructor` (nullable -- null when no matching constructor was found), the `HasDecodeErrors` flag (true when the blob could not be decoded; the decompiler emits such an attribute as a comment), the positional `FixedArguments`, and the `NamedArguments`. The `CustomAttributeDecoder` builds these from the attribute blob; `TypeSystemAstBuilder.ConvertAttribute` reads every accessor to build the `Attribute` AST node (TypeSystemAstBuilder.cs lines 791-813). `IEntity` / `IParameter` / `ITypeParameter` / `IMethod` expose attributes via `GetAttributes` / `GetReturnTypeAttributes`, so `IAttribute` is a leaf consumed across the member family. It lands now that all its deps are ported: `IType` (D271, the `AttributeType` return), the `CustomAttributeTypedArgument` / `CustomAttributeNamedArgument` value-argument structs (D385, the `FixedArguments` / `NamedArguments` element types). The remaining dep `IMethod` (the `Constructor` slot) is NOT yet ported, but a pointer return needs only a forward declaration (the `IEntity::ParentModule` / `ICompilationProvider` precedent), so `IAttribute` compiles with `IMethod` incomplete. `IMethod` <-> `IAttribute` is a cyclic pair (`IMethod` exposes `GetReturnTypeAttributes` returning `IEnumerable<IAttribute>`), resolved here the same way the `IEntity` <-> `ITypeDefinition` cyclic triangle was resolved in D381: forward declarations plus pointer/reference returns. KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) The C# `IType AttributeType { get; }` is NON-NULL (the `DefaultAttribute` ctor throws `ArgumentNullException` on a null type, and the `CustomAttribute` implementation falls back to `SpecialType.UnknownType`), so it ports to `const IType& AttributeType() const` -- a non-null reference return, the `IVariable::Type()` D374 "non-null owned-type reference" convention (the concrete implementation holds the `IType` via an `ITypePtr` or a value member and returns a reference valid for the attribute's lifetime). This is distinct from the nullable `ITypePtr` returns of `IEntity::DeclaringType` / `ITypeParameter::EffectiveBaseClass` (which model a possibly-absent type); the `AttributeType` contract is never-null. (b) The C# `IMethod? Constructor { get; }` (nullable -- "may return null if no matching constructor was found") ports to `const IMethod*` (a nullable raw pointer, the `IEntity::ParentModule` precedent); `IMethod` is forward-declared, a null pointer is the C# `null`. (c) The C# `ImmutableArray<CustomAttributeTypedArgument<IType>> FixedArguments` and `ImmutableArray<CustomAttributeNamedArgument<IType>> NamedArguments` port to `std::vector<CustomAttributeTypedArgument>` and `std::vector<CustomAttributeNamedArgument>` returned BY VALUE (the D385 value-struct convention -- the element types are concrete value structs, so the snapshot owns its argument values directly; the `<IType>` BCL generic instantiation is absorbed into the `TypeSystem` namespace, the D385 BCL-absorption convention). (d) NO name-hiding qualification is needed: `IAttribute` does NOT derive from `ISymbol` (it is a standalone interface), so there is no inherited `SymbolKind()` to hide the `SymbolKind` enum, and none of `AttributeType` / `Constructor` / `HasDecodeErrors` / `FixedArguments` / `NamedArguments` collides with a namespace-scope type -- the D375 `INamedElement` / D380 `Nullability` collision-free-accessor convention applies. (e) `IAttribute` declares NO `new string Name` (it has no `Name` accessor at all), so there is no multiple-inheritance diamond to disambiguate -- unlike `IEntity` (D381) and `ITypeParameter` (D383). STAND-IN RECONCILIATION (the documented "stand-ins are dropped when the real headers land" step): the three existing test files that each defined a minimal `class IAttribute { virtual ~IAttribute() = default; };` stand-in in the `ILSpy::Decompiler::TypeSystem` namespace (IEntity_Test.cpp, IParameter_Test.cpp, ITypeParameter_Test.cpp) were each updated to include the real `IAttribute.hpp`, drop the stand-in, and make their `TestAttribute` concrete stub derive from the real `IAttribute` and implement the 5 new pure-virtuals. Each `TestAttribute` keeps its test-specific accessor (`Kind()` / `id()`) and backing member so the existing `GetAttributes` pointer-identity / `HasAttribute` / `GetAttribute` tests continue to work, and adds the 5 IAttribute implementations with simple defaults: `AttributeType` returns a `KnownType(KnownTypeCode::Object)` value member by reference (the non-null owned-type convention), `Constructor` returns `nullptr` (no resolved ctor in those tests -- a null `const IMethod*` needs no `IMethod` stand-in, so no `IMethod` stand-in is added to those files), `HasDecodeErrors` returns `false`, and `FixedArguments` / `NamedArguments` return empty vectors. The real `IAttribute` (defined in the `TypeSystem` namespace) replaced the IDENTICAL stand-ins, so the ODR-safe-across-TUs invariant is preserved (no two DIFFERENT `IAttribute` definitions coexist). In C# a concrete `IMethod` (e.g. `MetadataMethod`) implements BOTH vtable slots -- the `IMethod.Specialize` slot (public, returns `IMethod`) and the `IMember.Specialize` slot (explicit-interface, returns `IMember`) -- both returning the same specialized-method object. The faithful C++ mapping is a SINGLE virtual override with a COVARIANT return type: `virtual const IMethod* Specialize(const TypeParameterSubstitution* substitution) const override = 0`, overriding the inherited `IMember::Specialize`'s `const IMember*` return. Dispatch through an `IMethod*` returns `const IMethod*` directly; dispatch through an `IMember*` reaches the SAME override (one C++ slot) and the returned `const IMethod*` implicitly converts to `const IMember*` (the derived-to-base pointer conversion) -- the observable behavior of the C# two slots realized as one C++ slot. The covariant return is legal because `IMethod` derives from `IMember` and `IMethod` is the enclosing class: the standard allows a covariant return that is a pointer to the enclosing class even while the class is incomplete at the point of the override declaration (verified -- it compiles on MSVC with the `override` keyword). This is the FIRST ported interface member that uses a covariant return type to mirror a C# `new`-with-covariant-return; the `CovariantSpecializeOverride` test pins it (calling through both `IMethod*` and `IMember*` reaches the same override; the `IMethod*` call yields `const IMethod*` directly, which would not compile without the covariant return).
