KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) THE SHARED-`ISymbol`-BASE DIAMOND (the key NEW structural crux this iteration, distinct from EVERY prior ported diamond): `IField : IMember, IVariable` is the FIRST ported interface whose TWO bases BOTH derive (transitively) from a SHARED base -- `IMember` : `IEntity` : `ISymbol` and `IVariable` : `ISymbol` -- so `ISymbol` appears in BOTH branches of the inheritance graph. With the NON-VIRTUAL inheritance the established convention uses (every prior TypeSystem interface port uses non-virtual `public` inheritance), `IField` has TWO independent `ISymbol` subobjects -- one inside the `IMember` subobject (via `IEntity`) and one inside the `IVariable` subobject. This has TWO consequences the prior diamonds did NOT have: the D381 `IEntity` (`ISymbol` + `ICompilationProvider` + `INamedElement`) and D383 `ITypeParameter` (`IType` + `ISymbol`) diamonds each had only ONE `ISymbol` subobject (the other base did not derive from `ISymbol`), so only the `Name` accessor (which `ISymbol` shares with `INamedElement` in the `IEntity` case, and with `IType` in the `ITypeParameter` case) was ambiguous through the interface pointer, and the C# `new string Name` redeclaration was the ONLY disambiguation needed; HERE, BOTH `SymbolKind` and `Name` (the entire `ISymbol` surface) are inherited via TWO paths, so BOTH are ambiguous through an `IField*`. The C# `IField` redeclares ONLY `Name` (`new string Name` -- "solve ambiguity between IMember.Name and IVariable.Name"); it does NOT redeclare `SymbolKind`, because C# INTERFACE FLATTENING unifies the shared `ISymbol` interface into a SINGLE vtable slot (one `ISymbol.SymbolKind`), so `field.SymbolKind` is unambiguous in C#. The non-virtual C++ port CANNOT flatten -- it has two `ISymbol` subobjects -- so a lookup of `SymbolKind` through an `IField*` is ambiguous (MSVC C2385) WITHOUT a C++-specific redeclaration. The faithful port therefore REDECLARES BOTH `Name()` (mirroring the C# `new string Name`) AND `SymbolKind()` (a C++-ONLY disambiguation with NO C# source counterpart, present purely so `field->SymbolKind()` compiles and dispatches the same single override `field.SymbolKind` reaches in C#). A single `IField::SymbolKind()` override is the final overrider for BOTH `ISymbol` subobjects (the standard rule: one derived function overrides every matching base virtual across all base subobjects), so dispatch is uniform; the redeclaration fixes the LOOKUP, not the dispatch. This is the documented C++-vs-C# divergence for the shared-base diamond; a future virtual-inheritance refactor of `ISymbol` (making `IEntity` / `IVariable` derive `public virtual ISymbol`) would unify the subobject and make the `SymbolKind` redeclaration redundant -- deferred, the same "forward-declare / defer the long-pole" shell strategy, since it would touch every existing TypeSystem interface header and the existing concrete test stubs. A SECOND consequence of the two-`ISymbol`-subobject layout: an UPCAST from `IField*` to `ISymbol*` is AMBIGUOUS (which `ISymbol` subobject?) -- `ISymbol* s = field;` does NOT compile (C2385). A consumer that needs `ISymbol` dispatch through an `IField*` must first upcast to ONE of the unambiguous intermediate bases (`IMember*` or `IVariable*`, each of which appears once and each of which IS-A `ISymbol`), then to `ISymbol*` from there. The test dispatches through `IMember*` and `IVariable*` (unambiguous) and does NOT attempt the ambiguous `ISymbol*` upcast. (b) The C# `new string Name` REDECLARES `Name` -- the D381 `IEntity` / D383 `ITypeParameter` multiple-inheritance-diamond `Name()` crux: `IMember` (via `IEntity`) and `IVariable` (via `ISymbol`) are TWO INDEPENDENT bases each declaring `virtual std::string Name() const = 0` with the same signature, so the `IField` `Name()` redeclaration overrides BOTH base `Name`s, keeps `IField` abstract, and makes `Name` lookup through an `IField*` unambiguous; a concrete field overrides `Name()` once and dispatch through `IMember*` / `IVariable*` / `IField*` all reach it. (c) The `SymbolKind()` return type is GLOBALLY QUALIFIED (`::ILSpy::Decompiler::TypeSystem::SymbolKind`) because the inherited `ISymbol::SymbolKind()` member function hides the namespace-scope `SymbolKind` enum in this derived class (the D372 / D383 cross-scope name-hiding crux), so an unqualified `SymbolKind` in the return type would resolve to the inherited function (a non-type), not the enum. (d) The three IField-own accessors (`IsReadOnly` / `ReturnTypeIsRefReadOnly` / `IsVolatile`) are plain bools with no namespace-scope collision and no base redeclaration -- the D375 `INamedElement` / D380 `Nullability` collision-free-accessor convention applies. `ReturnTypeIsRefReadOnly` IS a member of `IMethod` (D389) and `IProperty` (D390) too, but `IField` does NOT derive from either -- they are SEPARATE interface hierarchies sharing only the `IMember` / `IEntity` bases -- so the `ReturnTypeIsRefReadOnly()` virtuals do NOT clash (the D390 `IProperty`-vs-`IMethod` non-clash precedent). (e) The `IVariable`-own accessors (`Type` / `IsConst` / `GetConstantValue`) and the `IMember`-own accessors (`ReturnType` / `MemberDefinition` / ...) are inherited UNAMBIGUOUSLY: each name lives on only ONE of the two bases, so `field->Type()`, `field->ReturnType()`, `field->IsConst()`, `field->GetConstantValue()` all compile and dispatch without redeclaration. `IMember.ReturnType` and `IVariable.Type` are DIFFERENT names that both denote the field's type -- the C# `MetadataField` implements both to return the same `IType`; the `TestField` stub does the same, and the `ReturnTypeAndTypeAreTheSameFieldType` test pins the pointer-identity. In C++ with non-virtual inheritance (the established convention), listing `IType` directly AND via `ITypeDefinitionOrUnknown` creates a DIRECT-vs-INDIRECT `IType` DIAMOND: two `IType` subobjects, a `C4584` "base-class `IType` is already a base-class of `ITypeDefinitionOrUnknown`" warning, and -- worse -- AMBIGUOUS `IType` conversions (`td` -> `const IType&`, `static_cast<TestTypeDefinition&>(const IType&)`) that would force every consumer (notably `TypeSystemAstBuilder`, which passes type definitions as `const IType&`) to disambiguate with an explicit `static_cast<const ITypeDefinitionOrUnknown&>(td)` upcast. The `-1`-sentinel `Build` / `Revision` are real values compared by equality, so `Version(1,2) == Version(1,2,-1,-1)` and `Version(1,2) != Version(1,2,0,-1)`. (c) `ToString` mirrors `System.Version.ToString` EXACTLY: "Major.Minor" when `Build` is unspecified (`-1`), "Major.Minor.Build" when `Revision` is unspecified, "Major.Minor.Build.Revision" otherwise -- the C# `if (Build == -1) return ToString(2); if (Revision == -1) return ToString(3); return ToString(4);` shape ported as append-`Build`-when-`Build != -1` / append-`Revision`-when-`Revision != -1`. The decompiler's one consumer of the string form is `MetadataModule` formatting `assembly.Version.ToString()` into an `[AssemblyVersion("...")]` attribute (`MetadataModule.cs:856`), so the shape is load-bearing. (d) `Version` is a CONCRETE value struct (NOT an interface), so it needs no `CMakeLists.txt` `target_sources(ilspy)` entry (the `Accessibility` / `Nullability` / `TypeSystemOptions` / `KnownAttribute` header-only-concrete-leaf precedent) and no stand-in reconciliation (it is a NEW type no existing test file references). NO name-hiding qualification is needed: `Version` is the only type of that name in the `TypeSystem` namespace (the deep-nested `winmd` `AssemblyVersion` lives in `ILSpy::Decompiler::Metadata`'s vendored reader, not `TypeSystem`), and none of the four field names (`Major` / `Minor` / `Build` / `Revision`) or `ToString` collides with a namespace-scope type -- the D375 `INamedElement` / D380 `Nullability` collision-free-accessor convention applies. The C# `sealed class CacheManager` (a reference type with no virtual members) ports to a concrete C++ class (no virtual destructor -- it is sealed and non-derivable); the C# `ConcurrentDictionary<object, object>` keyed by `ReferenceComparer` ports to a `std::unordered_map<const void*, std::any>` guarded by a `std::mutex`. KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) The `ReferenceComparer` semantics (`Equals(x,y)` is `x == y` reference equality; `GetHashCode(obj)` is `RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode` the identity hash) are reproduced by a `const void*` key with NO separate comparer type: pointer `==` is the reference equality and `std::hash<const void*>` hashes the pointer value (the identity hash). The C# `object` key ports to `const void*` (the reference identity). (b) The C# `object?` value ports to `std::any` (the D374 `IVariable::GetConstantValue` precedent -- `std::any` is the type-erased boxed value, empty for `null`); `GetShared` returns an empty `std::any` for an absent key (the C# `TryGetValue`-miss null case), and consumers test `has_value` (the C# `null` test) and retrieve via `std::any_cast` (the C# object cast). (c) The four operations port verbatim: `GetShared(key)` (locked `find`, empty on miss); `GetOrAddShared(key, valueFactory)` (locked find-else-compute-emplace, factory called at most once under the lock -- a tighter port than the C# `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd` speculative factory calls but the stored value is the same); `GetOrAddShared(key, value)` (locked find-else-emplace, returns existing on hit); `SetShared(key, value)` (locked indexer assign). `mutable std::mutex` so the logically-const `GetShared` can lock. The class is non-copyable and non-movable (a per-compilation cache is a single shared instance held by reference by the compilation). (d) The `TypeKey<T>()` helper template (co-located in the header) returns a stable per-type address -- the C++ counterpart of the C# `typeof(T)` reference the `CSharpConversions` / `CSharpOperators` consumers use as a cache key: each instantiation has its own `static const char tag`, so `TypeKey<T>()` and `TypeKey<U>()` compare equal (pointer identity) iff `T` and `U` are the same type, matching `typeof` reference-equality-per-type. (e) CRUX -- the factory-vs-value overload ambiguity: the C# has two `GetOrAddShared` overloads (`Func<object,object>` factory and `object` value) cleanly separated because `Func<object,object>` is a distinct delegate type. A naive C++ port with `std::function<std::any(const void*)>` (factory) and `std::any` (value) overloads is AMBIGUOUS for a lambda argument: both `std::function` and `std::any` have greedy templated constructors, so a lambda converts to BOTH (C2668, surfaced on the first build). The faithful port takes the factory as an SFINAE-constrained template (`std::enable_if_t<std::is_invocable_r_v<std::any, F, const void*>, int> = 0`) accepting only callables invocable with a `const void*` returning something convertible to `std::any`: a non-callable argument (a `std::any` value, an `int`, a string) does NOT match the template (falls through to the `std::any` value overload), and a callable does NOT convert to `std::any` (so the two overloads never compete for the same argument). This is more faithful than `std::function` (it accepts any callable, not just the type-erased `std::function`) AND resolves the ambiguity; `<functional>` is not needed. (c) `FullTypeNameComparer::Equals` mirrors the C# structure verbatim: a `NestingLevel` mismatch short-circuits to false; the top-level triple (`TypeParameterCount`, `Name`, `Namespace` through `NameComparer`) is checked and short-circuits on a mismatch; then each nesting level's `GetNestedTypeAdditionalTypeParameterCount` and `GetNestedTypeName` are compared pairwise through `NameComparer`. (d) `FullTypeNameComparer::GetHashCode` mirrors the C# `unchecked` wraparound arithmetic by accumulating in `unsigned int` (well-defined modular wraparound, no signed-overflow UB) and casting the result back to `int` (the two's-complement bit pattern is identical to the C# `unchecked int` wrap). The C# loop body uses `obj.Name` (the innermost name) and `obj.TypeParameterCount` (the total count) on EVERY iteration -- NOT the per-level `GetNestedTypeName(i)` / `GetNestedTypeAdditionalTypeParameterCount(i)` accessors that `Equals` uses. This asymmetry is a C# source quirk (the loop adds the same value each iteration); it is consistent with `Equals` (equal names share the innermost name and total count, so they hash equal) but is not maximally discriminating. It is ported VERBATIM (not "fixed"), and documented in the header. ADDITIVE `FullTypeName.hpp` change: `FullTypeNameComparer::Equals` needs the per-level accessors `GetNestedTypeName(int)` / `GetNestedTypeAdditionalTypeParameterCount(int)`, which the C++ `FullTypeName.hpp` minimal port did NOT yet carry (the C# `FullTypeName` defines them, throwing `InvalidOperationException` when `nestedTypes == null`). Two additive inline accessors were added to `FullTypeName.hpp` (faithful to the C# -- throw `std::logic_error` when `nested_` is empty, the C++ `InvalidOperationException`-equivalent, requiring a new `#include <stdexcept>`), leaving the existing `operator==` / `ReflectionName` / `FullName` / `TypeParameterCount` definitions untouched (the C# `FullTypeName.Equals` / `GetHashCode` delegate to `FullTypeNameComparer.Ordinal`, but the C++ `FullTypeName::operator==` is an equivalent field-wise definition that predates this port and is left in place -- the D223 do-not-modify-working-code-without-a-consumer convention; the comparer port is a NEW class, not wired into `FullTypeName::operator==`). NO stand-in reconciliation was needed (both comparers are NEW types; no existing test file defined a stand-in for either, confirmed by grep). NO name-hiding qualification is needed (neither comparer redeclares an inherited member and none of the own members collides with a namespace-scope type -- the D375 collision-free-accessor convention). New files: cpp/Decompiler/TypeSystem/TopLevelTypeNameComparer.hpp + cpp/Decompiler/TypeSystem/FullTypeNameComparer.hpp (header-only `final` classes; the former includes `StringComparer.hpp` + `TopLevelTypeName.hpp`, the latter includes `FullTypeName.hpp` + `StringComparer.hpp`); cpp/tests/CMakeLists.txt added `Decompiler/TypeSystem/TopLevelTypeNameComparer_Test.cpp` + `Decompiler/TypeSystem/FullTypeNameComparer_Test.cpp` to `ilspy_tests` (after `ICompilation_Test.cpp`, before `Output/IAmbience_Test.cpp`). | D405 | TupleType (the C# 7 tuple type `(int, string)` / `(int x, string y)` built atop an underlying `System.ValueTuple<...>` parameterized type, the fourth and final of the four "concrete IType VisitChildren types" -- `ModifiedType` / `NullabilityAnnotatedType` / `FunctionPointerType` / `TupleType` -- that the not-yet-ported `TypeVisitor` / `TypeParameterSubstitution` need; a `class : AbstractType, ICompilationProvider` in ICSharpCode.Decompiler/TypeSystem/TupleType.cs) | port | Ported `TupleType` as a new concrete `IType` added to the minimal-port hub `cpp/Decompiler/TypeSystem/IType.hpp` (fully header-inline, like `NullabilityAnnotatedType` D402 and `FunctionPointerType` D404), the fourth and final of the four missing concrete `IType` types toward `TypeVisitor`/`TypeParameterSubstitution`/`TypeSystemAstBuilder`/`CSharpAmbience`. KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) The flatten-`AbstractType` convention: the C# `TupleType : AbstractType, ICompilationProvider` (the full IType base + the compilation-provider surface) is flattened to a direct `: IType` derivation in the C++ minimal port, exactly as `ModifiedType` D401 / `NullabilityAnnotatedType` D402 / `FunctionPointerType` D404 flatten their `TypeWithElementType`/`DecoratedType`/`AbstractType` bases. (b) The deferred-`CreateUnderlyingType` convention (the KEY design decision flagged in the D404 next-in-order analysis): the C# ctor builds its `UnderlyingType` (the `System.ValueTuple<...>` chain) at construction time via the recursive `CreateUnderlyingType` / `FindValueTupleType` helpers, which call `ICompilation.FindType` at runtime and thread 8-ary `ValueTuple<T1..T7,TRest>` nesting through `RestPosition = 8`. The minimal port DEFERS this recursion by accepting an ALREADY-BUILT `UnderlyingType` as a ctor parameter -- the caller (a future port of the `TupleType` ctor or `FromUnderlyingType` / the type-resolution stage) builds the `System.ValueTuple<...>` `ParameterizedType` and hands it in, so this minimal leaf needs no `ICompilation` at construction. This is distinct from D404 `FunctionPointerType` (whose names are a fixed literal `"delegate*"` so no underlying-type construction is needed) and is the structural reason `TupleType` was the heaviest of the four for a minimal port (its `Name`/`ReflectionName`/`FullName`/`Namespace` ALL delegate to the `UnderlyingType`, unlike `FunctionPointerType` whose names are fixed). (c) The deferred-`Compilation`-member convention (the D404 deferred-`module` precedent): the C# `public ICompilation Compilation` property (the `ICompilationProvider` surface) is OMITTED from the minimal port -- the minimal IType port does not implement `ICompilationProvider` on its concrete `IType` types (none of `KnownType`/`SimpleType`/`ParameterizedType`/`ArrayType`/... do), and the `Compilation` is consumed only by the deferred `CreateUnderlyingType` (the ctor recursion) and `VisitChildren` (the `TypeVisitor` dispatch). So the ctor takes `(ITypePtr underlyingType, std::vector<ITypePtr> elementTypes, std::vector<std::string> elementNames = {})` -- matching the C# ctor's post-recursion shape MINUS the `ICompilation compilation` / `IModule valueTupleAssembly` params (the recursion inputs) -- and the `Compilation` property / `ICompilationProvider` / `IsTupleCompatible` / `FromUnderlyingType` / `GetTupleElementTypes` static helpers / `GetHashCode` / `ToString` / the member-access delegations (`GetMethods`/`GetProperties`/`GetFields`/... forward to `UnderlyingType`) / `AcceptVisitor`/`VisitChildren` (the `TypeVisitor` dispatch) land with the rest of Phase 2. (d) `Kind()` is `TypeKind::Tuple` (a unique discriminator, unlike D402 `NullabilityAnnotatedType` whose `Kind` delegates to its base -- so a `TupleType`-vs-non-`TupleType` comparison short-circuits in `IType::Equals`'s `Kind()` guard before `StructuralEquals`, no UB; the D401/D404 unique-`Kind` precedent). (e) `Name()`/`ReflectionName()` delegate to the `UnderlyingType` verbatim (the C# `FullName`/`Name`/`ReflectionName`/`Namespace` all delegate to `UnderlyingType`) -- so a `(int, string)` tuple renders `Name()`="ValueTuple" and `ReflectionName()`="System.ValueTuple`2<System.Int32, System.String>" (the full underlying form, NOT a tuple-syntax form like "(int, string)" which the C# surfaces only in `ToString`). (f) `TypeParameterCount()` is `0` (the C# `TupleType` overrides it to `0`, distinct from the underlying `ValueTuple<...>` which has arity 2/8 -- the tuple's own type-parameter count is 0; the arity lives on the underlying parameterized type). (g) The `ElementNames` "not-provided" sentinel: the C# ctor fills `ElementNames` with `null` strings matching `ElementTypes.Length` when the caller passes `default(ImmutableArray<string>)` (the uninitialized `ImmutableArray` sentinel, distinct from an empty array). The C++ minimal port treats an EMPTY `elementNames` vector as the "not provided" sentinel and fills it with empty strings matching `elementTypes.size()` -- a slight deviation (an empty vector conflates with the `default` sentinel, but a 0-element tuple legitimately has both empty), documented in the header; the `C# Debug.Assert(elementNames.Length == elementTypes.Length)` when names ARE provided ports to an `assert` in the ctor that the names vector is either empty or matches the element count (`elementNames_.empty() or-else elementNames_.size() == elementTypes_.size()`, the D404 `Debug.Assert`-to-`assert` precedent). (h) `Equals` (via `IType::Equals` -> `StructuralEquals`) compares `UnderlyingType.Equals(o.UnderlyingType) && ElementNames` element-wise, faithful to the C# `Equals(IType)` override DE-DUPLICATED: the C# source calls `UnderlyingType.Equals(o.UnderlyingType)` TWICE (a redundant source quirk -- `if (!UnderlyingType.Equals(o.UnderlyingType)) return false; return UnderlyingType.Equals(o.UnderlyingType) && ElementNames.SequenceEqual(o.ElementNames);`); the effective condition is `UnderlyingType.Equals(o.UnderlyingType) && ElementNames.SequenceEqual`, ported as such with a note. (i) The accessors are `Cardinality()` (the C# `Cardinality => ElementTypes.Length`) / `ElementTypes()` / `ElementNames()` / `UnderlyingType()` -- the own accessors, NOT IType virtuals in the minimal port (the D404 convention). It is the concrete `TypeVisitor` the `IMember` long-pole references: `IMember` (D387) declares `Substitution` / `Specialize` / `Equals` over `const TypeParameterSubstitution*` / `const TypeVisitor*` (forward-declared there, deferred); a specialized member's `Specialize(substitution)` runs each of its types through `substitution` via `IType::AcceptVisitor`. Landing this class makes `TypeParameterSubstitution` a real `TypeVisitor` the member family can reference. KEY PORT CONVENTIONS: (a) The C# `IReadOnlyList<IType> classTypeArguments` / `methodTypeArguments` (nullable reference lists -- `null` = keep unmodified) port to `std::optional<std::vector<ITypePtr>>` -- `std::nullopt` = keep unmodified (the C# `null`), a present (possibly empty) vector = the substitute list; an empty list is distinct from `nullopt` (an empty list substitutes every index out of range to `UnknownType`; `nullopt` leaves the parameter unchanged). `std::optional` is the faithful C++ representation of the nullable `IReadOnlyList<IType>`: the `has_value()` test is the C# `!= null` test. (b) The `Identity` singleton (the C# `static readonly Identity = new TypeParameterSubstitution(null, null)`) ports to a function-local static (the Meyers-singleton pattern, the `StringComparer::Ordinal` D398 / `KnownAttributeTypeNames` D378 precedent) returning `const TypeParameterSubstitution&` -- the C++ counterpart of the C# `static readonly` reference-type field; the same instance is returned across calls (stable singleton, pointer-identity). (c) `Compose(g, f)` is the function-composition helper (`t.AcceptVisitor(Compose(g, f))` equals `t.AcceptVisitor(f).AcceptVisitor(g)`). The C# reference-type parameters (`g` / `f`, both nullable, returning a reference) port to NON-const nullable raw pointers and a by-value return: a fresh `TypeParameterSubstitution` (the C# heap allocation realized as a value). `Compose(nullptr, nullptr)` returns the `Identity` (a by-value copy of it) -- behaviorally equivalent to the C# `null` result (both leave every type parameter unchanged), since the C++ by-value return cannot express null. The pointers are NON-const because `Compose` runs `input[i].AcceptVisitor(*g)` and `AcceptVisitor(TypeVisitor&)` takes a non-const reference (the D406 non-const TypeVisitor convention). (d) The `VisitTypeParameter` body reads `type.Index()` / `type.OwnerType()` (the `ITypeParameter` interface D383 accessors), so it is OUT-OF-LINE in the .cpp (which includes `ITypeParameter.hpp`), mirroring the `TypeVisitor.cpp` out-of-line `VisitTypeParameter` default -- the header forward-declares `ITypeParameter` (already forward-declared by `TypeVisitor.hpp`) and declares only the override signature. (e) `GetHashCode`'s `element.GetHashCode()` (the C# `object.GetHashCode` identity hash that `AbstractType.GetHashCode` returns via `base.GetHashCode()` = `RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode(this)`) ports to `std::hash<IType*>{}(element.get())` cast to `int` (the identity hash of the shared `IType` object's address) -- the faithful C++ counterpart of the .NET identity-hash; the C++ minimal `IType` port has no `GetHashCode` member, so the pointer-identity hash is the faithful substitute (the production concrete types' value-based `GetHashCode` overrides are not ported yet). The `unchecked` wraparound arithmetic ports to `unsigned int` accumulation and a `static_cast<int>` return (the D400 `FullTypeNameComparer.GetHashCode` unchecked-wraparound convention). (f) The C# `VisitNullabilityAnnotatedType` override checks `type is NullabilityAnnotatedTypeParameter` (the nested subclass that wraps an `ITypeParameter`, D402 deferred). The minimal port DEFERS this override -- the base `VisitNullabilityAnnotatedType` (the `VisitChildren` reconstruct-the-wrapper default D406) handles a plain `NullabilityAnnotatedType`; the `NullabilityAnnotatedTypeParameter` nested subclass lands with the rest of Phase 2. (g) The C# `Equals(object)` overrides `object.Equals` (no C++ base); the port provides a standalone `bool Equals(const TypeParameterSubstitution* other) const` (nullable pointer, the C# `obj as TypeParameterSubstitution` and the `if (other == null) return false` check), distinguished from `Equals(other, normalization)` by parameter count. THE ACCEPTVISITOR-DISPATCH DESIGN DECISION (flagged in the D406 next-in-order analysis): the C# `AbstractTypeParameter.AcceptVisitor => visitor.VisitTypeParameter(this)` (ICSharpCode.Decompiler/TypeSystem/Implementation/AbstractTypeParameter.cs:279) is the bridge that dispatches an `ITypeParameter`-derived object's `AcceptVisitor` to `VisitTypeParameter`. The C++ minimal port's `ITypeParameter` interface (D383) inherits `IType::AcceptVisitor`'s default (dispatch to `VisitOtherType`, the D406 flattened-`AbstractType` convention), so a plain `ITypeParameter`-derived object does NOT dispatch to `VisitTypeParameter` by default.
